options.text: Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket.
Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster for the S3 bucket.
Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure an ALB to resolve to the Amplify website.
Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure EC2 instances to cache the website.

questions.explanation:
For a website that serves only static content, Amazon S3 is the appropriate origin because it can host static assets without running web servers, and Amazon CloudFront can cache and distribute that content globally at scale. This removes the ongoing cost of EC2 instances and the ALB while still supporting increasing traffic efficiently. ElastiCache is not the standard hosting layer for S3 static websites, and adding ALB or EC2 in front of AWS Amplify would add unnecessary infrastructure instead of minimizing cost.

**Learn more:** [Use Amazon S3 website hosting to host without a single web server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/build-static-websites-aws/use-amazon-s3-website-hosting-to-host-without-a-single-web-server.html) · [Get started with a secure static website](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/getting-started-secure-static-website-cloudformation-template.html)

A recent review of a company's IT spending shows a need to lower backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce expenses by removing the use of physical backup tapes. The company must retain its existing investment in on-premises backup applications and workflows.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.
Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway is built for replacing physical tape infrastructure while preserving existing backup applications and operational processes. It exposes a virtual tape library over an iSCSI interface, which lets current tape-based backup software continue to operate with minimal change while eliminating physical tapes and their associated management costs. Amazon EFS is a network file system, not a tape replacement service, and it does not provide the VTL capability required to maintain existing tape-oriented backup workflows.

**Learn more:** [How Tape Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A gaming company is migrating its public scoreboard from a data center to the AWS Cloud. The company uses Amazon EC2 Windows Server instances behind an Application Load Balancer to run its dynamic application. The company requires a highly available storage solution for the application. The application includes static files and dynamic server-side code.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront to cache objects at the edge.
Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache objects at the edge.
Store the server-side code on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
Store the server-side code on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
Store the server-side code on a General Purpose SSD (gp2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 provides highly available storage for static content, and Amazon CloudFront is the AWS service that caches that content at edge locations for low-latency delivery. For Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances that must share server-side code, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the appropriate highly available shared file storage service because it exposes SMB file shares that Windows instances can mount. Amazon EFS is not supported for Microsoft Windows–based EC2 instances, and Amazon EBS is not the right choice for shared highly available storage across multiple EC2 application servers.

**Learn more:** [Request and response behavior for Amazon S3 origins - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/RequestAndResponseBehaviorS3Origin.html) · [Amazon CloudFront Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution must analyze both existing and new data by using SQL. The company stores its data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted at rest and replicated to another AWS Region.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.

Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon RDS to query the data.
Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that analyzes data directly in Amazon S3 with standard SQL. S3 Cross-Region Replication replicates new and updated objects written after the replication configuration is created, so existing data must be loaded into a replication-configured bucket to ensure it is also replicated. Configuring the new bucket with SSE-KMS using multi-Region keys provides encryption at rest across the replicated S3 data.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Querying Amazon S3 tables with Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-tables-integrating-athena.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a global web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in Amazon Aurora.  
  
The company must create a disaster recovery solution and can tolerate up to **30 minutes** of downtime and possible data loss. The solution does **not** need to handle the load while the primary infrastructure is healthy.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
Host a scaled-down deployment of the application in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora Replica in the second Region.
Replicate the primary infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora database that is restored from the latest snapshot.

Back up data with AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora second primary instance in the second Region.

questions.explanation:
An active-passive disaster recovery design is the best fit because the secondary Region does not need to serve traffic during normal operations. Amazon Route 53 failover routing supports active-passive failover, and an Aurora cross-Region replica provides a ready secondary database that can be promoted during a regional disaster. This gives a substantially lower recovery time and recovery point than rebuilding from backups or snapshots, while avoiding the extra cost and complexity of an active-active design.

**Learn more:** [Active-active and active-passive failover - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html) · [Replicating Amazon Aurora MySQL DB clusters across AWS Regions - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Replication.CrossRegion.html)

3a:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company runs a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website delivers static content. Traffic to the website is increasing. The company wants to reduce the website hosting costs as much as possible."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket.","B":"Move the website to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster for the S3 bucket.","C":"Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure an ALB to resolve to the Amplify website.","D":"Move the website to AWS Amplify. Configure EC2 instances to cache the website."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"For a website that serves only static content, Amazon S3 is the appropriate origin because it can host static assets without running web servers, and Amazon CloudFront can cache and distribute that content globally at scale. This removes the ongoing cost of EC2 instances and the ALB while still supporting increasing traffic efficiently. ElastiCache is not the standard hosting layer for S3 static websites, and adding ALB or EC2 in front of AWS Amplify would add unnecessary infrastructure instead of minimizing cost.

**Learn more:** [Use Amazon S3 website hosting to host without a single web server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/build-static-websites-aws/use-amazon-s3-website-hosting-to-host-without-a-single-web-server.html) · [Get started with a secure static website](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/getting-started-secure-static-website-cloudformation-template.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"dc9b80ec-3ba2-4fad-9e05-164be732a6f2","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
51:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A recent review of a company's IT spending shows a need to lower backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce expenses by removing the use of physical backup tapes. The company must retain its existing investment in on-premises backup applications and workflows."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should a solutions architect recommend?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.","B":"Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.","C":"Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.","D":"Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway is built for replacing physical tape infrastructure while preserving existing backup applications and operational processes. It exposes a virtual tape library over an iSCSI interface, which lets current tape-based backup software continue to operate with minimal change while eliminating physical tapes and their associated management costs. Amazon EFS is a network file system, not a tape replacement service, and it does not provide the VTL capability required to maintain existing tape-oriented backup workflows.

**Learn more:** [How Tape Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c078d6f7-1330-4cb0-951d-63325bd1fcb0","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A gaming company is migrating its public scoreboard from a data center to the AWS Cloud. The company uses Amazon EC2 Windows Server instances behind an Application Load Balancer to run its dynamic application. The company requires a highly available storage solution for the application. The application includes static files and dynamic server-side code."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront to cache objects at the edge.","B":"Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache objects at the edge.","C":"Store the server-side code on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.","D":"Store the server-side code on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.","E":"Store the server-side code on a General Purpose SSD (gp2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files."},"correctAnswer":"AD","explanation":"Amazon S3 provides highly available storage for static content, and Amazon CloudFront is the AWS service that caches that content at edge locations for low-latency delivery. For Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances that must share server-side code, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the appropriate highly available shared file storage service because it exposes SMB file shares that Windows instances can mount. Amazon EFS is not supported for Microsoft Windows–based EC2 instances, and Amazon EBS is not the right choice for shared highly available storage across multiple EC2 application servers.

**Learn more:** [Request and response behavior for Amazon S3 origins - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/RequestAndResponseBehaviorS3Origin.html) · [Amazon CloudFront Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"5dd1daab-7158-4e7b-9759-f721e3df1acf","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company wants to migrate its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution must analyze both existing and new data by using SQL. ",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution meets these requirements with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST"}]," operational overhead?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.","B":"Create a new S3 bucket that uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use Amazon RDS to query the data.","C":"Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.","D":"Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the existing S3 bucket. A company has an application that ingests incoming messages. Dozens of other applications and microservices then consume these messages quickly.  
  
The number of messages varies drastically and sometimes suddenly increases to 100,000 each second. The company wants to decouple the solution and improve scalability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read and process the messages.
Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number of EC2 instances based on CPU metrics.

Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function to preprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the consumer applications to read from DynamoDB to process the messages.

Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the messages from the queues.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon SNS topic with multiple Amazon SQS queue subscriptions provides a scalable pub/sub fanout pattern. The producer publishes each message once to SNS, and SNS delivers copies to multiple SQS queues so each downstream application or microservice can process messages independently at its own rate. That design decouples publishers from consumers and allows each consumer tier to scale separately. A single Kinesis Data Streams shard cannot handle 100,000 messages per second, and Kinesis Data Analytics is for stream analytics rather than broad fanout consumption.

**Learn more:** [Fanout Amazon SNS notifications to Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous processing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-sqs-as-subscriber.html) · [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)

A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.

Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager can be configured natively to store session log data in a specified Amazon S3 bucket. Using the built-in S3 logging setting in Session Manager preferences is the most operationally efficient approach because it sends the session data directly to S3 for archival without extra agents, scheduled documents, CloudWatch export steps, or Kinesis Data Firehose components. AWS documentation specifically describes configuring Session Manager to log session data to an S3 bucket from the Systems Manager console.

**Learn more:** [Logging session data using Amazon S3 (console) - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-logging-s3.html) · [Enabling and disabling session logging - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-logging.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing an application. The application uses an AWS Lambda function to receive information through Amazon API Gateway and to store the information in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.  
  
During the proof-of-concept stage, the company must increase the Lambda quotas significantly to handle the high volumes of data that need to be loaded into the database.  
  
A solutions architect must recommend a new design to improve scalability and minimize the configuration effort.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Refactor the Lambda function code to Apache Tomcat code that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Connect the database by using native Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) drivers.
Change the platform from Aurora to Amazon DynamoDProvision a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Use the DAX client SDK to point the existing DynamoDB API calls at the DAX cluster.

Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon SQS queue between two Lambda functions provides asynchronous decoupling and buffering, which is the standard AWS pattern for absorbing traffic spikes and letting the database-loading function process messages at a manageable rate. AWS documents SQS as a service for decoupling and scaling distributed and serverless applications, and Lambda’s event-driven architecture guidance describes SQS as an elastic buffer that helps handle increased traffic. Lambda can also poll SQS in batches before invocation, which improves ingest scalability for database writes. SNS is better suited to push-based pub/sub fanout, not workload buffering for controlled downstream processing, and the EC2/Tomcat or DynamoDB/DAX options require unnecessary redesign or added management.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Simple Queue Service Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sqs/) · [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

A company’s application integrates with multiple software-as-a-service (SaaS) sources for data collection. The company uses Amazon EC2 instances to receive the data and upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for analysis. The same EC2 instance that receives and uploads the data also sends a notification to the user when an upload has completed.  
  
The company has noticed slow application performance and wants to improve performance as much as possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group so that EC2 instances can scale out. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.

Create an Amazon AppFlow flow to transfer data between each SaaS source and the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for each SaaS source to send output data. Configure the S3 bucket as the rule's target. Create a second EventBridge (Cloud Watch Events) rule to send events when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the second rule's target.

Create a Docker container to use instead of an EC2 instance. Host the containerized application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.

questions.explanation:
Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed service for transferring data between supported SaaS applications and AWS services such as Amazon S3, so it removes the custom EC2-based ingestion and upload work that is causing unnecessary operational burden. Amazon S3 can natively generate event notifications for object-created events and send them to Amazon SNS, which satisfies the upload-complete notification requirement without additional application infrastructure. This combination both maximizes offloading to managed services and minimizes operations.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon AppFlow?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/what-is-appflow.html) · [Supported source and destination applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/app-specific.html)

A company manages a data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket that many applications access. The S3 bucket has a unique prefix for each application. The company wants to restrict every application to its own prefix and provide granular control over the objects under each prefix.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create dedicated S3 access points and access point policies for each application.
Create an S3 Batch Operations job to set the ACL permissions for each object in the S3 bucket.
Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create replication rules by prefix.
Replicate the objects in the S3 bucket to new S3 buckets for each application. Create dedicated S3 access points for each application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Access Points are intended for shared S3 datasets and let you create a separate access endpoint and policy for each application. Those policies can limit access to objects under a specific prefix, which provides per-application isolation and fine-grained control without copying data or managing object ACLs individually. This is simpler operationally than replication to multiple buckets or ACL updates across objects.

**Learn more:** [Managing access to shared datasets with access points - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points.html) · [Access control in Amazon S3 - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-management.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application can handle the workload and avoid downtime?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling is the correct solution for a workload increase that occurs at a known recurring time. AWS documentation states that scheduled scaling is useful when you know exactly when to increase capacity because the need arises on a predictable schedule, and recurring schedules can be created for those times. In this case, increasing Auto Scaling capacity before midnight on the first day of each month lets the fleet absorb the batch-processing spike without waiting for CPU-based reactive scaling to trigger.

**Learn more:** [Choose your scaling method - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html) · [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC and the subnets use IPv4 CIDR blocks. There is one public subnet and one private subnet in each of three Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability. An internet gateway provides internet access for the public subnets. The private subnets need internet access so that Amazon EC2 instances can download software updates.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to enable internet access for the private subnets?

options.text: Create three NAT gateways, one for each public subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in its AZ.
Create three NAT instances, one for each private subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT instance in its AZ.
Create a second internet gateway on one of the private subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the private internet gateway.
Create an egress-only internet gateway on one of the public subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the egress-only Internet gateway.

questions.explanation:
For IPv4 private subnets, outbound internet access is provided by a NAT device, and AWS recommends using NAT gateways. In a multi-AZ design, AWS guidance is to create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and configure each private subnet's route table to send non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in the same AZ, which preserves resiliency if one AZ fails. An egress-only internet gateway applies only to IPv6, and an internet gateway does not provide the required private-subnet outbound pattern for IPv4.

**Learn more:** [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html) · [NAT gateway basics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-basics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an HTTP application behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB target group uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that contains multiple EC2 instances running the web service.  
  
The company finds that the NLB is not identifying HTTP errors for the application. These errors require the EC2 instances that run the web service to be restarted manually. The company must improve the availability of the application without writing custom scripts or code.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable HTTP health checks on the NLB, supplying the URL of the company's application.
Add a cron job to the EC2 instances to check the local application's logs once each minute. If HTTP errors are detected. the application will restart.
Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer. Enable HTTP health checks by supplying the URL of the company's application. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances.
Create an Amazon Cloud Watch alarm that monitors the UnhealthyHostCount metric for the NLB. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances when the alarm is in the ALARM state.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and does not support HTTP/HTTPS health checks with application-level URLs. An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports HTTP/HTTPS health checks with path-based routing, enabling detection of HTTP-level errors. Replacing the NLB with an ALB and configuring EC2 Auto Scaling to replace instances reported as unhealthy by ALB health checks provides the required automatic recovery without custom scripts.

**Learn more:** [Health checks for ALB target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-health-checks.html) · [Auto Scaling health checks with ELB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-health-checks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its primary public web application in one AWS Region spanning multiple Availability Zones. The application uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
A web development team requires a cost-optimized compute solution that improves the company’s ability to serve dynamic content globally to millions of customers.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the existing ALB as the origin.
Use Amazon Route 53 to serve traffic to the ALB and EC2 instances based on the geographic location of each customer.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket with public read access enabled. Migrate the web application to the S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting.
Use AWS Direct Connect to directly serve content from the web application to the location of each customer.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront provides global edge delivery and supports an Application Load Balancer as an origin. CloudFront can deliver and cache eligible responses close to viewers while forwarding dynamic requests to the existing ALB and EC2 Auto Scaling group, reducing latency and origin load without migrating the dynamic application.

**Learn more:** [Use various origins with CloudFront distributions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistS3AndCustomOrigins.html) · [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an application that runs in containers within a VPC. The application stores and retrieves data from an Amazon S3 bucket. During the development phase, the application will store and access 1 TB of data in Amazon S3 each day. The company wants to reduce costs and avoid traffic traversing the internet whenever possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the S3 bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 lets resources in a VPC access S3 over the AWS network without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device, and AWS documents that there is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints. Amazon S3 interface endpoints also keep traffic on the AWS network, but they are billed and are mainly needed for cases such as on-premises or cross-Region private access. Because this application runs inside the VPC and the goal is to minimize cost while avoiding internet paths, the S3 gateway endpoint is the correct solution.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an on-premises application on a Kubernetes cluster. The company has recently gained millions of new customers, and its current on-premises infrastructure cannot support the large number of new customers. The company must migrate the on-premises application to the AWS Cloud.  
  
The company will migrate to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The company does not want to manage the underlying compute infrastructure for the new AWS architecture.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use a self-managed node to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.
Use managed node groups to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.
Use AWS Fargate to supply compute capacity. Create a Fargate profile. Use the Fargate profile to deploy the application.
Use managed node groups with Karpenter to supply compute capacity. Deploy the application to the new EKS cluster.

questions.explanation:
AWS Fargate is serverless compute for Amazon EKS pods. AWS provisions, scales, and maintains the underlying infrastructure, removing the need to manage worker-node instances. A Fargate profile specifies which pods are scheduled onto Fargate, so it satisfies the requirement without administering self-managed nodes, managed node groups, or Karpenter-managed EC2 capacity.

**Learn more:** [Simplify compute management with AWS Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/fargate.html) · [Define which Pods use AWS Fargate when launched](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/fargate-profile.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores millions of objects across several prefixes in an Amazon S3 bucket using the Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. The company must delete all data older than 3 years, except for a subset of data that must be retained. The company has identified the data that must be retained and wants to implement a serverless solution.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use S3 Inventory to list all objects. Use the AWS CLI to create a script that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that deletes objects from the inventory list.
Use AWS Batch to delete objects older than 3 years except for the data that must be retained.
Provision an AWS Glue crawler to query objects older than 3 years. Save the manifest file of old objects. Create a script to delete objects in the manifest.
Enable S3 Inventory. Create an AWS Lambda function to filter and delete objects. Invoke the Lambda function with S3 Batch Operations to delete objects by using the inventory reports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Inventory can supply the object list for an S3 Batch Operations job. S3 Batch Operations can invoke an AWS Lambda function for each object in that manifest, allowing the function to retain the identified subset and delete the remaining objects older than 3 years without managing servers.

**Learn more:** [Performing object operations in bulk with Batch Operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops.html) · [Invoke AWS Lambda function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops-invoke-lambda.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a 100 GB Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Single-AZ DB instance in the `us-east-1` Region to store customer transactions. The company requires high availability and automatic recovery for the DB instance.  
  
The company must also run reports on the RDS database several times each year. The reporting process causes transactions to take longer than normal to post to customers’ accounts. The company needs a solution that will improve the performance of the reporting process.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Modify the DB instance from a Single-AZ DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment.
Take a snapshot of the current DB instance. Restore the snapshot to a new RDS deployment in another Availability Zone.
Create a read replica of the DB instance in a different Availability Zone. Point all requests for reports to the read replica.
Migrate the database to RDS Custom.
Use RDS Proxy to limit reporting requests to the maintenance window.

questions.explanation:
A Multi-AZ deployment is the Amazon RDS feature that provides high availability and automatic failover for Microsoft SQL Server by maintaining a synchronized standby in another Availability Zone. To improve reporting performance, the reporting workload should be offloaded from the primary DB instance to a read replica, with report requests directed to that replica. This combination satisfies both the HA/automatic recovery requirement and the need to reduce reporting impact on transactional workloads.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ deployments for Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_SQLServerMultiAZ.html) · [Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server in Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.ReadReplicas.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a shared storage solution for a web application that is deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The company plans to make frequent changes to the content. The solution must provide strong consistency so that new content is returned as soon as the changes occur.  
  
Which solutions meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) block storage that is mounted to the individual EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on the individual EC2 instances.
Create a shared Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the individual EC2 instances.
Use AWS DataSync to perform continuous synchronization of data between EC2 hosts in the Auto Scaling group.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the web content. Set the metadata for the Cache-Control header to no-cache. Use Amazon CloudFront to deliver the content.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS provides a managed file system with strong consistency semantics that can be mounted across multiple EC2 instances in different Availability Zones, eliminating data synchronization complexity. Amazon S3 with CloudFront and Cache-Control: no-cache ensures that updated content is revalidated from the origin on each request, providing immediate consistency. S3 offers strong read-after-write consistency for new uploads and overwrites, making this combination suitable for frequently updated web content.

**Learn more:** [Mounting EFS to multiple EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mount-multiple-ec2-instances.html) · [Managing how long content stays in the cache (expiration)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Expiration.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the `ap-southeast-3` Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company’s AWS account in `ap-southeast-3`.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company’s AWS account.

questions.explanation:
For Amazon Aurora, an encrypted manual snapshot can be shared across AWS accounts when the snapshot uses a customer managed KMS key and the target account is granted permission to use that key. The correct approach is to create a snapshot, update the KMS key policy to allow the acquiring AWS account, and then share the snapshot with that account. Using an unencrypted snapshot would weaken security, a KMS alias does not grant cross-account cryptographic permissions, and Aurora snapshots are shared through RDS snapshot-sharing features rather than by downloading and uploading them to Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [Sharing encrypted snapshots for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/share-encrypted-snapshot.html) · [Sharing a DB cluster snapshot - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-share-snapshot.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A social media company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The application has more than a billion images stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and processes thousands of images each second. The company wants to resize the images dynamically and deliver appropriate formats to clients.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Install an external image management library on an EC2 instance. Use the image management library to process the images.
Create a CloudFront origin request policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.
Use a Lambda@Edge function with an external image management library. Associate the Lambda@Edge function with the CloudFront behaviors that serve the images.
Create a CloudFront response headers policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.

questions.explanation:
Lambda@Edge is the only listed CloudFront feature that can execute custom logic at edge locations to transform requests or responses, which makes it suitable for dynamic image resizing and selecting an appropriate image format based on request characteristics. AWS documentation describes using Lambda@Edge for request customization and AWS guidance specifically shows image resizing with CloudFront and Lambda@Edge. By contrast, an origin request policy only controls which headers, cookies, and query strings CloudFront forwards to the origin, and a response headers policy only adds or removes HTTP headers in responses; neither policy performs image processing.

**Learn more:** [Ways to use Lambda@Edge - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-ways-to-use.html) · [Resizing Images with Amazon CloudFront & Lambda@Edge](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/resizing-images-with-amazon-cloudfront-lambdaedge-aws-cdn-blog/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must keep its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail for a group of AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail destination S3 bucket has S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy exists to delete current objects after 3 years.  
  
After the fourth year of using the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics indicate that the number of objects has continued to increase. However, the number of newly delivered CloudTrail logs to the S3 bucket has stayed consistent.  
  
Which solution will delete objects that are more than 3 years old in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.
Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.
Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
In a versioning-enabled S3 bucket, expiring only current objects does not remove noncurrent versions, so older object versions can continue to accumulate and increase storage usage. The correct fix is to add S3 Lifecycle expiration for previous (noncurrent) versions as well as current versions. This uses native S3 lifecycle management, which is the lowest-cost and simplest way to enforce the 3-year retention period for CloudTrail logs.

**Learn more:** [Retaining multiple versions of objects with S3 Versioning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Versioning.html) · [Troubleshooting versioning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-versioning.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application needs durable storage with consistent, low-latency performance.  
  
Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Instance store volume
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume

questions.explanation:
Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon EBS volumes are durable block storage designed for workloads that require predictable high IOPS and consistently low latency. Instance store volumes are ephemeral, ElastiCache for Memcached is a cache rather than durable application storage, and Throughput Optimized HDD EBS volumes are intended for throughput-focused sequential workloads instead of low-latency I/O.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company offers an online service for uploading video content and transcoding it for use on any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the service has become more popular over time, the storage costs have grown too expensive.  
  
Which storage solution is **MOST cost-effective**?

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is generally the most cost-effective AWS service for storing large volumes of video objects, while Amazon EBS is appropriate as temporary block storage attached to an EC2 instance during processing. AWS Storage Gateway is primarily for hybrid storage use cases that connect on-premises environments to AWS, not for reducing storage cost in a cloud-native EC2 workload. Amazon EBS also is not the right long-term shared repository for the video library; even though some io1/io2 volumes can use Multi-Attach, EBS is block storage and not the economical shared content store that Amazon S3 is for this pattern.

**Learn more:** [Choosing an AWS storage service - AWS Decision Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/decision-guides/latest/storage-on-aws-how-to-choose/storage-on-aws-how-to-choose.pdf) · [AWS Storage Gateway Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving its data center and needs to securely transfer 50 TB of data to AWS within 2 weeks. The current data center has a Site-to-Site VPN connection to AWS that is 90% utilized.  
  
Which AWS service should a solutions architect use to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: AWS DataSync with a VPC endpoint
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized
AWS Storage Gateway

questions.explanation:
AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized is the best fit for a secure bulk transfer when the available network connection is already heavily used. Snowball Edge is specifically intended for moving large datasets into AWS by shipping an encrypted physical device, which avoids dependence on limited WAN bandwidth and is commonly recommended for migrations where transferring data over the network would be too slow or impractical.

**Learn more:** [AWS Snowball Edge device hardware information](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/device-differences.html)

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket that has the necessary permissions for the VPC. Configure the subnet route table to use the gateway VPC endpoint.
Move the S3 bucket inside the VPC. Configure the subnet route table to access the S3 bucket through private IP addresses.
Create an Amazon S3 access point for the Amazon EC2 instance inside the VPConfigure the web application to upload by using the Amazon S3 access point.
Configure an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC that has the Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon S3 to provide a dedicated network path.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint provides private connectivity from a VPC to Amazon S3 over the AWS network. Associating the endpoint with the route table used by the EC2 instance’s subnet adds an S3 route that takes precedence over the default internet route for S3 traffic.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

A company plans to use Amazon ElastiCache for its multi-tier web application. A solutions architect creates a Cache VPC for the ElastiCache cluster and an App VPC for the application's Amazon EC2 instances. Both VPCs are in the `us-east-1` Region.  
  
The solutions architect must implement a solution to provide the application's EC2 instances with access to the ElastiCache cluster.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs. Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster’s security group to allow inbound connection from the application’s security group.

Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC. Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster's security group to allow inbound connection from the application’s security group.

Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs. Configure an inbound rule for the peering connection’s security group to allow inbound connection from the application’s security group.

Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC. Configure an inbound rule for the Transit VPC’s security group to allow inbound connection from the application’s security group.

questions.explanation:
For an ElastiCache cluster and application instances that are in different VPCs within the same AWS Region, AWS recommends using VPC peering so the resources can communicate over private IP routing. This requires adding routes for the peering connection in both VPCs. Access to the cache is then allowed by the ElastiCache cluster’s security group, which should permit inbound traffic from the application tier. A Transit VPC is a more complex and costly design intended for broader transit use cases, not the most economical way to connect two same-Region VPCs for this requirement.

A company is deploying a new business application. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon S3 bucket for document storage.  
  
A solutions architect must ensure that the EC2 instances can access the S3 bucket.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create an IAM role that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
Create an IAM policy that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the policy to the EC2 instances.
Create an IAM group that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the group to the EC2 instances.
Create an IAM user that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the user account to the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 applications should access Amazon S3 by assuming an IAM role attached to the instances through an instance profile. The role carries the permissions to the S3 bucket and supplies temporary credentials to software running on the instances. IAM policies are permission documents rather than identities you attach directly to EC2 instances, IAM groups apply to IAM users, and IAM users would require long-term credentials, which is not the recommended design for EC2-to-S3 access.

**Learn more:** [IAM roles for Amazon EC2 - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html) · [Attach an IAM role to an instance - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/attach-iam-role.html)

The company needs an AWS event-driven system that guarantees the order of the events.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Amazon EventBridge event bus
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topics
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topics
Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues

questions.explanation:
Amazon SNS FIFO topics are the AWS pub/sub option that supports fanout to multiple downstream services while preserving strict message ordering and deduplication. AWS documentation states that FIFO topics deliver messages in the exact order they are published, and for workloads that require strict ordering, the supported pattern is Amazon SNS FIFO topics with Amazon SQS FIFO queues as subscribers. EventBridge does not provide ordering guarantees, SNS standard topics do not preserve order, and a single SQS FIFO queue does not provide concurrent fanout to multiple separate services.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SNS message ordering details for FIFO topics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/fifo-topic-message-ordering.html) · [Amazon SNS message delivery for FIFO topics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/fifo-message-delivery.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a Java application that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to parse messages. The application cannot parse messages larger than 256 KB.  
  
The company wants to implement a solution that gives the application the ability to parse messages as large as 50 MB.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **fewest** code changes?

options.text: Use the Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java to host messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon EventBridge to post large messages from the application instead of Amazon SQS.
Change the limit in Amazon SQS to handle messages that are larger than 256 KB.
Store messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Configure Amazon SQS to reference this location in the messages.

questions.explanation:
The Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java is the AWS-supported way to work with SQS payloads larger than the 256 KB SQS limit. It stores the actual message body in Amazon S3 and places an SQS message containing a reference to that S3 object, allowing Java applications to handle payloads far larger than 256 KB, including 50 MB, with minimal changes to existing SQS-based code.

**Learn more:** [Managing large Amazon SQS messages with Extended Client Library and Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-managing-large-messages.html) · [Managing large Amazon SQS messages using Java and Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-s3-messages.html)

The workload will run on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances and will need parallel access to a shared file system to support distributed processing of large datasets. Datasets will be accessed simultaneously across multiple instances. The workload requires access latency of less than 1 ms.  
  
After processing is complete, engineers will need access to the dataset for manual postprocessing.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as a shared file system. Access the dataset from Amazon EFS.
Mount an Amazon S3 bucket to serve as the shared file system. Perform postprocessing directly from the S3 bucket.
Use Amazon FSx for Lustre as a shared file system. Link the file system to an Amazon S3 bucket for postprocessing.
Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share an Amazon S3 bucket so that it can be mounted to all instances for processing and postprocessing.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre is the AWS managed file system designed for HPC and other compute-intensive workloads that need a shared, highly parallel file system with sub-millisecond latency. It can be used by large numbers of EC2 instances concurrently for distributed processing, and it integrates with Amazon S3 so data can be imported from and exported back to an S3 bucket for durable storage and later manual postprocessing. Official AWS documentation describes FSx for Lustre as optimized for HPC workloads and notes sub-millisecond latency and S3 data repository integration, which matches both the processing and postprocessing requirements.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html) · [Linking your file system to an Amazon S3 bucket - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/create-dra-linked-data-repo.html)

A solutions architect is deploying a document review application that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for storage.  
  
The solution must:  
  
- prevent accidental deletion of the documents  
- ensure that all versions of the documents remain available  
- allow users to download, modify, and upload documents  
  
Which combination of actions should be taken to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Enable a read-only bucket ACL.
Enable versioning on the bucket.
Attach an IAM policy to the bucket.
Enable MFA Delete on the bucket.
Encrypt the bucket using AWS KMS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Versioning preserves multiple variants of an object in the same bucket, so when users download, modify, and upload documents, previous versions remain available instead of being lost to overwrite. S3 MFA Delete adds an extra layer of protection against accidental or unauthorized permanent deletion of object versions and against changes to the bucket’s versioning state, which addresses the accidental-deletion requirement.

**Learn more:** [How S3 Versioning works - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/versioning-workflows.html) · [Configuring MFA delete - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiFactorAuthenticationDelete.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s application uses Network Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, and databases deployed in an Amazon VPC. The company wants to capture information about traffic to and from the network interfaces in near real time in its Amazon VPC. The company also wants to send this information to Amazon OpenSearch Service for analysis.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.

Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.

questions.explanation:
VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic information for network interfaces in a VPC. CloudWatch Logs can receive this data and use subscription filters to route logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service in near real-time. AWS CloudTrail is for recording API activity, not VPC network traffic, so it is inappropriate for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Publish flow logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-cwl.html) · [Send CloudWatch Logs to Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/writing-with-cloudwatch-logs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A weather forecasting company must process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities.  
  
A solutions architect needs to identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can support large amounts of sustained throughput. Files stored in the solution must be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems are built for HPC and scale-out workloads that need consistent sub-millisecond latency, very high sustained throughput, and parallel access from large numbers of compute instances. Persistent FSx for Lustre is the highly available option because data is replicated and failed file servers are automatically replaced. Scratch FSx for Lustre is intended for temporary storage and is not replicated, while Amazon EFS Bursting Throughput is not appropriate for sustained high throughput because it relies on burst credits. Official AWS documentation describes persistent FSx for Lustre as ideal for longer-term, throughput-focused workloads and notes that the SSD storage class provides consistent sub-millisecond latency across the full dataset.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html) · [Amazon FSx for Lustre performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/performance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large volumes of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing so the data can be processed more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.
Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EMR is designed for distributed, parallel processing of large datasets in Amazon S3 by using engines such as Apache Spark. It is the best fit when the goal is to process large amounts of semistructured S3 data faster through parallel computation. EMR can also be used with Amazon Redshift data as part of an ETL or analytics workflow to enrich the S3 dataset. By contrast, Athena is primarily an interactive SQL query service, Kinesis Data Streams is for streaming ingestion rather than batch enrichment from S3, and AWS Lake Formation provides data lake governance rather than data processing or enrichment.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon EMR?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-what-is-emr.html) · [Redshift connections - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-redshift-home.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is testing an application that runs on an Amazon EC2 Linux instance. One 500 GB Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSO (gp2) volume is attached to the EC2 instance.  
  
The company plans to deploy the application on multiple EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Every instance needs access to the data stored on the EBS volume. The company requires a highly available, resilient solution that does not require significant changes to the application's code.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Provision an EC2 instance that uses NFS server software. Attach a single 500 GB gp2 EBS volume to the instance.
Provision an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Configure the file system as an SMB file store within a single Availability Zone.
Provision an EC2 instance with two 250 GB Provisioned IOPS SSD EBS volumes.
Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure the file system to use General Purpose performance mode.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that multiple Linux EC2 instances can mount and access concurrently, so it supports shared application data without substantive code changes. A Regional EFS file system stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones for availability and resilience, and AWS recommends General Purpose performance mode for EFS file systems.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Creating EFS file systems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/creating-using-create-fs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lake Formation provides native data filters to enforce fine-grained access control on table data, including row-level and cell-level security. That directly satisfies the need to hide only sensitive portions of the data while keeping the data available for analysis. Using built-in Lake Formation filtering has less operational overhead than building and maintaining Lambda functions to redact or delete data, and IAM permissions alone do not provide this level of granular data protection.

**Learn more:** [Data filtering and cell-level security in Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/data-filtering.html) · [Managing data filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/managing-filters.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has five organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations. Each OU corresponds to one of the five businesses that the company owns. The company's research and development (R&D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose.  
  
What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?

options.text: Have the R&D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.
Invite the R&D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&D AWS account has left the prior organization.
Create a new R&D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&D AWS account to the new R&D AWS account.
Have the R&D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.

questions.explanation:
An AWS member account can belong to only one organization at a time. To move the existing R&D account to the new organization, the account must first leave or be removed from the original organization, and then the new management account can invite it to join the new organization. AWS Organizations documentation describes this as the account migration process between organizations.

**Learn more:** [Terminology and concepts for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_getting-started_concepts.html) · [Migrate an account to another organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html)
