lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity from different web applications so it can process analytics and generate predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can suddenly increase.  
  
The company needs a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must also include an authorization step for security purposes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.

Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway provides an API endpoint that other web applications can call, and an API Gateway Lambda authorizer adds the required authorization control. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service for capturing streaming data and automatically delivering it to Amazon S3, which fits bursty, unpredictable activity and downstream analytics storage. Gateway Load Balancer is intended for network virtual appliances rather than this kind of application-facing event ingestion, and Kinesis Data Streams does not by itself store the data in Amazon S3 without additional consumer processing. 

**Learn more:** [Use API Gateway Lambda authorizers - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-use-lambda-authorizer.html) · [Tutorial: Create a REST API as an Amazon Kinesis proxy - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/integrating-api-with-aws-services-kinesis.html)

A company wants to implement a disaster recovery plan for its primary on-premises file storage volume. The file storage volume is mounted from an Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) device on a local storage server, and the file storage volume contains hundreds of terabytes (TB) of data.  
  
The company wants to make sure that end users keep immediate access to all file types from the on-premises systems without experiencing latency.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** amount of change to the company's existing infrastructure?

options.text: Provision an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual machine (VM) that is hosted on premises. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Modify existing applications to access the files through the NFS protocol. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and mount the S3 bucket that contains the files.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Use a data backup solution to back up all existing data to a virtual tape library. Configure the data backup solution to run nightly after the initial backup is complete. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and restore the data to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the volumes in the virtual tape library.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Mount the Volume Gateway cached volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volume with the same amount of disk space as the existing file storage volume. Mount the Volume Gateway stored volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway is designed to present cloud-backed block storage as iSCSI devices to on-premises application servers, so it preserves the existing iSCSI-based integration. For workloads that require low-latency access to the entire dataset, stored volumes are the appropriate option because all primary data remains stored locally while point-in-time snapshots are asynchronously backed up to AWS for disaster recovery. Cached volumes keep primary data in Amazon S3 and only retain frequently accessed subsets locally, which does not meet the requirement for immediate low-latency access to all file types across a very large dataset. File Gateway would require changing the protocol to NFS/SMB, and Tape Gateway is a backup solution rather than primary storage.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

A company is rolling out an application that handles streaming data in near-real time. The company intends to run the workload on Amazon EC2 instances. The network design must be configurable to deliver the lowest possible latency between nodes.  
  
Which combination of networking solutions will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Enable and configure enhanced networking on each EC2 instance.
Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
Run the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to each EC2 instance.
Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) optimized instance types.

questions.explanation:
For the lowest inter-instance latency on Amazon EC2, use **enhanced networking** and place the instances in a **cluster placement group**. Enhanced networking uses SR-IOV to deliver higher packet-per-second performance and consistently lower latency between instances. A cluster placement group places interdependent instances close together within a single Availability Zone and is specifically recommended for workloads that need low network latency and high throughput between nodes. Grouping instances in separate accounts does not improve latency, adding multiple ENIs does not inherently reduce node-to-node latency, and EBS optimization improves storage throughput rather than network communication.

**Learn more:** [Enhanced networking on Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/enhanced-networking.html) · [Placement groups for your Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-groups.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the website with an API that handles sales requests. The company hosts the API on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The API consists of static and dynamic front-end content, along with backend workers that process sales requests asynchronously.  
  
The company is expecting a significant and sudden increase in the number of sales requests during events for the launch of new products.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure that all the requests are processed successfully?

options.text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the increase in traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Add an Amazon ElastiCache instance in front of the ALB to reduce traffic for the API to handle.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to receive requests from the website for later processing by the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is a good fit for delivering the website’s static content from Amazon S3, which reduces load and improves content delivery. To handle a sudden burst of sales submissions reliably, Amazon SQS should be used to decouple request ingestion from backend processing. SQS buffers requests durably so backend workers on the EC2 instances can process them asynchronously at their own rate, preventing request loss during traffic spikes. Auto Scaling alone does not provide durable burst buffering, and ElastiCache is not the right service to sit in front of an ALB for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html) · [Ways to use CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/IntroductionUseCases.html)

A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content pages for its website. The company must ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website. The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.
Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.

questions.explanation:
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is the AWS service used to provision certificates for CloudFront, and DNS validation is the most operationally efficient validation method because ACM can automatically renew DNS-validated public certificates as long as the certificate remains in use and the required DNS CNAME records stay in place. Email validation is less efficient because renewal requires action through validation emails, and CloudFront security policies or origin access control (OAC) do not create certificates.

**Learn more:** [Requirements for using SSL/TLS certificates with CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html) · [Validate domain ownership for AWS Certificate Manager public certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/domain-ownership-validation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team is working with another company to build an integrated product. The other company needs access to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that resides in the development team's account. The other company wants to poll the queue without surrendering its own account permissions to do so.  
  
How should a solutions architect provide access to the SQS queue?

options.text: Create an instance profile that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an IAM policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an SQS access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS supports cross-account access through a resource-based queue policy. The queue owner attaches an SQS access policy that names the other AWS account or specific IAM principals as allowed to perform actions such as `ReceiveMessage`. This lets the external company access the queue from its own account instead of giving up or replacing its own permissions. SNS policies apply to topics, not queues, and an instance profile is only for EC2 role attachment.

**Learn more:** [Custom Amazon SQS Access Policy Language examples - Amazon Simple Queue Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-creating-custom-policies-access-policy-examples.html) · [Cross account resource access in IAM - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to operate its on-premises application in a hybrid environment. The application currently runs in containers on premises.  
  
The company requires one container solution that can scale across an on-premises, hybrid, or cloud environment. It must run new application containers in the AWS Cloud and must use a load balancer for HTTP traffic.  
  
Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type for the cloud application containers. Use an Amazon ECS Anywhere external launch type for the on-premises application containers.
Set up an Application Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
Set up a Network Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Use Fargate for the cloud application containers and the on-premises application containers.
Set up an ECS cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type for the cloud application containers. Use Amazon ECS Anywhere with an AWS Fargate launch type for the on-premises application containers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS Anywhere provides the EXTERNAL launch type for containers running on registered on-premises servers or virtual machines, while AWS Fargate runs ECS tasks in the AWS Cloud. An Application Load Balancer routes HTTP/HTTPS Layer 7 traffic to ECS services, making it the appropriate load balancer for the cloud tasks.

**Learn more:** [External (Amazon ECS Anywhere) for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/launch-type-external.html) · [Use load balancing to distribute Amazon ECS service traffic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-load-balancing.html?c=ho_ddc&p=gsrc)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has applications running on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. One of the applications must call the Amazon S3 API to store and read objects. Per the company's security regulations, no application traffic is allowed to travel across the internet.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint.
Create an S3 bucket in a private subnet.
Create an S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances.
Configure a NAT gateway in the same subnet as the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway endpoint provides private connectivity from a VPC to Amazon S3, allowing EC2 instances to access S3 without using an internet gateway or NAT device. This satisfies the requirement that application traffic must not traverse the internet. Amazon S3 buckets are regional resources rather than resources placed in subnets, and a NAT gateway is used for internet-bound access from private subnets, so those options do not meet the stated security constraint.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Controlling access from VPC endpoints with bucket policies - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies-vpc-endpoint.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A hospital recently implemented a RESTful API by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports in PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital must update the Lambda code to identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Textract is the AWS managed service designed to extract text from document formats such as PDF and JPEG, and Amazon Comprehend Medical is purpose-built to detect PHI in unstructured clinical text. Using Textract for OCR plus Comprehend Medical for PHI identification satisfies both file-format and healthcare-text requirements while avoiding custom parsing code or training and operating a SageMaker model. Rekognition is not the primary AWS document text-extraction service for this use case, and custom Python libraries would require more maintenance.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Textract FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/textract/faqs/) · [Detecting Document Text with Amazon Textract](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/detecting-document-text.html)

A global ecommerce company currently uses a monolithic architecture. It needs a solution to manage the growing volume of product data. The solution must scale and use a modular service architecture. The company must retain its structured database schemas. It also needs storage for product data and product images.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group to deploy a containerized application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute web traffic. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance to store product data and product images.

Use AWS Lambda functions to manage the existing monolithic application. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store product data and product images. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for event-driven communication between the Lambda functions.

Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with an Amazon EC2 deployment to deploy a containerized application. Use an Amazon Aurora cluster to store the product data. Use AWS Step Functions to manage workflows. Store the product images in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to deploy a containerized application. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store the product data. Store the product images in an Amazon S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate provides serverless container compute, so containerized modular services can run and scale without managing EC2 servers or clusters. Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that supports structured schemas, and a Multi-AZ deployment provides managed high availability. Amazon S3 is scalable object storage for product images.

**Learn more:** [Architect for AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html) · [What is Amazon RDS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an ecommerce application that stores all its data in one Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance that AWS fully manages. The company must reduce the risk of a single point of failure.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Modify the RDS DB instance to use a Multi-AZ deployment. Apply the changes during the next maintenance window.

Migrate the current database to a new Amazon DynamoDB Multi-AZ deployment. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with a heterogeneous migration strategy to migrate the current RDS DB instance to DynamoDB tables.
Create a new RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ deployment. Manually restore the data from the existing RDS DB instance from the most recent snapshot.
Configure the DB instance in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of three. Use Amazon Route 53 simple routing to distribute requests to all DB instances.

questions.explanation:
A Multi-AZ RDS DB instance deployment automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby DB instance in a different Availability Zone and provides failover support. Modifying the existing RDS for MySQL instance to use Multi-AZ therefore removes the single-instance availability risk with a direct managed-service configuration change.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [Converting a DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Migrating.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a multi-tier ecommerce web application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Amazon RDS is configured with the latest-generation DB instance and 2,000 GB of storage on a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Database performance affects the application during periods of high demand.  
  
A database administrator analyzes the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs and discovers that application performance always degrades when the number of read and write IOPS exceeds 20,000.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to improve application performance?

options.text: Replace the volume with a magnetic volume.
Increase the number of IOPS on the gp3 volume.
Replace the volume with a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume.
Replace the 2,000 GB gp3 volume with two 1,000 GB gp3 volumes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS gp3 storage allows storage performance to be provisioned independently of storage capacity, including increasing IOPS on the existing volume. Because the degradation occurs when read/write IOPS rise above 20,000, the appropriate remediation is to provision more IOPS on the gp3 volume so the database can sustain that demand. Magnetic storage is deprecated and unsuitable for performance-sensitive workloads, and replacing gp3 with io2 would be a larger change than necessary when the stated bottleneck can be addressed directly by increasing gp3 IOPS.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS DB instance storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html) · [Working with storage for Amazon RDS DB instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.StorageTypes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a Microsoft SQL Server database, and the company's applications are connected to that database. The company wants to migrate to an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database while making minimal changes to the application code.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.
Enable Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL to run the SQL queries from the applications.
Migrate the database schema and data by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
Use Amazon RDS Proxy to connect the applications to Aurora PostgreSQL.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.

questions.explanation:
Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL provides SQL Server–compatible endpoints and supports T-SQL so applications originally written for Microsoft SQL Server can continue to run against Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal code changes. For the database migration itself, AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) is used to convert the SQL Server schema to a PostgreSQL-compatible schema, and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) is used to migrate the data. That combination addresses both application compatibility and schema/data migration.

**Learn more:** [Using Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/babelfish.html) · [What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building machine learning (ML) models on AWS as independent microservices. At startup, the microservices retrieve approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 and load it into memory. Users access the ML models through an asynchronous API and can submit either one request or a batch of requests.  
  
The company offers the ML models to hundreds of users. Model usage is irregular: some models go unused for days or weeks, while others receive batches of thousands of requests at once.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that the NLB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the Lambda functions based on the traffic that the NLB receives.

Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that the ALB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the ECS cluster instances based on the traffic that the ALB receives.

Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that SQS events will invoke. Use auto scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the size of the SQS queue.

Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Use auto scaling for Amazon ECS to scale both the cluster capacity and number of the services based on the size of the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS buffers asynchronous requests and absorbs sudden batches, while Amazon ECS services can keep the approximately 1 GB model data loaded in memory across requests. ECS service auto scaling can use SQS queue depth to add or remove tasks, and cluster capacity scaling can supply the compute needed for those tasks. This accommodates both idle periods and large request bursts without requiring continuously provisioned capacity for every model.

**Learn more:** [Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html) · [Optimizing Amazon ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-autoscaling-best-practice.html)

A company's website hosted on Amazon EC2 instances processes classified data stored in Amazon S3. Because of security concerns, the company requires a private and secure connection between its EC2 resources and Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Set up S3 bucket policies to allow access from a VPC endpoint.
Set up an IAM policy to grant read-write access to the S3 bucket.
Set up a NAT gateway to access resources outside the private subnet.
Set up an access key ID and a secret access key to access the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 VPC endpoint provides private connectivity between resources in a VPC and S3 without requiring internet access, a NAT device, VPN, or Direct Connect. Bucket policies can then restrict the S3 bucket so that access is allowed only through that VPC endpoint. That combination meets the requirement for private, secure EC2-to-S3 access. IAM permissions and access keys control identity, not the network path, and a NAT gateway does not provide private S3 connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Controlling access from VPC endpoints with bucket policies - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies-vpc-endpoint.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A media company keeps movies in Amazon S3. Each movie is saved as a single video file ranging from 1 GB to 10 GB in size.  
  
The company must be able to deliver the streaming content for a movie within 5 minutes after a user purchases it. Demand is higher for movies that are less than 20 years old than for movies that are more than 20 years old. The company wants to minimize hosting service costs according to demand.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Store all media content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move media data into the Infrequent Access tier when the demand for a movie decreases.

Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using standard retrieval.

Store newer movie video files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using expedited retrieval.
Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using bulk retrieval.

questions.explanation:
S3 Standard-IA keeps every object immediately and continuously accessible at millisecond latency for a lower per-GB storage price than S3 Standard, so serving older, less-demanded movies from it with a normal GET request trivially meets a 5-minute delivery target with no restore process involved. Archival classes require an explicit restore job before an object becomes readable, and the 1-5 minute expedited retrieval window that AWS documents applies to smaller objects; for multi-gigabyte movie files, restore time is instead governed by a throughput rate rather than a guaranteed time, making an archive tier a riskier choice against a hard delivery deadline. Keeping newer, high-demand titles in S3 Standard preserves low-latency delivery for the content accessed most often.

**Learn more:** [Understanding archive retrieval options - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/restoring-objects-retrieval-options.html)

A company runs its enterprise resource planning (ERP) system in the `us-east-1` Region on Amazon EC2 instances. Customers use a public API hosted on the EC2 instances to exchange data with the ERP system. International customers report slow API response times from their data centers.  
  
Which solution will improve response times for the international customers **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection that has a public virtual interface (VIF) to provide connectivity from each customer's data center to us-east-1. Route customer API requests by using a Direct Connect gateway to the ERP system API.
Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API. Configure the CachingOptimized managed cache policy to provide improved cache efficiency.
Set up AWS Global Accelerator. Configure listeners for the necessary ports. Configure endpoint groups for the appropriate Regions to distribute traffic. Create an endpoint in the group for the API.
Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to establish dedicated VPN tunnels between Regions and customer networks. Route traffic to the API over the VPN connections.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator improves performance for globally distributed users of internet-facing applications by routing traffic to AWS close to the client and carrying it over the AWS global network, avoiding multiple public-internet hops. Standard accelerators support Amazon EC2 instances as endpoints, making this suitable for a dynamic public API. CloudFront caching is not a dependable fit for customer-specific ERP API exchanges, and provisioning individual Direct Connect connections or VPNs for every customer adds substantially more cost and operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Global Accelerator?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html) · [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A startup company hosts a website for its customers on an Amazon EC2 instance. The website consists of a stateless Python application and a MySQL database. The website handles only a small amount of traffic. The company is worried about instance reliability and must migrate to a highly available architecture. The company cannot modify the application code.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to achieve high availability for the website? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Provision an internet gateway in each Availability Zone in use.
Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance.
Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling.
Use AWS DataSync to synchronize the database data across multiple EC2 instances.
Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that are distributed across two Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
A highly available design for a stateless web tier on AWS is to place EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones and distribute requests with an Application Load Balancer. For the MySQL database tier, Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides synchronous standby replication in another Availability Zone and automatic failover while preserving MySQL compatibility, which avoids application-code changes. Internet gateways are not provisioned per Availability Zone, DynamoDB would require moving from MySQL to a different data model and access pattern, and AWS DataSync is not the right mechanism to make a transactional MySQL database highly available. Official AWS documentation states that Application Load Balancers distribute traffic across targets in multiple Availability Zones and that RDS Multi-AZ for MySQL is a high-availability failover solution. 

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application with a REST-based interface that enables data to be received in near real time from a third-party vendor. After the data is received, the application processes it and stores it for additional analysis. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
The third-party vendor has encountered many **503 Service Unavailable** errors while sending data to the application. When data volume spikes, compute capacity reaches its maximum limit, and the application cannot process all requests.  
  
Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.
Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.
Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
A streaming, decoupled ingestion layer is needed so burst traffic is absorbed instead of being sent directly to a compute tier that can saturate. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is designed for real-time data ingestion at scale, and AWS Lambda can natively consume and process records from Kinesis without requiring server management. This removes the tight coupling between the vendor's request rate and the application's immediate EC2 processing capacity, which is the condition causing the 503 errors. API Gateway quotas only limit callers, SNS is not the best fit for durable ordered stream buffering in this scenario, and moving the workload to ECS on EC2 still leaves the solution dependent on EC2 capacity scaling rather than introducing a managed burst-tolerant stream.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html) · [Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html)

A company is building a solution to report Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling events for all applications in an AWS account. The company must use a serverless approach to store the EC2 Auto Scaling status data in Amazon S3.  
  
The company will then use the data in Amazon S3 to deliver near-real-time updates in a dashboard.  
  
The solution must not impact the speed of Amazon EC2 instance launches.  
  
How should the company move the data to Amazon S3 to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an Amazon CloudWatch metric stream to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
Launch an Amazon EMR cluster to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a schedule. Configure the Lambda function to send the EC2 Auto Scaling status data directly to Amazon S3.

Use a bootstrap script during the launch of an EC2 instance to install Amazon Kinesis Agent. Configure Kinesis Agent to collect the EC2 Auto Scaling status data and send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Store the data in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends service events directly to Amazon EventBridge in near real time, and EventBridge can invoke AWS Lambda as a target. A Lambda function can write each event to Amazon S3 asynchronously, which satisfies the serverless and near-real-time requirements without adding work to the EC2 instance launch process. The other options fail because CloudWatch metric streams are for metrics rather than Auto Scaling event records, Amazon EMR is not serverless, and a bootstrap script plus Kinesis Agent adds launch-time overhead to instances.

**Learn more:** [Use EventBridge to handle Auto Scaling events - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/automating-ec2-auto-scaling-with-eventbridge.html) · [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-autoscaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing an application to help users complete and submit registration forms. The solutions architect intends to use a two-tier architecture consisting of a web application server tier and a worker tier.  
  
The application must process submitted forms quickly. It must process every form exactly once. The solution must ensure that no data is lost.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
Use an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create a synchronous workflow between the web application server tier and the worker tier that stores and forwards form data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS FIFO queues durably store messages between the web and worker tiers and support exactly-once processing through message deduplication. Workers can process queued form data asynchronously, while the queue retains messages until they are successfully processed and deleted. Standard SQS queues provide at-least-once delivery and can introduce duplicates.

**Learn more:** [Exactly-once processing in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html) · [Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html)

options.text: Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.
Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy is the correct service for Lambda workloads that create many short-lived database connections, because it pools and multiplexes connections so a large number of Lambda invocations do not translate into an equally large number of PostgreSQL connections. For a private RDS DB instance, the Lambda function must have VPC connectivity to reach the database or the proxy endpoint. An RDS custom endpoint does not solve connection-management for this use case; it is used for routing in Aurora, not for protecting the database from connection storms.

**Learn more:** [Automatically connecting a Lambda function and a DB instance - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/lambda-rds-connect.html) · [Common usage scenarios - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-best-practices.usage-scenarios.html)

A consumer-survey company has collected data for several years from a particular geographic region. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket in an AWS Region.  
  
The company has begun sharing the data with a marketing firm in a new geographic region. It has granted the firm’s AWS account access to the S3 bucket. The company wants to minimize data-transfer costs when the marketing firm requests data from the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company’s S3 bucket.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the company’s S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.
Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share the S3 bucket with the marketing firm AWS account.
Configure the company’s S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Requester Pays charges the requester, rather than the bucket owner, for S3 requests and data downloads. The marketing firm’s AWS account therefore pays the retrieval and associated data-transfer costs for its requests, while the company remains responsible for storage costs.

**Learn more:** [Using Requester Pays general purpose buckets for storage transfers and usage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application must store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the database data to be highly available. The company also requires increased capacity for read workloads.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment is the best fit because it supports PostgreSQL and combines high availability with read scaling in a single managed regional architecture. AWS documents that a Multi-AZ DB cluster has one writer and two readable instances in three separate Availability Zones in the same Region, providing high availability and increased capacity for read workloads. By contrast, a standard Multi-AZ DB instance deployment provides failover but its standby does not serve read traffic, so it does not meet the read-capacity requirement as efficiently.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html) · [Configuring and managing a Multi-AZ deployment for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a video-streaming web application in a VPC. It uses a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to process TCP traffic for real-time data processing. Unauthorized attempts have been made to access the application.  
  
The company needs to strengthen application security, with minimal architectural change, to stop unauthorized access attempts.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement a series of AWS WAF rules directly on the NLB to filter out unauthorized traffic.
Recreate the NLB with a security group to allow only trusted IP addresses.
Deploy a second NLB in parallel with the existing NLB configured with a strict IP address allow list.
Use AWS Shield Advanced to provide enhanced DDoS protection and prevent unauthorized access attempts.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer security group can restrict inbound listener traffic by protocol, port, and source CIDR, so an allow list of trusted IP addresses blocks unauthorized clients at the load balancer. If an NLB was created without a security group, AWS requires recreating it to add one. AWS WAF does not protect NLBs, and AWS Shield Advanced provides DDoS mitigation rather than trusted-source access control.

**Learn more:** [Update the security groups for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-security-groups.html) · [Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a highly dynamic batch processing job that uses many Amazon EC2 instances to finish the work. The job is stateless by nature, can be started and stopped at any time with no negative impact, and usually takes more than 60 minutes in total to complete. The company has asked a solutions architect to design a scalable and cost-effective solution that meets the job requirements.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Implement EC2 Spot Instances.
Purchase EC2 Reserved Instances.
Implement EC2 On-Demand Instances.
Implement the processing on AWS Lambda.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Spot Instances are the best fit for a stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible batch workload because they provide the lowest-cost EC2 capacity and are specifically recommended by AWS for interruptible batch processing. Reserved Instances are intended for predictable long-term usage, On-Demand Instances cost more for this use case, and AWS Lambda is unsuitable because standard Lambda function executions are limited to 15 minutes.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html) · [Select the best pricing model - Cost Optimization Pillar](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/cost-optimization-pillar/select-the-best-pricing-model.html)

",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.","B":"Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.","C":"Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.","D":"Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment is the best fit because it supports PostgreSQL and combines high availability with read scaling in a single managed regional architecture. ",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Implement a series of AWS WAF rules directly on the NLB to filter out unauthorized traffic.","B":"Recreate the NLB with a security group to allow only trusted IP addresses.","C":"Deploy a second NLB in parallel with the existing NLB configured with a strict IP address allow list.","D":"Use AWS Shield Advanced to provide enhanced DDoS protection and prevent unauthorized access attempts."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"A Network Load Balancer security group can restrict inbound listener traffic by protocol, port, and source CIDR, so an allow list of trusted IP addresses blocks unauthorized clients at the load balancer. AWS WAF does not protect NLBs, and AWS Shield Advanced provides DDoS mitigation rather than trusted-source access control.

A company currently holds 5 TB of data in on-premises block storage systems. Its existing storage solution has limited capacity for additional data. The company operates on-premises applications that need to retrieve frequently accessed data with low latency. The company needs a cloud-based storage solution.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway. Integrate S3 File Gateway with the on-premises applications to store and directly retrieve files by using the SMB file system.
Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with cached volumes as iSCSI targets.
Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with stored volumes as iSCSI targets.
Use an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway. Integrate Tape Gateway with the on-premises applications to store virtual tapes in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with cached volumes provides cloud-backed block volumes as iSCSI targets for on-premises applications. It stores primary data in Amazon S3 while keeping frequently accessed data in a local cache for low-latency access, minimizing the need to expand on-premises storage.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

A city has deployed a web application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application's users have reported sporadic performance, which appears to be related to DDoS attacks originating from random IP addresses. The city needs a solution that requires minimal configuration changes and provides an audit trail for the DDoS sources.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB, and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources.
Subscribe to Amazon Inspector. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the application, and set the ALB as the origin. Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the distribution, and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources

questions.explanation:
AWS Shield Advanced is the purpose-built AWS service for protecting ALB-backed applications from DDoS attacks with minimal architectural change, because it can be enabled directly for the protected resource instead of requiring a redesign such as adding CloudFront. It also includes access to the AWS DDoS Response Team/Shield Response Team for mitigation assistance. For the audit-trail requirement, Shield Advanced provides attack details and DDoS attack flow logs that capture source IP addresses and other packet-level metadata for forensic analysis and compliance reporting. AWS WAF alone is primarily for application-layer filtering and custom rule enforcement, not the best managed fit for random-source DDoS mitigation, and Amazon Inspector is not a DDoS protection service.

**Learn more:** [Managed DDoS event response with Shield Response Team (SRT) support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-srt-support.html) · [AttackDetail - AWS Shield Advanced API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/DDOSAPIReference/API_AttackDetail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an API-driven cloud communications platform. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The company uses Amazon API Gateway to give external users API access to the application.  
  
The company wants to protect the platform from web exploits such as SQL injection and also wants to detect and mitigate large, sophisticated DDoS attacks.  
  
Which combination of solutions provides the **MOST** protection? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use AWS WAF to protect the NLB.
Use AWS Shield Advanced with the NLB.
Use AWS WAF to protect Amazon API Gateway.
Use Amazon GuardDuty with AWS Shield Standard
Use AWS Shield Standard with Amazon API Gateway.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is the correct control for blocking application-layer web exploits such as SQL injection, and AWS supports associating AWS WAF with Amazon API Gateway. For DDoS protection, AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced detection and mitigation for large, sophisticated attacks and supports protecting Network Load Balancers through their associated Elastic IP addresses. AWS WAF does not protect Network Load Balancers directly, and Shield Standard is the baseline automatic protection rather than the most protective option.

**Learn more:** [Configuring protection in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html) · [Protect your REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/rest-api-protect.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must comply with a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in Amazon S3 for 7 years.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Object Lock is the native S3 feature for immutable retention. For a legal retention requirement, **compliance mode** is the appropriate choice because protected object versions cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the root user, during the retention period. **Governance mode** is weaker because authorized users can bypass it. To bring **existing** objects into compliance with the least operational effort, **S3 Batch Operations** can apply Object Lock retention to many existing objects at scale, which is more efficient than recopying objects individually. New objects can inherit the 7-year retention through the bucket’s Object Lock retention configuration.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with Object Lock - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [Managing S3 Object Lock using S3 Batch Operations - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/managing-object-lock-batchops.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has two VPCs named **Management** and **Production**.  
  
- The **Management VPC** uses VPNs through a customer gateway to connect to a single device in the data center.  
- The **Production VPC** uses a virtual private gateway with two attached AWS Direct Connect connections.  
- The **Management** and **Production** VPCs use a single VPC peering connection to enable communication between the applications.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to mitigate any single point of failure in this architecture?

options.text: Add a set of VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs.
Add a second virtual private gateway and attach it to the Management VPC.
Add a second set of VPNs to the Management VPC from a second customer gateway device.
Add a second VPC peering connection between the Management VPC and the Production VPC.

questions.explanation:
The risk is the single customer gateway device serving the Management VPC. AWS Site-to-Site VPN includes redundant tunnels for failures on the AWS side, but that does not remove the on-premises device as a single point of failure. AWS recommends creating a second Site-to-Site VPN connection that uses a second customer gateway device so traffic can fail over if one customer gateway becomes unavailable. The VPC peering connection is not the problem, because AWS states that VPC peering does not introduce a single point of failure or bandwidth bottleneck.

**Learn more:** [Redundant AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections for failover - AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-redundant-connection.html) · [Connect VPCs using VPC peering - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-peering.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an application in the AWS Cloud. The application will store data in Amazon S3 buckets in two AWS Regions.  
  
The company must use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt all data stored in the S3 buckets. The data in both S3 buckets must be encrypted and decrypted by using the same KMS key. The data and the key must reside in each of the two Regions.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.

Create a customer managed multi-Region KMS key. Create an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure replication between the S3 buckets. Configure the application to use the KMS key with client-side encryption.

Create a customer managed KMS key and an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.
Create a customer managed KMS key and an S3 bucket in each Region. Configure the S3 buckets to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure replication between the S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
An AWS KMS multi-Region key is the only option that provides the same cryptographic key material in multiple Regions, with a primary key and replica key stored regionally and usable interchangeably across those Regions. That satisfies the requirement for the key and the data to exist in each Region while still using the same KMS key material. Options that use SSE-S3 do not use a customer managed AWS KMS key, and separate single-Region customer managed KMS keys do not satisfy the same-key requirement. AWS KMS documents that multi-Region keys have the same key ID and key material in different Regions, and Amazon S3 documentation notes that S3 can use multi-Region KMS keys. In the provided choices, this makes the multi-Region KMS key approach the correct answer.

**Learn more:** [How multi-Region keys work - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/mrk-how-it-works.html) · [Replication process for multi-Region keys - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/cryptographic-details/replicate-key-details.html)

A company needs a solution to stop photos containing unwanted content from being uploaded to the company's web application. The solution must not require training a machine learning (ML) model.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create and deploy a model by using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Create a real-time endpoint that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
Create an Amazon CloudFront function that uses Amazon Comprehend to detect unwanted content. Associate the function with the web application.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition Video to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Rekognition includes a built-in image moderation capability that can detect inappropriate, unwanted, or offensive content in images by using the `DetectModerationLabels` API, so no custom model training is required. An AWS Lambda function can call that API when a photo is uploaded and return the result to the web application. SageMaker Autopilot would create a trained model, which violates the requirement, Amazon Comprehend is for text analysis rather than image moderation, and Amazon Rekognition Video is intended for video workflows rather than still-image uploads.

**Learn more:** [Detecting inappropriate images - Amazon Rekognition](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/procedure-moderate-images.html) · [Moderating content - Amazon Rekognition](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/moderation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company copies 200 TB of data from a recent ocean survey onto AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) cluster hosted on AWS to search for oil and gas deposits. A solutions architect must give the cluster consistent sub-millisecond latency and high-throughput access to the data on the Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. The company is returning the devices to AWS.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to use the S3 bucket. Access the file gateway from the HPC cluster instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, and integrate it with the S3 bucket. Access the FSx for Lustre file system from the HPC cluster instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Import the data into the S3 bucket. Copy the data from the S3 bucket to the EFS file system. Access the EFS file system from the HPC cluster instances.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Import the data directly into the FSx for Lustre file system. Access the FSx for Lustre file system from the HPC cluster instances.

questions.explanation:
For returned Snowball Edge import jobs, AWS imports the device data into an Amazon S3 bucket. For an AWS-hosted HPC cluster that needs consistent sub-millisecond latency and high throughput, Amazon FSx for Lustre is the appropriate file system because it is purpose-built for HPC workloads and integrates with Amazon S3 as a data repository. That combination satisfies both the import path from Snowball Edge and the required performance characteristics for the cluster.

**Learn more:** [Jobs to import data into Amazon S3 using a Snowball Edge device - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/importtype.html) · [How AWS Snowball Edge works - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/how-it-works.html)
