A company operates multiple websites on AWS for its various brands. Each website produces tens of gigabytes of web traffic logs per day. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution that gives the company's developers the ability to analyze traffic patterns across all the company's websites.  
  
The developers will perform this analysis on demand once each week for several months. The solution must support queries that use standard SQL.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena tor analysis.
Store the logs in Amazon RDS. Use a database client for analysis.
Store the logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Use OpenSearch Service for analysis.
Store the logs in an Amazon EMR cluster Use a supported open-source framework for SQL-based analysis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is designed for interactive analysis of data stored directly in Amazon S3 by using standard SQL, which fits web log analysis without requiring the company to run persistent infrastructure. Because the access pattern is only weekly and on demand, storing the logs in S3 and querying them with Athena avoids the ongoing cost of provisioned database instances, search clusters, or EMR clusters while still scaling to large log volumes.

**Learn more:** [Querying Amazon S3 tables with Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-tables-integrating-athena.html) · [Run SQL queries in Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-athena-tables.html)

A company is deploying a new application on AWS. It will run the application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones in multiple AWS Regions. The application will be internet accessible, and users around the world will access it.  
  
The company needs to ensure that every user who accesses the application is directed to the EC2 instances closest to that user’s location.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy. Use an internet-facing Application Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
Implement an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy. Use an internet-facing Network Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
Implement an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy. Use an internet-facing Application Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.
Implement an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy. Use an internet-facing Network Load Balancer to distribute the traffic across all Availability Zones within the same Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing uses the geographic locations of users and resources to route traffic to the closest available resource; each Regional Network Load Balancer can distribute that traffic across the Availability Zones in its Region.

**Learn more:** [Geoproximity routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geoproximity.html) · [Choosing a routing policy - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html)

options.text: Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to generate certificates. Use the certificates to encrypt the database volume.
Deploy AWS CloudHSM, generate encryption keys, and use the keys to encrypt database volumes.
Configure SSL encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt database volumes.
Configure Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption and Amazon RDS encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt instance and database volumes.

questions.explanation:
The built-in AWS features for encrypting data at rest in this architecture are Amazon EBS encryption for the EC2 instance volumes and Amazon RDS encryption for the database storage, both using AWS KMS keys. This meets the compliance requirement for at-rest encryption while minimizing architectural change because the services natively support KMS-based storage encryption. ACM certificates and SSL address certificates or encryption in transit, not storage encryption at rest, and AWS CloudHSM would add unnecessary complexity compared with native EBS and RDS encryption.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html) · [Encrypting Amazon RDS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability for Lustre clients to access the data. The solution must be fully managed.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre is the AWS fully managed file system that provides native Lustre functionality, so Lustre clients can mount and access the shared data directly. The other options do not meet the Lustre requirement: AWS DataSync is a transfer service, Storage Gateway file gateway exposes NFS/SMB shares, and Amazon EFS does not support Lustre as a client protocol. AWS documentation describes FSx for Lustre as a fully managed service for Lustre workloads and documents installing Lustre clients and mounting the file system from Linux instances.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html) · [Accessing file systems - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/accessing-fs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance
Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is designed to provide shared file storage that multiple Amazon EC2 instances can mount concurrently, including across multiple Availability Zones, which removes the single-instance dependency for the website images and improves resilience. An Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer with at least two instances improves web-tier availability by replacing unhealthy instances and distributing capacity across Availability Zones. Amazon CloudFront improves website performance by caching content such as images at edge locations, reducing latency for users and reducing load on the origin web servers. These requirements are matched by moving the images to EFS and deploying multiple EC2 instances behind an ALB with Auto Scaling and CloudFront.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Use Amazon EFS with Amazon EC2 Linux instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEFS.html)

A company maintains a searchable repository of items on its website. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database table that contains more than 10 million rows. The database has 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. There are millions of updates to this data every day through the company's website.  
  
The company has observed that some insert operations take 10 seconds or longer. The company has determined that database storage performance is the problem.  
  
Which solution addresses this performance issue?

options.text: Change the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD.
Change the DB instance to a memory optimized instance class.
Change the DB instance to a burstable performance instance class.
Enable Multi-AZ RDS read replicas with MySQL native asynchronous replication.

questions.explanation:
Provisioned IOPS SSD is the RDS storage type intended for I/O-intensive, latency-sensitive transactional database workloads and provides more consistent IOPS and lower latency than General Purpose SSD. Because the identified problem is storage performance causing slow inserts, changing the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD directly addresses the bottleneck. Memory-optimized or burstable instance classes affect compute and memory capacity rather than storage I/O, and Multi-AZ read replicas improve availability or read scaling rather than primary write performance.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS DB instance storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html) · [Modifying settings for Provisioned IOPS SSD storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/User_PIOPS.Increase.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a three-tier application on AWS.  
  
- The presentation tier will serve a static website.  
- The logic tier is a containerized application.  
- This application will store data in a relational database.  
  
The company wants to simplify deployment and reduce operational costs.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon CloudFront to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.

A managed Amazon RDS database satisfies the relational database requirement while offloading database administration. By contrast, Amazon EKS adds Kubernetes management complexity, Amazon EC2-based container hosting requires instance management, and CloudFront is a delivery layer rather than the primary static-content host. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EnableWebsiteHosting.html?utm_source=openai))

The company wants to create a robust, resilient architecture for the application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. Deploy an RDS DB instance in the same Availability Zone. Use Amazon S3 with versioning enabled to store static assets.
Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy a Multi-AZ RDS DB instance. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute static assets.
Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. Deploy an RDS DB instance in a second Availability Zone for cross-AZ redundancy. Serve static assets directly from the EC2 instances.

Use AWS Lambda functions to serve the web application. Use Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 for the database. Store static assets in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone-Infrequent Access (One Zone-IA).

questions.explanation:
An Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones provides web-tier redundancy and can replace capacity in healthy Availability Zones when one becomes unavailable. An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance maintains a synchronous standby in a different Availability Zone and automatically fails over during infrastructure failure or maintenance. This removes single-Availability-Zone failure points from the application and database tiers; Amazon CloudFront distributes the static content.

A company's reporting system delivers hundreds of `.csv` files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company needs to convert these files to Apache Parquet format and store the results in a transformed data bucket.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.
Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.

Use AWS Batch to create a job definition with Bash syntax to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Use the job definition to submit a job. Specify an array job as the job type.

Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Configure an event notification for the S3 bucket. Specify the Lambda function as the destination for the event notification.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL service for data in Amazon S3 and natively supports reading CSV and writing Parquet. A Glue crawler can discover the source schema, and a Glue ETL job can perform the conversion and write the output directly to the transformed S3 bucket. This meets the requirement with minimal custom development compared with building and operating an EMR Spark application, creating custom AWS Batch processing, or implementing per-object transformation logic in Lambda.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 connections - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-s3-home.html) · [Using files in Amazon S3 for the data source - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/edit-jobs-source-s3-files.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving a distributed application to AWS. The application handles variable workloads. The legacy environment includes a primary server that coordinates jobs across multiple compute nodes. The company wants to modernize the application by using a solution that maximizes resiliency and scalability.  
  
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling to use scheduled scaling.

Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the size of the queue.

Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure AWS CloudTrail as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the primary server.

Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the compute nodes.

questions.explanation:
A resilient and scalable worker architecture on AWS decouples job producers from compute nodes by placing jobs in Amazon SQS and having a fleet of workers consume from the queue. SQS is designed for distributed systems and allows work to accumulate durably while workers scale horizontally. For variable demand, EC2 Auto Scaling should scale the worker fleet based on queue backlog or queue size so capacity tracks outstanding work. Scheduled scaling is intended for predictable changes, while CloudTrail is for auditing and EventBridge is for event routing rather than serving as the processing queue for worker nodes in this pattern.

**Learn more:** [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html) · [Fully Managed Message Queuing – Amazon Simple Queue Service](https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/)

A company wants to standardize its Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption strategy. The company also wants to minimize the cost and configuration effort needed to run the volume encryption check.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Write API calls to describe the EBS volumes and to confirm the EBS volumes are encrypted. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to run the API calls.
Write API calls to describe the EBS volumes and to confirm the EBS volumes are encrypted. Run the API calls on an AWS Fargate task.

Create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy that requires the use of tags on EBS volumes. Use AWS Cost Explorer to display resources that are not properly tagged. Encrypt the untagged resources manually.
Create an AWS Config rule for Amazon EBS to evaluate if a volume is encrypted and to flag the volume if it is not encrypted.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config provides a managed rule for Amazon EBS volume encryption checks. The `encrypted-volumes` rule evaluates `AWS::EC2::Volume` resources and reports volumes as noncompliant when they are not encrypted, which gives the company a standardized, low-effort, low-maintenance way to check encryption status without building and operating custom API polling code in Lambda or Fargate. This directly satisfies the requirement to minimize both cost and configuration effort.

**Learn more:** [encrypted-volumes - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/encrypted-volumes.html) · [AWS Config Managed Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_use-managed-rules.html?3433df04_page=1)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A media company runs its website on AWS. The website application's architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company's cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection.  
  
How should the company address this issue?

options.text: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is the correct mitigation because it protects Application Load Balancers by inspecting incoming HTTP(S) requests through a web ACL, and it includes rules specifically for detecting malicious SQL code in requests. That makes it the appropriate AWS control to help block SQL injection attempts before they reach the EC2-based application. AWS Shield Advanced focuses on DDoS protection, Amazon Inspector identifies vulnerabilities rather than blocking live requests, and standard ALB listener rules do not provide SQL injection detection logic.

**Learn more:** [Configuring protection in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html) · [SQL injection attack rule statement - AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-sqli-match.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud. The on-premises data center is located near the `us-west-1` Region. The company uses the `eu-central-1` Region to host the website. The company wants to reduce website load time as much as possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the traffic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center. Send the traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1.
Set up a simple routing policy that routes all traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all traffic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.
Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.
Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the traffic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.

questions.explanation:
Geolocation routing directs traffic based on the geographic location of end users. Routing users located near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center and users near eu-central-1 to the AWS eu-central-1 region minimizes latency for each group. This explicit geographic mapping is more operationally predictable than relying on measured latency across arbitrary endpoints in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Geolocation routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a static website hosted on Amazon CloudFront with Amazon S3 as the origin. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not show updates that were made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured correctly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments.  
  
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Add an Application Load Balancer.
Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront caches website objects at edge locations, so even when the CI/CD pipeline has successfully deployed updated files to Amazon S3, viewers can continue to receive the older cached versions until they expire. Invalidating the CloudFront cache removes those stale objects so the next request causes CloudFront to fetch the latest content from the origin. Adding an Application Load Balancer, adding ElastiCache to the database tier, or validating an ACM certificate does not address stale cached website content.

**Learn more:** [Invalidate files to remove content - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Invalidation.html) · [Speeding up your website with Amazon CloudFront - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/website-hosting-cloudfront-walkthrough.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's web application includes an Amazon API Gateway API in front of an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB database. The Lambda function handles the business logic, and the DynamoDB table stores the data. The application uses Amazon Cognito user pools to identify individual users of the application. A solutions architect must update the application so that only users who have a subscription can access premium content.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Enable API caching and throttling on the API Gateway API.
Set up AWS WAF on the API Gateway API. Create a rule to filter users who have a subscription.
Apply fine-grained IAM permissions to the premium content in the DynamoDB table.
Implement API usage plans and API keys to limit the access of users who do not have a subscription.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway usage plans paired with API keys let specific resources or methods, such as the premium-content endpoints, be gated behind a key that is only issued to subscribers, using a fully managed API Gateway feature with no new code, infrastructure, or changes to the existing Lambda/DynamoDB backend. This is lower overhead than building fine-grained IAM policies for direct DynamoDB access, which would require restructuring the client's access path away from the current API Gateway/Lambda flow, or maintaining custom AWS WAF rules, while API caching and throttling alone do nothing to enforce subscription entitlement.

**Learn more:** [Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores text files in Amazon S3. The text files contain customer chat messages, date and time information, and customer personally identifiable information (PII).  
  
The company needs a solution to provide samples of the conversations to an external service provider for quality control. The external service provider must be able to randomly select sample conversations up to the most recent conversation. The company must not share the customer PII with the external service provider. The solution must scale as the number of customer conversations grows.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an Object Lambda Access Point. Create an AWS Lambda function that redacts the PII when the function reads the file. Instruct the external service provider to access the Object Lambda Access Point.

Create a batch process on an Amazon EC2 instance that regularly reads all new files, redacts the PII from the files, and writes the redacted files to a different S3 bucket. Instruct the external service provider to access the bucket that does not contain the PII.

Create a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance that presents a list of the files, redacts the PII from the files, and allows the external service provider to download new versions of the files that have the PII redacted.

Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads only the data in the files that does not contain PII. Configure the Lambda function to store the non-PII data in the DynamoDB table when a new file is written to Amazon S3. Grant the external service provider access to the DynamoDB table.

Amazon S3 Object Lambda intercepts S3 GET requests and transforms the returned data using AWS Lambda functions. A Lambda function using Amazon Comprehend can automatically detect and redact PII before the external service provider receives the data. This eliminates the need to maintain duplicate redacted copies or manage EC2-based batch processes, providing the lowest operational overhead at scale.

A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The application must ingest real-time data from third-party applications.  
  
The company requires a data ingestion solution that stores the ingested raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon Kinesis data streams for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume the Kinesis data streams. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.

Create database migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Specify replication instances of the EC2 instances as the source endpoints. Specify the S3 bucket as the target endpoint. Set the migration type to migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes.
Create and configure AWS DataSync agents on the EC2 instances. Configure DataSync tasks to transfer data from the EC2 instances to the S3 bucket.

Create an AWS Direct Connect connection to the application for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume direct PUT operations from the application. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is designed to deliver real-time streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3, and it can use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams as its source. That makes Kinesis Data Streams for ingestion plus Firehose for delivery the correct architecture for collecting real-time data from third-party applications and storing the raw data in S3. AWS DMS is intended for database migration and change data capture, DataSync is for file and object transfers rather than event streaming, and Direct Connect provides private network connectivity rather than acting as the data ingestion service itself.

**Learn more:** [Configure source settings for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/writing-with-kinesis-streams.html) · [What is Amazon Data Firehose?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An entertainment company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read-intensive and is experiencing delays. The company does not have staff to manage additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB **without reconfiguring the application**.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache designed for read-heavy workloads. It can reduce DynamoDB read latency from milliseconds to microseconds while keeping operational overhead low, and it is intended to integrate with existing DynamoDB applications with only minimal changes compared with building and managing a separate caching layer. That makes it the best fit when the primary issue is slow read performance on DynamoDB and the requirement is to avoid added operational burden. Official AWS documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html

**Learn more:** [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html) · [Developing with the DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) client - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.client.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a serverless solution for large-scale, parallel, on-demand processing of a semistructured dataset. The data includes logs, media files, sales transactions, and IoT sensor data that is stored in Amazon S3. The company wants the solution to process thousands of items in the dataset in parallel.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Inline mode to process the data in parallel.
Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode to process the data in parallel.
Use AWS Glue to process the data in parallel.
Use several AWS Lambda functions to process the data in parallel.

questions.explanation:
AWS Step Functions **Map state in Distributed mode** is built for large-scale parallel workloads and can process data stored in Amazon S3 by launching thousands of parallel child workflow executions. That makes it the best fit for a serverless, on-demand design that must handle thousands of dataset items with minimal custom orchestration. Inline mode is limited to smaller concurrency, and using multiple Lambda functions directly adds orchestration overhead. AWS Glue can process semistructured data, but it is an ETL-focused service rather than the most operationally efficient choice for this pattern of large-scale parallel item processing.

**Learn more:** [Using Map state in Distributed mode for large-scale parallel workloads in Step Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/state-map-distributed.html) · [Using Map state in Inline mode in Step Functions workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/state-map-inline.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application development team is designing a microservice to convert large images into smaller, compressed images.  
  
When a user uploads an image through the web interface, the microservice must:  
  
- store the image in an Amazon S3 bucket  
- process and compress the image by using an AWS Lambda function  
- store the compressed image in a different S3 bucket  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that uses durable, stateless components to process the images automatically.  
  
Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the S3 bucket to send a notification to the SQS queue when an image is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
Configure the Lambda function to use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the invocation source. When the SQS message is successfully processed, delete the message in the queue.

Configure the Lambda function to monitor the S3 bucket for new uploads. When an uploaded image is detected, write the file name to a text file in memory and use the text file to keep track of the images that were processed.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to monitor an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. When items are added to the queue, log the file name in a text file on the EC2 instance and invoke the Lambda function.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) event to monitor the S3 bucket. When an image is uploaded, send an alert to an Amazon ample Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with the application owner's email address for further processing.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can publish object-created event notifications to an Amazon SQS queue, and AWS Lambda can use that SQS queue as its event source. This creates a durable, decoupled, stateless processing pipeline: the upload event is persisted in SQS until Lambda successfully processes it, after which the message is removed from the queue. Approaches that rely on in-memory tracking, local files on an EC2 instance, or manual email-driven handling do not meet the durability, statelessness, and automatic-processing requirements.

**Learn more:** [Event notification types and destinations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html) · [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

options.text: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to generate secure Amazon S3 access tokens for users when they successfully log in.
Use the existing Amazon Cognito user pool to generate Amazon S3 access tokens for users when they successfully log in.
Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint in the same VPC where the company hosts the application.
Create a NAT gateway in the VPC where the company hosts the application. Assign a policy to the S3 bucket to deny any request that is not initiated from Amazon Cognito.
Attach a policy to the S3 bucket that allows access only from the users' IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon Cognito identity pool can exchange authenticated user-pool tokens for temporary AWS credentials associated with IAM roles, allowing permissions to be limited to the required Amazon S3 actions and resources. An Amazon S3 VPC endpoint gives workloads in a private subnet private network access to S3, without requiring a NAT gateway or public internet routing.

**Learn more:** [Accessing AWS services using an identity pool after sign-in](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-integrating-user-pools-with-identity-pools.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application includes:  
  
- a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets  
- a database tier consisting of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet  
  
Security is a high priority for the company.  
  
How should the security groups be configured in this scenario? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.

questions.explanation:
A public web tier should permit inbound HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443 from the internet, and the SQL Server tier should permit inbound TCP port 1433 only from the web tier’s security group. AWS documentation shows HTTPS web servers commonly allow inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, and database access is best restricted by referencing the application tier security group rather than opening database ports broadly. Because security groups are stateful, return traffic is automatically allowed, so the extra outbound database rules are unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Security group rules for different use cases - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules-reference.html) · [Security group rules - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases for its data tier. The company needs to implement password rotation for the databases.  
  
Which solution satisfies this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager. Enable automatic rotation on the secret.
Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Enable automatic rotation on the parameter.
Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Write an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password.
Store the password in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable automatic rotation on the AWS KMS key.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the correct service because it is designed to store and rotate secrets such as database credentials, including Amazon RDS passwords, with built-in automatic rotation support. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store can store encrypted values, but AWS recommends Secrets Manager when credentials require automatic rotation. AWS KMS key rotation applies only to encryption key material and does not rotate database passwords.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently migrated its application to AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 Linux instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that uses EFS Standard-Infrequent Access storage. The application indexes the company's files. The index is stored in an Amazon RDS database.  
  
The company needs to optimize storage costs with some application and services changes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses an Intelligent-Tiering lifecycle policy. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files.
Deploy Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file shares. Update the application to use CIFS protocol to store and retrieve files.
Deploy Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system shares. Update the application to use the new mount point to store and retrieve files.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Copy all files to the S3 bucket. Update the application to use Amazon S3 API to store and retrieve files as standard retrievals.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is typically the lowest-cost AWS storage option for file content when an application can be changed to use object storage instead of a shared file system. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is specifically intended for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns and automatically moves objects to lower-cost access tiers while keeping low-latency access for active objects. By contrast, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is archive storage that requires restore operations and has retrieval times measured in hours, so it is not appropriate for normal application reads. FSx for Windows File Server and FSx for OpenZFS remain managed file systems and are generally less cost-effective than moving the files to S3 when the application can be updated to use the S3 API.

**Learn more:** [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html) · [Cost optimization - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cost-optimization.html)

A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

questions.explanation:
The most operationally efficient design is to use a wildcard custom domain for API Gateway so each customer can have an individual subdomain without creating separate APIs or separate hosted zones. API Gateway supports wildcard custom domain names for REST APIs, and AWS states that wildcard custom domains can support very large numbers of customer-specific subdomains. For a Regional API Gateway custom domain, the ACM certificate must be requested or imported in the same Region as the API. Route 53 then maps the wildcard domain to the API Gateway custom domain endpoint. That makes the correct combination the wildcard Route 53 domain/record, the same-Region wildcard ACM certificate, and the API Gateway custom domain that uses that certificate.

**Learn more:** [Custom domain name for public REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-custom-domains.html) · [Set up a Regional custom domain name in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-regional-api-custom-domain-create.html)

Assign a policy to the S3 bucket to deny any request that is not initiated from Amazon Cognito.","E":"Attach a policy to the S3 bucket that allows access only from the users' IP addresses."},"correctAnswer":"AC","explanation":"An Amazon Cognito identity pool can exchange authenticated user-pool tokens for temporary AWS credentials associated with IAM roles, allowing permissions to be limited to the required Amazon S3 actions and resources. ",["$","li",null,{"children":"a database tier consisting of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet"}],"
"]}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Security is a high priority for the company."}],"

",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.","B":"Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.","C":"Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.","D":"Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.","E":"Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier."},"correctAnswer":"AC","explanation":"A public web tier should permit inbound HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443 from the internet, and the SQL Server tier should permit inbound TCP port 1433 only from the web tier’s security group. AWS documentation shows HTTPS web servers commonly allow inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, and database access is best restricted by referencing the application tier security group rather than opening database ports broadly. Because security groups are stateful, return traffic is automatically allowed, so the extra outbound database rules are unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Security group rules for different use cases - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules-reference.html) · [Security group rules - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"43c460c0-a5b7-4a0f-a443-955dd9fe756e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]

Amazon S3 is typically the lowest-cost AWS storage option for file content when an application can be changed to use object storage instead of a shared file system. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is specifically intended for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns and automatically moves objects to lower-cost access tiers while keeping low-latency access for active objects. By contrast, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is archive storage that requires restore operations and has retrieval times measured in hours, so it is not appropriate for normal application reads. FSx for Windows File Server and FSx for OpenZFS remain managed file systems and are generally less cost-effective than moving the files to S3 when the application can be updated to use the S3 API.

**Learn more:** [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html) · [Cost optimization - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cost-optimization.html)54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company recently migrated its application to AWS. The most operationally efficient design is to use a wildcard custom domain for API Gateway so each customer can have an individual subdomain without creating separate APIs or separate hosted zones. API Gateway supports wildcard custom domain names for REST APIs, and AWS states that wildcard custom domains can support very large numbers of customer-specific subdomains. For a Regional API Gateway custom domain, the ACM certificate must be requested or imported in the same Region as the API. Route 53 then maps the wildcard domain to the API Gateway custom domain endpoint. That makes the correct combination the wildcard Route 53 domain/record, the same-Region wildcard ACM certificate, and the API Gateway custom domain that uses that certificate.

A company wants to limit access to the content of one of its primary web applications and protect that content by using authorization capabilities available on AWS.  
  
The company wants to implement:  
  
- a serverless architecture, and  
- an authentication solution for fewer than 100 users.  
  
The solution must also:  
  
- integrate with the main web application,  
- serve web content globally,  
- scale as the company's user base grows, and  
- provide the lowest login latency possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito is the most cost-effective managed authentication service for a small web user base and can scale to millions of users. Amazon CloudFront is the AWS global content delivery service for serving web content worldwide, and Lambda@Edge runs authorization logic at edge locations close to users, which reduces authentication and authorization latency. By contrast, AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is a managed AD deployment with persistent directory cost and is not the most economical serverless choice for fewer than 100 users, and Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration is intended to speed uploads and transfers to S3 rather than to serve and authorize a global web application. Using Amazon Cognito with Lambda@Edge and CloudFront therefore best satisfies the serverless, global, scalable, and low-latency requirements.

**Learn more:** [Edge Computing with AWS Lambda@Edge](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/edge/) · [Ways to use Lambda@Edge - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-ways-to-use.html)

A company is building a marketing communications service that targets mobile application users. The company must send confirmation messages to users by using Short Message Service (SMS). Users must be able to reply to the SMS messages. The company also must retain the responses for 1 year for analysis.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Connect contact flow to send the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.
Build an Amazon Pinpoint journey. Configure Amazon Pinpoint to send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream for analysis and archiving.
Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to distribute the SMS messages. Use AWS Lambda to process the responses.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topic. Subscribe an Amazon Kinesis data stream to the SNS topic for analysis and archiving.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Pinpoint is the AWS service built for targeted communications to mobile app users and supports SMS campaigns and journeys, including two-way SMS use cases. Amazon Pinpoint can stream SMS and journey event data to Amazon Kinesis, which can then be used for downstream analytics and long-term retention such as storing the records for a year. The other options do not provide the required combination of app-user messaging, SMS replies, and analytics-oriented event streaming.

**Learn more:** [Set up SMS in Amazon Pinpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pinpoint/latest/userguide/tutorials-two-way-sms-part-1.html) · [SMS event data stream from Amazon Pinpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pinpoint/latest/developerguide/event-streams-data-sms.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its ecommerce application on AWS. Each new order is published as a message in a RabbitMQ queue that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a single Availability Zone. These messages are processed by a separate application that runs on another EC2 instance. This application stores the details in a PostgreSQL database on a different EC2 instance. All the EC2 instances are in the same Availability Zone.  
  
The company needs to redesign its architecture to provide the highest availability with the least operational overhead.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database.

Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.

Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.

Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create a third Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database

questions.explanation:
For the lowest operational overhead and highest availability, the stateful components should move to managed multi-AZ services. Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ provides managed RabbitMQ broker deployments for high availability, and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL supports Multi-AZ deployments with automatic standby/failover in another Availability Zone. The application tier is best placed in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group so instances can run across Availability Zones and be replaced automatically. A self-managed PostgreSQL or RabbitMQ deployment on EC2 Auto Scaling groups adds substantially more operational work and is not the preferred HA design for these services. Official AWS documentation supports Amazon MQ high-availability RabbitMQ deployments, Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling behavior across Availability Zones, and Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL deployments.

**Learn more:** [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/rabbitmq-broker-architecture.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

A company uses NFS to store large video files on on-premises network-attached storage. Each video file is between 1 MB and 500 GB in size. The total amount of storage is 70 TB and is no longer increasing. The company decides to migrate the video files to Amazon S3.  
  
The company must migrate the video files as quickly as possible while using the least amount of network bandwidth.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an S3 bucket. Create an IAM role that has permissions to write to the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to copy all files locally to the S3 bucket.

Create an AWS Snowball Edge job. Receive a Snowball Edge device on premises. Use the Snowball Edge client to transfer data to the device. Return the device so that AWS can import the data into Amazon S3.

Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public service endpoint to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.

Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and AWS. Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public virtual interface (VIF) to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.

questions.explanation:
AWS Snowball Edge is the best fit for a one-time bulk transfer of 70 TB from on-premises storage to Amazon S3 because the data is copied locally to the device and then physically shipped back to AWS for import into S3, which minimizes WAN bandwidth use. This also aligns with the urgency requirement better than provisioning a network-based migration path. Amazon S3 object size limits support files up to 5 TB, so video files as large as 500 GB can be migrated this way. By contrast, AWS CLI uploads and S3 File Gateway-based approaches send the data over the network, and Direct Connect still depends on network transfer and setup time.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Snowball Edge works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/how-it-works.html) · [Creating a job to order a Snowball Edge device](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/create-ec2-edge-job.html)

A company uses Amazon API Gateway to host a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to verify that sufficient funds are available before a stock purchase can occur. The company has observed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service is calling the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet rather than through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **fewest changes to the code**?

options.text: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
Use an interface endpoint.
Use a gateway endpoint.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway private REST APIs are invoked from within a VPC by using an **interface VPC endpoint** for the `execute-api` service. That keeps traffic on private IPs within the Amazon network instead of traversing the public internet. This change addresses the network path without changing the application interaction pattern, so it is the lowest-code-change solution.

**Learn more:** [Private REST APIs in API Gateway - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html) · [Invoke a private API - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-api-test-invoke-url.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has engaged an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account owned by the vendor. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account. The company must grant the vendor access to the company’s AWS account.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST securely**?

options.text: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the automated tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM user in the company’s account that has a permission boundary that allows the vendor’s account. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

questions.explanation:
The most secure solution is to create a cross-account IAM role in the company account that the vendor can assume. AWS recommends using IAM roles to delegate access across AWS accounts and to third parties because roles provide temporary security credentials instead of long-term IAM user credentials. The role’s trust policy can allow the vendor’s account or IAM role to assume it, and the attached permissions policies can be limited to only the actions the vendor requires. IAM users are less secure for this use case because they require long-term credentials, IAM groups cannot include identities from another AWS account, and permission boundaries do not by themselves grant third-party cross-account access.

**Learn more:** [Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html) · [IAM tutorial: Delegate access across AWS accounts using IAM roles - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_cross-account-with-roles.html)

A global video streaming company uses Amazon CloudFront as a content distribution network (CDN). The company wants to roll out content in a phased manner across multiple countries.  
  
The company needs to ensure that viewers outside the countries where the company has rolled out the content cannot view it.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Add geographic restrictions to the content in CloudFront by using an allow list. Set up a custom error message.
Set up a new URL tor restricted content. Authorize access by using a signed URL and cookies. Set up a custom error message.
Encrypt the data for the content that the company distributes. Set up a custom error message.
Create a new URL for restricted content. Set up a time-restricted access policy for signed URLs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront provides geographic restrictions (geo restriction) to control access by country for content served through a distribution. For a phased rollout across countries, an allow list is the best fit because it permits access only from the countries currently approved for release and denies viewers elsewhere. Signed URLs or cookies govern authenticated or time-limited access, not country-based availability, and encryption by itself does not block viewing from unauthorized countries. AWS documentation states that CloudFront geographic restrictions can use an allow list of approved countries and return HTTP 403 for blocked locations.

**Learn more:** [Restrict the geographic distribution of your content - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/georestrictions.html) · [Geographic restrictions - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesEnableGeoRestriction.html)

A company must implement a new data-retention policy for regulatory compliance. Under this policy, sensitive documents stored in an Amazon S3 bucket must be safeguarded against deletion or modification for a fixed duration.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable governance mode.
Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable compliance mode.
Enable versioning on the S3 bucket. Set a lifecycle policy to delete the objects after a specified period.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for the retention duration.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces write-once-read-many (WORM) retention. Protected object versions cannot be deleted or overwritten until the retention period expires, even by the AWS account root user.

questions.question:
A company must implement a new data-retention policy for regulatory compliance. Under this policy, sensitive documents stored in an Amazon S3 bucket must be safeguarded against deletion or modification for a fixed duration.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
Configure an Amazon Cognito identity pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Lambda authorizer.
Configure an IAM user to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with an IAM authorizer.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito user pools are the managed service for authenticating application users and issuing JWTs for web and mobile apps. Amazon API Gateway REST APIs can use a Cognito user pool authorizer directly to validate those tokens and control API access without custom authentication code. That makes this approach more operationally efficient than building authentication in AWS Lambda, and more appropriate than identity pools, which are primarily for obtaining temporary AWS credentials to access AWS services rather than serving as the core end-user authentication store for REST API access.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Cognito user pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools.html) · [How authentication works with Amazon Cognito](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-how-to-authenticate.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a shared storage solution for a gaming application hosted in an on-premises data center. The company requires the ability for Lustre clients to access the data. The solution also must be fully managed.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre is AWS’s fully managed Lustre file system service, so it satisfies the requirement for a managed shared storage solution that Lustre clients can use. AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway exposes NFS or SMB shares, not Lustre, and Amazon EFS is an NFS-based service rather than a Lustre file system. A self-managed Windows file server on Amazon EC2 also fails the fully managed requirement. FSx for Lustre is therefore the only service that matches both the protocol and management constraints.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html) · [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application in a private subnet behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. The VPC includes a NAT gateway and an internet gateway. The application invokes the Amazon S3 API to store objects.  
  
Under the company’s security policy, application traffic must not traverse the internet.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Configure an S3 interface endpoint. Create a security group that allows outbound traffic to Amazon S3.
Configure an S3 gateway endpoint. Update the VPC route table to use the endpoint.
Configure an S3 bucket policy to allow traffic from the Elastic IP address that is assigned to the NAT gateway.
Create a second NAT gateway in the same subnet where the legacy application is deployed. Update the VPC route table to use the second NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint adds an S3 prefix-list route to the private subnet’s route table, sending S3 traffic over the AWS network without using a NAT gateway or internet gateway. Gateway endpoints for S3 have no additional charge; S3 interface endpoints are billed.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company gathers 10 GB of telemetry data each day from multiple machines. The company stores this data in an Amazon S3 bucket in a source data account.  
  
The company has engaged several consulting agencies to analyze the data. Each agency requires read access to the data for its analysts. The company must share the data from the source data account by selecting a solution that maximizes security and operational efficiency.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure S3 global tables to replicate data for each agency.
Make the S3 bucket public for a limited time. Inform only the agencies.
Configure cross-account access for the S3 bucket to the accounts that the agencies own.
Set up an IAM user for each analyst in the source data account. Grant each user access to the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 supports secure cross-account sharing, allowing a bucket owner to grant read access to IAM identities in other AWS accounts by using resource-based policies and related access controls. This is more operationally efficient than creating IAM users for every external analyst in the source account, because each agency can manage its own users. It is also more secure than making the bucket public, which AWS recommends against unless public internet access is explicitly required. Option A is incorrect because Amazon S3 does not have a “global tables” feature.

**Learn more:** [Access control in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-management.html) · [S3 Access Grants cross-account access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-grants-cross-accounts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a self-managed Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Daily snapshots are created for the EBS volumes.  
  
Recently, while executing a snapshot-cleanup script that deletes all expired EBS snapshots, the company accidentally deleted all of its EBS snapshots. A solutions architect must update the architecture to prevent data loss without keeping EBS snapshots forever.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Change the IAM policy of the user to deny EBS snapshot deletion.
Copy the EBS snapshots to another AWS Region after completing the snapshots daily.
Create a 7-day EBS snapshot retention rule in Recycle Bin and apply the rule for all snapshots.
Copy EBS snapshots to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS Recycle Bin can retain deleted EBS snapshots for a defined period and restore them before that period expires. A 7-day, Region-level retention rule protects all snapshots from accidental deletion while ensuring they are permanently removed after the finite retention period. AWS documents a Region-level rule that retains all deleted EBS snapshots for 7 days.

**Learn more:** [Create a Recycle Bin retention rule - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin-create-rule.html) · [Recover deleted EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, and EBS-backed AMIs with Recycle Bin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has several on-premises Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (ISCSI) network storage servers. The company wants to reduce the number of these servers by moving to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must provide low-latency access to frequently used data and reduce dependence on on-premises servers with a minimal amount of infrastructure change.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway.
Deploy Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage with backups to Amazon S3.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with stored volumes.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with cached volumes.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with **cached volumes** is designed for on-premises applications that use **iSCSI** block storage but want primary data stored in AWS. Cached volumes keep the full dataset in **Amazon S3** while retaining **frequently accessed data locally** for **low-latency access**, which minimizes on-premises storage needs and preserves the existing iSCSI-based access pattern. Stored volumes are intended when low-latency access is needed for the entire dataset and primary data remains on premises, so they do not reduce on-premises storage dependency as effectively.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to host a digital media streaming application.  
  
The EKS cluster will use a managed node group that is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for storage.  
  
The company must encrypt all data at rest by using a customer managed key that is stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
  
Which combination of actions will meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Use a Kubernetes plugin that uses the customer managed key to perform data encryption.
After creation of the EKS cluster, locate the EBS volumes. Enable encryption by using the customer managed key.
Enable EBS encryption by default in the AWS Region where the EKS cluster will be created. Select the customer managed key as the default key.
Create the EKS cluster. Create an IAM role that has a policy that grants permission to the customer managed key. Associate the role with the EKS cluster.
Store the customer managed key as a Kubernetes secret in the EKS cluster. Use the customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS provides native encryption at rest with AWS KMS, so the lowest-overhead solution is to enable **EBS encryption by default** in the target Region and set the **customer managed KMS key** as the default key. Amazon EKS documentation specifically notes that to deploy managed node groups with encrypted EBS volumes **without using a launch template**, you should encrypt all new EBS volumes created in the account. In addition, when using a customer managed KMS key for EBS encryption, the key must allow its use for EBS on behalf of the workload, so granting the necessary KMS permissions through IAM is required. Options that try to encrypt volumes after creation or use Kubernetes-level secrets/plugins are not the native EBS-at-rest encryption path and add unnecessary operational effort.

**Learn more:** [Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/managed-node-groups.html) · [Set up for Amazon EBS - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/setting-up.html)
