A solutions architect must securely store a database user name and password that an application uses to access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The application that accesses the database runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The solutions architect wants to create a secure parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create an IAM role that has read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM role to the EC2 instance.

Create an IAM policy that allows read access to the Parameter Store parameter. Allow Decrypt access to an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is used to encrypt the parameter. Assign this IAM policy to the EC2 instance.
Create an IAM trust relationship between the Parameter Store parameter and the EC2 instance. Specify Amazon RDS as a principal in the trust policy.
Create an IAM trust relationship between the DB instance and the EC2 instance. Specify Systems Manager as a principal in the trust policy.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store `SecureString` values are encrypted with AWS KMS, and retrieving the plaintext value requires permission to read the parameter and permission for KMS decryption. For an application running on Amazon EC2, the standard secure approach is to attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance so the application can call Parameter Store without embedded credentials. That role must allow access to the parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on the KMS key used to encrypt it.

**Learn more:** [AWS KMS encryption for AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/secure-string-parameter-kms-encryption.html) · [Restricting access to Parameter Store parameters using IAM policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-paramstore-access.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a self-managed DNS solution on three Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the **us-west-2** Region. Most of the company's users are in the United States and Europe. The company wants to improve the solution's performance and availability. The company launches and configures three EC2 instances in the **eu-west-1** Region and adds those EC2 instances as targets for a new NLB.  
  
Which solution can the company use to route traffic to all the EC2 instances?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to route requests to one of the two NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution’s origin.
Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Create endpoint groups in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Add the two NLBs as endpoints for the endpoint groups.

Attach Elastic IP addresses to the six EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to route requests to one of the six EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution's origin.

Replace the two NLBs with two Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Create an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to route requests to one of the two ALBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use the Route 53 record as the distribution’s origin.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct fit because it improves global performance and availability for internet traffic by directing users to the optimal regional endpoint over the AWS global network, and a standard accelerator can use endpoint groups in multiple Regions with Network Load Balancers as endpoints. That matches a multi-Region DNS service behind NLBs. CloudFront is not suitable for routing DNS traffic, and Application Load Balancers do not support UDP-based DNS workloads. Official AWS documentation also states that standard accelerators use regional endpoint groups and support NLB endpoints.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Endpoint groups for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoint-groups.html)

A company has NFS servers in an on-premises data center that must periodically back up small amounts of data to Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements and is **MOST** cost-effective?

options.text: Set up AWS Glue to copy the data from the on-premises servers to Amazon S3.
Set up an AWS DataSync agent on the on-premises servers, and sync the data to Amazon S3.
Set up an SFTP sync using AWS Transfer for SFTP to sync data from on premises to Amazon S3.
Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and a VPC, and copy the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is the correct service because it is designed to move data from on-premises file storage, including NFS file servers, to AWS storage services such as Amazon S3 by using a DataSync agent. That makes it the most direct managed solution for periodic backups from NFS to S3. AWS Glue is intended for ETL workloads, AWS Transfer for SFTP is centered on SFTP-based transfers rather than NFS-based storage synchronization, and AWS Direct Connect adds unnecessary dedicated-network cost for small periodic data transfers.

**Learn more:** [Transferring to or from on-premises storage with AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/transferring-on-premises-storage.html) · [AWS DataSync network requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/datasync-network.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a fleet of web servers that use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.  
  
After a routine compliance review, the company establishes a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployments provide high availability by maintaining a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone. Because replication to the standby is synchronous, committed transactions are kept in sync closely enough to satisfy a near-zero-data-loss objective such as an RPO of less than 1 second. Read replicas and AWS DMS CDC use asynchronous replication and can have lag, so they do not guarantee that recovery will meet this RPO requirement. Auto Scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone does not provide cross-AZ synchronized recovery capability.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A news company with reporters located worldwide hosts its broadcast system on AWS. The reporters send live broadcasts to the broadcast system by using software on their phones to transmit live streams over the Real Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP).  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that gives the reporters the ability to send the highest-quality streams. The solution must provide accelerated TCP connections back to the broadcast system.  
  
What should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Client VPN
Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Elastic IP addresses

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct service because it improves performance for global users by routing traffic onto the AWS global network and specifically accelerates TCP connections by terminating client TCP sessions at AWS edge locations and establishing optimized connections to the application endpoints. That directly matches RTMP ingest over TCP from reporters worldwide. Amazon CloudFront is not appropriate here because CloudFront RTMP distributions were deprecated, and neither AWS Client VPN nor plain EC2 instances with Elastic IP addresses provide global TCP acceleration for live stream contribution.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works - AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Working with standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/work-with-standard-accelerators.html)

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Rekognition is the AWS managed service designed for image and video content moderation. Its moderation APIs can detect inappropriate, unwanted, or offensive content in images and return confidence scores for the detected moderation labels. For cases that are uncertain, AWS supports routing images for human review, which fits the requirement to use human review for low-confidence predictions while still minimizing development effort because no custom model training or custom ML infrastructure is required.

**Learn more:** [DetectModerationLabels - Amazon Rekognition](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/APIReference/API_DetectModerationLabels.html) · [Amazon Rekognition Content Moderation](https://aws.amazon.com/rekognition/content-moderation/)

A company has a custom application containing embedded credentials that retrieves information from a database in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB cluster. The company needs to improve the application's security with minimal programming effort. The company has created database credentials for the application user on the RDS for MySQL database.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store the credentials in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Create keys in AWS KMS. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation
Store the credentials in encrypted local storage. Configure the application to load the database credentials from the local storage. Set up a credentials rotation schedule by creating a cron job.

Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule by creating an AWS Lambda function for Secrets Manager.

Store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule in the RDS for MySQL database by using Parameter Store.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager securely stores database credentials so the application can retrieve them at runtime instead of embedding them in code. For Amazon RDS database secrets, Secrets Manager can schedule automatic rotation and invoke a Lambda rotation function to update both the secret and the database credential.

**Learn more:** [Move hardcoded database credentials to AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/hardcoded-db-creds.html) · [Set up automatic rotation for Amazon RDS secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company offers an API interface to customers so they can retrieve their financial information. The company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year.  
  
The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda provides the lowest operational overhead because it is fully managed and avoids operating container hosts or Kubernetes clusters. For the low-latency requirement, Lambda provisioned concurrency is the key feature because it keeps execution environments pre-initialized so requests avoid cold-start delays and can deliver more consistent response times during peak periods. Reserved concurrency only guarantees concurrency capacity and prevents throttling by setting aside capacity for the function; it does not pre-initialize environments to provide consistently low latency. AWS documentation specifically describes provisioned concurrency as useful for reducing cold-start latency and making functions available with very fast response times for interactive workloads.

**Learn more:** [Configuring reserved concurrency for a function - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html) · [Understanding Lambda function scaling - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses high block storage capacity to run its workloads on premises. options.text: GP2 volume type

questions.explanation:

AWS also states that gp3 has a lower price per GiB than gp2, while gp2 ties performance to allocated size, and io1/io2 are Provisioned IOPS offerings better suited to higher-end or latency-sensitive needs rather than the most cost-effective choice here.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company gathers data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data. The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to remain at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.

questions.explanation:
For a steady, predictable workload, DynamoDB provisioned mode with fixed RCUs and WCUs is the most cost-effective option because you pay only for the capacity you reserve rather than per-request pricing. On-demand mode is designed for unpredictable or variable traffic patterns. Reserved capacity can further optimize costs for predictable provisioned workloads.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB provisioned capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/provisioned-capacity-mode.html) · [DynamoDB throughput capacity modes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/capacity-mode.html)

A solutions architect must enable team members to access Amazon S3 buckets in two different AWS accounts: a development account and a production account. The team already accesses S3 buckets in the development account by using unique IAM users that are assigned to an IAM group with the appropriate permissions in that account.  
  
The solutions architect has created an IAM role in the production account. The role includes a policy that grants access to an S3 bucket in the production account.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements while following the principle of least privilege?

options.text: Attach the Administrator Access policy to the development account users.
Add the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the role in the production account.
Turn off the S3 Block Public Access feature on the S3 bucket in the production account.
Create a user in the production account with unique credentials for each team member.

questions.explanation:
AWS recommends cross-account access by allowing the trusted account to assume a role in the trusting account. Here, the production account role already contains the S3 permissions, so the correct configuration is to add the development account as a principal in that role’s trust policy and allow the relevant development users to assume it with `sts:AssumeRole`. That uses existing identities, grants only the role’s limited S3 permissions through temporary credentials, and avoids broad administrative access, public exposure, or duplicate long-term user credentials.

**Learn more:** [Update a role trust policy - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_update-role-trust-policy.html) · [Grant a user permissions to switch roles - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_permissions-to-switch.html)

A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses a database running on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The application becomes slow as traffic rises. During high-traffic periods, the database is under heavy read load.  
  
Which actions should a solutions architect take to address these performance problems? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Turn on auto scaling for the DB instance.
Create a read replica for the DB instance. Configure the application to send read traffic to the read replica.
Convert the DB instance to a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Configure the application to send read traffic to the standby DB instance.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Configure the application to cache query results in the ElastiCache cluster.
Configure the Auto Scaling group subnets to ensure that the EC2 instances are provisioned in the same Availability Zone as the DB instance.

questions.explanation:
For a read-heavy Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workload, creating a read replica allows the application to route read queries away from the primary instance and scale out read capacity. Adding Amazon ElastiCache can further improve performance by caching frequently requested query results so the database receives fewer repeated reads. A standard Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not allow read traffic to be sent to the standby replica; the standby is for high availability and failover, not read scaling. AWS documentation specifically recommends read replicas for read-heavy workloads and notes that the standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not serve read traffic.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Working with read replicas for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PostgreSQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has users worldwide who access its HTTP-based application, which is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple AWS Regions.  
  
The company wants to:  
  
- improve the application's availability and performance  
- protect the application from common web exploits that could affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources  
- use static IP addresses  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to achieve this?

options.text: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the NLBs as endpoints.
Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the ALBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the ALBs as endpoints.

Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the NLBs.

Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the ALBs. Deploy AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the AWS service that provides static anycast IP addresses and routes users over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy regional endpoint, improving both availability and performance. For HTTP applications that need protection from common web exploits, AWS WAF must be attached to a supported Layer 7 resource such as an Application Load Balancer or CloudFront distribution; Network Load Balancers are not AWS WAF resources. Using Application Load Balancers in each Region, associating AWS WAF with those ALBs, and registering the ALBs as AWS Global Accelerator endpoints satisfies every requirement together.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html)

A company requires guaranteed Amazon EC2 capacity in three specific Availability Zones within a particular AWS Region for an upcoming event that will last **1 week**.  
  
What should the company do to guarantee the EC2 capacity?

options.text: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region needed.
Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region needed.
Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.

questions.explanation:
On-Demand Capacity Reservations are the AWS feature intended to guarantee Amazon EC2 capacity for short-term or long-term needs in a specific Availability Zone. AWS documentation states that Capacity Reservations reserve compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration, which matches a 1-week event. Regional Reserved Instances do not reserve capacity, and although zonal Reserved Instances can provide capacity reservation, the standard AWS solution for guaranteeing temporary event capacity in specified Availability Zones is to create On-Demand Capacity Reservations in those Availability Zones.

**Learn more:** [Reserve compute capacity with EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservations - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html) · [Create a Capacity Reservation - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-reservations-create.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts its application on AWS. The company uses Amazon Cognito to manage users. When users sign in to the application, the application retrieves required data from Amazon DynamoDB through a REST API hosted in Amazon API Gateway. The company wants an AWS-managed solution to control access to the REST API and reduce development effort.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Configure an AWS Lambda function to be an authorizer in API Gateway to validate which user made the request.
For each user, create and assign an API key that must be sent with each request. Validate the key by using an AWS Lambda function.
Send the user’s email address in the header with every request. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to validate that the user with that email address has proper access.
Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer in API Gateway to allow Amazon Cognito to validate each request.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway can use an Amazon Cognito user pool authorizer (`COGNITO_USER_POOLS`) to natively validate Cognito tokens on REST API requests, providing a fully managed authorization mechanism with minimal custom development and operations. Lambda authorizers require custom code and maintenance, while API keys and email headers do not provide proper user authorization for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Control access to REST APIs using Amazon Cognito user pools as an authorizer - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html) · [Create an Amazon Cognito user pool for a REST API - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-create-cognito-user-pool.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 2–3 months.  
  
What should the company do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.
Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.

questions.explanation:
Compute Savings Plans are designed for workloads that need pricing discounts without committing to a specific EC2 instance family or type. They automatically apply to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, Region, operating system, or tenancy, so the company can move between different instance families every few months and still keep the discount. By contrast, EC2 Instance Savings Plans are limited to a specific instance family in one Region, and Reserved Instances require commitment to a more specific instance configuration. A 1-year term best matches the need for flexibility while still reducing cost.

**Learn more:** [Savings Plans types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html) · [Compute Savings Plans and Reserved Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-ris.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently migrated a message-processing system to AWS. The system receives messages in an ActiveMQ queue that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Messages are processed by a consumer application running on Amazon EC2. The consumer application processes the messages and writes the results to a MySQL database running on Amazon EC2. The company wants this application to be highly available with low operational complexity.  
  
Which architecture provides the **HIGHEST** availability?

options.text: Add a second ActiveMQ server to another Availability Zone. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.

Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Replicate the MySQL database to another Availability Zone.

Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an additional consumer EC2 instance in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled.

Use Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers configured across two Availability Zones. Add an Auto Scaling group for the consumer EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled.

questions.explanation:
The highest-availability, lowest-operations design uses managed, multi-AZ services for the stateful tiers and automatic instance replacement for the stateless compute tier. Amazon MQ active/standby for ActiveMQ places redundant brokers across two Availability Zones and provides broker failover. Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ provides a synchronously replicated standby in another Availability Zone with automatic failover, which is more highly available and simpler to operate than self-managed MySQL replication on EC2. For the consumer application, an Auto Scaling group spanning two Availability Zones maintains the desired number of EC2 instances and replaces failed instances automatically, which is more available than manually running only two fixed instances.

**Learn more:** [Deployment options for Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ brokers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/amazon-mq-broker-architecture.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

A solutions architect is designing a two-tier architecture that includes a public subnet and a database subnet. The web servers in the public subnet must be accessible from the internet on port 443. The Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in the database subnet must be reachable only by the web servers on port 3306.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create a network ACL for the public subnet. Add a rule to deny outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow traffic from the public subnet CIDR block on port 3306.
Create a security group for the web servers in the public subnet. Add a rule to allow traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443.
Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow traffic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.
Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to deny all traffic except traffic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.

questions.explanation:
The web tier needs an inbound security group rule that allows HTTPS from anywhere, so the web servers’ security group should permit TCP port 443 from `0.0.0.0/0`. The database tier should not be opened to an entire subnet CIDR; instead, the DB instance security group should allow MySQL traffic on port 3306 only from the web servers’ security group. AWS documentation for EC2 security group use cases shows HTTPS access from `0.0.0.0/0` for web servers, and RDS documentation specifically supports allowing DB access from another security group for application servers. Security groups also do not provide explicit deny rules. 

**Learn more:** [Security group rules for different use cases - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules-reference.html) · [Controlling access with security groups - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.RDSSecurityGroups.html)

A company uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to expose its application to the internet. The company discovers abnormal traffic access patterns across the application. A solutions architect must increase visibility into the infrastructure to help the company better understand these abnormalities.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a table in Amazon Athena for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create a query for the relevant information.
Enable ALB access logging to Amazon S3. Create a table in Amazon Athena, and query the logs.
Enable ALB access logging to Amazon S3. Open each file in a text editor, and search each line for the relevant information.
Use Amazon EMR on a dedicated Amazon EC2 instance to directly query the ALB to acquire traffic access log information.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer access logs are designed to capture detailed request information for traffic sent to the load balancer, including client IP address, request details, latencies, and response codes. AWS supports storing these logs in Amazon S3 and querying them with Amazon Athena, which provides a serverless and efficient way to investigate abnormal traffic patterns. AWS CloudTrail records API calls to AWS services rather than the application’s inbound HTTP request traffic through the ALB, so it does not meet the traffic-analysis need as directly or effectively.

**Learn more:** [Access logs for your Application Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html) · [Query Application Load Balancer logs - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/application-load-balancer-logs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Shield.
Configure AWS WAF.
Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is the correct service because it protects web applications and APIs from common web exploits, including SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). Amazon API Gateway REST API stages can be associated directly with an AWS WAF web ACL, so no CloudFront distribution is required to meet this need. AWS Shield is intended for DDoS protection rather than application-layer filtering for SQLi and XSS, making AWS WAF the most operationally efficient solution here.

**Learn more:** [Use AWS WAF to protect your REST APIs in API Gateway - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html) · [AWS Decision guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/decision-guides/latest/waf-or-shield/waf-or-shield.pdf?did=wp_card)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team has deployed a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in a development VPC. A solutions architect must create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is `192.168.0.0/24`. The solutions architect must create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC.  
  
What is the **SMALLEST** CIDR block that meets these requirements?
questions.explanation:
An IPv4 CIDR block for an Amazon VPC must be between `/16` and `/28`, so a `/32` block cannot be used for a VPC. In addition, VPC peering requires that the requester and accepter VPC CIDR blocks do not overlap. Therefore, `192.168.0.0/24` is invalid because it overlaps the development VPC exactly, and both `/32` options are invalid VPC sizes. `10.0.1.0/24` is the only option that is both a valid VPC CIDR block and non-overlapping with `192.168.0.0/24`.

**Learn more:** [VPC CIDR blocks - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-cidr-blocks.html) · [How VPC peering connections work - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a new web application for its subscribers. The application will include a static single-page front end and a persistent database layer. It will have millions of users for 4 hours each morning, but only a few thousand users during the remainder of the day. The company's data architects have requested the ability to rapidly evolve the schema.  
  
Which solutions will satisfy these requirements and provide the **MOST** scalability? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Provision on-demand capacity.
Deploy Amazon Aurora as the database solution. Choose the serverless DB engine mode.
Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Ensure that DynamoDB auto scaling is enabled.
Deploy the static content into an Amazon S3 bucket. Provision an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin.

Deploy the web servers for static content across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. Configure the instances to periodically refresh the content from an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront is the standard highly scalable design for serving static web content, because S3 stores the static assets and CloudFront distributes them globally at edge locations. For the database tier, Amazon DynamoDB best matches the need to evolve the schema quickly because it is a NoSQL database with flexible data modeling, and its on-demand capacity mode automatically scales with traffic without capacity planning. AWS documentation specifically describes on-demand mode as the recommended option for workloads that can start small and scale to millions of requests per second, which aligns better with the sharp daily traffic surge than provisioned capacity with auto scaling or a relational Aurora deployment.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html) · [What is Amazon DynamoDB?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global company runs its workloads on AWS. The company's application uses Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions for sensitive data storage and analysis. The company stores millions of objects in multiple S3 buckets daily. The company wants to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up an AWS CloudTrail event that has a rule to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
Enable IAM Access Analyzer for S3 to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Storage Lens is the AWS feature that provides cross-Region visibility into S3 bucket configuration and data-protection metrics, including versioning status. AWS documentation states that you can use the **Versioning-enabled bucket count** metric to see which buckets have S3 Versioning enabled and then take action for the other buckets, which directly supports identifying buckets that are not versioning-enabled. CloudTrail tracks API events, IAM Access Analyzer for S3 analyzes bucket access exposure, and S3 Multi-Region Access Points are for routing requests to buckets in multiple Regions rather than auditing versioning settings.

**Learn more:** [Using S3 Storage Lens to protect your data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-lens-data-protection.html) · [Understanding Amazon S3 Storage Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_basics_metrics_recommendations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A group needs permission to list an Amazon S3 bucket and delete objects from that bucket. An administrator created the following IAM policy to grant access to the bucket and attached the policy to the group. The group cannot delete objects in the bucket. The company follows least-privilege access rules.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785599506648-m6n22x00.png)  
  
Which statement should a solutions architect add to the policy to fix bucket access?

options.text: ![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785599509185-c17j2lkd.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785599511441-gb1v0l2q.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785599513644-ispg4w3d.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785599516246-jqbieio7.png)

questions.explanation:
`s3:ListBucket` is a bucket-level permission and uses the bucket ARN, while `s3:DeleteObject` is an object-level permission and must use object ARNs. Granting only `s3:DeleteObject` for `arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*` permits deletion of objects in that specific bucket while maintaining least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Required permissions for Amazon S3 API operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-with-s3-policy-actions.html) · [DeleteObject API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteObject.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a website analytics application on a single Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instance. The analytics application is written in PHP and uses a MySQL database. The analytics software, the web server that serves PHP, and the database server are all running on the EC2 instance.  
  
The application is showing signs of performance degradation during busy periods and is returning 5xx errors. The company needs the application to scale seamlessly.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the load to each EC2 instance.

Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.

Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AWS Lambda function to stop the EC2 instance and change the instance type. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function when CPU utilization surpasses 75%.

Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Apply the AMI to a launch template. Create an Auto Scaling group with the launch template Configure the launch template to use a Spot Fleet. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
The most cost-effective way to make this workload scale seamlessly is to decouple the database from the web/application tier, move MySQL to Amazon RDS for MySQL, and place multiple EC2 web servers behind an Application Load Balancer. An ALB distributes incoming application traffic across multiple EC2 targets, which is the correct mechanism for horizontal web-tier scaling, while RDS removes database workload and operational burden from the instance hosting PHP. DNS weighted routing does not provide the same request-level load balancing behavior as an ALB, vertical resizing a single instance does not scale seamlessly, and relying solely on Spot capacity for a user-facing website can introduce interruption risk. 

**Learn more:** [What is an Application Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html) · [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html)

A company must export its database to Amazon S3 once each day so other teams can access it. The exported object size ranges from 2 GB to 5 GB. The S3 access pattern for this data is variable and changes quickly. The data must be available immediately and must stay accessible for as long as 3 months. The company needs the most cost-effective solution that does not increase retrieval time.  
  
Which S3 storage class should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the best fit for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns. It keeps objects immediately available with low-latency access while automatically moving them to the most cost-effective access tier as usage changes. That matches the requirement for rapidly variable access without increasing retrieval time. S3 Standard costs more for this pattern, S3 Standard-IA adds retrieval fees for infrequently accessed data, and S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is aimed at archival data accessed rarely, such as about once per quarter.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a three-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. The application uses a self-managed MySQL database on an EC2 instance, and it stores data on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The MySQL database currently uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volume. The company expects peak traffic to require 1,000 IOPS for reads and 1,000 IOPS for writes.  
  
The company wants to minimize disruptions, stabilize performance, and lower costs while keeping the ability to support double the IOPS. The company also wants to move the database tier to a fully managed solution that is highly available and fault tolerant.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with an io2 Block Express EBS volume.
Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with a General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume.
Use Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers.
Use two large EC2 instances to host the database in active-passive mode.

questions.explanation:
A Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance satisfies the need for a fully managed, highly available, fault-tolerant database service because Amazon RDS automatically maintains a synchronous standby replica in another Availability Zone and can fail over automatically. For storage, General Purpose SSD gp2 is the most cost-effective choice here because a 1 TB gp2 volume provides baseline IOPS proportional to size, which is enough to cover the required doubled capacity of about 2,000 IOPS without paying for Provisioned IOPS io2 storage. io2 is intended for more latency-sensitive, consistently high-I/O workloads and would add unnecessary cost for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS DB instance storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that collects data from IoT sensors on automobiles. The data is streamed to and stored in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. The data generates trillions of S3 objects each year. Every morning, the company uses data from the previous 30 days to retrain a suite of machine learning (ML) models.  
  
Four times per year, the company uses data from the previous 12 months to run analysis and train other ML models. The data must remain available with minimal delay for up to 1 year. After 1 year, the data must be retained for archival purposes.  
  
Which storage solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
Use the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.

Use the S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days, and then to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.

questions.explanation:
S3 Standard-IA is intended for data that must be retrieved immediately but is accessed less frequently than S3 Standard, making it a better cost fit for data that must stay available with minimal delay for up to 1 year. A lifecycle rule can then transition the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year for the lowest-cost archival storage. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is less cost-effective here because it is meant for unknown or changing access patterns and charges monitoring and automation fees per object, which is especially undesirable with trillions of objects. In addition, enabling Intelligent-Tiering archive tiers can move data into delayed-retrieval archive tiers before 1 year. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is appropriate only after the 1-year point because archived objects are not immediately accessible and require restore time.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html)

A hospital wants to create digital copies of its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will also keep adding hundreds of new documents every day. The hospital’s data team will scan the documents and upload them to the AWS Cloud.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.
Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.

Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 with Amazon Athena provides a highly scalable, serverless way to store data and run SQL queries directly on data in S3, avoiding operational overhead from managing databases on Amazon EC2. For the document-processing pipeline, AWS Lambda can run automatically when new files arrive, Amazon Textract can extract raw text from scanned documents, and Amazon Comprehend Medical can identify and extract medical entities from unstructured clinical text. This combination best satisfies the requirements for document analysis, medical information extraction, SQL querying, scalability, and operational efficiency.

A company runs an internal serverless application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company’s employees report problems with high latency when they start using the application each day. The company wants to reduce latency.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Increase the API Gateway throttling limit.
Set up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin to use the application each day.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to initiate a Lambda function as a target for the alarm at the beginning of each day.
Increase the Lambda function memory.

questions.explanation:
Lambda provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments pre-initialized so requests can be served immediately without the usual cold-start delay. For workloads with predictable daily usage, AWS recommends automating provisioned concurrency with scheduled scaling so capacity is increased before traffic begins. That directly addresses the recurring latency spike at the start of each day, unlike API Gateway throttling changes, ad hoc warming, or simply increasing function memory.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Lambda function scaling - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html) · [Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html)

A solutions architect must design a new microservice for a company's application. Clients need to be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to access the microservice. The microservice also must use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to authenticate calls. The solutions architect will implement the logic for this microservice by using a single AWS Lambda function written in Go 1.x.  
  
Which solution will deploy the function in the **MOST operationally efficient** way?

options.text: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.
Create a Lambda function URL for the function. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to Lambda@Edge. Integrate IAM authentication logic into the Lambda@Edge function.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda function URLs provide a dedicated HTTPS endpoint directly for a Lambda function, and they support `AWS_IAM` as the authentication type. That satisfies both the HTTPS-access and IAM-authentication requirements with the fewest managed components. An Amazon API Gateway REST API could also front the function and use IAM authorization, but it adds an additional service layer that is unnecessary for a single-function microservice when a Lambda function URL already meets the requirements more simply. CloudFront options do not provide a native `AWS_IAM` authentication type for this purpose, and Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions would be more operationally complex.

**Learn more:** [Control access to Lambda function URLs - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-auth.html) · [Creating and managing Lambda function URLs - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates demonstration environments for its customers on Amazon EC2 instances. Each environment is isolated within its own VPC.  
  
The company’s operations team must be notified when RDP or SSH connectivity to an environment has been established.

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights to create AWS Systems Manager OpsItems when RDP or SSH access is detected.
Configure the EC2 instances with an IAM instance profile that has an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy attached.
Publish VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create required metric filters. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm with a notification action for when the alarm is in the ALARM state.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to listen for events of type EC2 Instance State-change Notification. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the operations team to the topic.

questions.explanation:
Publishing VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs and then creating metric filters and a CloudWatch alarm is the correct approach because VPC Flow Logs record network traffic metadata, including accepted connections to specific ports such as TCP 22 for SSH and TCP 3389 for RDP. CloudWatch metric filters can count matching flow-log entries, and a CloudWatch alarm can trigger a notification action when such access occurs. By contrast, EC2 instance state-change events only indicate lifecycle transitions, Systems Manager instance-profile permissions only enable Systems Manager capabilities, and CloudWatch Application Insights is for detecting application and resource problems rather than remote-login events.

**Learn more:** [Process flow log records in CloudWatch Logs - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/process-records-cwl.html) · [Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores sensitive user data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to provide secure access to this bucket from the application tier that runs on Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to achieve this? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 within the VPC.
Create a bucket policy to make the objects in the S3 bucket public.
Create a bucket policy that limits access to only the application tier running in the VPC.
Create an IAM user with an S3 access policy and copy the IAM credentials to the EC2 instance.
Create a NAT instance and have the EC2 instances use the NAT instance to access the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoints let EC2 instances in a VPC access S3 privately without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device. S3 bucket policies can then restrict access so the bucket is reachable only from the specified VPC endpoint or VPC, which enforces that only the application tier inside the VPC can access the sensitive data. Public bucket access is insecure for this requirement, and using a NAT instance is unnecessary when an S3 gateway endpoint is available.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Controlling access from VPC endpoints with bucket policies - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies-vpc-endpoint.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a web-based portal that gives users global breaking news, local alerts, and weather updates. The portal presents each user with a personalized view by using a mixture of static and dynamic content. Content is delivered over HTTPS through an API server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company wants the portal to deliver this content to users around the world as quickly as possible.  
  
How should a solutions architect design the application to ensure the **LEAST** amount of latency for all users?

options.text: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve all static and dynamic content by specifying the ALB as an origin.
Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.
Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the static content. Serve the dynamic content directly from the ALB.
Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is intended to speed up delivery of both static and dynamic web content through globally distributed edge locations, and an Application Load Balancer can be configured as the CloudFront origin. For a worldwide application that mixes static assets with personalized dynamic responses, placing CloudFront in front of the ALB minimizes latency more effectively than routing users only to the nearest Region with Route 53. Route 53 latency-based routing can choose the lowest-latency Region among multiple deployments, while geolocation routing is based on user location rather than measured latency, but neither by itself provides CloudFront’s edge delivery and dynamic acceleration.

**Learn more:** [Amazon CloudFront Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/) · [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html)

A business application runs on Amazon EC2 and uses Amazon S3 for encrypted object storage. The chief information security officer has directed that no application traffic between the two services should traverse the public internet.  
  
Which capability should the solutions architect use to meet the compliance requirements?

options.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
VPC endpoint
Private subnet
Virtual private gateway

questions.explanation:
A VPC endpoint provides private connectivity from resources in a VPC to supported AWS services. For Amazon S3, a gateway VPC endpoint lets EC2 instances access S3 over the AWS network without needing an internet gateway or NAT device, which satisfies the requirement that the traffic not traverse the public internet. AWS KMS is only for key management, a private subnet does not by itself create private S3 access, and a virtual private gateway is used for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity rather than EC2-to-S3 private service access.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

An IAM user made several configuration changes to AWS resources in their company's account during a production deployment last week. A solutions architect learned that a couple of security group rules are not configured as desired. The solutions architect wants to confirm which IAM user was responsible for making changes.  
  
Which service should the solutions architect use to find the desired information?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail is the correct service because it logs AWS API activity and records who made a request, when it was made, and other event details. That makes it the service used to identify which IAM user changed security group rules. AWS Config can show that a resource configuration changed, but CloudTrail is the service used to attribute the change to a specific IAM identity.

**Learn more:** [CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events - AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-event-reference-record-contents.html) · [AWS Service Integrations with AWS Config - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/service-integrations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving its data-processing application to the AWS Cloud. The application runs several short-lived batch jobs that must not be interrupted. Data is produced after each batch job completes. The data is accessed for 30 days and retained for 2 years.  
  
The company wants to minimize the cost of operating the application in the AWS Cloud.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Instant. Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Move the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

Deploy Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

Deploy Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances are appropriate for batch jobs that cannot tolerate interruption, whereas Spot Instances can be interrupted by Amazon EC2. Amazon S3 Standard supports the initial 30-day access period, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive is AWS’s lowest-cost storage class for long-lived archival data. An S3 Lifecycle expiration rule can delete the data after two years.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html) · [Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes for long-term data storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs more than 300 websites and applications worldwide. The company needs a platform to analyze over 30 TB of clickstream data every day.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to transmit and process the clickstream data?

options.text: Design an AWS Data Pipeline to archive the data to an Amazon S3 bucket and run an Amazon EMR cluster with the data to generate analytics.
Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to process the data and send it to an Amazon S3 data lake for Amazon Redshift to use for analysis.
Cache the data to Amazon CloudFront. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. When an object is added to the S3 bucket. run an AWS Lambda function to process the data for analysis.
Collect the data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to transmit the data to an Amazon S3 data lake. Load the data in Amazon Redshift for analysis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is built to ingest and process large real-time data streams, and Amazon Data Firehose can take streaming data from a Kinesis data stream, deliver it to Amazon S3, and then load it into Amazon Redshift for analytics. That provides a managed, scalable pipeline for very high-volume clickstream collection and downstream analysis, which is the appropriate architecture for more than 30 TB per day.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html) · [What is Amazon Data Firehose?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During normal business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries take a long time to run. The company must eliminate the timeouts without stopping employees from performing queries.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS read replicas are intended to offload read-heavy activity from the primary DB instance. AWS documentation specifically identifies business reporting as a use case for directing reporting queries to a read replica instead of the production instance. Keeping order-processing transactions on the primary DB instance and moving reporting reads to a read replica reduces contention on the primary and prevents the reporting workload from causing order-processing timeouts.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Working with MySQL read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_MySQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer. The company stores the product’s objects in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems. The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the information on a dashboard.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.

questions.explanation:
Amazon GuardDuty is the AWS threat detection service that continuously monitors an AWS environment for suspicious and malicious activity by analyzing sources such as account activity and S3 data events, and it generates security findings when threats are detected. AWS Security Hub can ingest those findings and present them in a centralized dashboard, which satisfies the reporting and visibility requirement. Macie focuses on sensitive data discovery and S3 data security posture, Inspector focuses on vulnerability management, and AWS Config focuses on configuration compliance rather than malicious activity detection.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon GuardDuty?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html) · [GuardDuty S3 Protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/s3-protection.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a three-tier web application that processes customer orders. The web tier consists of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The processing tier consists of EC2 instances. The company has decoupled the web tier from the processing tier by using Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). The storage layer uses Amazon DynamoDB.  
  
At peak times, some users report delays and halls in order processing. The company has observed that, during these delays, the EC2 instances run at 100% CPU utilization and the SQS queue fills up. Peak times are variable and unpredictable.  
  
The company needs to improve application performance.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale out the processing tier instances for the duration of peak usage times. Use the CPU Utilization metric to determine when to scale.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of the DynamoDB backend tier. Use target utilization as a metric to determine when to scale.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache the responses for the web tier. Use HTTP latency as a metric to determine when to scale.
Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling target tracking policy to scale out the processing tier instances. Use the ApproximateNumberOfMessages attribute to determine when to scale.

questions.explanation:
A target tracking policy dynamically scales the EC2 processing fleet in response to demand. Queue depth, represented by the SQS `ApproximateNumberOfMessages` attribute, identifies accumulating order-processing work and triggers scale-out of the saturated consumers; this suits unpredictable peaks. AWS recommends deriving backlog per instance from the SQS message count for the most proportional target-tracking metric.

**Learn more:** [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html) · [Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a production workload that runs on 1,000 Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The workload is powered by third-party software. The company must patch the third-party software on all the EC2 instances as quickly as possible to remediate a critical security vulnerability.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Schedule an AWS Systems Manager maintenance window to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a custom command that applies the patch to all EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Run Command is the best fit because it can run a custom shell command or script across a fleet of managed EC2 instances at scale, which lets the company immediately execute the third-party software vendor’s patch procedure on all 1,000 Linux instances. Patch Manager automates patching for operating systems and has limited application patch support on Windows for Microsoft applications, so it is not the right choice for generic third-party software on Linux. A maintenance window is intended for scheduled operations within a defined window, not the fastest possible immediate remediation.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Run Command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/run-command.html)
