A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replicate to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
Use the pg_dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora supports migrating an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance by creating an Aurora read replica and then promoting that replica to a standalone Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. During this process, updates to the source RDS for PostgreSQL instance are asynchronously replicated to the Aurora read replica, which minimizes cutover downtime and reduces data loss compared with snapshot-based, S3 import, or pg_dump/restore methods. Because this is a built-in managed migration path, it also has the least operational overhead among the listed options.

**Learn more:** [Migrating data from an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster using an Aurora read replica](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Migrating.RDSPostgreSQL.Replica.html) · [Migrating data to Amazon Aurora with PostgreSQL compatibility](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Migrating.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an aging network-attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array provides SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations. The company does not want to buy a new NAS array. The company also does not want to pay to renew the NAS array's support contract. Some of the data is accessed often, but much of the data is inactive.  
  
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and preserves the same look and feel for the client workstations. The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution.  
  
Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?

options.text: Volume Gateway
Tape Gateway
Amazon FSx File Gateway
Amazon S3 File Gateway

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway is the AWS Storage Gateway option that presents standard SMB and NFS file shares to on-premises clients while storing the files as objects in Amazon S3. That matches the need to keep the same user experience for NAS clients and to use S3 Lifecycle policies for less-active data. Volume Gateway is iSCSI block storage, Tape Gateway is for virtual tapes, and Amazon FSx File Gateway is for access to FSx for Windows File Server rather than storing the data in Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect needs to migrate a Windows Internet Information Services (IIS) web application to AWS. The application currently depends on a file share hosted on the user's on-premises network-attached storage (NAS). The solutions architect has proposed migrating the IIS web servers to Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones that are connected to the storage solution, and configuring an Elastic Load Balancer that is attached to the instances.  
  
Which replacement for the on-premises file share is **MOST** resilient and durable?

options.text: Migrate the file share to Amazon RDS.
Migrate the file share to AWS Storage Gateway.
Migrate the file share to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
Migrate the file share to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the correct replacement because it provides a managed Windows-native SMB file share for EC2-based Windows workloads and supports Multi-AZ deployment for high availability across Availability Zones. AWS recommends Multi-AZ FSx for Windows File Server for most production workloads that require high availability to shared Windows file data, making it the most resilient and durable fit for an IIS application that relies on a shared Windows file share.

**Learn more:** [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html) · [What is FSx for Windows File Server? - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization contains multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each company application, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources as they are created.  
  
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that allows the development team to create resources only when the application name tag has an approved value.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations tag policies let you define permitted tag keys and allowed tag values across accounts in an organization. When enforcement is enabled for supported resource types, AWS can prevent noncompliant tagging operations, which satisfies the requirement that developers can create resources only if the application name tag uses an approved value. Resource Groups does not enforce creation-time controls, and the IAM-based alternatives do not provide the intended centralized Organizations-based tag-value governance for these accounts.

**Learn more:** [Enforce tagging consistency - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-enforcement.html) · [Tag policies - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an automobile sales website that stores its listings in a database on Amazon RDS.  
  
When an automobile is sold, the listing must be removed from the website, and the data must be sent to multiple target systems.  
  
Which design should a solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for the targets to consume.
Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue for the targets to consume.

Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.

Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS event notifications only cover administrative and operational events for a DB instance, cluster, snapshot, or parameter/security group; there is no RDS event category for row-level data changes such as a listing being deleted from a table, so a design built around subscribing to an RDS event notification cannot actually fire when a car is sold. The requirement can only be met by a mechanism that reacts to the data change itself, invoking a Lambda function that publishes the sold-listing information to an SQS queue for the downstream systems to consume; a standard queue is sufficient since strict message ordering across targets is not required.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Amazon RDS event notification](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Events.overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs and must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed.  
  
Which solution will achieve this goal with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Storage Lens advanced activity metrics are the built-in S3 feature for finding cold buckets by showing request and download activity over time. AWS documentation specifically states that advanced activity metrics can be used to understand how cold S3 buckets are and to identify buckets that are no longer accessed or only rarely accessed. This directly satisfies the requirement with less setup and maintenance than building Athena analysis on CloudWatch metrics or collecting and analyzing CloudTrail object-level logs.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon S3 Storage Lens to optimize your storage costs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-lens-optimize-storage.html?icmpid=docs_s3_user_guide_object-lifecycle-mgmt.html) · [Understanding Amazon S3 Storage Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_basics_metrics_recommendations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's web application that runs in the AWS Cloud has recently become more popular. The application currently runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance in one public subnet. The web application has been unable to handle the increased volume of web traffic.  
  
The company needs a solution that provides high availability and scalability to support the increased user demand without rewriting the web application.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger compute optimized instance.
Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with multiple Availability Zones in private subnets.
Configure a NAT gateway in a public subnet to handle web requests.
Replace the EC2 instance with a larger memory optimized instance.
Configure an Application Load Balancer in a public subnet to distribute web traffic.

questions.explanation:
High availability and horizontal scalability for a web application on AWS are achieved by placing an internet-facing Application Load Balancer in public subnets to distribute incoming requests and by configuring Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling across multiple Availability Zones so the application can scale out and remain available if an Availability Zone or instance fails. A NAT gateway is used for outbound internet access from private subnets, not to receive or balance inbound web traffic, and simply choosing a larger EC2 instance only increases single-instance capacity without providing fault tolerance. AWS documentation states that internet-facing load balancers must use public subnets, and Auto Scaling groups can span multiple Availability Zones to balance and replace capacity automatically.

**Learn more:** [Provide network connectivity for your Auto Scaling instances using Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-in-vpc.html) · [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's infrastructure includes hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. A solutions architect must make sure that each EC2 instance can be recovered after a disaster.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the **LEAST** amount of effort?

options.text: Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to launch new EC2 instances from the EBS storage.
Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to set the environment based on the EC2 template and attach the EBS storage.
Use AWS Backup to set up a backup plan for the entire group of EC2 instances. Use the AWS Backup API or the AWS CLI to speed up the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.

Create an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance and copy the Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Create another Lambda function to perform the restores with the copied AMIs and attach the EBS storage.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the lowest-effort way to protect and recover an EC2 fleet because it provides centralized backup plans for Amazon EC2 and supports restoring entire EC2 instances, including the AMI, instance configuration, and associated EBS root and data volumes. EBS snapshots by themselves protect volume data, but they do not provide the most operationally efficient full-instance recovery process for hundreds of instances. Elastic Beanstalk is not a backup-and-recovery service for existing EC2 fleets, and custom Lambda snapshot/AMI orchestration adds unnecessary implementation and maintenance overhead.

**Learn more:** [Restore an Amazon EC2 instance - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/restoring-ec2.html) · [Amazon EBS snapshots - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshots.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently completed a lift-and-shift migration of its on-premises Oracle database workload to an Amazon EC2 memory-optimized Linux instance. The EC2 Linux instance uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume with 64,000 IOPS.  
  
Database storage performance after the migration is slower than that of the on-premises database.  
  
Which solution will improve storage performance?

options.text: Add more Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volumes. Use OS commands to create a Logical Volume Management (LVM) stripe.
Increase the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to more than 64,000 IOPS.
Increase the size of the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to 2 TB.
Change the EC2 Linux instance to a storage optimized instance type. Do not change the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume.

questions.explanation:
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) volumes have a maximum of 64,000 provisioned IOPS per volume. Striping multiple io1 EBS volumes with LVM distributes I/O across the volumes and aggregates their provisioned IOPS and throughput, subject to the EC2 instance’s aggregate EBS-performance limit. AWS documents that instance EBS performance is limited by the lower of the instance limit and the combined performance of its attached volumes.

**Learn more:** [Get the maximum Amazon EBS optimized performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimization-performance.html) · [Amazon EBS-optimized instance types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an application that will run on a production Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster uses managed node groups that are provisioned with On-Demand Instances.  
  
The company requires a separate EKS cluster dedicated to development work. The company will use the development cluster only occasionally to test the application's resiliency. The EKS cluster must manage all of the nodes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Create a managed node group that contains only Spot Instances.
Create two managed node groups. Provision one node group with On-Demand Instances. Provision the second node group with Spot Instances.
Create an Auto Scaling group that has a launch configuration that uses Spot Instances. Configure the user data to add the nodes to the EKS cluster.
Create a managed node group that contains only On-Demand Instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS managed node groups let EKS provision and manage the worker nodes, satisfying the requirement that the cluster manage all nodes. AWS documentation also states that a managed node group can use Spot capacity, and that a managed node group contains only On-Demand instances or only Spot instances. Because the development cluster is used infrequently and for resiliency testing, Spot Instances provide the lowest-cost managed compute option. Using any On-Demand node group would add unnecessary cost, and using a separate Auto Scaling group with user data would be self-managed rather than EKS-managed.

**Learn more:** [Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/managed-node-groups.html) · [Create a managed node group for your cluster - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/create-managed-node-group.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a VPC architecture with multiple subnets. The architecture will host applications that use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The architecture consists of six subnets across two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone contains:  
  
- a public subnet  
- a private subnet  
- a dedicated subnet for databases  
  
Only EC2 instances running in the private subnets can access the RDS databases.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a new route table that excludes the route to the public subnets' CIDR blocks. Associate the route table with the database subnets.
Create a security group that denies inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the public subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
Create a security group that allows inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
Create a new peering connection between the public subnets and the private subnets. Create a different peering connection between the private subnets and the database subnets.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS access inside a VPC is controlled with VPC security groups. The correct approach is to attach a security group to the DB instances that permits inbound database traffic from the security group assigned to the EC2 instances in the private subnets. That limits database access to only those private-tier instances. Route tables do not selectively prevent communication between subnets in the same VPC in this way because the VPC has local routing, security groups do not support explicit deny rules, and VPC peering is used between separate VPCs rather than between subnets in one VPC.

**Learn more:** [Controlling access with security groups - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.RDSSecurityGroups.html) · [Subnet route tables - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/subnet-route-tables.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its application on AWS and uses an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as its database. During peak-usage periods, when multiple users access and read data, monitoring shows degraded database performance for write queries. The company wants to improve application scalability to meet peak-usage demand.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create a second Aurora DB cluster. Configure a copy job to replicate the users’ data to the new database. Update the application to use the second database to read the data.

Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the DAX cluster for read-only queries. Write data directly to the Aurora DB cluster.
Create an Aurora read replica in the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the replica endpoint for read-only queries and to use the cluster endpoint for write queries.
Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Copy the users' data to the Redshift cluster. Update the application to connect to the Redshift cluster and to perform read-only queries on the Redshift cluster.

questions.explanation:
Aurora Replicas provide read scaling by handling read-only queries separately from the primary writer instance. Directing read-only traffic to the replica endpoint reduces load on the writer, allowing the cluster endpoint to continue handling write queries. AWS documents that Aurora reader endpoints distribute read-only connections across Aurora Replicas, while the cluster endpoint connects to the primary instance for writes.

**Learn more:** [Replication with Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html) · [Cluster endpoints for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Cluster.html)

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudFront in front of the website to use HTTPS functionality.
Deploy an AWS WAF web ACL in front of the website to provide HTTPS functionality.
Create and deploy an AWS Lambda function to manage and serve the website content.
Create the new website and an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the website on the S3 bucket with static website hosting enabled.
Create the new website. Deploy the website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

questions.explanation:
A static website hosted in Amazon S3 minimizes operational overhead because there are no servers or CMS platforms to patch or maintain, and S3 provides highly scalable object storage for static content. Amazon CloudFront is the correct companion service for enhanced security and HTTPS delivery in front of an S3-hosted static site; AWS documentation explicitly states that if you want HTTPS for a static website hosted on Amazon S3, you can use CloudFront. AWS WAF can add request filtering protection, but it does not itself provide HTTPS functionality, and EC2 or Lambda-based approaches introduce more management overhead than necessary for a static site.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Configuring a static website on Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/HostingWebsiteOnS3Setup.html) · [Enabling website hosting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EnableWebsiteHosting.html)

A company runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are part of an Auto Scaling group that scales based on user demand. The company wants to maximize cost savings without entering into a long-term commitment.  
  
Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Dedicated Instances only
On-Demand Instances only
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances

questions.explanation:
For an Auto Scaling workload, combining On-Demand Instances with Spot Instances provides elasticity and better cost savings without a long-term commitment. On-Demand capacity can cover the steady baseline, while Spot Instances can supply lower-cost scalable capacity for variable demand. AWS documentation states that On-Demand Instances require no long-term commitment, Spot Instances can significantly reduce costs, and Auto Scaling groups can use both purchase options together. Reserved Instances are not the best fit here because they require a 1-year or 3-year commitment.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html) · [Choosing a purchasing option for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/decision-guides/latest/ec2-purchasing-options-aws-how-to-choose/ec2-purchasing-options-aws-how-to-choose.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its application in the AWS Cloud. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group, along with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to make sure the application can be made available in another AWS Region with minimal downtime.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the **LEAST** downtime?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group and a load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, load balancers, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when needed Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and a load balancer to be launched when needed. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

Create an Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to trigger an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 pointing to the disaster recovery load balancer.

questions.explanation:
A warm standby deployment in the disaster recovery Region minimizes recovery time because the load balancer and Auto Scaling group already exist and can serve traffic after failover. Amazon DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions, so the database is already available in the secondary Region instead of needing restoration or creation during the event. Amazon Route 53 DNS failover is the native mechanism to route users to the healthy regional load balancer when the primary Region is unavailable. This combination provides lower downtime than launching infrastructure only after failure and is simpler and more appropriate than building custom failover automation.

**Learn more:** [Disaster recovery options in the cloud - Disaster Recovery of Workloads on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html) · [Disaster Recovery (DR) Architecture on AWS, Part III: Pilot Light and Warm Standby](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/disaster-recovery-dr-architecture-on-aws-part-iii-pilot-light-and-warm-standby/)

A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its corporate data center to its VPC in the `us-east-1` Region. The company recently acquired a corporation that has several VPCs and a Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and the `eu-west-2` Region. The CIDR blocks for the VPCs of the company and the corporation do not overlap. The company requires connectivity between the two Regions and the data centers. The company needs a solution that is scalable while reducing operational overhead.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up inter-Region VPC peering between the VPC in us-east-1 and the VPCs in eu-west-2.
Create private virtual interfaces from the Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 to the VPCs in eu-west-2.
Establish VPN appliances in a fully meshed VPN network hosted by Amazon EC2. Use AWS VPN CloudHub to send and receive data between the data centers and each VPC.
Connect the existing Direct Connect connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Route traffic from the virtual private gateways of the VPCs in each Region to the Direct Connect gateway.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Direct Connect gateway allows a Direct Connect connection to be associated with virtual private gateways for VPCs in multiple Regions, providing private connectivity between on-premises environments and multiple VPCs with less management overhead than building a mesh of VPN appliances. This is the scalable design for multi-Region Direct Connect connectivity. A private virtual interface alone is for connecting to a VPC in the same Region unless it is attached through a Direct Connect gateway, and inter-Region VPC peering does not by itself provide the required integrated data-center-to-VPC connectivity model.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways.html) · [Direct Connect gateways introduction - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to handle credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and must process each request at least once.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda with an Amazon SQS event source mapping is appropriate for asynchronous processing, and AWS states that SQS event source mappings process each event at least once. Because the requirement does not call for message ordering or deduplication guarantees, an SQS standard queue is more cost-effective than a FIFO queue. For an SQS queue encrypted with SSE-KMS, the Lambda execution role needs permission to decrypt with the KMS key, so the valid configuration among the choices is the one using a standard queue with SSE-KMS and `kms:Decrypt` on the execution role.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [How Lambda processes records from stream and queue-based event sources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-eventsourcemapping.html)

A company requires a secure connection between its on-premises environment and AWS. This connection does not require high bandwidth and will carry only a small amount of traffic. The connection must be established quickly.  
  
What is the **MOST cost-effective** way to establish this type of connection?

options.text: Implement a client VPN.
Implement AWS Direct Connect.
Implement a bastion host on Amazon EC2.
Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN is the correct choice because it provides an IPsec-encrypted connection between an on-premises network and AWS, can be created quickly, and is typically more cost-effective than AWS Direct Connect for low-bandwidth, low-traffic connectivity. Direct Connect is a dedicated private link better suited to higher or more consistent bandwidth requirements and usually involves additional provisioning time and cost. Client VPN is for remote user devices rather than site-to-site network connectivity, and a bastion host does not create a private connection between on-premises and AWS. Official AWS documentation describes Site-to-Site VPN as the connection between a VPC and an on-premises network, while Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection. AWS official guidance also notes that Site-to-Site VPN can be the more cost-effective option for lower bandwidth requirements.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html) · [What is Direct Connect?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

A company stores several petabytes of data across multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Lake Formation to manage its data lake. The company's data science team wants to securely share selective data from its accounts with the company's engineering team for analytical purposes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Copy the required data to a common account. Create an IAM access role in that account. Grant access by specifying a permission policy that includes users from the engineering team accounts as trusted entities.
Use the Lake Formation permissions Grant command in each account where the data is stored to allow the required engineering team users to access the data.
Use AWS Data Exchange to privately publish the required data to the required engineering team accounts.
Use Lake Formation tag-based access control to authorize and grant cross-account permissions for the required data to the engineering team accounts.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lake Formation natively supports cross-account sharing of Data Catalog resources, and LF-Tag-based access control is the recommended approach when many databases, tables, or columns must be governed because permissions are granted by attributes instead of managing many individual resource grants. Tagging only the required data and granting cross-account access to the engineering accounts provides selective sharing with fine-grained control and lower administrative effort than copying data or issuing separate grants in each account.

**Learn more:** [Lake Formation tag-based access control - AWS Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/tag-based-access-control.html) · [Data sharing using tag-based access control - AWS Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_us/lake-formation/latest/dg/cross-account-TBAC.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a web-based application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. The web application will provide access to a repository of text documents totaling about 900 TB in size. The company expects the web application to have periods of high demand.  
  
A solutions architect must make sure that the storage component for the text documents can scale to meet the application's demand at all times. The company is concerned about the overall cost of the solution.  
  
Which storage solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
Amazon S3

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the correct choice because it is AWS object storage built to store and retrieve any amount of data and is designed for massive scale, high durability, and web access. For a 900 TB document repository serving a web application, S3 provides essentially unlimited scale and is typically far more cost-effective than provisioning shared file storage with Amazon EFS. Amazon EBS is block storage for individual instance attachment and does not fit a large shared multi-Availability-Zone document repository, and Amazon OpenSearch Service is for indexing and search rather than primary bulk document storage.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/) · [Amazon Simple Storage Service Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/s3/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical records company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes customer data files stored in Amazon S3. The EC2 instances are deployed in public subnets. The EC2 instances currently access Amazon S3 over the internet, and they do not need any other network access.  
  
A new requirement states that network traffic for file transfers must use a private path and must not traverse the internet.  
  
Which change to the network architecture should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the public subnets to send traffic to Amazon S3 through the NAT gateway.
Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to restrict outbound traffic so that only traffic to the S3 prefix list is permitted.
Move the EC2 instances to private subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, and link the endpoint to the route table for the private subnets.
Remove the internet gateway from the VPC. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection, and route traffic to Amazon S3 over the Direct Connect connection.

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 allows EC2 instances in private subnets to access S3 without traversing the internet. The route table directs S3-destined traffic to the VPC endpoint, keeping it on the AWS network. Moving EC2 instances to private subnets and creating a VPC endpoint for S3 meets the requirement for private file transfer without internet access. NAT gateways still route traffic through the internet gateway.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company generates operations data and stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. For the company’s annual audit, an external consultant needs access to an annual report that is stored in the S3 bucket. The external consultant must be able to access the report for 7 days.  
  
The company must implement a solution that allows the external consultant to access **only** the report.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket that is configured to host a public static website. Migrate the operations data to the new S3 bucket. Share the S3 website URL with the external consultant.
Enable public access to the S3 bucket for 7 days. Remove access to the S3 bucket when the external consultant completes the audit.
Create a new IAM user that has access to the report in the S3 bucket. Provide the access keys to the external consultant. Revoke the access keys after 7 days.
Generate a presigned URL that has the required access to the location of the report on the S3 bucket. Share the presigned URL with the external consultant.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 presigned URL provides temporary access to a specific S3 object without requiring the bucket to be made public or an IAM user to be created for the external party. This matches the requirement to allow access only to the report, and AWS states that a presigned URL created with the AWS CLI or SDK can be valid for as long as 7 days. That makes it the most operationally efficient and least permissive option.

**Learn more:** [Download and upload objects with presigned URLs - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html) · [Sharing objects with presigned URLs - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs containers in a Kubernetes environment in the company's local data center. The company wants to use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and other AWS managed services. Data must remain locally in the company's data center and cannot be stored in any remote site or cloud to maintain compliance.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy AWS Local Zones in the company's data center.
Use an AWS Snowmobile in the company's data center.
Install an AWS Outposts rack in the company's data center.
Install an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized node in the data center.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Outposts rack extends AWS-managed infrastructure and services into the company’s own data center, allowing workloads and storage to remain on premises while using Amazon EKS and other AWS managed services. This directly fits a compliance requirement for local data residency. Local Zones are extensions of an AWS Region rather than equipment installed in the customer’s facility, Snowmobile is a bulk data transfer service, and Snowball Edge is primarily an edge/data-transfer device that supports EKS Anywhere rather than the managed Amazon EKS deployment model required here.

**Learn more:** [Deploy Amazon EKS on-premises with AWS Outposts - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-outposts.html) · [What is AWS Outposts? - AWS Outposts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/what-is-outposts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a business-critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants the application to be highly available with minimum downtime and minimum data loss.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Place the EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks to redirect traffic. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Cross-Region Replication.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to use one Availability Zone. Generate hourly snapshots of the database. Recover the database from the snapshots in the event of a failure.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple AWS Regions. Write the data from the application to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to launch an AWS Lambda function to write the data to the database.

questions.explanation:
The lowest-effort way to achieve high availability with minimal downtime and minimal data loss is to run the Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones and use a Multi-AZ database deployment. EC2 Auto Scaling balances instances across enabled Availability Zones and can replace capacity in a healthy zone if one zone fails. A Multi-AZ Aurora/RDS deployment provides standby failover for the database, which is far better for availability and data protection than hourly snapshots or custom cross-Region designs. Amazon RDS Proxy further improves application availability during failover by preserving application connections and automatically reconnecting to the standby database instance.

**Learn more:** [Add an Availability Zone - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html) · [Amazon RDS Proxy - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to present the application's frontend to users. The REST APIs must access backend services that the company hosts in containers in private VPC subnets.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway REST APIs can integrate with backend services running privately in a VPC by using a private integration through a VPC link. AWS documentation shows REST APIs using VPC links to reach Amazon ECS services hosted in private subnets, which fits a containerized microservices backend. WebSocket APIs do not satisfy the stated REST requirement, and a security group alone is not the API Gateway private-integration method for connecting to private ECS backends.

**Learn more:** [Private integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/private-integration.html) · [Tutorial: Create a REST API with a private integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/getting-started-with-private-integration.html)

A research laboratory must process approximately 8 TB of data. The storage subsystem must provide sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances running Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.  
  
Which solution will meet the performance requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre with persistent SSD storage is purpose-built for distributed, high-performance computing workloads that use many Linux-based compute instances in parallel. AWS documentation states that FSx for Lustre provides consistent sub-millisecond latencies for file operations, and the SSD storage class is optimized for workloads that need low latency and very high throughput. It also integrates directly with Amazon S3 so the dataset can be imported from and exported to S3 while being mounted concurrently by the EC2 fleet. HDD-based Lustre does not satisfy the low-latency requirement for the full dataset, and FSx for ONTAP option A is disqualified because the ALL tiering policy moves cold data to capacity pool storage that has much higher latency.

**Learn more:** [Performance characteristics of SSD and HDD storage classes - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/ssd-storage.html) · [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre? - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)

A company wants to migrate an application to AWS. The company wants to improve the application's current availability. The company also wants to use AWS WAF in the application's architecture.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the ALB.

Create a cluster placement group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that hosts the application. Configure an Application Load Balancer and set the EC2 instances as the targets. Connect a WAF to the placement group.
Create two Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure the EC2 instances as the targets of an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Connect a WAF to the ALB.

Create an Auto Scaling group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
The correct design is to place the application on multiple EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spanning two Availability Zones and send traffic through an Application Load Balancer. This increases availability by distributing traffic across healthy instances in multiple AZs and allowing failed instances to be replaced automatically. AWS WAF web ACLs can be associated with an Application Load Balancer, not with an Auto Scaling group or a placement group. AWS also integrates Auto Scaling groups with ALB target groups so instances launched by the group are registered automatically.

**Learn more:** [Target groups for your Application Load Balancers - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html) · [Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute incoming application traffic in your Auto Scaling group - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.html)

A company has deployed a Java Spring Boot application as a pod that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in private subnets. The application needs to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. A solutions architect must ensure that the application can interact with the DynamoDB table without exposing traffic to the internet.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
Attach an IAM user that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
Allow outbound connectivity to the DynamoDB table through the private subnets’ network ACLs.
Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
Embed the access keys in the Java Spring Boot code.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS workloads should use an IAM role associated with the Kubernetes service account so the pod receives temporary AWS credentials with only the required DynamoDB permissions, instead of using long-term IAM user credentials or embedded access keys. To keep access private from subnets that do not use the internet, Amazon DynamoDB should be reached through a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, which provides private connectivity from the VPC without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device.

**Learn more:** [IAM roles for service accounts - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html) · [Assign IAM roles to Kubernetes service accounts - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/associate-service-account-role.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a small Python application that processes JSON documents and writes the results to an on-premises SQL database. The application runs thousands of times per day. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a highly available solution that maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the Python code on multiple Amazon EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs the Python code to process the documents as they arrive in the S3 bucket. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use the EBS Multi-Attach feature to attach the volume to multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Run the Python code on the EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.

Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as messages. Deploy the Python code as a container on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that is configured with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Use the container to process the SQS messages. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon S3 for the JSON documents and invoking AWS Lambda when objects arrive provides a serverless, event-driven architecture that scales automatically for thousands of executions per day without requiring server management. Amazon S3 event notifications can trigger Lambda processing for new objects, which minimizes operational overhead compared with managing EC2 instances or ECS on EC2. Storing the processed results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster satisfies the high-availability requirement because Aurora replicates data across multiple Availability Zones and supports automatic failover.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Event Notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html) · [High availability for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html)

A company uses a SQL database to store publicly accessible movie data. The database runs on an Amazon RDS Single-AZ DB instance. A script runs queries at random times each day to record how many new movies have been added to the database. The script must report a final total during business hours.  
  
The company's development team notices that database performance is insufficient for development tasks while the script is running. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to resolve this issue.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica.
Instruct the development team to manually export the entries in the database at the end of each day.
Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS read replica is the correct solution because read replicas are intended to offload read-intensive workloads from the primary DB instance. By directing the script's read queries to the replica, the company reduces contention on the source database and improves performance for development work while keeping the process managed by Amazon RDS. A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not help because its standby replica is for high availability and failover, not for serving read traffic.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has stored **10 TB of log files** in **Apache Parquet** format in an **Amazon S3 bucket**. The company occasionally needs to use **SQL** to analyze the log files.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Migrate the data from the S3 bucket into Aurora by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Issue SQL statements to the Aurora database.
Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use Redshift Spectrum to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
Create an AWS Glue crawler to store and retrieve table metadata from the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Use Apache Spark SQL to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is designed to run standard SQL queries directly against data stored in Amazon S3, including Apache Parquet files, and it uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog for table metadata. Because Athena is serverless and priced per query based on data scanned, it is typically the most cost-effective choice for occasional analysis of data already stored in S3. Redshift Spectrum can also query S3 data, but it requires Redshift infrastructure; Aurora requires loading the data into a database first; and EMR requires managing cluster compute, all of which add unnecessary cost for infrequent SQL access.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Athena - Big Data Analytics Options on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/big-data-analytics-options/amazon-athena.html) · [Service Quotas - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/service-limits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a mobile app for customers. The app's data is sensitive and must be encrypted at rest. The company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).  
  
The company needs a solution that prevents accidental deletion of KMS keys. The solution must use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send an email notification to administrators when a user attempts to delete a KMS key.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Configure an AWS Config rule that cancels any deletion of a KMS key. Add the AWS Config rule as a target of the EventBridge rule. Create an SNS topic that notifies the administrators.

Create an AWS Lambda function that has custom logic to prevent KMS key deletion. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is activated when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function when the DeleteKey operation is performed. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed. Configure the rule to initiate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure the runbook to cancel the deletion of the KMS key. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.

Create an AWS CloudTrail trail. Configure the trail to deliver logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the metric filter for the CloudWatch log group. Configure the alarm to use Amazon SNS to notify the administrators when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed.

questions.explanation:
AWS KMS key removal is scheduled first, not deleted immediately, and AWS KMS supports canceling that scheduled deletion during the waiting period. Amazon EventBridge can match the KMS deletion-scheduling API call delivered through CloudTrail, and a Systems Manager Automation runbook can automatically invoke `CancelKeyDeletion`. AWS provides the managed `AWSConfigRemediation-CancelKeyDeletion` runbook for this purpose, which avoids custom code and therefore has less operational overhead than Lambda. The same EventBridge rule can also publish to an Amazon SNS topic so administrators receive email notification.

**Learn more:** [Delete an AWS KMS key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/deleting-keys.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

A company runs a real-time data ingestion solution on AWS. The solution uses the latest version of Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). The solution is deployed in a VPC in private subnets across three Availability Zones.  
  
A solutions architect must redesign the data ingestion solution so that it is publicly accessible over the internet. Data in transit must also be encrypted.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Configure public subnets in the existing VPC. Deploy an MSK cluster in the public subnets. Update the MSK cluster security settings to enable mutual TLS authentication.
Create a new VPC that has public subnets. Deploy an MSK cluster in the public subnets. Update the MSK cluster security settings to enable mutual TLS authentication.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that uses private subnets. Configure an ALB security group inbound rule to allow inbound traffic from the VPC CIDR block for HTTPS protocol.
Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) that uses private subnets. Configure an NLB listener for HTTPS communication over the internet.

questions.explanation:
Amazon MSK supports public accessibility through cluster-level settings and encryption configuration without requiring brokers to be moved into public subnets or load balancers. Configuring public subnets, deploying MSK brokers there, and enabling mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication provides encrypted internet-facing connectivity with minimal operational overhead. Load balancers add complexity; Kafka manages its own internal load balancing.

**Learn more:** [Turn on public access to an MSK cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/public-access.html) · [Mutual TLS authentication for Amazon MSK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/msk-authentication.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a two-tier web application in a VPC. The web tier uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in public subnets that span multiple Availability Zones. The database tier consists of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in separate private subnets. The web tier needs access to the database to retrieve product information.  
  
The web application is not working as intended. It reports that it cannot connect to the database. The database is confirmed to be up and running. All configurations for the network ACLs, security groups, and route tables remain in their default states.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to fix the application?

options.text: Add an explicit rule to the private subnet’s network ACL to allow traffic from the web tier’s EC2 instances.
Add a route in the VPC route table to allow traffic between the web tier’s EC2 instances and the database tier.
Deploy the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier’s RDS instance into two separate VPCs, and configure VPC peering.
Add an inbound rule to the security group of the database tier’s RDS instance to allow traffic from the web tiers security group.

questions.explanation:
Resources in different subnets within the same VPC can already communicate through the VPC’s local route, so no additional route is required. The default network ACL also allows inbound and outbound traffic, so it is not preventing connectivity. The missing requirement is database access in the RDS instance’s security group: Amazon RDS must allow inbound MySQL traffic from the web tier, typically by referencing the web tier’s security group as the source. That permits only the application servers to connect to the database. Official AWS documentation also distinguishes default network ACL behavior from security-group-based instance access control.

**Learn more:** [Default network ACL for a VPC - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-network-acl.html) · [Subnets for your VPC - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/configure-subnets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to satisfy requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to concentrate on maintaining the critical applications. The company does not want to be responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that runs the containerized workload.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate is the correct choice because Fargate provides serverless compute for containers, so the company can run containerized applications without provisioning or managing the underlying EC2 infrastructure. That directly matches the requirement to focus on the applications themselves while still using a scalable and highly available container platform.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Elastic Container Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/Welcome.html) · [Amazon ECS launch types and capacity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-launch-type-comparison.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a cloud-based application on AWS that will process sensitive customer data. The application uses Amazon RDS for its database, Amazon S3 for object storage, and S3 Event Notifications that invoke AWS Lambda for serverless processing.  
  
The company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to manage user credentials. The development, testing, and operations teams require secure access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3 while preserving the confidentiality of sensitive customer data. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which solution fulfills these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use IAM roles with least privilege to grant all the teams access. Assign IAM roles to each team with customized IAM policies defining specific permission for Amazon RDS and S3 object access based on team responsibilities.

Enable IAM Identity Center with an Identity Center directory. Create and configure permission sets with granular access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3. Assign all the teams to groups that have specific access with the permission sets.

Create individual IAM users for each member in all the teams with role-based permissions. Assign the IAM roles with predefined policies for RDS and S3 access to each user based on user needs. Implement IAM Access Analyzer for periodic credential evaluation.

Use AWS Organizations to create separate accounts for each team. Implement cross-account IAM roles with least privilege. Grant specific permission for RDS and S3 access based on team roles and responsibilities.

questions.explanation:
IAM Identity Center permission sets define granular permissions for users and groups, and group assignments simplify access administration as team membership changes. Permission sets can apply least-privilege IAM policies for the required RDS and S3 actions, while IAM Identity Center centrally provisions and manages the corresponding account roles.

**Learn more:** [Manage AWS accounts with permission sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/permissionsetsconcept.html) · [Assign user or group access to AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/assignusers.html)

A company's applications use Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark to process data on premises. The current infrastructure is not scalable and is difficult to manage.  
  
A solutions architect needs to design a scalable solution that reduces operational complexity. The solution must keep the data processing on premises.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to access the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data and application. Use an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
Use AWS DataSync to connect to the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) cluster. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
Migrate the Apache Hadoop application and the Apache Spark application to Amazon EMR clusters on AWS Outposts. Use the EMR clusters to process the data.
Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EMR provides a managed platform for Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark, which reduces the operational burden compared with self-managed on-premises clusters. AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and services into an on-premises facility, and Amazon EMR on Outposts is intended for workloads that need to run in close proximity to on-premises data and applications. That combination preserves on-premises processing while improving scalability and manageability.

**Learn more:** [EMR clusters on AWS Outposts - Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-outposts.html) · [What is AWS Outposts? - AWS Outposts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/what-is-outposts.html)

options.text: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.
Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.
Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.
Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.

questions.explanation:
For a stateful production workload that must keep at least two instances running, the Auto Scaling group should have a **minimum capacity of two** so Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling maintains that baseline. To provide **high availability and fault tolerance**, the instances should be distributed across **two Availability Zones**, because Auto Scaling balances instances across enabled AZs and can launch replacement instances in another healthy AZ if one AZ becomes unhealthy. **On-Demand Instances** are the appropriate purchase option here because Spot Instances can be interrupted and are therefore a poor fit for a stateful production application with an always-on minimum-capacity requirement. Official AWS documentation also notes that Auto Scaling maintains the minimum group size, balances instances across Availability Zones, and that Spot is suited to flexible/interruption-tolerant workloads rather than this kind of requirement.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html) · [Set scaling limits for your Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-capacity-limits.html)

A company wants to redesign a large-scale web application into a serverless microservices architecture. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and is written in Python.  
  
The company has chosen one component of the web application to test as a microservice. This component handles hundreds of requests per second. The company wants to build and test the microservice on an AWS solution that supports Python. The solution must also scale automatically and require minimal infrastructure and minimal operational support.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use a Spot Fleet with auto scaling of EC2 instances that run the most recent Amazon Linux operating system.
Use an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server environment that has high availability configured.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Launch Auto Scaling groups of self-managed EC2 instances.
Use an AWS Lambda function that runs custom developed code.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the best fit because it is a serverless compute service that natively supports Python, runs custom code without requiring server management, and scales automatically in response to request volume. That aligns directly with the need for a Python-based microservice that handles hundreds of requests per second while minimizing infrastructure and operational effort. By contrast, EC2-based fleets, Elastic Beanstalk environments, and self-managed Amazon EKS worker nodes all require more infrastructure administration.

**Learn more:** [Building Lambda functions with Python](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-python.html) · [Microservices with AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/serverless-multi-tier-architectures-api-gateway-lambda/microservices-with-lambda.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global company runs its web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application contains static data and dynamic data. The company stores the static data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to improve performance and reduce latency for both the static data and the dynamic data. The company uses its own domain name that is registered with Amazon Route 53.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket and the ALB as origins. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the ALB and the CloudFront distribution as endpoints. Create a custom domain name that points to the accelerator DNS name. Use the custom domain name as an endpoint for the web application.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint. Create two domain names. Point one domain name to the CloudFront DNS name for dynamic content. Point the other domain name to the accelerator DNS name for static content. Use the domain names as endpoints for the web application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront can use multiple origins in a single distribution, including an Amazon S3 bucket and an Application Load Balancer, and route requests to the appropriate origin by cache behavior. This lets static content be cached at edge locations while dynamic requests are forwarded to the ALB with lower latency through the CloudFront global network. Route 53 can point the application’s domain name to the CloudFront distribution. AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators do not support Amazon S3 buckets or CloudFront distributions as endpoints, so the alternatives that depend on those endpoint types are not valid.

**Learn more:** [Use various origins with CloudFront distributions - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistS3AndCustomOrigins.html) · [Origin - Amazon CloudFront API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_Origin.html)

A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to store and retrieve data in Amazon S3 buckets. According to regulatory requirements, the data must not travel across the public internet.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Deploy a NAT gateway to access the S3 buckets.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway to access the S3 buckets.
Deploy an S3 interface endpoint to access the S3 buckets.
Deploy an S3 gateway endpoint to access the S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint lets instances in a VPC access S3 privately without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device, so the traffic does not traverse the public internet. For EC2 instances in private subnets, this is the most cost-effective option because AWS documents that S3 gateway endpoints have no additional charge, whereas S3 interface endpoints use PrivateLink pricing and NAT gateways also add cost.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)
