lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company runs its analytics application in the AWS Cloud. The application produces about 300 MB of data each month, and the data is stored in JSON format. The company is assessing a disaster recovery solution to back up this data. The data must be available within milliseconds when needed, and it must be retained for 30 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
Amazon S3 Glacier
Amazon S3 Standard
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Standard is the best fit because it provides millisecond access and has no minimum storage duration charge, which aligns well with keeping a small backup set for 30 days. Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is designed for archive and disaster recovery data but requires a restore operation and retrieval commonly takes minutes to hours, so it does not meet the millisecond-access requirement. OpenSearch Service and RDS for PostgreSQL are significantly more expensive and are not appropriate as simple backup storage for small JSON files. AWS documentation identifies S3 Standard as suitable for frequently accessed data with millisecond access, while Glacier Flexible Retrieval is not available for real-time access.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes for long-term data storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)

A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes `etcd` key-value store.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.
Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.
Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.
Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS meets this requirement by using AWS KMS envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets in `etcd`. AWS documents that enabling Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption causes Kubernetes secrets to be encrypted with the selected KMS key, and the EKS API supports an `EncryptionConfig` whose supported resource is `secrets`. EBS volume encryption or the EBS CSI driver protects block storage, not Kubernetes secrets in `etcd`, and AWS Secrets Manager is an external secrets service rather than the mechanism that encrypts Kubernetes secrets stored by EKS itself.

**Learn more:** [Encrypt Kubernetes secrets with KMS on existing clusters - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-kms.html) · [Data encryption and secrets management - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)

A company runs applications in an organization that uses AWS Organizations. The company outsources operational support for the applications and must provide the external support engineers with access without compromising security.  
  
The external support engineers require access to the AWS Management Console. They also require operating-system access to the company’s fleet of Amazon EC2 instances running Amazon Linux in private subnets.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST** securely?

options.text: Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use AWS IAM Identity Center to provide the external support engineers console access. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to assign the required permissions.

Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to provide local IAM user credentials in each AWS account to the external support engineers for console access.

Confirm that all instances have a security group that allows SSH access only from the external support engineers’ source IP address ranges. Provide local IAM user credentials in each AWS account to the external support engineers for console access. Provide each external support engineer an SSH key pair to log in to the application instances.

Create a bastion host in a public subnet. Set up the bastion host security group to allow access from only the external engineers’ IP address ranges. Ensure that all instances have a security group that allows SSH access from the bastion host. Provide each external support engineer an SSH key pair to log in to the application instances. Provide local account IAM user credentials to the engineers for console access.

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce access to AWS accounts in an organization, avoiding separate long-lived IAM users in each account. Systems Manager Session Manager uses IAM permissions and the SSM Agent/instance role to provide interactive access to managed EC2 instances, including private-subnet instances, without opening inbound SSH ports, distributing SSH keys, or maintaining bastion hosts.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html) · [Use Systems Manager instead of SSH or RDP](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/aws-startup-security-baseline/wkld-06.html)

A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who can access it.  
  
Some of the company’s users use a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some other users cannot change the hardcoded URLs they use for access.  
  
Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the **least impact to the users**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Signed cookies
Signed URLs
AWS AppSync
JSON Web Token (JWT)
AWS Secrets Manager

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront supports two native mechanisms for restricting access to private content: signed URLs and signed cookies. Signed URLs are appropriate when clients cannot use cookies, because the authorization information is embedded in the URL itself. Signed cookies are appropriate when users must continue using unchanged or hardcoded resource URLs, because access control is carried in cookies rather than by modifying each URL. Using both methods satisfies the two different client constraints while keeping the access model aligned with CloudFront private content delivery.

**Learn more:** [Use signed URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html) · [Use signed cookies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-cookies.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating a three-tier application to AWS, and the application requires a MySQL database.  
  
Previously, users reported poor application performance when creating new entries. Those performance problems occurred because users were generating different real-time reports from the application during working hours.  
  
Which solution will improve the application's performance after it is moved to AWS?

options.text: Import the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity. Refactor the application to use DynamoDB for reports.
Create the database on a compute optimized Amazon EC2 instance. Ensure compute resources exceed the on-premises database.
Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster with multiple read replicas. Configure the application to use the reader endpoint for reports.
Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Configure the application to use the backup instance of the cluster as an endpoint for the reports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora MySQL improves this pattern by separating write traffic from read-heavy reporting traffic. Aurora Replicas can serve read-only queries, and the Aurora reader endpoint load-balances reporting connections across those replicas, reducing contention on the primary writer instance and improving insert performance for new entries. This directly addresses the problem of real-time reports degrading transactional performance while preserving MySQL compatibility.

**Learn more:** [Reader endpoints for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Reader.html) · [Amazon Aurora endpoint connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.Endpoints.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zonas. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application performs best when the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances is at or near 40%.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to maintain the desired performance across all instances in the group?

options.text: Use a simple scaling policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
Use a target tracking policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
Use an AWS Lambda function ta update the desired Auto Scaling group capacity.
Use scheduled scaling actions to scale up and scale down the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
A target tracking scaling policy is intended to keep an Auto Scaling group's average utilization at a specified target, such as 40% CPU. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically scales out when average CPU rises above the target and scales in when it falls below, which matches the requirement to maintain instance performance near a defined utilization level under changing load. Simple scaling, scheduled scaling, and custom Lambda-based capacity updates do not provide the same direct metric-to-target control. Official AWS documentation for target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling describes maintaining CPU utilization at a chosen target value.

**Learn more:** [Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html) · [Dynamic scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scale-based-on-demand.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. Users of the application upload images from a mobile device. The application creates a thumbnail for each image and returns a message to the user confirming that the image was uploaded successfully.  
  
Thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to give users a faster response that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application so that requests are dispatched asynchronously across the different application tiers.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.

Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is the best fit because it decouples application tiers and supports asynchronous task processing. After the image upload is accepted, the application can immediately notify the user that the original image was received, while a background worker later reads the queued message and performs thumbnail generation. AWS documentation describes Amazon SQS as a queue service for decoupling distributed application components and processing tasks asynchronously, whereas Amazon SNS is primarily for push-based fanout notifications and Step Functions is for workflow orchestration rather than simple queue-based buffering between tiers.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, or EventBridge? - AWS Decision Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/decision-guides/latest/sns-or-sqs-or-eventbridge/sns-or-sqs-or-eventbridge.html) · [Fanout Amazon SNS notifications to Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous processing - Amazon Simple Notification Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-sqs-as-subscriber.html)

A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.

Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the AWS service that provides automated backup scheduling, lifecycle management, and retention management for DynamoDB backups. DynamoDB with AWS Backup advanced features supports lifecycle transition to cold storage, so a monthly AWS Backup plan can create the backups automatically, keep them readily available for the first 6 months, transition them to cold storage afterward, and retain them for a total of 7 years. Native DynamoDB on-demand backups do not use Amazon S3 lifecycle policies or direct Glacier transitions, and the DynamoDB backup commands themselves do not define archive and deletion lifecycles.

**Learn more:** [Using AWS Backup with DynamoDB - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/backuprestore_HowItWorksAWS.html) · [Creating backups of DynamoDB tables with AWS Backup - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/CreateBackupAWS.html)

A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During migration testing, a technical team notices that the application takes a long time to start and load memory before it becomes fully productive.  
  
Which solution will reduce the application's launch time during the next testing phase?

options.text: Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools are intended to reduce latency for applications with long boot times by keeping pre-initialized instances ready for use. If the warm pool uses the **Hibernated** state, the instance saves RAM contents to the EBS root volume and reloads that memory when started again, which directly helps when the application is slow because it must launch and reload memory before becoming productive. Capacity Reservations only reserve compute capacity, Spot Instances change the purchase option rather than solving startup delay, and simply launching more On-Demand instances does not eliminate the long initialization process for each new instance.

**Learn more:** [Decrease latency for applications with long boot times using warm pools - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html) · [Amazon EC2 instance state changes - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html)

Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.  
  
A company has deployed an application in an AWS account. The application is made up of microservices that run on AWS Lambda and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). A different team supports each microservice. The company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to provide each team with its own account for that team's microservices.  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that provides service-to-service communication over HTTPS (port 443). The solution also must provide a service registry for service discovery.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Create an inspection VPC. Deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to the inspection VPC. Attach the inspection VPC to a new transit gateway. Route VPC-to-VPC traffic to the inspection VPC. Apply firewall rules to allow only HTTPS communication.

Create a VPC Lattice service network. Associate the microservices with the service network. Define HTTPS listeners for each service. Register microservice compute resources as targets. Identify VPCs that need to communicate with the services. Associate those VPCs with the service network.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an HTTPS listener and target groups for each microservice. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for each microservice. Create an interface VPC endpoint in each VPC that needs to consume that microservice.

Create peering connections between VPCs that contain microservices. Create a prefix list for each service that requires a connection to a client. Create route tables to route traffic to the appropriate VPC. Create security groups to allow only HTTPS communication.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC Lattice is the AWS-managed application networking service designed for service-to-service connectivity, security, and discovery across multiple VPCs and AWS accounts. A VPC Lattice service network provides a central registry of services, DNS-based service discovery, and communication controls for clients and services in associated VPCs. VPC Lattice services can front heterogeneous targets, including Lambda functions and Kubernetes pods or other EKS-backed targets, and each service can expose an HTTPS listener. This directly satisfies the HTTPS and service registry requirements with less operational effort than building transit inspection, maintaining many peering relationships, or creating separate PrivateLink endpoint services and interface endpoints for each microservice.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon VPC Lattice?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc-lattice/latest/ug/what-is-vpc-lattice.html) · [How VPC Lattice works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc-lattice/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to make an existing application highly available and resilient. The current version of the application is hosted in the company's data center. The application recently experienced data loss after a database server crashed because of an unexpected power outage.  
  
The company needs a solution that eliminates any single points of failure. The solution also must allow the application to scale to meet user demand.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration.
Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. Deploy the database on an EC2 instance. Enable EC2 Auto Recovery.

Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance with a read replica in a single Availability Zone. Promote the read replica to replace the primary DB instance if the primary DB instance fails.

Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy the primary and secondary database servers on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to create shared storage between the instances.

questions.explanation:
Running the application servers in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones provides both horizontal scaling and resilience to the loss of an instance or an Availability Zone. Using an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration provides high availability by maintaining a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone and supports automatic failover, which is the AWS-managed database design intended to avoid a single point of failure for the database tier. Read replicas are mainly for read scaling rather than primary high availability, and a database on EC2 or shared EBS Multi-Attach does not provide the same managed HA pattern.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)

A company hosts its customer-facing web application in containers. The workload uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. The web application is resource-intensive.  
  
The web application must be available to customers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The company anticipates that the application will have short bursts of high traffic. The workload must be highly available.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Conduct load testing by using a third-party tool. Rightsize the Fargate tasks in Amazon CloudWatch.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate for steady state and Fargate Spot for burst traffic.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate Spot for steady state and Fargate for burst traffic.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Use AWS Compute Optimizer to rightsize the Fargate task.

questions.explanation:
On-demand Fargate provides reliable baseline capacity for the continuously available workload. Fargate Spot is discounted but can be interrupted or temporarily unavailable, so it is appropriate for scalable burst capacity rather than the highly available steady-state service. An ECS capacity provider strategy can combine Fargate and Fargate Spot to reduce the cost of short-lived traffic spikes while retaining on-demand capacity for the baseline workload.

**Learn more:** [Amazon ECS clusters for Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-capacity-providers.html) · [Amazon ECS cluster capacity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-cluster-best-practice.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a web application with sporadic usage patterns. There is heavy usage at the beginning of each month, moderate usage at the start of each week, and unpredictable usage during the week. The application consists of a web server and a MySQL database server running inside the data center. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud and needs to choose a cost-effective database platform that will not require database modifications.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon RDS for MySQL
MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless
MySQL deployed on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group

questions.explanation:
MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless is the best fit because it preserves MySQL compatibility, minimizing or avoiding database changes, while also automatically scaling capacity up and down for intermittent and unpredictable demand. AWS documentation states that Aurora Serverless is intended to be a cost-effective option for intermittent or unpredictable workloads, and Aurora is compatible with MySQL. Standard Amazon RDS for MySQL avoids database changes but does not provide the same serverless, on-demand scaling advantage for this bursty pattern.

**Learn more:** [Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.Aurora_Fea_Regions_DB-eng.Feature.ServerlessV2.html) · [What is Amazon Aurora?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v1.how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A gaming company has a web application that shows scores. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are beginning to experience long delays and interruptions caused by database read performance. The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application architecture.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ElastiCache is the best fit for a read-heavy application that is experiencing database read latency, because caching frequently requested data or query results reduces load on Amazon RDS for MySQL and improves response times with minimal architectural change. AWS documentation states that query caching with ElastiCache is most effective for read-heavy applications where the same queries are executed repeatedly, and that it reduces database load and average query latency. RDS Proxy is intended for connection pooling and connection management rather than accelerating repeated read queries.

**Learn more:** [Caching database query results - Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/caching-database-query-results.html) · [Amazon RDS Proxy - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a three-tier application on AWS that ingests sensor data from its users’ devices. The traffic passes through a Network Load Balancer (NLB), then to Amazon EC2 instances for the web tier, and finally to EC2 instances for the application tier. The application tier calls a database.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to improve the security of the data in transit?

options.text: Configure a TLS listener. Deploy the server certificate on the NLB.
Configure AWS Shield Advanced. Enable AWS WAF on the NLB.
Change the load balancer to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Enable AWS WAF on the ALB.
Encrypt the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instances by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

questions.explanation:
A TLS listener on the Network Load Balancer encrypts the client connection to the load balancer by using a server certificate, which directly improves protection for data in transit. AWS documentation for Network Load Balancers states that secure listeners use TLS and require at least one server certificate on the load balancer. The other options focus on DDoS or web request filtering, or on storage encryption, rather than encrypting the application traffic flowing through the load balancer.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Network Load Balancers - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [Server certificates for your Network Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/tls-listener-certificates.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must help a company optimize the cost of running an application on AWS. The application will use Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda for compute within the architecture.  
  
The EC2 instances will run the data ingestion layer of the application. EC2 usage will be sporadic and unpredictable. Workloads that run on EC2 instances can be interrupted at any time. The application front end will run on Fargate, and Lambda will serve the API layer. The front-end utilization and API layer utilization will be predictable over the course of the next year.  
  
Which combination of purchasing options will provide the **MOST** cost-effective solution for hosting this application? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer
Use On-Demand Instances for the data ingestion layer
Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved instances for the data ingestion layer.
Purchase a 1-year EC2 instance Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Spot Instances are the most cost-effective choice for interruptible, unpredictable EC2 workloads because AWS can reclaim them when capacity conditions change, making them suitable when interruptions are acceptable. For predictable one-year usage on AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda, a 1-year Compute Savings Plan is the right commitment model because Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda, whereas EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply only to EC2 usage. Using Reserved Instances for the sporadic ingestion layer would overcommit, and an EC2 Instance Savings Plan would not cover the Fargate front end or Lambda API layer.

**Learn more:** [How Spot Instances work - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/how-spot-instances-work.html) · [Savings Plans types - Savings Plans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company must set up multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select

questions.explanation:
For development environments that are active only part of the day, the lowest-cost database option is the PostgreSQL-compatible Aurora serverless/on-demand model because it is designed for intermittent workloads and can automatically pause, eliminating database instance compute charges while idle. Provisioned Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ instances continue charging for provisioned database capacity even when developers are not using them, and Amazon S3 Object Select is not a relational PostgreSQL database platform. The AWS documentation describes Aurora Serverless as a cost-effective option for intermittent or unpredictable workloads and notes that when auto-paused to 0 ACUs, compute usage drops to zero while storage charges remain.

**Learn more:** [Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2-auto-pause.html) · [Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.Aurora_Fea_Regions_DB-eng.Feature.ServerlessV2.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online gaming company runs its platform on Amazon EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in multiple AWS Regions. The NLBs can route requests to targets over the internet. The company wants to improve the customer playing experience by reducing end-to-end load time for its global customer base.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region to replace the existing NLBs. Register the existing EC2 instances as targets for the ALBs in each Region.
Configure Amazon Route 53 to route equally weighted traffic to the NLBs in each Region.
Create additional NLBs and EC2 instances in other Regions where the company has large customer bases.
Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the existing NLBs as target endpoints.

questions.explanation:
A standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator improves performance for global internet applications by bringing client traffic onto the AWS global network at the edge and routing it to the optimal healthy regional endpoint based on factors such as client location and endpoint health. Standard accelerators support Network Load Balancers as endpoints, so the existing multi-Region NLB architecture can be used directly without replacing the load balancers.

**Learn more:** [Standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-accelerators.html) · [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website is made up of static documents and operates on a single server. An administrator updates the website content only occasionally and uses an SFTP client to upload new documents.  
  
The company decides to move its website to AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The company’s solutions architect creates a CloudFront distribution. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to act as the CloudFront origin.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a virtual server by using Amazon Lightsail. Configure the web server in the Lightsail instance. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
Create an AWS Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.
Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.

questions.explanation:
For a static website behind Amazon CloudFront, the most cost-effective and resilient origin is Amazon S3 rather than compute instances. Keeping the S3 bucket private and allowing CloudFront to access it through an origin access identity satisfies the requirement to use CloudFront as the public entry point while avoiding the cost and operational overhead of servers. AWS documentation for CloudFront states that an origin access identity can be used so end users access S3 objects only through CloudFront, and AWS recommends restricting access to the S3 origin instead of exposing the bucket publicly. This makes the private S3 origin design the best fit here.

**Learn more:** [Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html) · [S3Origin - Amazon CloudFront API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_S3Origin.html)

A company runs multiple workloads in its AWS account by using Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda. The company wants to fully use its Compute Savings Plans. The company also wants to be notified when Compute Savings Plans coverage decreases.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Create a daily budget for the Savings Plans by using AWS Budgets. Configure the budget with a coverage threshold to send notifications to the appropriate email message recipients.
Create a Lambda function that runs a coverage report against the Savings Plans. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to email the report to the appropriate email message recipients.
Create an AWS Budgets report for the Savings Plans budget. Set the frequency to daily.
Create a Savings Plans alert subscription. Enable all notification options. Enter an email address to receive notifications.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets natively supports Savings Plans coverage budgets. You can set a coverage threshold for Savings Plans, and AWS notifies recipients when overall coverage falls below that percentage. This is the managed, lowest-operations approach for monitoring Compute Savings Plans coverage across eligible services such as Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda. Savings Plans alert subscriptions are for expiration and queued-purchase events, not coverage drops, and a custom Lambda report is less operationally efficient than using the built-in budget notification feature.

**Learn more:** [Using budgets for Savings Plans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-usingBudgets.html) · [Customizing a Savings Plans budget](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-create-savingsplans-budget.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to lower the cost of its current three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers run on Amazon EC2 instances in the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during off-peak hours.  
  
The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not being used.  
  
Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet the company's requirements in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Reserved Instances are the best fit for the production environment because production runs continuously and represents predictable, steady-state usage. AWS documents that Reserved Instances reduce EC2 cost when you commit to a consistent instance configuration, and AWS billing applies RI pricing hourly for the full term whether usage occurs or not. Because the development and test instances will be stopped when idle, they do not have continuous usage, so On-Demand Instances avoid paying for unused reserved hours. Spot purchasing is not the right choice for production because Spot capacity can be interrupted.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html) · [EC2 Reserved Instance Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/reserved-instances/pricing/)

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.
Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.

questions.explanation:
S3 File Gateway extends on-premises SMB environments with virtually unlimited S3-backed capacity while maintaining low-latency local caching for frequently accessed files. S3 Lifecycle policies automatically transition older files to Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days, reducing storage costs and meeting both the low-latency and lifecycle-management requirements.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)

A streaming-media company is rebuilding its infrastructure to support growing demand for video content that users watch every day.  
  
The company must process terabyte-sized videos to block certain content within them. Video processing can require up to 20 minutes.  
  
The company needs a solution that can scale with demand while remaining cost-effective.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Lambda functions to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon DynamoDB. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and AWS Fargate to implement microservices to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon Aurora. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to process videos. Store video content in Amazon S3 Standard. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for queuing and to decouple processing tasks.

Deploy a containerized video processing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on Amazon EC2. Store video metadata in Amazon RDS in a single Availability Zone. Store video content in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can adjust worker capacity as demand changes, while Amazon SQS decouples queued video-processing jobs from the worker fleet and supports queue-based scaling. EC2 workers can be configured with storage and compute capacity appropriate for terabyte-scale processing and workloads longer than 15 minutes. Amazon S3 Standard is intended for frequently accessed data, which fits video content consumed daily. AWS Lambda is limited to 15 minutes per invocation, and AWS Fargate task ephemeral storage is limited to 200 GiB.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html) · [Fargate task ephemeral storage for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-task-storage.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving an application from on-premises servers to Amazon EC2 instances. As part of the migration design requirements, a solutions architect must implement infrastructure metric alarms.  
  
The company does not need to take action if CPU utilization rises above 50% for a short burst of time. However, if CPU utilization rises above 50% and disk read IOPS are high at the same time, the company needs to act as quickly as possible.  
  
The solutions architect also must reduce false alarms.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms where possible.
Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visualize the metrics and react to issues quickly.
Create Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to monitor the application and raise an alarm.
Create single Amazon CloudWatch metric alarms with multiple metric thresholds where possible.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms let you combine separate metric alarms by using logic such as AND, so an alert can be raised only when the CPU utilization alarm and the disk read IOPS alarm are both in the ALARM state at the same time. This matches the requirement to act only on the combined condition and helps reduce alarm noise and false positives. CloudWatch dashboards provide visibility but not alerting logic, Synthetics canaries are for application endpoint testing, and this requirement is best met by combining alarms rather than relying on a single basic metric alarm.

**Learn more:** [Create a composite alarm - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) · [Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner to help with an application migration initiative.  
  
A solutions architect needs to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volume snapshots.  
  
What is the **MOST secure** way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?

options.text: Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.

Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.

questions.explanation:
For an encrypted EBS-backed AMI that uses a customer managed KMS key, the secure cross-account pattern is to share the AMI only with the specific destination AWS account by using AMI launch permissions and to allow that external account to use the KMS key that encrypts the underlying snapshots. AWS requires the customer managed key used for encrypted snapshots to be shared as well for cross-account access, so targeted account-level sharing plus KMS key policy access is the least-privilege and most secure approach.

**Learn more:** [Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html) · [Share the KMS key used to encrypt a shared Amazon EBS snapshot - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/share-kms-key.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 within 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps internet uplink, and other on-premises applications also use that uplink. The company can allocate 80% of the internet bandwidth to this one-time migration task.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.
Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.
Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.
Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices. Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Using the available internet capacity, the migration would have only 400 Mbps of bandwidth, which is nowhere near enough to move 10 PB in 6 weeks. Network-based methods such as AWS DataSync, rsync, or AWS CLI uploads would therefore miss the deadline. AWS Snowball is the correct service for very large one-time transfers when network bandwidth is limited, and AWS documentation specifically describes using multiple Snowball Edge devices for migrations from 500 TB to multiple petabytes and then importing the data into Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [Estimating migration timelines - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/datasync-large-migration-timelines.html) · [Creating a large data migration plan with Snowball Edge - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/create-data-migration-plan.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The total amount of data is growing and is nearing the company's total storage capacity. A solutions architect must increase the available storage space without losing low-latency access to the most recently accessed files. The solutions architect must also provide file lifecycle management to prevent future storage issues."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.","B":"Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.","C":"Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.","D":"Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"S3 File Gateway extends on-premises SMB environments with virtually unlimited S3-backed capacity while maintaining low-latency local caching for frequently accessed files. S3 Lifecycle policies automatically transition older files to Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days, reducing storage costs and meeting both the low-latency and lifecycle-management requirements.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"4e089a16-4bc8-4a75-abd0-6fe0829a05e8","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A streaming-media company is rebuilding its infrastructure to support growing demand for video content that users watch every day."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company must process terabyte-sized videos to block certain content within them. Video processing can require up to 20 minutes."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company needs a solution that can scale with demand while remaining cost-effective."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use AWS Lambda functions to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon DynamoDB. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.","B":"Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and AWS Fargate to implement microservices to process videos. Store video metadata in Amazon Aurora. Store video content in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering.","C":"Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to process videos. Store video content in Amazon S3 Standard. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for queuing and to decouple processing tasks.","D":"Deploy a containerized video processing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on Amazon EC2. Store video metadata in Amazon RDS in a single Availability Zone. Store video content in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can adjust worker capacity as demand changes, while Amazon SQS decouples queued video-processing jobs from the worker fleet and supports queue-based scaling. EC2 workers can be configured with storage and compute capacity appropriate for terabyte-scale processing and workloads longer than 15 minutes. Amazon S3 Standard is intended for frequently accessed data, which fits video content consumed daily. AWS Lambda is limited to 15 minutes per invocation, and AWS Fargate task ephemeral storage is limited to 200 GiB.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html) · [Fargate task ephemeral storage for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-task-storage.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"31175d79-d2f8-46f2-a40d-e220ec006872","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
55:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is moving an application from on-premises servers to Amazon EC2 instances. As part of the migration design requirements, a solutions architect must implement infrastructure metric alarms."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company does not need to take action if CPU utilization rises above 50% for a short burst of time. However, if CPU utilization rises above 50% and disk read IOPS are high at the same time, the company needs to act as quickly as possible."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The solutions architect also must reduce false alarms."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms where possible.","B":"Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visualize the metrics and react to issues quickly.","C":"Create Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to monitor the application and raise an alarm.","D":"Create single Amazon CloudWatch metric alarms with multiple metric thresholds where possible."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms let you combine separate metric alarms by using logic such as AND, so an alert can be raised only when the CPU utilization alarm and the disk read IOPS alarm are both in the ALARM state at the same time. This matches the requirement to act only on the combined condition and helps reduce alarm noise and false positives. CloudWatch dashboards provide visibility but not alerting logic, Synthetics canaries are for application endpoint testing, and this requirement is best met by combining alarms rather than relying on a single basic metric alarm.

**Learn more:** [Create a composite alarm - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) · [Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"aaa37654-5500-451c-ad7d-5608d921adff","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
56:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner to help with an application migration initiative."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"A solutions architect needs to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volume snapshots."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["What is the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"MOST secure"}]," way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?"]}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.","B":"Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.","C":"Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.","D":"Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"For an encrypted EBS-backed AMI that uses a customer managed KMS key, the secure cross-account pattern is to share the AMI only with the specific destination AWS account by using AMI launch permissions and to allow that external account to use the KMS key that encrypts the underlying snapshots. AWS requires the customer managed key used for encrypted snapshots to be shared as well for cross-account access, so targeted account-level sharing plus KMS key policy access is the least-privilege and most secure approach.

**Learn more:** [Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html) · [Share the KMS key used to encrypt a shared Amazon EBS snapshot - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/share-kms-key.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"70f561f9-a39f-41ce-8de5-f7d3d5589439","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
57:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company needs to migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 within 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps internet uplink, and other on-premises applications also use that uplink. The company can allocate 80% of the internet bandwidth to this one-time migration task."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.","B":"Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.","C":"Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.","D":"Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices. Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"Using the available internet capacity, the migration would have only 400 Mbps of bandwidth, which is nowhere near enough to move 10 PB in 6 weeks. Network-based methods such as AWS DataSync, rsync, or AWS CLI uploads would therefore miss the deadline. AWS Snowball is the correct service for very large one-time transfers when network bandwidth is limited, and AWS documentation specifically describes using multiple Snowball Edge devices for migrations from 500 TB to multiple petabytes and then importing the data into Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [Estimating migration timelines - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/datasync-large-migration-timelines.html) · [Creating a large data migration plan with Snowball Edge - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/create-data-migration-plan.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"65599a89-5dc8-4bf9-b992-b8db9f509569","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
A company runs an application on Amazon ECS. The application creates resized versions of an original image and then makes Amazon S3 API calls to store the resized images in Amazon S3.  
  
How can a solutions architect make sure that the application has permission to access Amazon S3?

options.text: Update the S3 role in AWS IAM to allow read/write access from Amazon ECS, and then relaunch the container.
Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.
Create a security group that allows access from Amazon ECS to Amazon S3, and update the launch configuration used by the ECS cluster.
Create an IAM user with S3 permissions, and then relaunch the Amazon EC2 instances for the ECS cluster while logged in as this account.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS applications should access AWS services by using a task IAM role. The IAM role is granted the required Amazon S3 permissions and is associated with the task definition by using `taskRoleArn`, which provides temporary credentials to the containers running the application. Security groups do not grant AWS API permissions, and using an IAM user for workloads is not the recommended mechanism for ECS tasks. AWS documentation states that the task role allows application code in the container to use other AWS services such as Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [Amazon ECS task IAM role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html) · [IAM roles for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-iam-role-overview.html)

A company plans to migrate data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted at rest in the S3 bucket, and the encryption key must rotate automatically every year.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). Use the built-in key rotation behavior of SSE-S3 encryption keys.

Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Enable automatic key rotation. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket.

Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Set the S3 bucket's default encryption behavior to use the customer managed KMS key. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Manually rotate the KMS key every year.

Use customer key material to encrypt the data. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key without key material. Import the customer key material into the KMS key. Enable automatic key rotation.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon S3 default encryption with SSE-KMS and an AWS KMS customer managed symmetric key that has automatic rotation enabled satisfies both requirements: the objects are encrypted at rest in S3, and AWS KMS automatically rotates the key material every 365 days by default. This avoids the ongoing manual work required by manual rotation. A KMS key with imported key material does not support automatic rotation, so that approach does not meet the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configuring default encryption - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/default-bucket-encryption.html) · [Enable automatic key rotation - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotating-keys-enable.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company is running a seasonal online sale. The company hosts its website on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The company wants the website to handle sudden increases in traffic during the sale.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that is large enough to handle peak traffic load. Stop half of the Amazon EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the stopped instances to scale out when traffic increases.
Create an Auto Scaling group for the website. Set the minimum size of the Auto Scaling group so that it can handle high traffic volumes without the need to scale out.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon ElastiCache to cache dynamic content with an Auto Scaling group set as the origin. Configure the Auto Scaling group with the instances necessary to populate CloudFront and ElastiCache. Scale in after the cache is fully populated.
Configure an Auto Scaling group to scale out as traffic increases. Create a launch template to start new instances from a preconfigured Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling is designed to increase and decrease EC2 capacity automatically as demand changes, which is more cost-effective than keeping enough instances running for peak load at all times. A launch template with a preconfigured Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lets the Auto Scaling group rapidly launch additional, consistently configured instances when traffic rises. This directly fits a multi-AZ web tier that must absorb sudden spikes without permanent overprovisioning.

**Learn more:** [Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html) · [Increase or decrease compute capacity of your application with scaling - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scale-your-group.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage. Application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects the application's read and write throughput to the database to be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.  
  
Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB **on-demand** capacity mode is the best fit for **unpredictable** traffic because it automatically scales with request volume and uses pay-per-request pricing, avoiding the need to preprovision throughput for spikes. The **DynamoDB Standard** table class is appropriate when the workload has **frequent or moderate-to-high reads and writes**, because Standard-IA is intended for tables where storage cost dominates and data is accessed infrequently; Standard-IA has lower storage cost but higher read/write cost. Together, these requirements make **on-demand mode with the Standard table class** the most cost-effective choice.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html) · [Evaluate your DynamoDB table's capacity mode - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/CostOptimization_TableCapacityMode.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company collects and processes data from a vendor. The vendor stores its data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in the vendor's own AWS account. The company’s VPC does not have an internet gateway, an AWS Direct Connect connection, or an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The company needs to access the data that is in the vendor database.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Instruct the vendor to sign up for the AWS Hosted Connection Direct Connect Program. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
Configure a client VPN connection between the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
Instruct the vendor to create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Place the NLB in front of the Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Use AWS PrivateLink to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
Use AWS Transit Gateway to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company’s VPC and the vendor's VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink, powered by a Network Load Balancer in the provider VPC, enables private access to resources across AWS accounts without requiring internet gateways, AWS Direct Connect, or VPN connections. The consumer VPC creates an interface VPC endpoint to securely access the vendor's RDS database through the private AWS network infrastructure. VPC peering requires routing configuration and direct connectivity, which doesn't meet the constraint. Transit Gateway similarly requires connectivity mechanisms not available in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Access Amazon RDS across VPCs using AWS PrivateLink and Network Load Balancer](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/access-amazon-rds-across-vpcs-using-aws-privatelink-and-network-load-balancer/) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts an SFTP server that stores its data on an NFS-based file system. The server contains 200 GB of data that must be transferred. The server must run on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to automate this task? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Launch the EC2 instance into the same Availability Zone as the EFS file system.
Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center.
Create a secondary Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instance for the data.
Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data to the EC2 instance.
Use AWS DataSync to create a suitable location configuration for the on-premises SFTP server.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is the managed service used to automate transfers from on-premises NFS storage to Amazon EFS. For an on-premises NFS source, a DataSync agent must be deployed in the on-premises environment so the service can access the file server. DataSync then uses transfer locations for the source and destination, with Amazon EFS supported as a destination location. An additional EBS volume and manual copy commands do not meet the automation requirement, and EC2 placement in the same Availability Zone as EFS is not a required migration step because EFS is accessed through mount targets in the VPC. AWS documentation supports deploying an on-premises DataSync agent and configuring NFS and EFS locations for this type of transfer.

**Learn more:** [Transferring to or from on-premises storage with AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_us/datasync/latest/userguide/transferring-on-premises-storage.html) · [Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with an NFS file server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-nfs-location.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A gaming company runs a browser-based application on AWS. The application's users consume a large volume of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3. This content is identical for all users.  
  
The application has grown in popularity, and millions of users worldwide are accessing these media files. The company wants to deliver the files to users while reducing the load on the origin.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the correct choice because it is a content delivery network that caches static objects such as images and video at AWS edge locations around the world. When Amazon S3 is used as the origin, CloudFront serves repeated requests from cache near users, which improves performance and reduces the number of requests sent to the S3 origin. That directly satisfies the need to support millions of global users while lowering origin load in the most cost-effective way. AWS Global Accelerator optimizes routing to application endpoints but does not cache content, and ElastiCache Redis or Memcached are application-side in-memory caches rather than the standard global distribution layer for static S3 media.

**Learn more:** [Speeding up your website with Amazon CloudFront - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/website-hosting-cloudfront-walkthrough.html) · [Performance design patterns for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-design-patterns.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has two AWS accounts: Production and Development.  
  
The company needs to push code changes from the Development account to the Production account.  
  
During the alpha phase, only two senior developers on the development team need access to the Production account. During the beta phase, additional developers will need access to perform testing.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create two policy documents by using the AWS Management Console in each account. Assign the policy to developers who need access.
Create an IAM role in the Development account. Grant the IAM role access to the Production account. Allow developers to assume the role.
Create an IAM role in the Production account. Define a trust policy that specifies the Development account. Allow developers to assume the role.
Create an IAM group in the Production account. Add the group as a principal in a trust policy that specifies the Production account. Add developers to the group.

questions.explanation:
For AWS cross-account access, the role should be created in the account being accessed: the Production account. Its trust policy should trust the Development account or specific principals from that account, and the developers then assume that role to obtain temporary credentials in Production. This is the standard AWS cross-account role pattern, avoids creating separate IAM users in Production, and scales easily as more developers need access later. IAM groups cannot be used as principals in a role trust policy.

**Learn more:** [Cross account resource access in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html) · [IAM tutorial: Delegate access across AWS accounts using IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_cross-account-with-roles.html)
