A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance reasons. Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any data.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments is the best fit because it creates a separate staging environment that copies and stays in sync with the production RDS for MySQL database, allows a major or minor engine version upgrade in the green environment, and supports testing before switchover. AWS documentation states that Blue/Green Deployments can be used to upgrade RDS for MySQL and test changes before promoting the green environment to production, with switchover typically taking under a minute. That provides the quickest managed upgrade-and-test path with minimal operational effort and no data loss from manual migration processes.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments-overview.html) · [Using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments for database updates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an AWS account that is used for software engineering. The AWS account can access the company’s on-premises data center by using a pair of AWS Direct Connect connections. All non-VPC traffic is routed to the virtual private gateway.  
  
A development team recently created an AWS Lambda function in the console. The team needs to permit the function to access a database that runs in a private subnet in the company’s on-premises data center.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.
Set up a VPN connection from AWS to the data center. Route the traffic from the Lambda function through the VPN.
Update the route tables in the VPC to allow the Lambda function to access the on-premises data center through Direct Connect.
Create an Elastic IP address. Configure the Lambda function to send traffic through the Elastic IP address without an elastic network interface.

questions.explanation:
To access a private on-premises database over existing hybrid connectivity, the Lambda function must be attached to the VPC so Lambda can create network interfaces in the selected subnets and use the VPC’s routing path to the virtual private gateway and Direct Connect. AWS Lambda VPC-enabled functions can reach private resources reachable from that VPC, whereas creating a new VPN is unnecessary when Direct Connect already exists, route-table changes alone do not place Lambda on that network path, and an Elastic IP does not provide this kind of private connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html) · [Troubleshoot networking issues in Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/troubleshooting-networking.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying an application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to route traffic to at least two Amazon EC2 instances within a single target group. The instances are deployed in an Auto Scaling group for each environment. The company needs both a development environment and a production environment. The production environment will experience periods of high traffic.  
  
Which solution will configure the development environment in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Reconfigure the target group in the development environment to have only one EC2 instance as a target.
Change the ALB balancing algorithm to least outstanding requests.
Reduce the size of the EC2 instances in both environments.
Reduce the maximum number of EC2 instances in the development environment’s Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
The most cost-effective configuration is to set a lower maximum capacity for the development environment’s Auto Scaling group. This keeps the development environment using the same ALB and target-group pattern while limiting how many EC2 instances it can launch, which directly reduces cost. Using only one target would conflict with the stated design of directing traffic to at least two EC2 instances, changing the ALB algorithm does not reduce infrastructure cost, and downsizing instances in both environments could undermine the production environment’s ability to handle high traffic.

**Learn more:** [Set scaling limits for your Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-capacity-limits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application that stores and shares photos. Users upload photos to an Amazon S3 bucket. Each day, users upload approximately 150 photos. The company wants to design a solution that creates a thumbnail for every new photo and stores that thumbnail in a second S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a long-running Amazon EMR cluster. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a memory-optimized Amazon EC2 instance that is always on. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.

Configure an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to the second S3 bucket.

Configure S3 Storage Lens to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to a second S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 event notifications can invoke an AWS Lambda function whenever a new photo is uploaded. Lambda can generate and store the thumbnail while incurring charges only for the relatively small number of executions required, rather than paying for continuously running EC2 or EMR compute capacity. S3 Storage Lens is an analytics feature, not a per-object event trigger.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect uses an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application.  
  
The web application consists of:  
  
- a web tier  
- an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables  
  
The web tier and application tier run on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible.  
  
The application EC2 instances must access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.

Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.

Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.

Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.

questions.explanation:
For applications running on Amazon EC2, the correct way to access AWS services without hardcoding credentials is to assign an IAM role to the instances through an instance profile. The role should include the permissions the application actually needs. Because the application tier both stores and retrieves data in DynamoDB, it requires read and write permissions rather than read-only access. Using IAM user access keys in CloudFormation parameters or user data would expose and require management of long-term credentials, which AWS recommends avoiding. AWS documentation states that EC2 uses an instance profile as a container for an IAM role, and applications on the instance can use the temporary credentials provided by that role.

**Learn more:** [IAM roles for Amazon EC2 - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html) · [AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-iam-instanceprofile.html)

A company hosts a static website on Amazon S3 and uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS. The website is seeing increased demand from users around the world.  
  
The company must reduce latency for users who access the website.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Replicate the S3 bucket that contains the website to all AWS Regions. Add Route 53 geolocation routing entries.
Provision accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator. Associate the supplied IP addresses with the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the IP addresses of the accelerators.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the CloudFront distribution.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the new endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the most cost-effective way to lower latency for a globally accessed static website on Amazon S3 because it caches and serves the site's content from edge locations worldwide, delivering objects from the location with the lowest latency. AWS documentation specifically recommends CloudFront to improve the performance of an S3 website, and Route 53 records can be updated to point to the CloudFront distribution. S3 Transfer Acceleration is intended for accelerating transfers to and from S3 rather than general website content delivery, and replicating buckets across Regions or using Global Accelerator would be more complex and less appropriate for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Speeding up your website with Amazon CloudFront - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/website-hosting-cloudfront-walkthrough.html) · [What is Amazon CloudFront?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/InvalidationLimits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon S3 to host its static website. The company wants to add a contact form to the webpage. The contact form will include dynamic, server-side components so users can enter their name, email address, phone number, and message.  
  
The company expects fewer than 100 site visits each month. The contact form must notify the company by email when a customer submits the form.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Host the dynamic contact form in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to a third-party email provider.

Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that returns the contact form from an AWS Lambda function. Configure another Lambda function on the API Gateway to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

Host the website by using AWS Amplify Hosting for static content and dynamic content. Use server-side scripting to build the contact form. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to deliver the message to the company.

Migrate the website from Amazon S3 to Amazon EC2 instances that run Windows Server. Use Internet Information Services (IIS) for Windows Server to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

questions.explanation:
For a static site with very low traffic, the lowest-cost architecture is a serverless submission flow. Amazon API Gateway can expose an endpoint for the form, AWS Lambda can run the server-side logic only when a submission occurs, and Amazon SNS can publish notifications to email subscribers. That avoids paying for continuously running compute such as Amazon ECS or Amazon EC2, while still providing the required dynamic processing and email notification. SQS does not itself deliver email notifications, so it does not directly meet the stated requirement.

**Learn more:** [Invoking a Lambda function using an Amazon API Gateway endpoint - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-apigateway.html) · [Amazon SNS email subscription setup and management - Amazon Simple Notification Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-email-notifications.html)

A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives traffic only on weekdays during business hours. The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.
Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.
Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.
Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL supports stopping and starting DB instances, and AWS documents this as a common cost-optimization use case for databases that are not needed continuously. AWS also provides the managed Instance Scheduler on AWS solution, which can automatically start and stop Amazon RDS instances on customer-defined schedules such as weekday business hours. That matches the usage pattern while minimizing custom operational work. Reserved DB instances are better for steady long-term usage, and disabling automatic backups or building a custom Lambda solution would either increase risk or add unnecessary management effort.

**Learn more:** [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html) · [Automate starting and stopping AWS instances - Instance Scheduler on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/instance-scheduler-on-aws/solution-overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of cost and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account is allowed to use.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.
Create organization units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.
Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.
Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations provides centralized multi-account governance, and service control policies (SCPs) let you set permission guardrails for member accounts or for accounts grouped into organizational units (OUs). By placing each department's accounts into its own OU and attaching SCPs, the company can centrally restrict which AWS services and actions those accounts may use with minimal ongoing administration. AWS Service Catalog governs approved products rather than account-wide service availability, and AWS CloudFormation or Systems Manager do not provide the same centralized preventive control over which AWS services an account can access.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [Best practices for managing organizational units (OUs) with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_ous_best_practices.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has multiple web servers that must frequently connect to a common Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants a secure way for the web servers to connect to the database while also satisfying a security requirement to rotate user credentials often.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store the database user credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access AWS Secrets Manager.
Store the database user credentials in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access OpsCenter.
Store the database user credentials in a secure Amazon S3 bucket. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to retrieve credentials and access the database.

Store the database user credentials in files encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) on the web server file system. The web server should be able to decrypt the files and access the database.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the correct service for securely storing database credentials and allowing applications to retrieve them at runtime by using IAM permissions. It also supports automatic rotation of database secrets, including Amazon RDS credentials, which directly satisfies the requirement to rotate user credentials frequently. The other options do not provide purpose-built secret management with automated credential rotation for shared database access.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its multi-tier applications on AWS. For compliance, governance, auditing, and security, the company needs to track configuration changes on its AWS resources and record a history of API calls made to those resources.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CloudTrail to track configuration changes and AWS Config to record API calls.
Use AWS Config to track configuration changes and AWS CloudTrail to record API calls.
Use AWS Config to track configuration changes and Amazon CloudWatch to record API calls.
Use AWS CloudTrail to track configuration changes and Amazon CloudWatch to record API calls.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config is used to assess, audit, and evaluate the configurations of AWS resources and to track configuration changes over time. AWS CloudTrail records a history of AWS API calls and account activity for auditing and governance. Using AWS Config for configuration-change tracking and AWS CloudTrail for API-call history satisfies both requirements.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Config Works - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/how-does-config-work.html) · [What Is AWS Config? - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center contains a storage server that stores data in an NFS-based file system. The storage server contains 200 GB of data. The company must migrate the data with no interruption to existing services. Multiple resources in AWS need to be able to access the data by using the NFS protocol.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket to receive the data.
Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data into the AWS destination.
Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Use a DataSync task between the on-premises location and AWS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is AWS’s shared file storage service that multiple AWS resources can mount concurrently by using NFS, which matches the requirement for shared NFS access. AWS DataSync is designed to transfer data between an on-premises NFS file server and Amazon EFS by deploying a DataSync agent on premises and running a transfer task, making it the appropriate low-overhead migration approach for an online migration of 200 GB without disrupting existing services. FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance workloads rather than the most economical general-purpose NFS file sharing, and Amazon S3 is object storage rather than a native NFS shared file system. Official AWS documentation confirms that EFS supports concurrent access from multiple clients over NFS and that DataSync can transfer data from NFS file servers to Amazon EFS.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Creating and managing EFS resources - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/creating-using.html)

options.text: Use Amazon GuardDuty to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for GuardDuty findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF rules.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for Firewall Manager findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF web ACL.
Use Amazon Inspector to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.
Use Amazon Macie to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon GuardDuty is the AWS service designed for continuous threat detection by analyzing AWS data sources and generating security findings for suspicious or malicious activity. GuardDuty findings can be published to Amazon EventBridge, where rules can filter specific findings and invoke an AWS Lambda function for automated remediation. That Lambda function can modify AWS WAF protections to block or mitigate detected threats. AWS Firewall Manager manages security policies rather than serving as the primary threat detection engine, Amazon Inspector focuses on vulnerability management, and Amazon Macie focuses on sensitive data discovery and protection. 

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon GuardDuty?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html) · [Processing GuardDuty findings with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_eventbridge.html)

A company that mainly runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to reduce its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to stay stored locally.  
  
Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Amazon S3 File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes are designed for on-premises applications that use iSCSI volumes while storing primary data in Amazon S3 and keeping only frequently or recently accessed data in the local cache. This minimizes the amount of on-premises storage that must be scaled while still providing low-latency access to hot data. Stored volumes are the opposite model because they keep the entire primary dataset on premises, and S3 File Gateway uses file protocols rather than iSCSI.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs several Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances that have high utilization. The RDS DB instances run in member accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
The company's finance team has access to the organization's management account and member accounts. The finance team wants to find ways to optimize costs by using AWS Trusted Advisor.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the management account.
Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the member accounts where the RDS DB instances are running.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for compute optimization. Crosscheck the results by using AWS Compute Optimizer.

questions.explanation:
AWS Trusted Advisor can be integrated with AWS Organizations so the management account can view aggregated check results for accounts in the organization, which makes the management account the appropriate place to review organization-wide recommendations. For heavily used Amazon RDS On-Demand DB instances, the relevant cost optimization action is the **Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization** check, because Reserved Instances are intended for predictable, sustained database usage and can reduce cost versus On-Demand pricing. The **Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances** check does not apply to highly utilized databases, and **Compute Optimizer** is not the right crosscheck for RDS for Oracle because its RDS DB instance recommendations support Aurora, RDS for MySQL, and RDS for PostgreSQL, not Oracle.

**Learn more:** [Organizational view for AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/organizational-view.html) · [AWS Trusted Advisor and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-ta.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a highly available image-processing application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single VPC. The EC2 instances run in multiple subnets across several Availability Zones. The EC2 instances do not communicate with one another. However, the EC2 instances download images from Amazon S3 and upload images to Amazon S3 through a single NAT gateway. The company is concerned about data transfer charges.  
  
What is the **MOST cost-effective** way for the company to avoid Regional data transfer charges?

options.text: Launch the NAT gateway in each Availability Zone.
Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance.
Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3.
Provision an EC2 Dedicated Host to run the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 lets EC2 instances access S3 privately without using a NAT gateway, and AWS documents that gateway endpoints for S3 have no additional charge. Because the application traffic of concern is S3 upload and download traffic, routing that traffic through an S3 gateway endpoint removes the need to send it through a single NAT gateway across Availability Zones, which is the source of the extra transfer cost. Creating NAT gateways in every AZ could reduce cross-AZ NAT traffic, but it still costs more than using the free S3 gateway endpoint and is therefore not the most cost-effective option.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Pricing for NAT gateways - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-pricing.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations to create dedicated AWS accounts for each business unit so each business unit's account can be managed independently upon request.  
  
The root email recipient missed a notification that was sent to the root user email address of one account.  
  
The company wants to ensure that future notifications are not missed. Future notifications must be limited to account administrators.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the company’s email server to forward notification email messages that are sent to the AWS account root user email address to all users in the organization.

Configure all AWS account root user email addresses as distribution lists that go to a few administrators who can respond to alerts. Configure AWS account alternate contacts in the AWS Organizations console or programmatically.
Configure all AWS account root user email messages to be sent to one administrator who is responsible for monitoring alerts and forwarding those alerts to the appropriate groups.

Configure all existing AWS accounts and all newly created accounts to use the same root user email address. Configure AWS account alternate contacts in the AWS Organizations console or programmatically.

questions.explanation:
For AWS accounts in an organization, the root user email should use a shared distribution list instead of an individual mailbox so important account and recovery communications are not missed when personnel change or one person overlooks a message. AWS also supports configuring alternate contacts for member accounts from AWS Organizations or programmatically, and those contacts can be team distribution lists for billing, operations, or security notifications. This satisfies the requirement to keep notifications limited to account administrators while avoiding a single-person dependency.

**Learn more:** [Root user best practices for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html) · [Update the alternate contacts for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-update-contact-alternate.html)

**Learn more:** [Root user best practices for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html) · [Update the alternate contacts for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-update-contact-alternate.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"ce2ec58d-f09b-46e3-84f9-6dd3ecc0a506","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is running low on disk space.  
  
A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** amount of effort?

options.text: Enable storage autoscaling in RDS
Increase the RDS database instance size
Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS
Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS storage autoscaling is designed to automatically increase allocated storage when a DB instance is running low on free space, which is the simplest way to address a storage-capacity problem without performing a backup-and-restore migration or changing compute size. DB instance size affects CPU and memory rather than disk capacity, and changing to Provisioned IOPS changes the storage type for performance, not the core need for effortless capacity growth. AWS documents storage autoscaling specifically for avoiding manual storage scale-up when free database space becomes low.

**Learn more:** [Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html) · [Settings for DB instances - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ModifyInstance.Settings.html)

A company offers a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service that uses UDP connections. The service is made up of Amazon EC2 instances running in an Auto Scaling group. The company has deployments in multiple AWS Regions.  
  
The company must route users to the Region with the lowest latency. The company also requires automated failover between Regions.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the ALB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency record that points to aliases for each NLB. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the latency record as an origin.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted record that points to aliases for each ALB. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the weighted record as an origin.

questions.explanation:
For a multi-Region UDP-based VoIP application, the correct choice is to place the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer in each Region and use AWS Global Accelerator. Network Load Balancer supports UDP, while Application Load Balancer does not. AWS Global Accelerator is built for TCP and UDP workloads and routes users to the optimal regional endpoint based on client location, performance, and endpoint health, which also provides automatic cross-Region failover when an endpoint becomes unhealthy.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Global Accelerator?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html) · [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html)

A company is building a new mobile app. It must implement appropriate traffic filtering to protect its Application Load Balancer (ALB) from common application-layer attacks, such as cross-site scripting and SQL injection. The company has minimal infrastructure and operations staff. It also needs to minimize its portion of the responsibility for managing, updating, and securing servers in its AWS environment.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.
Deploy the application using Amazon S3 with public hosting enabled.
Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and add the ALB as a protected resource.
Create a new ALB that directs traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance running a third-party firewall, which then passes the traffic to the current ALB.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is the managed AWS service for application-layer request filtering on resources such as an Application Load Balancer. It supports rules that detect and block malicious SQL code and scripting, including SQL injection and cross-site scripting, without requiring the company to deploy and maintain its own firewall servers. That directly satisfies both the security requirement and the goal of reducing operational responsibility for server management.

**Learn more:** [Configuring protection in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html) · [AWS WAF rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rules.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently stores the user session state.  
  
The company wants to ensure high availability and prevent loss of user session state if a web server outage occurs.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.
Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.
Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.

questions.explanation:
To prevent session loss when an EC2 web server fails, the session state must be moved off the individual instance to a shared external store that all web servers can access. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is designed for low-latency in-memory data storage and supports high-availability features such as replication and failover, making it a strong fit for shared session state in an Auto Scaling web tier. Memcached does not provide the same replication and failover characteristics for preserving session data, AWS Storage Gateway cached volumes are not intended for this pattern, and Amazon RDS is typically less appropriate than Redis for transient web session state. Official AWS documentation also identifies Redis and Memcached as common technologies for session data, with Redis being the HA-oriented choice.

**Learn more:** [Implementing Microservices on AWS – Data store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/microservices-on-aws/data-store.html) · [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has migrated a fleet of hundreds of on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run a diverse set of Windows Server versions together with several Linux distributions. The company wants a solution to automate inventory and operating system updates.  
  
The company also needs a summary of common vulnerabilities for each instance for regular monthly reviews.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Security Hub to produce monthly reports.
Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Deploy Amazon Inspector, and configure monthly reports.
Set up AWS Shield Advanced, and configure monthly reports. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
Set up Amazon GuardDuty in the account to monitor all EC2 instances. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates patch scanning and installation for supported Windows Server and Linux managed nodes, making it the appropriate service for managing operating system updates across a large mixed EC2 fleet. Systems Manager also provides inventory capabilities for managed instances. Amazon Inspector is the AWS service that continuously assesses EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and generates findings based on CVEs, which can be reviewed and summarized on a recurring basis. Shield Advanced, GuardDuty, and AWS Config do not provide this combination of patch automation plus per-instance vulnerability assessment.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-inventory.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a new web-based customer relationship management application. The application will use several Amazon EC2 instances, backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes, behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application will also use an Amazon Aurora database. All application data must be encrypted both at rest and in transit.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) certificates on the ALB to encrypt data in transit. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest.

Use the AWS root account to log in to the AWS Management Console. Upload the company’s encryption certificates. While in the root account, select the option to turn on encryption for all data at rest and in transit for the account.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.
Use BitLocker to encrypt all data at rest. Import the company’s TLS certificate keys to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Attach the KMS keys to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS volume encryption and Amazon Aurora storage encryption at rest use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). For data in transit, an Application Load Balancer uses an HTTPS listener with an SSL/TLS certificate, and AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is the standard service for provisioning and attaching that certificate to the ALB. That combination satisfies both the at-rest and in-transit encryption requirements.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS encryption - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html) · [Encrypting Amazon Aurora resources - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. The application connects to an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
  
For disaster recovery (DR), the company wants to make sure that the application is available from another AWS Region with minimal downtime.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** downtime?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, ELBs, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when necessary. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.

Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and an ELB to be launched when necessary. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.

Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm with an evaluation period of 10 minutes to invoke an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 to point to the DR Region's ELB.

questions.explanation:
The lowest-downtime DR design is a warm standby or multi-Region pattern in which the DR Region already has the application tier deployed and DynamoDB data is already replicated there. DynamoDB global tables replicate table data across Regions and are intended to support multi-Region resilience with low recovery time. With an Auto Scaling group and ELB already running in the DR Region, failover is reduced to redirecting DNS to that Region's load balancer. Building EC2, ELB, or DynamoDB resources only after a failure takes longer, and introducing a 10-minute CloudWatch alarm delay increases downtime compared with direct Route 53 DNS failover.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon DynamoDB?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html) · [Using DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/dynamodb-global-tables/routing-strategies.html)

A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and during peak times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for the applications that connect to the database.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy is the managed AWS service designed for Amazon RDS applications that experience surges in concurrent connections. It provides connection pooling and lets applications connect through the proxy endpoint instead of directly to the database, which improves scalability while keeping operational effort low. A custom proxy on Amazon EC2 or a Lambda-based intermediary would require the company to build, operate, and maintain its own solution, and DynamoDB is not a drop-in scaling solution for an existing Amazon RDS database workload.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)

A company needs to manage Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company currently copies AMIs into the same AWS Region in which the AMIs were created. The company must design an application that captures AWS API calls and sends alerts whenever the Amazon EC2 `CreateImage` API operation is invoked within the company's account.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to query AWS CloudTrail logs and to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.

Configure AWS CloudTrail with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification that occurs when updated logs are sent to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create a new table and to query on CreateImage when an API call is detected.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.

Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a target for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an alert to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a CreateImage API call is detected.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge can receive `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` events for management API calls recorded by AWS CloudTrail and match a specific API action such as `CreateImage`. Configuring an EventBridge rule with an Amazon SNS topic as the target provides a fully managed, event-driven alerting solution without custom polling, log parsing, Athena queries, or intermediary queue processing, so it has the lowest operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create an EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS API calls via CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-api-call.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a web application that is based on Java and PHP. The company plans to move the application from on premises to AWS.  
  
The company needs the ability to test new site features frequently. The company also needs a highly available, managed solution that requires minimal operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable static web hosting on the S3 bucket. Upload the static content to the S3 bucket. Use AWS Lambda to process all dynamic content.
Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.
Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that are configured with Java and PHP. Use Auto Scaling groups and an Application Load Balancer to manage the website’s availability.

Containerize the web application. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to dynamically route traffic between containers that contain the new site features for testing.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Beanstalk is designed to deploy and manage web applications in supported languages such as Java and PHP while handling much of the underlying provisioning and scaling. It also supports blue/green deployments by using environment URL swapping, so a new application version can be deployed and tested in a separate environment and then promoted with a CNAME swap. That combination satisfies the need for frequent feature testing, high availability, and low operational overhead better than managing Amazon EC2 instances directly or redesigning the application around other services.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/Welcome.html) · [Elastic Beanstalk supported platforms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/platforms/platforms-supported.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on AWS that lets users upload photos and saves those photos in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to use Amazon CloudFront with a custom domain name to upload the photo files to the S3 bucket in the eu-west-1 Region.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a public certificate in the us-east-1 Region. Use the certificate in CloudFront.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a public certificate in eu-west-1. Use the certificate in CloudFront.
Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront. Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration.
Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront origin access control (OAC).
Configure Amazon S3 to allow uploads from CloudFront. Configure an Amazon S3 website endpoint.

questions.explanation:
An ACM certificate attached to a CloudFront distribution for viewer HTTPS and a custom domain must be requested or imported in us-east-1. CloudFront origin access control (OAC) supports dynamic requests, including `PUT`, to an Amazon S3 origin when the S3 bucket policy grants CloudFront the required permissions.

**Learn more:** [Requirements for using SSL/TLS certificates with CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html) · [Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application workflow that uses an AWS Lambda function to download and decrypt files from Amazon S3. These files are encrypted by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. A solutions architect must design a solution to ensure that the required permissions are configured correctly.  
  
Which combination of actions accomplishes this? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Attach the kms:decrypt permission to the Lambda function’s resource policy
Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda IAM role in the KMS key's policy
Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda resource policy in the KMS key's policy.
Create a new IAM policy with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the policy to the Lambda function.
Create a new IAM role with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the execution role to the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda accesses other AWS services by using its execution role, so the role must have an identity-based permission that allows `kms:Decrypt`. AWS KMS key usage must also be permitted for the principal in the KMS key policy, so the Lambda IAM execution role needs decrypt access in that key policy. A Lambda resource policy is for invocation and similar access to the function itself, not for granting the function permission to decrypt with KMS.

**Learn more:** [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html) · [Using IAM policies with AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/iam-policies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a three-tier ecommerce application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). All ecommerce data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instance.  
  
The company wants to optimize customer session management during transactions. The application must store session data durably.  
  
Which solutions will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Turn on the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) on the ALB.
Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store customer session information.
Deploy an Amazon Cognito user pool to manage user session information.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store customer session information.
Use AWS Systems Manager Application Manager in the application to manage user session information.

questions.explanation:
Durable session management in a load-balanced, auto-scaled web tier requires moving session state out of individual EC2 instances into a shared data store. Amazon DynamoDB provides durable persistent storage and is suitable as an external session store. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is a common centralized session store for web applications and, when configured with durability features, can retain session data beyond a single instance. ALB sticky sessions only influence request routing and do not durably store session state. Amazon Cognito focuses on user identity and authentication, and AWS Systems Manager Application Manager is an operations tool rather than an application session store.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon DynamoDB?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html) · [Managing complex workflows with DynamoDB transactions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/transactions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a Java-based job on an Amazon EC2 instance. The job runs every hour and takes 10 seconds to complete. The job runs on a scheduled interval and uses 1 GB of memory. The instance's CPU utilization is low except for brief spikes during which the job uses the maximum available CPU.  
  
The company wants to optimize the cost of running the job.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Run the job as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate with 0.5 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 1 GB of memory.
Copy the code into an AWS Lambda function that has 1 GB of memory. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to run the code each hour.
Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Install the container in the existing Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Ensure that the schedule stops the container when the task finishes.
Configure the existing schedule to stop the EC2 instance at the completion of the job and restart the EC2 instance when the next job starts.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the best fit for a short, scheduled, event-driven workload because it runs only when invoked and charges per request and execution duration instead of requiring a continuously running server. An hourly 10-second job with a 1 GB memory requirement maps well to a Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge schedule. Lambda also allocates CPU in proportion to configured memory, so short CPU bursts are handled without needing to keep an EC2 instance running. By contrast, AWS Fargate charges per second with a 1-minute minimum for each task, so it is less cost-efficient for a 10-second hourly workload, and the EC2-based options still retain unnecessary instance overhead.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function memory - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-memory.html) · [Amazon EventBridge Scheduler - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/using-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a production web application in which users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. Under a new regulatory requirement, newly uploaded documents must not be modified or deleted after they are stored.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.
Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.
Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read-only mode.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Object Lock is the AWS feature for write-once-read-many (WORM) protection. It is specifically intended to help satisfy regulatory requirements by preventing protected object versions from being overwritten or deleted for a retention period or legal hold. Because S3 Object Lock requires S3 Versioning, the correct design is to store the uploads in an S3 bucket with Versioning and Object Lock enabled.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with Object Lock - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [Configuring S3 Object Lock - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-configure.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple Microsoft Windows SMB file servers and Linux NFS file servers for file sharing in an on-premises environment. As part of its AWS migration plan, the company wants to consolidate these file servers in the AWS Cloud.  
  
The company requires a managed AWS storage service that supports both NFS and SMB access. The solution must support sharing between the protocols and provide Availability Zone-level redundancy.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage. Configure multi-protocol access.
Create two Amazon EC2 instances. Use one EC2 instance for Windows SMB file server access and one EC2 instance for Linux NFS file server access.
Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for SMB access. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre for NFS access.
Use Amazon S3 storage. Access Amazon S3 through an Amazon S3 File Gateway.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports concurrent NFS and SMB multiprotocol access to the same volume. Its Multi-AZ deployment replicates data and supports failover across multiple Availability Zones, providing the required Availability Zone-level redundancy.

**Learn more:** [Managing FSx for ONTAP volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/managing-volumes.html) · [Availability, durability, and deployment options for FSx for ONTAP](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/high-availability-AZ.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and requires the necessary permissions to complete that task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials for Amazon S3.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to grant the required permissions?

options.text: Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda functions access other AWS services by using an execution role. The role’s identity-based policy should grant the S3 actions the function needs, such as object upload permissions, and Lambda assumes that role automatically when the function runs. A Lambda resource-based policy is for allowing principals or services to invoke the function, not for granting the function permission to write to Amazon S3. AWS documentation states that functions use an execution role to access other resources and that if a function uses the AWS SDK to manage Amazon S3 resources, it needs Amazon S3 permissions in its execution role.

**Learn more:** [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html) · [How Lambda works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/concepts-basics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Systems Manager for regular administration and patching of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an IP address type target group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
New security protocols require the company to take EC2 instances out of service during patching. When the company tries to follow the security protocol during the next patch, it receives errors in the patching window.  
  
Which combination of solutions will resolve the errors? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change the target type of the target group from IP address type to instance type.
Continue to use the existing Systems Manager document without changes because it is already optimized to handle instances that are in an IP address type target group behind an ALB.
Implement the AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalanacerInstance Systems Manager Automation document to manage the patching process.
Use Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to automatically remove the instances from service to patch the instances.
Configure Systems Manager State Manager to remove the instances from service and manage the patching schedule. Use ALB health checks to re-route traffic.

questions.explanation:
The AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance Automation runbook removes an EC2 instance from its load balancer or target group, waits for connection draining, patches it with AWS-RunPatchBaseline, and reattaches it. Its workflow identifies the target by EC2 instance ID, so the ALB target group must use the instance target type rather than the IP target type, whose targets are registered by IP address.

**Learn more:** [AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance — AWS Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-awsec2-patch-load-balancer-instance.html) · [Target groups for Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff complain that the application is very slow at the beginning of the day, although it performs well by mid-morning.  
  
How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints while keeping costs to a minimum?

options.text: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.

questions.explanation:
Because the morning increase in load is predictable, the Auto Scaling group should use scheduled scaling to add capacity before users arrive. AWS documentation states that a scheduled action can set a new desired capacity at a specified time, which lets the group proactively launch instances shortly before business hours. That removes the cold-start delay seen when scaling reacts only after CPU rises. Changing thresholds and cooldowns is still reactive, and setting both minimum and maximum to 20 would unnecessarily constrain the group at full size and raise cost.

**Learn more:** [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Scaling cooldowns for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scaling-cooldowns.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company has observed performance degradation in its Amazon RDS-based web application. The degradation is caused by an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries initiated by business analysts. A solutions architect must address this issue with minimal changes to the existing web application.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS read replicas are a read-only copy of a DB instance and are specifically intended to reduce load on the primary database by routing read queries to the replica. AWS documentation explicitly identifies business reporting scenarios as a use case for running reporting queries against a read replica instead of the production DB instance. This solves a read-heavy workload with minimal application change compared with moving data to DynamoDB, ElastiCache, or Redshift.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Scaling and high availability in Amazon RDS - Getting Started Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/gettingstartedguide/scaling-ha.html)

options.text: Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy is the best fit because it improves application resilience during Aurora PostgreSQL failovers by pooling connections, automatically routing to the new writer, and avoiding DNS propagation and client reconnection delays that often extend outage time. Adding replicas can provide promotion targets but does not make failover transparent to the application, while a second cluster or ElastiCache adds unnecessary complexity or does not solve writer failover downtime.

**Learn more:** [Planning where to use RDS Proxy - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_us/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy-planning.html) · [RDS Proxy concepts and terminology - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.howitworks.html)

A company that uses AWS needs a solution to predict the resources required for manufacturing processes each month. The solution must use historical values that are currently stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has no machine learning (ML) experience and wants to use a managed service for training and generating predictions.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker model. Create a SageMaker endpoint for inference.
Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses Amazon SageMaker endpoints to create predictions based on the inputs.
Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses an Amazon Forecast predictor to create a prediction based on the inputs.
Train an Amazon Forsecast predictor by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Forecast is a fully managed time-series forecasting service that automatically builds and selects an appropriate model from historical data in S3 without requiring the user to write training code, tune algorithms, or hold machine learning expertise, which matches a team with no ML background. Training a predictor on the historical manufacturing data and then invoking it, for example from a Lambda function behind a function URL, to generate monthly predictions satisfies both the managed-service and prediction-generation requirements. Using SageMaker to deploy and train a custom model still requires the customer to design and manage the modeling process, which conflicts with having no ML experience.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Forecast? - Amazon Forecast](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/forecast/latest/dg/what-is-forecast.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is worried about the security of its public web application because of recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect must lower the risk of DDoS attacks against the application.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.
Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.
Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.

questions.explanation:
AWS Shield Advanced is the AWS service designed to protect against DDoS attacks, and it directly supports Application Load Balancers. It provides enhanced detection and mitigation for DDoS events, including application-layer protections for supported resources such as ALBs. Amazon Inspector is for vulnerability management, Amazon Macie is for sensitive-data discovery in Amazon S3, and Amazon GuardDuty detects suspicious activity but does not provide DDoS prevention for an ALB.

**Learn more:** [AWS Shield Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/shield/) · [List of resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-protections-by-resource-type.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a file-sharing application that will use an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. The company wants to deliver all files through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company does not want the files to be reachable by directly navigating to the S3 URL.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Write individual policies for each S3 bucket to grant read permission for only CloudFront access.
Create an IAM user. Grant the user read permission to objects in the S3 bucket. Assign the user to CloudFront.
Write an S3 bucket policy that assigns the CloudFront distribution ID as the Principal and assigns the target S3 bucket as the Amazon Resource Name (ARN).
Create an origin access identity (OAI). Assign the OAI to the CloudFront distribution. Configure the S3 bucket permissions so that only the OAI has read permission.

questions.explanation:
To keep Amazon S3 objects from being accessed directly while allowing delivery through CloudFront, the S3 bucket must allow read access only to CloudFront. In the answer set provided, this is done by creating an origin access identity (OAI), associating it with the CloudFront distribution, and updating the bucket permissions so only that OAI can read the objects. AWS currently recommends origin access control (OAC) for new designs, but OAI is the matching correct choice here because it is the mechanism listed that restricts S3 access to CloudFront.

**Learn more:** [Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html) · [S3OriginConfig - Amazon CloudFront API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_S3OriginConfig.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is evaluating a recent migration of a three-tier application into a VPC. The security team finds that the principle of least privilege is not being enforced for Amazon EC2 security group ingress and egress rules between the application tiers.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to fix this issue?

options.text: Create security group rules using the instance ID as the source or destination.
Create security group rules using the security group ID as the source or destination.
Create security group rules using the VPC CIDR blocks as the source or destination.
Create security group rules using the subnet CIDR blocks as the source or destination.

questions.explanation:
To enforce least privilege between application tiers, security group rules should reference the security group attached to the source tier or destination tier. AWS security groups support using a security group ID as the source or destination, which limits traffic to instances associated with that specific group instead of allowing all resources in a subnet or the entire VPC CIDR range. Instance IDs are not valid targets in security group rules.

**Learn more:** [Security group rules - Amazon VPC User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html) · [Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups - Amazon VPC User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-security-groups.html)

A company runs a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability.  
  
To maintain security compliance, the company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with:  
  
- endpoint private access set to `true`  
- endpoint public access set to `false`  
  
The company must also place the data plane in private subnets. However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster.  
  
Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?

options.text: Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.
Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.

questions.explanation:
For a private-only Amazon EKS cluster, worker nodes must communicate with the Kubernetes API server through the cluster’s private endpoint from within the VPC. AWS states that the private cluster endpoint is controlled through the cluster security group and that EKS interface VPC endpoints do not provide access to the Kubernetes API. Because the nodes remain in private subnets, the needed fix is to permit the required egress from the nodes so they can reach the control plane endpoint and complete cluster join.

**Learn more:** [Cluster API server endpoint - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/cluster-endpoint.html) · [Access Amazon EKS using AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)
