A company hosts its public ecommerce website on AWS. The website uses an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for internet traffic. The Global Accelerator accelerator forwards this traffic to an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that serves as the entry point for an Auto Scaling group.  
  
The company recently detected a DDoS attack against the website. The company needs a solution to mitigate future attacks.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL for the Global Accelerator accelerator to block traffic by using rate-based rules
Configure an AWS Lambda function to read the ALB metrics to block attacks by updating a VPC network ACL
Configure an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB to block traffic by using rate-based rules
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the Global Accelerator accelerator

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF can be associated with an Application Load Balancer, and a rate-based rule counts requests and rate-limits or blocks traffic that exceeds the configured threshold. This directly mitigates application-layer request floods at the ALB with a managed configuration. AWS WAF does not list AWS Global Accelerator as a supported web ACL association target. [AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html) [AWS WAF rate-based rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based.html)

**Learn more:** [Associating or disassociating protection with an AWS resource](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html) · [Using rate-based rule statements in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based.html)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a possible rise in cost.

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache state files at edge locations
Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files
Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files
Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user traffic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is designed to cache static web content at AWS edge locations, so repeated requests can be served from the cache instead of reaching the Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. That reduces load on the origin infrastructure and can lower overall cost for a growing static-content workload. AWS WAF is for inspecting and filtering web requests, not caching content, and an ALB does not use Amazon ElastiCache as a backend file cache. Creating another ALB in a different Region also does not solve the core need of caching static content close to users.

**Learn more:** [Amazon CloudFront Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/) · [How CloudFront delivers content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 VPC endpoint allows EC2 instances in private subnets to access S3 privately without requiring an internet gateway or NAT gateway. S3 bucket access can be restricted so requests are allowed only through the specified VPC endpoint by using a bucket policy condition such as `aws:SourceVpce`. That makes a VPC endpoint the solution that meets both the private-subnet and no-internet requirements.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Bucket policy examples using condition keys - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/amazon-s3-policy-keys.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on-premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from one central location.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS Connector is built to register and connect external Kubernetes clusters to the Amazon EKS console, where you can view cluster status, configuration, and workloads alongside Amazon EKS clusters. That directly satisfies the need for a centralized view across EKS and on-premises Kubernetes with minimal management effort. The other options either focus on monitoring data rather than unified cluster/workload visibility, use a service not intended for this purpose, or require operating an additional Kubernetes platform instead of using the managed EKS console integration.

**Learn more:** [Connect a Kubernetes cluster to an Amazon EKS Management Console with Amazon EKS Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html) · [Grant access to view Kubernetes cluster resources on an Amazon EKS console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/connector-grant-access.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is creating a new internal web application in the AWS Cloud. The application must securely store and retrieve multiple employee usernames and passwords by using an AWS managed service.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Store the employee credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use AWS CloudFormation and the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve usernames and passwords from Parameter Store.
Store the employee credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Use AWS CloudFormation and AWS Batch with the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Secrets Manager.

Store the employee credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use AWS CloudFormation and AWS Batch with the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Parameter Store.
Store the employee credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Use AWS CloudFormation and the BatchGetSecretValue API to retrieve the usernames and passwords from Secrets Manager.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager securely manages credentials, and its `BatchGetSecretValue` API retrieves the encrypted values of up to 20 secrets in one operation. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store instead uses APIs such as `GetParameter` and `GetParameters`, not `BatchGetSecretValue`. AWS Batch is unnecessary for secret retrieval and adds operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [BatchGetSecretValue - AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_BatchGetSecretValue.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon Aurora database. The EC2 instances connect to the database by using user names and passwords stored locally in a file.  
  
The company wants to minimize the operational overhead of credential management.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

options.text: Use AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation.
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Migrate the credential file to the S3 bucket. Point the application to the S3 bucket.

Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for each EC2 instance. Attach the new EBS volume to each EC2 instance. Migrate the credential file to the new EBS volume. Point the application to the new EBS volume.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the correct service for database credentials because it is designed to store, retrieve, and rotate secrets such as Aurora user names and passwords. Enabling automatic rotation reduces ongoing credential-management effort and avoids keeping static credentials in local files on EC2 instances. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store can store encrypted values, but AWS recommends Secrets Manager when automatic rotation is required. Storing the file in Amazon S3 or on encrypted Amazon EBS volumes improves storage handling only; it does not provide managed secret rotation or materially reduce credential-management overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Rotation schedules - AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_schedule.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed its application on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS database. The company used the principle of least privilege to configure the database access credentials.  
  
The company's security team wants to protect the application and the database from SQL injection and other web-based attacks.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use security groups and network ACLs to secure the database and application servers.
Use AWS WAF to protect the application. Use RDS parameter groups to configure the security settings.
Use AWS Network Firewall to protect the application and the database.
Use different database accounts in the application code for different functions. Avoid granting excessive privileges to the database users.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is purpose-built to detect and block application-layer attacks including SQL injection at the web application edge using managed rule groups and custom rules. RDS parameter groups configure database engine behavior but do not protect against web-based attacks. Network-layer controls (security groups, NACLs) operate at the traffic level and cannot inspect malicious SQL patterns. Separate database accounts follow defense-in-depth principles but do not stop attack ingestion.

**Learn more:** [SQL injection attack rule statement (AWS WAF)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-sqli-match.html) · [Working with DB parameter groups (Amazon RDS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithParamGroups.html)

A company creates dedicated AWS accounts in AWS Organizations for its business units. Recently, an important notification was sent to the root user email address of a business unit account instead of the assigned account owner. The company wants to ensure that all future notifications can be sent to different employees based on the notification categories of billing, operations, or security.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST securely**?

options.text: Configure each AWS account to use a single email address that the company manages. Ensure that all account owners can access the email account to receive notifications. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.

Configure each AWS account to use a different email distribution list for each business unit that the company manages. Configure each distribution list with administrator email addresses that can respond to alerts. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.

Configure each AWS account root user email address to be the individual company managed email address of one person from each business unit. Configure alternate contacts for each AWS account with corresponding distribution lists for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team for each business unit.

Configure each AWS account root user to use email aliases that go to a centralized mailbox. Configure alternate contacts for each account by using a single business managed email distribution list each for the billing team, the security team, and the operations team.

questions.explanation:
AWS guidance is to avoid tying an account's root user contact to a single individual; each account's root user should instead use an email alias that forwards to a centralized, monitored mailbox, which keeps root notifications from being lost or from being tied to one employee's inbox. Configuring the account's alternate contacts for billing, operations, and security with dedicated, company-managed distribution lists then ensures future notifications are routed by category to the right team regardless of staff turnover, which directly satisfies the requirement without loosening control over the sensitive root identity. Granting multiple account owners shared access to one mailbox, or assigning the root email to a specific person, both introduce unnecessary exposure or a single point of failure compared with this approach.

**Learn more:** [Update the alternate contacts for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-update-contact-alternate.html) · [Root user best practices for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html)

A company stores a large volume of image files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The images must remain readily available for the first 180 days. For the following 180 days, the images are accessed infrequently. After 360 days, the images must be archived, but they still need to be instantly available on request. After 5 years, only auditors will access the images, and the auditors must be able to retrieve them within 12 hours. The images must not be lost at any point during this process.  
  
A developer will use S3 Standard storage for the initial 180 days. The developer must configure an S3 Lifecycle rule.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.

questions.explanation:
S3 Standard-IA is the appropriate transition after 180 days because it is designed for infrequently accessed data while preserving multi-Availability Zone resilience. S3 One Zone-IA is cheaper, but it stores objects in only one Availability Zone, so it does not satisfy the requirement that the images cannot be lost during the lifecycle. For the archive phase after 360 days, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is the correct class because archived objects must still be available immediately; S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires a restore operation and is intended when immediate access is not needed. After 5 years, S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost archival class that still supports retrieval within about 12 hours, matching the auditor requirement.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Data protection in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html)

A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it expects high traffic to the application at launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.

questions.explanation:
For Amazon ECS services running on Fargate, scaling the number of running tasks is done by AWS Application Auto Scaling, not Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, because Fargate removes instance management. Target tracking policies are designed to automatically adjust the ECS service desired task count to keep CPU or memory utilization near a specified target, which matches the need to scale out during heavy launch traffic and scale in later to lower cost. AWS documentation for ECS service auto scaling states that target tracking is supported for ECS services and that Application Auto Scaling creates and manages the CloudWatch alarms used by the policy.

**Learn more:** [Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html) · [Use a target metric to scale Amazon ECS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-autoscaling-targettracking.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has two VPCs in the **us-west-2** Region within the same AWS account. The company must allow network traffic between these VPCs. About **500 GB** of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month.  
  
What is the **MOST cost-effective** solution to connect these VPCs?

options.text: Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.
Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.
Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.
Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.

questions.explanation:
For two VPCs in the same account and same Region, a VPC peering connection is the lowest-cost native choice for direct inter-VPC connectivity. AWS documentation describes VPC peering as commonly used to connect a small number of VPCs within a Region, whereas AWS Transit Gateway is aimed at larger-scale hub-and-spoke connectivity and adds attachment and per-GB data-processing charges. AWS Site-to-Site VPN also adds hourly connection cost, and AWS Direct Connect adds port-hour charges and is intended for on-premises-to-AWS connectivity rather than connecting two VPCs in one Region. Updating each VPC route table to send the other VPC's CIDR through the peering connection completes the design.

**Learn more:** [Create a VPC peering connection - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/create-vpc-peering-connection.html) · [Amazon VPC Announces Pricing Change for VPC Peering](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2021/05/amazon-vpc-announces-pricing-change-for-vpc-peering/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The company needs to ensure that Kubernetes service accounts in the EKS cluster have secure, granular access to specific AWS resources by using IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA).  
  
Which combination of solutions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an IAM policy that defines the required permissions Attach the policy directly to the IAM role of the EKS nodes.
Implement network policies within the EKS cluster to prevent Kubernetes service accounts from accessing specific AWS services.
Modify the EKS cluster's IAM role to include permissions for each Kubernetes service account. Ensure a one-to-one mapping between IAM roles and Kubernetes roles.
Define an IAM role that includes the necessary permissions. Annotate the Kubernetes service accounts with the Amazon ResourceName (ARN) of the IAM role.
Set up a trust relationship between the IAM roles for the service accounts and an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider.

questions.explanation:
IRSA associates a Kubernetes service account with an IAM role that carries only its required AWS permissions. The IAM role’s trust policy must trust the EKS cluster’s IAM OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider and restrict web-identity assumption to the intended service account. The service account is annotated with the IAM role ARN (`eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`).

**Learn more:** [Assign IAM roles to Kubernetes service accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/associate-service-account-role.html) · [Create an IAM OIDC provider for your cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a security solution for a company that wants to provide developers with individual AWS accounts through AWS Organizations, while still maintaining standard security controls.  
  
Because the individual developers will have AWS account root user-level access to their own accounts, the solutions architect wants to ensure that the mandatory AWS CloudTrail configuration applied to new developer accounts cannot be changed.  
  
Which action meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM policy that prohibits changes to CloudTrail. and attach it to the root user.
Create a new trail in CloudTrail from within the developer accounts with the organization trails option enabled.
Create a service control policy (SCP) that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it the developer accounts.
Create a service-linked role for CloudTrail with a policy condition that allows changes only from an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the management account.

questions.explanation:
A service control policy (SCP) is the correct control because SCPs set the maximum available permissions for an AWS Organizations member account and apply to all principals in that account, including the root user. AWS CloudTrail organization trails are created from the management account or a delegated administrator account, are automatically applied to member accounts, and member accounts can see them but cannot modify or delete them. An SCP that denies CloudTrail modification actions on the developer accounts preserves the mandatory logging configuration even when developers have root-level access.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [Working with CloudTrail trails - AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-trails.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use NAT gateways in its AWS environment. The company's Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets must be able to connect to the public internet through the NAT gateways.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create public NAT gateways in the same private subnets as the EC2 instances.
Create private NAT gateways in the same private subnets as the EC2 instances.
Create public NAT gateways in public subnets in the same VPCs as the EC2 instances.
Create private NAT gateways in public subnets in the same VPCs as the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
To provide outbound internet access for Amazon EC2 instances that are in private subnets, AWS uses a **public NAT gateway** placed in a **public subnet**. The private subnet's route table sends internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway, and the NAT gateway reaches the internet through the VPC's internet gateway. A private NAT gateway is intended for private connectivity scenarios, such as communication across VPCs or with on-premises networks, not for public internet access.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateway use cases - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html) · [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must design the architecture for an application that a vendor supplies as a Docker container image. The container requires **50 GB of storage** for temporary files to be available.  
  
The infrastructure must be **serverless**.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon S3 mounted volume that has more than 50 GB of space.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Create a task definition for the container image with an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create a service with that task definition.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space. Create a task definition for the container image. Create a service with that task definition.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda can use container images, but its writable temporary storage is limited to `/tmp` with a maximum of 10,240 MB, so it cannot provide the required 50 GB. Amazon ECS with the AWS Fargate launch type is a serverless container platform, and ECS tasks can use Amazon EFS for shared persistent storage that can exceed 50 GB without managing servers. An ECS cluster using the EC2 launch type would add instance-management overhead and is not serverless. Therefore, the correct design is ECS on Fargate with an EFS volume.

**Learn more:** [Configure ephemeral storage for Lambda functions - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-ephemeral-storage.html) · [Create a Lambda function using a container image - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a shared storage solution for a media application hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company requires the ability for SMB clients to access the data. The solution must be fully managed.  
  
Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Configure tapes to use Amazon S3. Connect the application server to the tape gateway.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed Windows file storage with native support for the SMB protocol, which matches both the SMB-access and fully managed requirements. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block storage rather than SMB shares, Tape Gateway is designed for backup and archive workflows, and a Windows file server on Amazon EC2 requires customer management of the instance and file services rather than providing a fully managed storage service.

**Learn more:** [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [What is Volume Gateway?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company must run a scheduled daily job to aggregate and filter sales records for analytics. The company stores the sales records in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each object can be as large as 10 GB. Depending on the number of sales events, the job might take up to an hour to finish. The job's CPU and memory requirements are constant and known ahead of time.  
  
A solutions architect needs to minimize the operational effort required for this job to run.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that has an Amazon EventBridge notification. Schedule the EventBridge event to run once a day.

Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, and integrate the API with the function. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that calls the API and invokes the function.
Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type and an Auto Scaling group with at least one EC2 instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is not an appropriate fit because a Lambda invocation can run for at most 15 minutes, while this batch job can take up to 1 hour. An Amazon ECS scheduled task on AWS Fargate satisfies the runtime and resource requirements and minimizes operations because Fargate is serverless for containers, so there are no EC2 instances or cluster capacity to manage. EventBridge Scheduler can directly launch ECS tasks on a schedule, making it a good match for a once-per-day batch process that has known CPU and memory needs.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function timeout - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html) · [Using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to schedule Amazon ECS tasks - Amazon Elastic Container Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/tasks-scheduled-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

A company runs a web application on AWS on a single Amazon EC2 instance that stores user-uploaded documents on an Amazon EBS volume.  
  
To improve scalability and availability, the company duplicated the architecture and created a second EC2 instance and EBS volume in another Availability Zone, and placed both instances behind an Application Load Balancer.  
  
After this change was completed, users reported that every time they refreshed the website, they could see either one subset of their documents or the other, but never all of the documents at the same time.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend so that users can see all of their documents at once?

options.text: Copy the data so both EBS volumes contain all the documents
Configure the Application Load Balancer to direct a user to the server with the documents
Copy the data from both EBS volumes to Amazon EFS. Modify the application to save new documents to Amazon EFS
Configure the Application Load Balancer to send the request to both servers. Return each document from the correct server

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS volumes are block devices attached to EC2 instances within a single Availability Zone, so storing user files separately on two instance-specific EBS volumes causes inconsistent results when the load balancer sends requests to different servers. Amazon EFS is a shared file system that multiple EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones in the same Region can mount concurrently, so moving the documents to EFS and writing new uploads there gives both application servers access to the same complete document set.

**Learn more:** [Attach an Amazon EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-attaching-volume.html) · [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A gaming company is designing a highly available architecture. The application runs on a modified Linux kernel and supports only UDP-based traffic. The company needs the front-end tier to provide the best possible user experience. That tier must:  
  
- have low latency,  
- route traffic to the nearest edge location, and  
- provide static IP addresses for entry into the application endpoints.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in AWS Application Auto Scaling.
Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in an AWS Application Auto Scaling group.
Configure AWS Global Accelerator to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
Configure Amazon API Gateway to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct front-end service because it provides fixed anycast static IP addresses and accepts traffic at the AWS edge location closest to the user, improving latency and user experience. Because the application supports only UDP traffic, the traffic should be forwarded to a Network Load Balancer, which supports UDP listeners; an Application Load Balancer does not meet that protocol requirement. Since the application runs on a modified Linux kernel, it should run on Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group rather than AWS Lambda.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [What is AWS Global Accelerator?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)

options.text: Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure one or more subscribers to read events from the SQS queue.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the SNS topic.
Configure an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API to write to a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the data stream.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the topic.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SNS topics provide managed one-to-many pub/sub delivery: publishing a message to a topic delivers it to every subscribed endpoint. API Gateway HTTP APIs can invoke Lambda and are designed with a smaller feature set and lower cost than REST APIs, making an HTTP API plus Lambda and an SNS topic the most cost-effective listed pub/sub architecture.

**Learn more:** [API Gateway HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api.html) · [Amazon SNS Publish API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/api/API_Publish.html)

A company is planning a shared storage solution for a gaming application hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company requires that SMB clients be able to access the data. The solution also must be fully managed.  
  
Which AWS solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed AWS file storage service that provides native SMB access for shared file storage. It is specifically designed for Windows-compatible file workloads and removes the need to build and administer your own file server infrastructure. That makes it the correct fit for a fully managed shared storage solution that must support SMB clients.

**Learn more:** [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [Accessing your data - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a database in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Because transaction volume has increased, the database support team reports slow read performance on the DB instance and recommends adding a read replica.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take **before** implementing this change? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Enable binlog replication on the RDS primary node.
Choose a failover priority for the source DB instance.
Allow long-running transactions to complete on the source DB instance.
Create a global table and specify the AWS Regions where the table will be available.
Enable automatic backups on the source instance by setting the backup retention period to a value other than 0.

questions.explanation:
Before creating an Amazon RDS for MySQL read replica, the source DB instance must have automated backups enabled, which requires setting the backup retention period to a value other than 0. AWS also recommends allowing any active long-running transactions on the source DB instance to finish first, because they can slow the creation of the read replica. These are the documented prerequisites and preparation steps for RDS for MySQL read replicas.

**Learn more:** [Working with MySQL read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_MySQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.html) · [Creating a read replica - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Create.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage AWS accounts that host applications. The company creates a dedicated monitoring member account in the organization. The company wants to query and visualize observability data across the accounts by using Amazon CloudWatch.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability for the monitoring account. Deploy an AWS CloudFormation template provided by the monitoring account in each AWS account to share the data with the monitoring account.
Set up service control policies (SCPs) to provide access to CloudWatch in the monitoring account under the Organizations root organizational unit (OU).

Configure a new IAM user in the monitoring account. In each AWS account, configure an IAM policy to have access to query and visualize the CloudWatch data in the account. Attach the new IAM policy to the new IAM user.
Create a new IAM user in the monitoring account. Create cross-account IAM policies in each AWS account. Attach the IAM policies to the new IAM user.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch cross-account observability is the correct solution for centralized querying and visualization of observability data across AWS accounts. In this model, you configure a monitoring account and then link source accounts so their metrics, logs, traces, and other supported telemetry can be viewed from that monitoring account. AWS documentation specifically supports Organizations-based onboarding and provides a CloudFormation template from the monitoring account to deploy in source accounts or across an organization/OU, which is what enables the sharing relationship. SCPs cannot provide this telemetry-sharing setup, and standalone IAM users with cross-account policies do not implement CloudWatch cross-account observability.

**Learn more:** [CloudWatch cross-account observability - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account.html) · [Link monitoring accounts with source accounts - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Unified-Cross-Account-Setup.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables.  
  
A solutions architect needs to provide the application with the ability to retrieve the data with no effect on the application's baseline performance.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST operationally efficient** way?

options.text: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers
Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions
Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions
Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector

questions.explanation:
AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers are built to resolve a single request by invoking multiple functions in sequence across multiple data sources, including Amazon DynamoDB tables. That makes them a strong fit for aggregating data from several DynamoDB tables without adding custom compute logic into the application path. This approach is more operationally efficient than building and maintaining Lambda-based aggregation behind API Gateway, and it is more appropriate for application-serving workloads than Athena Federated Query, which is intended for federated SQL access and analytics rather than low-latency transactional retrieval.

**Learn more:** [Resolver - AWS AppSync API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/APIReference/API_Resolver.html) · [Configuring and using pipeline resolvers in AWS AppSync (VTL)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/devguide/pipeline-resolvers.html)

A company wants to deploy an internal web application on AWS. The web application must be accessible only from the company's office. The company also needs to download security patches for the web application from the internet.  
  
The company has created a VPC and configured an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the company's office. A solutions architect must design a secure architecture for the web application.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to 0.0.0.0/0.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in public subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to the company's office network CIDR block.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in private subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPSet the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to the company's office network CIDR block.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to 0.0.0.0/0.

questions.explanation:
An internal Application Load Balancer keeps the application private to the VPC and connected networks, including an on-premises office reached through AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Hosting the EC2 instances in private subnets prevents direct internet access, while NAT gateways in public subnets with an attached internet gateway provide outbound-only internet connectivity so the instances can download patches without accepting unsolicited inbound traffic. Limiting the ALB security group's inbound source to the company's office network CIDR ensures access is restricted to the office network.

**Learn more:** [Internal and internet-facing load balancers in the Elastic Load Balancing User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html) · [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html)

A company must migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs **24 hours a day, 7 days a week**. The application's database storage continues to increase over time.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.

questions.explanation:
For a workload that runs continuously, Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances are more economical than On-Demand pricing, while Spot Instances are not appropriate because capacity can be interrupted. For the database tier, Amazon Aurora is a relational managed database service whose storage automatically expands as data grows, and using Reserved Instances for a steady-state database workload is more cost-effective than On-Demand pricing. This combination best matches both the always-on runtime requirement and the growing database storage requirement at the lowest cost.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/reserved-instances/pricing/) · [Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to try using individual AWS accounts for its engineering team. The company wants to be notified as soon as Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month goes over a specific threshold for each account.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly. Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets is designed to track monthly cost or usage against a defined threshold and send alerts when the threshold is exceeded. A cost budget can be created for each account, scoped with filters such as the Amazon EC2 service, set to a monthly period, and configured to send notifications through Amazon SNS. This directly matches the requirement with minimal operational overhead and lower cost than building a custom reporting pipeline with Cost and Usage Reports, Athena, and EventBridge. Official AWS documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-cost-budget.html

**Learn more:** [Creating a cost budget - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-cost-budget.html) · [Budget filters - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-create-filters.html)

A company needs to replicate existing data and ongoing data changes from an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. The volume of data to replicate changes throughout the day. The company wants to use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) for replication. The solution must provision only the capacity required by the replication instance.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Configure the AWS DMS replication instance with a Multi-AZ deployment to provision instances across multiple Availability Zones.
Create an AWS DMS Serverless replication task to analyze and replicate the data while provisioning the required capacity.
Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale the size of the AWS DMS replication instance up or down based on the amount of data toreplicate.

Provision AWS DMS replication capacity by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type to analyze and replicate the data while provisioning the required capacity.

questions.explanation:
AWS DMS Serverless analyzes the replication workload, computes and provisions the required capacity, and automatically scales the underlying replication resources to adapt to changing workloads. It therefore supports variable replication demand without managing a fixed-capacity DMS replication instance.

**Learn more:** [Working with AWS DMS Serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Serverless.html) · [AWS DMS Serverless components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Serverless.Components.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure. The company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation is the correct automation service because it provisions and manages infrastructure as code from templates, enabling consistent automated deployment of systems and network resources. AWS Config is the correct auditing service because it records resource configurations, captures configuration changes as they occur, and retains configuration history so teams can track and audit incremental infrastructure changes over time. AWS Organizations does not provision infrastructure, and AWS Service Catalog is for managing approved products rather than recording detailed configuration change history.

**Learn more:** [What is CloudFormation? - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html) · [How AWS Config Works - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/how-does-config-work.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large company wants to provide its globally distributed developers with separate, limited-size, managed PostgreSQL databases for development purposes. The databases will have low volume, and the developers need them only when they are actively working.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Give the developers the ability to launch separate Amazon Aurora instances. Set up a process to shut down Aurora instances at the end of the workday and to start Aurora instances at the beginning of the next workday.
Develop an AWS Service Catalog product that enforces size restrictions for launching Amazon Aurora instances. Give the developers access to launch the product when they need a development database.
Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless cluster. Develop an AWS Service Catalog product to launch databases in the cluster with the default capacity settings. Grant the developers access to the product.
Monitor AWS Trusted Advisor checks for idle Amazon RDS databases. Create a process to terminate identified idle RDS databases.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Serverless is designed for intermittent and unpredictable workloads, including Aurora PostgreSQL, and can automatically scale capacity down to 0 ACUs and pause when there are no user connections, so compute charges stop while the database is idle. Using AWS Service Catalog to provision access also supports controlled, limited self-service database creation for developers. That combination best satisfies the need for separate managed development databases that are low volume and used only during active work periods.

**Learn more:** [Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2-auto-pause.html) · [Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an application. The company stores application test data in multiple on-premises locations.  
  
The company must connect the on-premises locations to VPCs in an AWS Region in the AWS Cloud. The number of accounts and VPCs will grow over the next year. The network architecture must simplify the administration of new connections and must provide scalability.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Create a VPN connection between the VPCs and the on-premises locations.
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. On the instance, include VPN software that uses a VPN connection to connect all VPCs and on-premises locations.
Create a transit gateway. Create VPC attachments for the VPC connections. Create VPN attachments for the on-premises connections.
Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises locations and a central VPC. Connect the central VPC to other VPCs by using peering connections.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is the scalable hub-and-spoke networking service for connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. AWS documentation states that a transit gateway lets you attach VPCs and VPN connections, works across AWS accounts, and can serve as a centralized router for VPCs and Site-to-Site VPN connections. This central attachment model reduces the complexity and operational overhead that come from managing many VPC peering links or individual VPN connections as the environment grows.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html) · [How AWS Transit Gateway works - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must store its accounting records in Amazon S3.  
  
The records must:  
  
- be immediately accessible for 1 year  
- then be archived for an additional 9 years  
- not be deletable by anyone at the company, including administrative users and root users, during the entire 10-year period  
- be stored with maximum resiliency  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Object Lock in compliance mode provides WORM protection that prevents object versions from being overwritten or deleted by any user, including the AWS account root user, for the defined retention period. S3 Lifecycle can keep the records in S3 Standard for immediate access and then transition them after 1 year to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term archiving. This also preserves high resiliency because S3 Standard and S3 Glacier Deep Archive store data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones, whereas S3 One Zone-IA uses only a single Availability Zone and governance mode can be bypassed by authorized users.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with Object Lock - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [Object Lock considerations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-managing.html)

A company must use cryptographic keys in its on-premises key manager. Because of regulatory and compliance requirements, the key manager is outside the AWS Cloud. The company wants to manage encryption and decryption by using cryptographic keys that remain outside the AWS Cloud and that support a range of external key managers from different vendors.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS CloudHSM key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster.
Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store backed by an external key manager.
Use the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed key store.
Use a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster.

questions.explanation:
An AWS KMS external key store (XKS) lets AWS KMS use keys that are retained in an external key manager outside AWS, with encryption and decryption operations performed through that external system. This directly satisfies the requirement to keep key material on premises and outside the AWS Cloud, while supporting external key managers from different vendors. CloudHSM-based custom key stores place key material in an AWS CloudHSM cluster that the customer must operate in AWS, so they do not meet the outside-of-AWS requirement and involve more administration.

**Learn more:** [KMS keys in external key stores - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/keystore-external-key-manage.html) · [External key stores - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/keystore-external.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises SFTP file transfer solution. The company is migrating to the AWS Cloud to scale the file transfer solution and to optimize costs by using Amazon S3. The company's employees will use their credentials from the on-premises Microsoft Active Directory (AD) to access the new solution. The company wants to retain the current authentication and file access mechanisms.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Configure an S3 File Gateway. Create SMB file shares on the file gateway that use the existing Active Directory to authenticate.
Configure an Auto Scaling group with Amazon EC2 instances to run an SFTP solution. Configure the group to scale up at 60% CPU utilization.
Create an AWS Transfer Family server with SFTP endpoints. Choose the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider. Use AD Connector to connect the on-premises Active Directory.
Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint. Configure the endpoint to use the AWS Directory Service option as the identity provider to connect to the existing Active Directory.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP service integrated with Amazon S3 backend, eliminating operational overhead of managing SFTP servers. It supports AWS Directory Service with AD Connector, which connects to on-premises Active Directory for user authentication, preserving existing AD credentials. This approach requires the least operational overhead compared to maintaining EC2-based SFTP servers or configuring S3 File Gateway for SMB access (which doesn't offer SFTP).

**Learn more:** [Using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Transfer Family)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/directory-services-users.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is planning a new web service that will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer.  
  
However, many of the web service clients can reach only IP addresses that are authorized on their firewalls.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet the clients' needs?

options.text: A Network Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
An Application Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
An A record in an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone pointing to an Elastic IP address.
An EC2 instance with a public IP address running as a proxy in front of the load balancer.

questions.explanation:
An internet-facing Network Load Balancer is the ELB option designed for static IP addressing. AWS documentation states that a Network Load Balancer gets a static IP address for each enabled Availability Zone and can optionally associate one Elastic IP address per subnet, which lets clients allowlist fixed addresses on their firewalls. An Application Load Balancer does not use customer-associated Elastic IPs in this way, so it does not meet the requirement for fixed allowlisted client destinations.

**Learn more:** [How Elastic Load Balancing works - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html) · [What is a Network Load Balancer? - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A pharmaceutical company is developing a new drug. The volume of data the company generates has increased exponentially over the last few months. The company's researchers regularly need a subset of the full dataset to be available immediately with minimal lag. However, the complete dataset does not need to be accessed every day. All data currently resides in on-premises storage arrays, and the company wants to reduce ongoing capital expenses.  
  
Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Run AWS DataSync as a scheduled cron job to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket on an ongoing basis.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with cached volumes with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the on-premises environment to AWS. Migrate data to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with **cached volumes** stores the primary dataset in Amazon S3 and keeps a locally cached subset of frequently accessed data on premises for low-latency access. That matches the need for researchers to access only part of the dataset immediately while allowing the full dataset to reside cost-effectively in AWS instead of expanding on-premises storage. AWS documents that cached volumes let you retain frequently accessed data locally while storing the full volume data in Amazon S3, which is designed to reduce the need to scale on-premises storage infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsVGW.html) · [AWS Storage Gateway features](https://aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/features/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an application to support customer demands. The company wants to deploy the application on multiple Amazon EC2 Nitro-based instances in the same Availability Zone. The company also wants the application to be able to write to multiple block storage volumes across multiple EC2 Nitro-based instances at the same time to achieve higher application availability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
Use Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
Use General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS Multi-Attach allows a single EBS volume to be attached to multiple Nitro-based EC2 instances within the same Availability Zone simultaneously. AWS documentation states that Multi-Attach is supported for Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes, including io2, while gp2, gp3, and st1 do not support Multi-Attach. Therefore, a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volume with Amazon EBS Multi-Attach satisfies the requirement for concurrent write access from multiple Nitro-based instances.

**Learn more:** [Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html) · [Amazon EBS volume types - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volume-types.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online retail company has more than 50 million active customers and receives more than 25,000 orders each day. The company collects customer purchase data and stores this data in Amazon S3. Additional customer data is stored in Amazon RDS.  
  
The company wants to make all the data available to various teams so the teams can perform analytics. The solution must provide the ability to manage fine-grained permissions for the data and must minimize operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the purchase data to write directly to Amazon RDS. Use RDS access controls to limit access.
Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon RDS to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler. Use Amazon Athena to query the data. Use S3 policies to limit access.
Create a data lake by using AWS Lake Formation. Create an AWS Glue JDBC connection to Amazon RDS. Register the S3 bucket in Lake Formation. Use Lake Formation access controls to limit access.
Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift access controls to limit access.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lake Formation is built to create and govern data lakes on Amazon S3 with centralized fine-grained access control for Data Catalog resources and underlying S3 data. AWS documentation also states that Lake Formation can import data from databases such as Amazon RDS by using AWS Glue connections/JDBC. That makes it the lowest-operational-overhead option for exposing both S3 and RDS-sourced data for analytics while enforcing fine-grained permissions from a single service.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Lake Formation?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/what-is-lake-formation.html) · [Creating a data lake from a JDBC source in Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/getting-started-tutorial-jdbc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company generates batch data from multiple databases.  
  
The company also generates real-time streaming data from network sensors and application APIs.  
  
The company must consolidate all the data in a single location for business analytics. It needs to process the incoming data and then stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets. Teams will later run one-time queries and import the data into a business intelligence tool to display key performance indicators (KPIs).  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
Create custom AWS Lambda functions to move the individual records from the databases to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Use an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the data into JSON format. Load the data into multiple Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) clusters.

Use blueprints in AWS Lake Formation to identify the data that can be ingested into a data lake. Use AWS Glue to crawl the source, extract the data, and load the data into Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lake Formation blueprints and AWS Glue are designed to ingest data from multiple sources into an Amazon S3 data lake, with Glue workflows/crawlers handling discovery and loading, and Parquet providing an efficient analytics format for downstream querying. For the querying and visualization layer, Amazon Athena is the serverless service for running ad hoc SQL directly against data in Amazon S3, and Amazon QuickSight integrates with Athena to build KPI dashboards. This combination matches the required S3-based staging architecture while minimizing infrastructure management.

**Learn more:** [Blueprints and workflows in Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/workflows-about.html) · [Using AWS Lake Formation with AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/glue-features-lf.html)

A development team uses multiple AWS accounts for its development, staging, and production environments. Team members have been launching large Amazon EC2 instances that are underutilized. A solutions architect must stop large instances from being launched in all accounts.  
  
How can the solutions architect meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Update the IAM policies to deny the launch of large EC2 instances. Apply the policies to all users.
Define a resource in AWS Resource Access Manager that prevents the launch of large EC2 instances.
Create an IAM role in each account that denies the launch of large EC2 instances. Grant the developers IAM group access to the role.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the management account with the default policy. Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the launch of large EC2 instances, and apply it to the AWS accounts.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations service control policies (SCPs) provide centralized guardrails across multiple AWS accounts by limiting the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles in those accounts. An SCP that denies `ec2:RunInstances` for disallowed instance types can be attached to the relevant accounts or OUs, enforcing the restriction consistently in development, staging, and production with minimal per-account or per-user administration. IAM policies or roles in each account require distributed management, and AWS Resource Access Manager is not the mechanism used to block EC2 instance launches.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [SCP syntax - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_syntax.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a containerized application on premises and plans to move the application to AWS. The application is expected to have thousands of users shortly after deployment. The company is not sure how to manage container deployment at scale. The company must deploy the containerized application in a highly available architecture while minimizing operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.

Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Amazon EC2 launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.

Store container images in a repository that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Run the containers on EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Monitor the average CPU utilization in Amazon CloudWatch. Launch new EC2 instances as needed.

Create an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that contains the container image. Launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale out EC2 instances when the average CPU utilization threshold is breached.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS with the AWS Fargate launch type is the managed, serverless container option that removes the need to provision and manage EC2 worker nodes, which best minimizes operational overhead. Amazon ECS services can run tasks across multiple Availability Zones for high availability, and ECS Service Auto Scaling supports target tracking policies to automatically increase or decrease the number of running tasks based on demand. Using Amazon ECR for container images is the standard AWS-managed registry for this architecture. EC2-based approaches add instance management responsibility and therefore do not minimize operational overhead as effectively as Fargate does.

**Learn more:** [Amazon ECS launch types and capacity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-launch-type-comparison.html) · [Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)
