lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect wants to use the following JSON text as an identity-based policy to grant specific permissions:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783644182948-5elrl3d5.png)  
  
Which IAM principals can the solutions architect attach this policy to? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Role
Group
Organization
Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) resource
Amazon EC2 resource

questions.explanation:
An IAM identity-based policy can be attached only to IAM identities, specifically users, groups, or roles. From the listed options, **groups** and **roles** are the valid attachment targets. AWS resources such as Amazon EC2 or Amazon ECS are not direct attachment targets for IAM identity-based policies, and an AWS Organization is not an IAM identity for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [IAM identities (users, groups, roles)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id.html) · [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company runs a PostgreSQL database on premises. The database stores data by using high-IOPS Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) block storage. The daily peak I/O transactions per second do not exceed **15,000 IOPS**. The company wants to migrate the database to **Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL** and provision disk IOPS performance **independently of disk storage capacity**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
Configure the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
Configure the EBS magnetic volume type to achieve maximum IOPS.

questions.explanation:
For Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, General Purpose SSD **gp3** supports provisioning IOPS separately from allocated storage capacity, which directly satisfies the independence requirement. It is also the more cost-effective choice than Provisioned IOPS **io1** for a workload whose peak demand is only **15,000 IOPS**. By contrast, **gp2** ties performance to storage size and burst behavior rather than separately provisioned IOPS, and magnetic storage does not provide the needed SSD performance characteristics.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS DB instance storage - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html) · [Modifying settings for General Purpose SSD (gp3) storage - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.gp3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has arranged the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs).  
  
The solutions architect needs a solution to identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution must also notify the company's operations team about any changes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower continuously and automatically detects governance drift, including changes to the organizational-unit hierarchy such as accounts moving between OUs, and surfaces these as Amazon SNS notifications aggregated in the audit account (or via EventBridge on newer landing zones). Provisioning accounts with Control Tower and subscribing the operations team to the drift notifications meets the requirement with the least operational overhead because the detection and notification are built in. Option C (Service Catalog plus a CloudTrail organization trail) and option D (CloudFormation drift detection on a stack) both require building custom parsing/alerting pipelines, and CloudFormation drift detection does not track the Organizations OU hierarchy. Option B's AWS Config aggregated rules would require authoring and maintaining custom rules.

**Learn more:** [Detect and resolve drift in AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/drift.html) · [Types of governance drift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/governance-drift.html)

Provisioning accounts with Control Tower and subscribing the operations team to the drift notifications meets the requirement with the least operational overhead because the detection and notification are built in. A company sells datasets to customers who conduct research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the `us-east-1` Region. The company runs a web application that customers use to buy access to a specific dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is completed, customers receive an S3 signed URL that permits access to the files.  
  
The customers are located across North America and Europe. The company wants to lower the cost associated with data transfers while maintaining or improving performance.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.

Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.

Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the correct solution because it distributes large downloadable objects through edge locations near users in North America and Europe, which improves download performance, and Amazon S3 data transfer out to CloudFront is not charged, which helps reduce transfer cost. Because the files must remain private and customers currently receive time-limited access, CloudFront signed URLs are the appropriate replacement for S3 signed URLs when CloudFront sits in front of the S3 bucket. S3 Transfer Acceleration is intended to speed long-distance transfers to S3 and can add transfer charges, cross-Region replication adds replication and storage cost, and streaming the files through EC2 and the load balancer would increase application-path data transfer and reduce scalability.

**Learn more:** [AWS Billing reports for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/aws-billing-reports.html) · [Use signed URLs - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html)

A company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt AWS Lambda environment variables. A solutions architect must make sure the necessary permissions exist so the environment variables can be decrypted and used.  
  
Which steps must the solutions architect take to implement the correct permissions? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda resource policy.
Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role.
Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda function policy.
Allow the Lambda execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.
Allow the Lambda resource policy in the AWS KMS key policy.

questions.explanation:
When AWS Lambda environment variables are encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key, the function’s execution role is the identity that needs permission to use AWS KMS at runtime, including `kms:Decrypt`. AWS KMS also requires the key policy to allow that principal to use the key, either directly or by enabling IAM policy-based access. Therefore the correct implementation is to grant AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role and allow that execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.

**Learn more:** [Securing Lambda environment variables - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-envvars-encryption.html) · [Defining Lambda function permissions with an execution role - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a VPC. The application processes logs that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The EC2 instance must access the S3 bucket without internet connectivity.  
  
Which solution provides private network connectivity to Amazon S3?

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint to the S3 bucket.
Stream the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the logs to the S3 bucket.
Create an instance profile on Amazon EC2 to allow S3 access.
Create an Amazon API Gateway API with a private link to access the S3 endpoint.

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 provides private connectivity from resources in a VPC to S3 over the AWS network, without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device. This satisfies the requirement that the EC2 instance access the S3 bucket privately and without internet connectivity. An instance profile only grants IAM permissions, not network connectivity, and the other options do not create a private VPC-to-S3 data path.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently migrated its web application to AWS by rehosting it on Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company wants to redesign the application's architecture so that it is highly available and fault tolerant. Traffic must be routed randomly to all running EC2 instances.  
  
Which combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy.
Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy.
Create an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
Launch three EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and one instance in another Availability Zone.
Launch four EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 **multivalue answer routing** is designed to return up to eight **healthy** records selected **approximately at random**, which matches the requirement for traffic to reach all running EC2 instances randomly. To make the application highly available and fault tolerant within a single Region, the EC2 instances should be distributed across **multiple Availability Zones** so that an Availability Zone failure does not take down the application. Launching **two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone** provides balanced cross-AZ redundancy, unlike an uneven 2-and-1 placement.

**Learn more:** [Choosing a routing policy - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html) · [ResourceRecordSet - Amazon Route 53 API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/APIReference/API_ResourceRecordSet.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has registered its domain name with Amazon Route 53. The company uses Amazon API Gateway in the `ca-central-1` Region as a public interface for its backend microservice APIs. Third-party services securely consume the APIs. The company wants to design its API Gateway URL by using the company's domain name and corresponding certificate so that the third-party services can use HTTPS.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create stage variables in API Gateway with Name=

Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point the alias record to the Regional API Gateway stage endpoint. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.

Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint.

Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway APIs. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point an A record to the company's domain name.

questions.explanation:
For an API Gateway **Regional** custom domain name, AWS requires an ACM certificate that is in the **same Region** as the API. You then associate that custom domain name with the Regional API Gateway endpoint and create a Route 53 DNS record that routes the company’s domain to that API Gateway endpoint. Certificates in `us-east-1` are for **edge-optimized** custom domain names, not Regional custom domains, and stage variables do not replace the default invoke URL.

**Learn more:** [Set up a Regional custom domain name in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-regional-api-custom-domain-create.html) · [Custom domain name for public REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-custom-domains.html)

A company is moving its on-premises PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.  
  
The on-premises database must stay online and available throughout the migration, and the Aurora database must stay synchronized with the on-premises database.  
  
Which combination of actions must a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an ongoing replication task.
Create a database backup of the on-premises database.
Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication server.
Convert the database schema by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT).
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to monitor the database synchronization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Database Migration Service supports migrations that keep the source database online by using a replication instance to perform the migration and an ongoing replication task to capture and apply ongoing source changes to the target. For PostgreSQL, AWS DMS uses change data capture from the source transaction logs so the Aurora PostgreSQL target remains synchronized during the migration. Schema conversion with AWS SCT is not the required step for a PostgreSQL-to-Aurora PostgreSQL migration, because this is not a heterogeneous engine conversion.

**Learn more:** [Working with an AWS DMS replication instance - AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.html) · [Creating tasks for ongoing replication using AWS DMS - AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a specific instance family and on various instance sizes based on the company's current needs.  
  
The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company must also be able to change the instance family and instance sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Compute Savings Plan
EC2 Instance Savings Plan
Zonal Reserved Instances
Standard Reserved Instances

questions.explanation:
A **Compute Savings Plan** is the best fit because it provides discounted pricing in exchange for a 1-year or 3-year usage commitment while remaining flexible across **EC2 instance families, instance sizes, Regions, operating systems, and tenancy**. That directly satisfies the need to change both the instance family and sizes within 6 months while still optimizing cost over a 3-year term. By contrast, an **EC2 Instance Savings Plan** is limited to a single instance family in one Region, and **Zonal Reserved Instances** and **Standard Reserved Instances** do not provide the same family-level flexibility required here.

**Learn more:** [Compute Savings Plans](https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/compute-pricing/) · [Savings Plans Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a large Microsoft SharePoint deployment running on-premises that requires Microsoft Windows shared file storage. The company wants to migrate this workload to the AWS Cloud and is evaluating different storage options.  
  
The storage solution must be:  
  
- highly available  
- integrated with Active Directory for access control  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon EFS storage and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
Create an SMB file share on an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in two Availability Zones.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure Microsoft Windows Server to mount it as a volume.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the AWS service built for Windows SMB shared storage and integrates directly with Microsoft Active Directory for authentication and share, file, and folder permissions. It also offers Multi-AZ deployment for high availability, which makes it the best fit for a SharePoint workload that depends on highly available Windows shared file storage and AD-based access control.

**Learn more:** [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html)

A company has resources in multiple AWS Regions and accounts. A newly hired solutions architect finds that a previous employee did not leave information about the resource inventory. The solutions architect must build and map the relationship details of the different workloads across all accounts.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST operationally efficient** way?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to generate a map view from the detailed view report.
Use AWS Step Functions to collect workload details. Build architecture diagrams of the workloads manually.
Use Workload Discovery on AWS to generate architecture diagrams of the workloads.
Use AWS X-Ray to view the workload details. Build architecture diagrams with relationships.

questions.explanation:
Workload Discovery on AWS is built for this use case: it maintains an inventory of AWS resources across accounts and Regions, maps the relationships among those resources, and lets you generate, customize, and share architecture diagrams based on live AWS data. That directly satisfies the need to discover existing workloads and their relationships with minimal manual effort.

**Learn more:** [Workload Discovery on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/workload-discovery-on-aws/) · [Features and benefits - Workload Discovery on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/workload-discovery-on-aws/features-and-benefits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users.  
  
Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Private endpoint
Regional endpoint
Interface VPC endpoint
Edge-optimized endpoint

questions.explanation:
For Amazon API Gateway REST APIs, an **edge-optimized endpoint** is designed for globally distributed clients because API requests are routed to the nearest Amazon CloudFront edge location, which reduces latency for users in different geographic areas. A Regional endpoint is mainly for clients in the same AWS Region, and a private endpoint is only for access from within a VPC through an interface VPC endpoint. This matches AWS documentation on API Gateway endpoint types.

**Learn more:** [API endpoint types for REST APIs in API Gateway - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html) · [Amazon API Gateway - Serverless Applications Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/amazon-api-gateway.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to support the company's average daily workload.  
  
Once each month, the database performance degrades when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants the ability to run reports while maintaining performance for the daily workloads.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.
Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance. Direct the queries to the new database.
Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.
Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS read replicas are designed to offload read-only workloads from the primary DB instance. AWS documentation specifically notes business reporting as a use case, where reporting queries run against a read replica instead of the production instance. That lets the company keep normal transactional performance on the primary RDS for MySQL instance while directing the monthly report queries to the replica.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Tutorial: Managing a MySQL DB instance environment from development to production - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/tutorial-managing-MySQL-DB.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an API that ingests real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API saves this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for later analysis. The volume of data that the monitoring devices send to the API varies. During times of heavy traffic, the API frequently returns timeout errors.  
  
After reviewing the logs, the company determines that the database cannot process the amount of write traffic coming from the API. A solutions architect must minimize the number of connections to the database and must ensure that data is not lost during periods of heavy traffic.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Increase the size of the DB instance to an instance type that has more available memory.
Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.
Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is designed to decouple components and buffer bursty workloads, and it durably stores messages until consumers process them. Using the API to enqueue incoming records in SQS and using AWS Lambda to read batches from the queue and write them to Amazon RDS smooths write spikes, prevents requests from being lost while the database is overloaded, and reduces the number of concurrent database connections because writes are performed asynchronously by the Lambda consumer rather than by every API call. Multi-AZ does not increase write capacity for this pattern, and Amazon SNS is primarily for pub/sub fanout rather than queue-based buffering of database writes.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service? - Amazon SQS Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)

A solutions architect must design a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a high-volume software as a service (SaaS) platform. All platform data is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster.  
  
The DR plan must replicate the data to a secondary AWS Region.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use MySQL binary log replication to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Provision one DB instance for the Aurora cluster in the secondary Region.
Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. When setup is complete, remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Global Database is the managed cross-Region disaster recovery option built for Aurora. It replicates an Aurora DB cluster to a secondary AWS Region and supports DR failover with minimal replication lag. An Aurora global database must include at least one secondary Aurora DB cluster in a different Region, and that secondary cluster must have at least one DB instance, so options that remove the secondary Region DB instance do not satisfy the design. This makes the Aurora global database with a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region the correct and most cost-effective choice for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html) · [Configuration requirements of an Amazon Aurora global database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.configuration.requirements.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and needs to keep local access to all data while that data is backed up on AWS. The company also wants the data backed up to AWS to be transferred automatically and securely.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway stored volumes are designed for workloads that need low-latency local access to the entire dataset while asynchronously backing up that data to AWS for durable offsite protection. In contrast, cached volumes keep the primary data in Amazon S3 and retain only frequently accessed data locally, so they do not satisfy the requirement to maintain local access to all data. Snowball devices are for data migration and edge transfer use cases, not continuous backup. AWS documentation for Volume Gateway states that stored volumes store all data locally and back it up asynchronously to Amazon S3, and that gateway uploads occur over an encrypted SSL connection.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running low on storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performance solution that supports local caching without rearchitecting its existing applications.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.
Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway is the hybrid service that fits these requirements. **File Gateway** provides NFS file shares for on-premises applications and serves reads and writes through a local cache, making it suitable to replace existing NFS storage. **Volume Gateway** provides block storage to on-premises servers as iSCSI volumes and supports cached volumes, where primary data is stored in Amazon S3 while frequently accessed data is retained locally for low-latency access. This combination preserves existing application access patterns and adds local caching without requiring application redesign.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [File Gateway setup requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/Requirements.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is planning the architecture for a software demonstration environment. The environment will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The system will have significant traffic increases during working hours, but it does not need to operate on weekends.  
  
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to ensure that the system can scale to meet demand? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use AWS Auto Scaling to adjust the ALB capacity based on request rate.
Use AWS Auto Scaling to scale the capacity of the VPC internet gateway.
Launch the EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions to distribute the load across Regions.
Use a target tracking scaling policy to scale the Auto Scaling group based on instance CPU utilization.
Use scheduled scaling to change the Auto Scaling group minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to zero for weekends. Revert to the default values at the start of the week.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling should scale the EC2 fleet, and a target tracking scaling policy based on instance CPU utilization is a recommended way to dynamically add or remove instances as load changes. For the weekend shutdown requirement, scheduled scaling can set the Auto Scaling group's minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to 0 when the environment is not needed, then restore those values at the beginning of the week. The ALB itself scales automatically, and internet gateways are not scaled with AWS Auto Scaling.

**Learn more:** [Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html) · [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has sensitive and critical data in on-premises relational databases that run on SQL Server instances.  
  
The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2 instances. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
Migrate the databases to a Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
Migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to ensure data security.
Migrate the databases to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to ensure data security.

questions.explanation:
A Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for SQL Server DB instance best satisfies these requirements because Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that reduces database administration overhead, and RDS for SQL Server supports encryption at rest through AWS KMS. Multi-AZ deployments add higher availability and automatic failover, further strengthening the overall security and resiliency posture for critical SQL Server databases. By contrast, running SQL Server on Amazon EC2 leaves the company responsible for much more database and instance management, while Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB are not appropriate replacements for an on-premises relational SQL Server database in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html) · [Encrypting Amazon RDS resources - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a new mobile app. Anywhere in the world, users can see local news on topics they choose. Users also can post photos and videos from inside the app.  
  
Users access content often in the first minutes after the content is posted. New content quickly replaces older content, and then the older content disappears. The local nature of the news means that users consume 90% of the content within the AWS Region where it is uploaded.  
  
Which solution will optimize the user experience by providing the **LOWEST latency** for content uploads?

options.text: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront for the uploads.
Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for the uploads.
Upload content to Amazon EC2 instances in the Region that is closest to the user. Copy the data to Amazon S3.
Upload and store content in Amazon S3 in the Region that is closest to the user. Use multiple distributions of Amazon CloudFront.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration is purpose-built to reduce upload latency for geographically distributed clients uploading objects to Amazon S3. It routes uploads to the nearest AWS edge location and then carries the data across the AWS network to the target S3 bucket, which is exactly the pattern for a global mobile app whose users upload photos and videos from many locations. Using CloudFront alone is mainly a content delivery solution, and introducing Amazon EC2 before S3 adds extra processing and network hops instead of minimizing upload latency. Storing content in nearby Regions can help, but the AWS feature specifically intended to accelerate uploads into S3 is S3 Transfer Acceleration.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration-getting-started.html) · [Performance design patterns for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-design-patterns.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use Amazon Managed Grafana as its visualization tool. The company wants to visualize data from its Amazon RDS database as one data source. The company needs a secure solution that does not expose the data over the internet.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a private endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the private endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.

Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPCreate an AWS PrivateLink endpoint to establish a connection between Amazon Managed Grafana and Amazon RDS. Set up Amazon RDS as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Managed Grafana must be configured with an outbound VPC connection to access private-facing data sources inside a VPC. Amazon RDS can then be reached over its private endpoint within that VPC, keeping database traffic off the public internet. AWS documentation says that, by default, Amazon Managed Grafana reaches publicly accessible data sources via the public internet, and that a VPC connection is required when the data source is only available in a private VPC. AWS PrivateLink for Amazon Managed Grafana applies to private access to the Amazon Managed Grafana service and workspace APIs, not as a substitute for connecting the workspace to a VPC-hosted RDS database.

**Learn more:** [Connect to data sources or notification channels in Amazon VPC from Amazon Managed Grafana](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/grafana/latest/userguide/AMG-configure-vpc.html) · [Troubleshoot using VPC with Amazon Managed Grafana](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/grafana/latest/userguide/AMG-configure-vpc-faq.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A gaming company is developing an application with Voice over IP capabilities. The application will serve traffic to users worldwide. The application must be highly available with automated failover across AWS Regions. The company wants to minimize user latency without depending on IP address caching on user devices.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Global Accelerator with health checks.
Use Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation routing policy.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that includes multiple origins.
Create an Application Load Balancer that uses path-based routing.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct choice because it provides static anycast IP addresses as a fixed global entry point, routes clients to the nearest AWS edge location to reduce latency, and directs traffic only to healthy regional endpoints with automatic failover across AWS Regions. This specifically avoids reliance on DNS-based routing behavior and client-side IP caching, which makes it a better fit than Route 53 for latency-sensitive, highly available VoIP traffic.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works - AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Ensure health check access for your accelerator - AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoint-groups-health-check-options.html)

options.text: An AWS Glue job
An AWS Lambda function
A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the best fit for an API Gateway workload with unpredictable, infrequent traffic because it is serverless and billed per request and execution duration, which minimizes cost when there can be long idle periods. It also supports rapid event-driven processing suitable for completing asynchronous work within seconds. The other options introduce unnecessary ongoing or batch-oriented cost: AWS Glue is intended for ETL jobs and has minimum job billing, Amazon EKS has per-cluster hourly charges, and Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2 requires running EC2 capacity even when idle.

**Learn more:** [AWS Lambda Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/) · [Select a method to invoke your Lambda function using an HTTP request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/apig-http-invoke-decision.html)

A company delivers a dynamic website from a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website must support multiple languages for customers worldwide. The architecture runs in the `us-west-1` Region and is showing high request latency for users in other parts of the world.  
  
The website must handle requests quickly and efficiently regardless of where a user is located. However, the company does not want to re-create the current architecture across multiple Regions.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Replace the existing architecture with a website that is served from an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.

Create an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with the ALB. Configure the API to use the HTTP integration type. Set up an API Gateway stage to enable the API cache based on the Accept-Language request header.

Launch an EC2 instance in each additional Region and configure NGINX to act as a cache server for that Region. Put all the EC2 instances and the ALB behind an Amazon Route 53 record set with a geolocation routing policy.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront improves global response times by serving content through edge locations while keeping the existing application origin in a single Region. For a multilingual site, CloudFront can include the `Accept-Language` request header in the cache key so different language versions are cached separately. CloudFront also supports using an Application Load Balancer as the origin, which satisfies the requirement to keep the current EC2-behind-ALB architecture instead of rebuilding it across Regions.

**Learn more:** [Cache content based on request headers - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/header-caching.html) · [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html)

A company needs a storage solution for its application.  
  
The solution must:  
  
- be highly available and scalable  
- operate as a file system  
- be mountable by multiple Linux instances in AWS and on premises through native protocols  
- have no minimum size requirements  
  
The company has configured a Site-to-Site VPN for access from its on-premises network to its VPC.  
  
Which storage solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Amazon FSx Multi-AZ deployments
Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volumes
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with multiple mount targets
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a single mount target and multiple access points

questions.explanation:
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is a managed, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple Linux clients, including on-premises Linux servers connected to a VPC through AWS Site-to-Site VPN. It is designed for scalable shared file storage, and using multiple mount targets supports high availability across Availability Zones. Amazon EFS also has no minimum fee or setup charge, matching the requirement for no minimum size commitment. By contrast, Amazon EBS Multi-Attach is shared block storage within a single Availability Zone rather than a native shared file system, and a single EFS mount target is not the high-availability design.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Mounting with on-premises Linux clients - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mounting-fs-mount-helper-direct.html) · [Internetwork privacy - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/internetwork-privacy.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses GPS trackers to record the migration patterns of thousands of sea turtles. The trackers check every 5 minutes whether a turtle has moved more than 100 yards (91.4 meters). If a turtle has moved, its tracker sends the updated coordinates to a web application running on three Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region.  
  
Recently, the web application became overwhelmed while processing an unexpected volume of tracker data. Data was lost and there was no way to replay the events. A solutions architect must prevent this issue from occurring again and requires the solution with the least operational overhead.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the data. Configure the application to scan for new data in the bucket for processing.
Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to handle transmitted location coordinates. Use an AWS Lambda function to process each item concurrently.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to store the incoming data. Configure the application to poll for new messages for processing.
Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store transmitted location coordinates. Configure the application to query the table for new data for processing. Use TTL to remove data that has been processed.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is a fully managed, durable message queue that decouples data ingestion from processing. It buffers high-volume tracker events, lets the EC2 application poll and process them at a sustainable rate, and retains messages until they are consumed or expire, enabling retries after failures. Standard queues provide very high throughput and at-least-once delivery, so consumers should process messages idempotently.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html) · [Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, or Amazon EventBridge?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/decision-guides/latest/sns-or-sqs-or-eventbridge/sns-or-sqs-or-eventbridge.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Several applications write to the same tables in the database. The applications must be migrated one at a time, with a month between each migration. Management is concerned because the database has a high volume of reads and writes. The data must remain synchronized across both databases for the entire migration period.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.

questions.explanation:
For an Oracle-to-Aurora PostgreSQL migration, AWS Schema Conversion Tool is used to convert the heterogeneous database schema, and AWS Database Migration Service should run a full load plus CDC task so the target is initially loaded and then continuously updated as source changes occur during the staggered application cutover. For a high-throughput system with many ongoing writes, AWS DMS guidance favors memory-optimized replication instances because CDC relies heavily on in-memory buffers and sorter components during ongoing replication. Replicating all tables is required to keep both databases synchronized throughout the migration.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_BestPractices.html) · [Choosing the right AWS DMS replication instance for your migration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.Types.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which compute service should the solutions architect configure the API to invoke to meet these requirements at the lowest cost?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"An AWS Glue job","B":"An AWS Lambda function","C":"A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)","D":"A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2"},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"AWS Lambda is the best fit for an API Gateway workload with unpredictable, infrequent traffic because it is serverless and billed per request and execution duration, which minimizes cost when there can be long idle periods. ",["$","p",null,{"children":"The solution must:"}],"
",["$","ul",null,{"children":["
",["$","li",null,{"children":"be highly available and scalable"}],"

"]}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company has configured a Site-to-Site VPN for access from its on-premises network to its VPC."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which storage solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Amazon FSx Multi-AZ deployments","B":"Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volumes","C":"Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with multiple mount targets","D":"Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a single mount target and multiple access points"},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is a managed, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple Linux clients, including on-premises Linux servers connected to a VPC through AWS Site-to-Site VPN. It is designed for scalable shared file storage, and using multiple mount targets supports high availability across Availability Zones. Amazon EFS also has no minimum fee or setup charge, matching the requirement for no minimum size commitment. By contrast, Amazon EBS Multi-Attach is shared block storage within a single Availability Zone rather than a native shared file system, and a single EFS mount target is not the high-availability design.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on CPU usage.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on network usage.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on the number of items in the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:

A media company is assessing whether to migrate its systems to the AWS Cloud.  
  
The company requires:  
  
- at least 10 TB of storage with the highest possible I/O performance for video processing,  
- 300 TB of highly durable storage for media content, and  
- 900 TB of storage for archival media that is no longer being used.  
  
Which combination of services should a solutions architect recommend to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 for archival storage
Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 instance store is the best fit when the requirement is the maximum possible I/O performance because it provides temporary block-level storage physically attached to the host. Amazon S3 is the correct choice for 300 TB of very durable media storage because it is designed for massive scale and 11 nines of durability. Amazon S3 Glacier is designed for low-cost archival storage for data that is rarely accessed. Therefore the correct combination is EC2 instance store, Amazon S3, and Amazon S3 Glacier.

**Learn more:** [Instance store temporary block storage for EC2 instances - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html) · [Object Storage Classes – Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates thousands of AWS Lambda functions. It needs a solution that securely stores sensitive information used by all the Lambda functions. The solution must also automatically rotate that sensitive information.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Create HTTP security headers by using Lambda@Edge to retrieve and create sensitive information
Create a Lambda layer that retrieves sensitive information
Store sensitive information in AWS Secrets Manager
Store sensitive information in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
Create a Lambda consumer with dedicated throughput to retrieve sensitive information and create environmental variables

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager securely centralizes sensitive values and supports automatic secret rotation on a schedule. A Lambda layer packages shared retrieval logic so all Lambda functions can use the same implementation, minimizing duplicated code and operational maintenance.

**Learn more:** [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html) · [Rotation by Lambda function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_lambda.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that serves clients deployed in more than **20,000 retail storefront locations** worldwide. The application consists of backend web services exposed over **HTTPS on port 443**. It runs on **Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB)**. The retail locations communicate with the web application over the **public internet**. The company allows each retail location to register the **IP address** allocated to that location by its local ISP.  
  
The company's security team recommends increasing the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the **IP addresses registered by the retail locations**.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP rule sets on the ALB to filter traffic. Update the IP addresses in the rule to include the registered IP addresses.
Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALConfigure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALModify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.
Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.
Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF can be associated with an Application Load Balancer and can allow or block web requests based on the source IP address by using IP sets in a web ACL. That makes it the appropriate control for restricting HTTPS access to the ALB so that only requests originating from the registered retail-location IP addresses are accepted. AWS Firewall Manager is for centralized administration of protections, not the primary data-plane filter needed here; ALB does not use a Lambda authorizer pattern for client-IP validation; and subnet network ACLs are the wrong fit for managing a web allowlist at this scale.

**Learn more:** [AWS WAF Developer Guide – Using IP set match statements in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-ipset-match.html) · [AWS CLI Command Reference – associate-web-acl (example with Application Load Balancer)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/wafv2/associate-web-acl.html)

A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that stores critical data. The company must protect the data from accidental deletion.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket.
Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket.
Create a bucket policy on the S3 bucket.
Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket.
Create a lifecycle policy for the objects in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Versioning protects against accidental deletion by preserving prior object versions and placing a delete marker instead of permanently removing the object during a standard delete request. MFA Delete adds another safeguard by requiring multi-factor authentication to permanently delete an object version or to change the bucket’s versioning state. Together, these controls directly address accidental deletion protection for critical S3 data.

**Learn more:** [Retaining multiple versions of objects with S3 Versioning - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Versioning.html) · [Configuring MFA delete - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiFactorAuthenticationDelete.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as its database layer. The application has seen a significant increase in users. The company wants to:  
  
- improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds, and  
- cache requests to the database.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is the correct choice because it is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache designed specifically to speed up DynamoDB read workloads from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds. It also caches requests to DynamoDB without requiring the company to redesign the application around a separate caching layer, so it has less operational overhead than managing Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Migrating to Amazon Redshift or Amazon RDS would change the database platform and would not be the simplest way to achieve microsecond cached access for a DynamoDB-backed serverless application.

**Learn more:** [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html) · [Troubleshooting latency issues in Amazon DynamoDB - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TroubleshootingLatency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs a solution that prevents AWS CloudFormation stacks from deploying AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resources that contain an inline policy or `"*"` in the statement. The solution also must prohibit deployment of Amazon EC2 instances that have public IP addresses.  
  
The company has AWS Control Tower enabled in its organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower proactive controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
Use AWS Control Tower detective controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
Use AWS Config to create rules for EC2 and IAM compliance. Configure the rules to run an AWS Systems Manager Session Manager automation to delete a resource when it is not compliant.
Use a service control policy (SCP) to block actions for the EC2 instances and IAM resources if the actions lead to noncompliance.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower proactive controls are evaluated before provisioning and are designed to block noncompliant AWS CloudFormation deployments. AWS documents proactive IAM controls that deny inline policies with wildcard permissions, including `Action: *` and `Resource: *`, and proactive EC2 controls that require EC2 instances to avoid public IP association. Detective controls only identify drift after resources exist, and AWS Config remediation deletes or fixes resources after deployment instead of preventing them. SCPs are preventive at the Organizations level, but the Control Tower feature that directly validates CloudFormation templates against these resource configuration requirements is proactive controls.

**Learn more:** [AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/iam-rules.html) · [Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) controls - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/ec2-rules.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a content management system that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance hosts both the web server and the database software.  
  
The company must make its website platform highly available and must allow the website to scale to meet user demand.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Move the database to Amazon RDS, and enable automatic backups. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer in the Availability Zone, and set the two instances as targets.

Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora instance with a read replica in the same Availability Zone as the existing EC2 instance. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer, and set the two EC2 instances as targets.

Move the database to Amazon Aurora with a read replica in another Availability Zone. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.

Move the database to a separate EC2 instance, and schedule backups to Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the original EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
A highly available and scalable design separates the web and database tiers, runs the web tier behind an Application Load Balancer, and uses an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones so instances can be replaced automatically and scale out with demand. The database tier should move off the instance to Amazon Aurora, which provides storage replicated across multiple Availability Zones and supports Aurora Replicas in different Availability Zones for higher availability and failover. Options limited to a single Availability Zone do not satisfy high availability, and hosting the database on another EC2 instance with backups does not make the database tier highly available.

**Learn more:** [Application Load Balancers - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/application-load-balancers.html) · [Tutorial: Set up a scaled and load-balanced application - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/tutorial-ec2-auto-scaling-load-balancer.html)
