A university research laboratory must migrate **30 TB of data** from an on-premises Windows file server to **Amazon FSx for Windows File Server**. The laboratory has a **1 Gbps network link** that is shared by many other departments in the university.  
  
The laboratory wants to use a **data migration service** that will **maximize data transfer performance**. However, it must also be able to **control how much bandwidth** the service uses so it can minimize the effect on other departments. The migration must be completed **within the next 5 days**.  
  
Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: AWS Snowcone
Amazon FSx File Gateway
AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is the managed AWS service for accelerating online data transfers from on-premises storage to AWS storage services, including Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. It supports creating FSx for Windows File Server as a transfer location and lets you set a per-task bandwidth limit, which satisfies the need to maximize transfer performance while throttling usage on a shared 1 Gbps link. Amazon FSx File Gateway is for low-latency on-premises access to FSx shares rather than managed bulk migration, AWS Transfer Family is for protocol-based file transfer workflows, and AWS Snowcone is not the best fit for moving 30 TB on this timeline.

**Learn more:** [Configuring transfers with FSx for Windows File Server - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-fsx-location.html) · [Setting bandwidth limits for your AWS DataSync task - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-bandwidth.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has several AWS accounts for development work. Some employees repeatedly use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, causing the company to go over the annual budget for the development accounts.  
  
The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST development effort**?

options.text: Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.
Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.
Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations service control policies (SCPs) provide centralized guardrails for member accounts and organizational units by limiting the maximum permissions available to principals in those accounts. That makes SCPs the most direct way to prevent developers in multiple development accounts from launching disallowed EC2 instance types. The other options require building custom provisioning paths or reactive automation, which involves more implementation effort and does not provide the same centralized preventive control.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [Restrict access using AWS Organizations service control policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/using-orgs-example-scps.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden traffic increases on random days of the week. The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden traffic increases.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
Dynamic scaling is the best fit because it automatically adds or removes EC2 instances in response to real-time demand signals such as CloudWatch metrics, so the Auto Scaling group increases capacity only when unexpected traffic spikes actually occur. AWS documentation describes predictive scaling as most suitable for regular daily or weekly traffic patterns, while scheduled scaling is for known times. Because the increases happen on random days, dynamic scaling provides the needed responsiveness without paying for extra capacity in advance.

**Learn more:** [Choose your scaling method - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html) · [Predictive scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is creating a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.
Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.
Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.
Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon EC2 Capacity Reservation is the option that actually reserves compute capacity ahead of time, which is what a failover disaster recovery design needs when capacity must be available in the recovery Region. AWS documentation states that On-Demand Capacity Reservations can be used for disaster recovery and to reserve capacity in a different Availability Zone or Region. By contrast, Savings Plans are pricing discounts and do not provide capacity reservations, and regional Reserved Instances also do not reserve capacity.

**Learn more:** [On-Demand Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks for ML - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-reservation-overview.html) · [Compute Savings Plans and Reserved Instances - Savings Plans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-ris.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect creates a VPC that contains two public subnets and two private subnets. A corporate security requirement mandates that all Amazon EC2 instances be launched in a private subnet. However, when the solutions architect launches an EC2 instance running a web server on ports 80 and 443 in a private subnet, external internet traffic cannot connect to the server.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to fix this issue?

options.text: Attach the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group in a private subnet. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the Auto Scaling group identifier.

Provision an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a public subnet. Add the EC2 instance to the target group that is associated with the ALEnsure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the ALB.
Launch a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Update the route table for the private subnets to add a default route to the NAT gateway. Attach a public Elastic IP address to the NAT gateway.

Ensure that the security group that is attached to the EC2 instance allows HTTP traffic on port 80 and HTTPS traffic on port 443. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the public IP address of the EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
An internet-facing Application Load Balancer deployed in public subnets is the correct way to expose a web application to the internet while keeping the EC2 web server in a private subnet. The ALB provides the public entry point, and it forwards HTTP/HTTPS requests to registered targets by using their private IP addresses. A NAT gateway only enables outbound connections from private subnets and cannot accept unsolicited inbound web traffic, and Auto Scaling by itself does not make the application internet-accessible.

**Learn more:** [Create an Application Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-application-load-balancer.html) · [How Elastic Load Balancing works - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must protect a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances store highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet. Per company policy, the EC2 instances in the VPC may access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party’s URL. All other internet traffic must be blocked.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound traffic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.
Set up an AWS WAF web ACL. Create a custom set of rules that filter traffic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.
Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows traffic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.

Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound traffic to the ALB. Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB’s target group for outbound access to the internet.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall can be placed on the private subnet’s outbound path by updating routing so egress traffic is inspected before reaching the internet. Network Firewall stateful domain list rule groups support allow lists and deny lists based on domain names, evaluating HTTP host headers and HTTPS SNI, which is the AWS-native way to restrict VPC egress so instances can reach only approved third-party repositories while blocking other internet destinations. AWS WAF protects web applications rather than general subnet egress, security groups cannot filter by URL/domain name, and an ALB is not an outbound URL-filtering control.

**Learn more:** [Stateful domain list rule groups in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/stateful-rule-groups-domain-names.html) · [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company keeps data in an on-premises Oracle relational database. The company needs to make that data available in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for analysis. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect its on-premises network to AWS.  
  
The company must capture the changes that occur to the source database during the migration to Aurora PostgreSQL.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use the AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) full-load migration task to migrate the data.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the existing data and replicate the ongoing changes.
Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.

questions.explanation:
For an Oracle-to-Aurora PostgreSQL migration, AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) is used to convert the Oracle schema to a PostgreSQL-compatible schema, and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) is used for heterogeneous data migration. To preserve changes that occur while the migration is in progress, the DMS task must use full load plus change data capture (CDC), which migrates the existing data and then replicates ongoing source changes. File-transfer options such as DataSync or Snowball do not provide database CDC, and a DMS full-load-only task does not capture subsequent changes.

**Learn more:** [Creating tasks for ongoing replication using AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html) · [Migrating from Oracle to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with AWS Schema Conversion Tool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.Oracle.ToPostgreSQL.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Organizers for a global event want to publish daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to receive millions of views from users worldwide. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket, and a solutions architect must design an efficient and effective solution.  
  
Which action should the solutions architect take to achieve this?

options.text: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the correct solution because it is AWS’s global content delivery network for serving static website content at high scale with low latency. With the S3 bucket as the origin, CloudFront caches the HTML files at edge locations around the world, which is the efficient way to handle millions of requests from global users. Presigned URLs only provide temporary controlled access, cross-Region replication copies data without accelerating delivery to viewers, and Route 53 geoproximity routes DNS queries but does not cache or distribute the website content itself.

**Learn more:** [Speeding up your website with Amazon CloudFront - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/website-hosting-cloudfront-walkthrough.html) · [Get started with a secure static website - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/getting-started-secure-static-website-cloudformation-template.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises application that uses a MySQL database. The company is migrating the application to AWS to improve the application's elasticity and availability.  
  
The current architecture has heavy read activity on the database during normal operations. Every 4 hours, the development team performs a full export of the production database to populate a database in the staging environment. During this time, users experience unacceptable application latency. The development team also cannot use the staging environment until the process is finished.  
  
A solutions architect must recommend a replacement architecture that resolves the application latency issue. The replacement architecture must also allow the development team to continue using the staging environment without delay.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.
Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Use database cloning to create the staging database on-demand.
Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Use the standby instance for the staging database.
Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas addresses the production workload because Aurora Replicas are dedicated to read scaling and high availability. Aurora cloning addresses the staging requirement because it can create a new staging database quickly using copy-on-write, which is specifically useful for development, testing, and workload-intensive operations without running a full export/import from production. An RDS Multi-AZ standby instance cannot be used for staging or read traffic, and a mysqldump-based refresh would still introduce the same lengthy, disruptive refresh process.

**Learn more:** [Replication with Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html) · [Cloning a volume for an Amazon Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Clone.html)

A company routinely uploads confidential data to Amazon S3 buckets for analysis.  
  
The company’s security policies require that objects be encrypted at rest. The company must automatically rotate the encryption key each year, track key rotation by using AWS CloudTrail, and minimize encryption-key costs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)
Use server-side encryption with customer managed AWS KMS keys

questions.explanation:
SSE-KMS using the AWS managed KMS key provides server-side encryption at rest. AWS KMS automatically rotates AWS managed key material annually and records rotation events in AWS CloudTrail. AWS managed keys have no monthly key fee, unlike customer managed KMS keys, which minimizes key cost.

**Learn more:** [AWS KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/concepts.html) · [Rotate AWS KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large international university has deployed all of its compute services in the AWS Cloud. These services include Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB. The university currently relies on many custom scripts to back up its infrastructure. However, the university wants to centralize management and automate data backups as much as possible by using AWS native options.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use third-party backup software with an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway virtual tape library.
Use AWS Backup to configure and monitor all backups for the services in use.
Use AWS Config to set lifecycle management to take snapshots of all data sources on a schedule.
Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to manage the configuration and monitoring of backup tasks.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the AWS-native service for centrally configuring, automating, and monitoring backups across supported AWS services. It supports the services named here, including Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB, so it replaces custom scripts with centralized backup policies and monitoring.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Backup? - AWS Backup Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html) · [How AWS Backup works with supported AWS services - AWS Backup Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/working-with-supported-services.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is planning a tightly coupled high performance computing (HPC) environment in the AWS Cloud. The company must include features that optimize the HPC environment for networking and storage.  
  
Which combination of solutions will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure custom routing for the accelerator.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure the file system with scratch storage.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the viewer protocol policy to be HTTP and HTTPS.
Launch Amazon EC2 instances. Attach an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to the instances.
Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment to manage the environment.

questions.explanation:
Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) is the AWS feature built for tightly coupled HPC workloads because it improves inter-instance communication with lower and more consistent latency and higher throughput than standard TCP networking. Amazon FSx for Lustre is the AWS high-performance shared file system for HPC workloads, and scratch storage is intended for temporary, shorter-term, processing-heavy workloads that need high burst throughput. Together, these directly address the networking and storage requirements of a tightly coupled HPC environment.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Fabric Adapter for AI/ML and HPC workloads on Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/efa.html) · [What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
Use the S3 storage class analysis tool to determine the correct tier for each object in the S3 bucket. Move each object to the identified storage tier.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the recommended storage class for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns because it automatically moves objects to the most cost-effective access tier without operational overhead. Applying an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition bucket objects to Intelligent-Tiering gives an automated per-bucket solution. S3 Storage Class Analysis is not the best choice because it mainly provides recommendations for transitions from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA and requires additional action to move data. Glacier Instant Retrieval and One Zone-IA are intended for specific infrequent-access use cases, not broadly unknown access patterns.

**Learn more:** [Managing storage costs with Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering.html) · [Amazon S3 analytics – Storage Class Analysis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/analytics-storage-class.html)

A company operates a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application uses a microservices architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights is the AWS feature built for containerized applications and microservices on Amazon EKS. It collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs, and surfaces them centrally in Amazon CloudWatch. Standard CloudWatch agent deployment alone is not the best match for the full summarized EKS container observability requirement, AWS App Mesh is primarily for service-to-service networking and observability integrations rather than serving as the centralized log/metrics solution itself, and AWS CloudTrail records API activity rather than application metrics and logs.

**Learn more:** [Container Insights - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights.html) · [Monitor your cluster performance and view logs - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-observe.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing an application that will perform batch processing on large volumes of data. The input data will reside in Amazon S3, and the output data will be saved in a separate S3 bucket. During processing, the application will move data across the network among multiple Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to lower the total data transfer costs?

options.text: Place all the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.
Place all the EC2 instances in the same AWS Region.
Place all the EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone.
Place all the EC2 instances in private subnets in multiple Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
Data transferred between Amazon EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone is free, whereas data transfer between Availability Zones in the same AWS Region incurs a charge in each direction. Locating all processing instances in one Availability Zone therefore avoids inter-Availability-Zone transfer charges.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 On-Demand Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand-backup/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must migrate a MySQL database from its on-premises data center to AWS within 2 weeks. The database is 20 TB in size, and the company wants to complete the migration with minimal downtime.  
  
Which solution will migrate the database **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes. Send the Snowball Edge device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.

Order an AWS Snowmobile vehicle. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowmobile vehicle back to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.

Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowball device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication

Order a 1 GB dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.

questions.explanation:
A Snowball Edge storage-optimized device is the right bulk-transfer service for tens of terabytes, and AWS DMS can keep the source database running while replicating ongoing changes so cutover downtime stays minimal. Snowmobile is intended for much larger migrations, on the order of exabytes, so it is not cost-effective for 20 TB. A compute-optimized Snowball Edge with GPU adds specialized compute capability that is unnecessary for database transport. A 1 Gbps Direct Connect link can provide connectivity for replication, but for a one-time 20 TB seed load it is generally less cost-effective than using Snowball for the initial transfer and DMS for ongoing changes. For homogeneous MySQL migrations, AWS DMS supports full load plus ongoing replication, and AWS generally positions Snowball Edge as a device for large-scale offline data transfer.

**Learn more:** [Migrating databases to their Amazon RDS equivalents with AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/data-migrations.html) · [What is Snowball Edge?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)

A telemarketing company is designing its customer call center functionality on AWS. The company needs a solution that provides multiple speaker recognition and generates transcript files. The company wants to query the transcript files to analyze the business patterns. The transcript files must be stored for 7 years for auditing purposes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use machine learning models for transcript file analysis.
Use Amazon Transcribe for multiple speaker recognition. Use Amazon Athena for transcript file analysis.
Use Amazon Translate for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon Redshift. Use SQL queries for transcript file analysis.
Use Amazon Rekognition for multiple speaker recognition. Store the transcript files in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Textract for transcript file analysis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Transcribe supports speaker partitioning (diarization) to distinguish multiple speakers in audio and produce transcript files. Those transcript outputs are typically stored in Amazon S3, where long-term retention such as 7 years can be enforced. Amazon Athena can query files in Amazon S3, including JSON data, to analyze transcript content with SQL. Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Translate do not provide the required call transcription with multi-speaker diarization.

**Learn more:** [Partitioning speakers (diarization) - Amazon Transcribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/diarization.html) · [Data input and output - Amazon Transcribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/how-input.html)

A media company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content over the internet. The company wants only premium customers to be able to access the media streams and file content. The company stores all content in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company also provides content to customers **on demand** for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Generate and provide S3 signed cookies to premium customers.
Generate and provide CloudFront signed URLs to premium customers.
Use origin access control (OAC) to limit the access of non-premium customers.
Generate and activate field-level encryption to block non-premium customers.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront signed URLs are designed to restrict access to individual private objects and to grant time-limited access after an application verifies that a user is entitled to the content, such as having paid for a rental or download. AWS documentation distinguishes signed URLs from signed cookies by recommending signed URLs for individual files, while signed cookies are intended for access to multiple restricted files. Origin access control secures the S3 origin behind CloudFront but does not enforce premium-customer entitlement by itself, and field-level encryption protects submitted data rather than controlling viewer access to media content.

**Learn more:** [Use signed URLs - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html) · [Decide to use signed URLs or signed cookies - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-choosing-signed-urls-cookies.html)

A company's website processes millions of requests per day, and the request volume keeps growing. A solutions architect must improve the web application's response time. The solutions architect determines that the application needs to reduce latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.
Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.
Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.
Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is the best fit because it is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache built specifically to accelerate DynamoDB read workloads. AWS documentation states that DAX can reduce eventually consistent read latency from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, supports millions of requests per second, and reduces operational and application complexity because it is API-compatible with DynamoDB and requires only minimal code changes. By contrast, using Amazon ElastiCache requires a separate cache layer and more cache-management design, and adding DynamoDB Streams with AWS Lambda to populate ElastiCache introduces additional components and operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html) · [Troubleshooting latency issues in Amazon DynamoDB - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TroubleshootingLatency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company needs to transform a large volume of clinical-trial data from several customers. The company must extract the customer data from a relational database, transform it by using a series of complex rules, and load it into Amazon S3 after the transformations are finished.  
  
All data must be encrypted where it is processed before the company stores it in Amazon S3. All data must be encrypted by using customer-specific keys.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Create one AWS Glue job for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each job that uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) to encrypt the data.
Create one Amazon EMR cluster for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each cluster that uses client-side encryption with a custom client-side root key (CSE-Custom) to encrypt the data.
Create one AWS Glue job for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each job that uses client-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (CSE-KMS) to encrypt the data.
Create one Amazon EMR cluster for each customer. Attach a security configuration to each cluster that uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) to encrypt the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EMR supports client-side encryption with a custom client-side root key (CSE-Custom), which encrypts data on the processing client before the objects are stored in Amazon S3. Creating one EMR cluster per customer permits each customer’s data to use its own root key. AWS Glue S3 output encryption uses server-side modes, while its CSE-KMS setting is for job bookmarks and does not provide client-side encryption for transformed S3 output.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 client-side encryption - Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-emrfs-encryption-cse.html) · [Managing security configurations on the AWS Glue console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/console-security-configurations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. The application is reachable by using the transport layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. The company requires the application architecture to provide high availability.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Configure new EC2 instances in a different Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to all instances.
Configure a Network Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
Configure a Network Load Balancer for TCP traffic to the instances. Configure an Application Load Balancer for HTTP and HTTPS traffic to the instances.

Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to run application health checks on the instances.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Configure the alarm to restart EC2 instances that transition to a stopped state.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed for TCP traffic, so it matches an application that is accessed through the transport layer. High availability across Availability Zones is achieved by placing the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that spans multiple Availability Zones, where Auto Scaling distributes capacity across those zones and replaces unhealthy instances based on health checks. Together, these services provide resilient multi-AZ TCP traffic distribution without adding unnecessary components such as an Application Load Balancer.

**Learn more:** [Auto Scaling groups - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html) · [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling? - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an environment in which data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Objects are accessed frequently throughout the day. The company has strict data-encryption requirements for data stored in the S3 bucket and currently uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for encryption.  
  
The company wants to optimize the costs of encrypting S3 objects without making additional calls to AWS KMS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Use an S3 Bucket Key for server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) on the new objects.
Use client-side encryption with AWS KMS customer managed keys.
Use server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C) stored in AWS KMS.

questions.explanation:
S3 Bucket Keys work with SSE-KMS and use a time-limited bucket-level key within Amazon S3 to create data keys for new objects. This decreases S3-to-KMS request traffic and lowers AWS KMS request costs while preserving encryption with AWS KMS keys.

**Learn more:** [Reducing the cost of SSE-KMS with Amazon S3 Bucket Keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-key.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing an application in which users upload small files to Amazon S3. After a user uploads a file, the file needs one-time simple processing to transform the data and store the data in JSON format for later analysis.  
  
Each file must be processed as soon as possible after upload. Demand will vary. On some days, users will upload many files. On other days, users will upload only a few files or no files.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Configure Amazon EMR to read text files from Amazon S3. Run processing scripts to transform the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.

Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.

Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams when a new file is uploaded. Use an AWS Lambda function to consume the event from the stream and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

questions.explanation:
An event-driven serverless design best fits a workload of small files that must be processed quickly after upload and that can spike or drop to zero unpredictably. Amazon S3 can publish object-created events to Amazon SQS, and AWS Lambda can poll SQS and scale automatically to process messages without managing servers. This minimizes operational overhead while still handling variable demand. Amazon DynamoDB supports document data models, which fits storing the transformed JSON output. EMR, EC2 fleets, Kinesis Data Streams, and Aurora introduce unnecessary infrastructure and administration for this simple one-time transformation workflow.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Event Notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html) · [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances in two Availability Zones in the `us-east-1` Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly recurring increase in workload.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled actions are designed for predictable, recurring demand changes. A scheduled action can automatically set the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity at a specific recurring time, allowing the group to run two instances normally and increase to six every Friday evening while still distributing instances across the specified Availability Zones. This avoids the ongoing effort of manual scaling and is a better match than reactive automatic scaling when the load pattern is known in advance.

**Learn more:** [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Auto Scaling groups - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s DNS provider that hosts the domain name records is having outages, causing disruptions for a website that runs on AWS.  
  
The company must move to a more resilient managed DNS service and wants that service to run on AWS.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to migrate the DNS hosting service quickly?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
Create a Simple AD directory in AWS. Enable zone transfer between the DNS provider and AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for the domain records.

Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Specify the IP addresses that the provider's DNS will forward DNS queries to. Configure the provider's DNS to forward DNS queries for the domain to the IP addresses that are specified in the inbound endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 public hosted zones are the AWS authoritative DNS service for internet-facing domains, and Route 53 can rapidly replicate an existing DNS configuration by importing the current provider’s zone file. A private hosted zone would only resolve inside associated VPCs, not for public website users. AWS Directory Service and Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints do not replace a public authoritative DNS host for an internet domain.

**Learn more:** [Creating records by importing a zone file - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-creating-import.html) · [Making Route 53 the DNS service for a domain that's in use - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/migrate-dns-domain-in-use.html)

A company is moving a large volume of data from on-premises storage to AWS. Amazon EC2 instances that run Windows, Mac, and Linux in the same AWS Region will access the data by using SMB and NFS storage protocols. The company will access some of the data regularly. The rest of the data will be accessed infrequently.  
  
The company must design a solution to host the data.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume that uses EFS Intelligent-Tiering. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to the EFS volume.
Create an Amazon FSx for ONTAP instance. Create an FSx for ONTAP file system with a root volume that uses the auto tiering policy. Migrate the data to the FSx for ONTAP volume.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket by using an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway.
Create an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system. Migrate the data to the new volume.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the managed AWS file service in these options that supports both SMB and NFS access for the same workload, which is required for Windows, macOS, and Linux EC2 instances. It also provides automatic tiering policies such as auto tiering so colder data can move to capacity pool storage with less administration, while frequently accessed data remains on primary storage. Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx for OpenZFS do not meet the dual-protocol SMB-and-NFS requirement, and using Amazon S3 with File Gateway adds gateway infrastructure to operate instead of using a native managed file system service.

**Learn more:** [Accessing your FSx for ONTAP data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html) · [Amazon Elastic File System quotas that you can increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/limits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application on more than 10 Amazon EC2 instances, with traffic routed by Amazon Route 53. The company sometimes encounters timeout errors when users browse the application. The networking team determines that some DNS queries are returning the IP addresses of unhealthy instances, which causes the timeout errors.  
  
What should a solutions architect implement to resolve these timeout errors?

options.text: Create a Route 53 simple routing policy record for each EC2 instance. Associate a health check with each record.
Create a Route 53 failover routing policy record for each EC2 instance. Associate a health check with each record.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with EC2 instances as its origin. Associate a health check with the EC2 instances.
Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a health check in front of the EC2 instances. Route to the ALB from Route 53.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer should be placed in front of the EC2 instances so the load balancer can run target health checks and route requests only to healthy instances. Route 53 should then route users to the ALB instead of to individual instance IP addresses. Route 53 simple routing does not health-check multiple returned IP addresses for this use case, and failover routing is designed for primary/secondary recovery rather than balancing across a pool of active web servers. AWS Route 53 documentation states that simple routing with multiple IP addresses is not health checked, while Route 53 can route to healthy resources when health-aware policies are used, and ELB provides health-checked distribution for instance fleets.

**Learn more:** [Simple routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-simple.html) · [How health checks work in simple Amazon Route 53 configurations - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-simple-configs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts its website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The website does not require a database.  
  
The company is growing, and the engineering team deploys the website to a second Region. The company wants to distribute traffic across both Regions to support growth and for disaster recovery. The solution must not send traffic to a Region where the website is unhealthy.  
  
Which policy or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.text: An Amazon Route 53 simple routing policy
An Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy
An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the EC2 instance IDs from both Regions
An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the IP addresses of the EC2 instances from both Regions

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing returns multiple IP addresses (one for each Region's healthy endpoint) and performs health checks on each record, excluding unhealthy Regions from DNS responses. This enables active-active traffic distribution across Regions while automatically excluding failed endpoints. Simple routing returns all records without health awareness. Application Load Balancers are regional services and cannot natively target EC2 instances across multiple Regions in a single target group.

**Learn more:** [Multivalue answer routing (Amazon Route 53)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-multivalue.html) · [Choosing a routing policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An image-processing company has a web application that users use to upload images. The application uploads the images to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has configured S3 event notifications to publish object creation events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. The SQS queue is the event source for an AWS Lambda function that processes the images and emails the results to users.  
  
Users report that they receive multiple email messages for each uploaded image. A solutions architect determines that SQS messages are invoking the Lambda function more than once, resulting in multiple email messages.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Set up long polling in the SQS queue by increasing the ReceiveMessage wait time to 30 seconds.
Change the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Use the message deduplication ID to discard duplicate messages.
Increase the visibility timeout in the SQS queue to a value that is greater than the total of the function timeout and the batch window timeout.
Modify the Lambda function to delete each message from the SQS queue immediately after the message is read before processing.

questions.explanation:
With Amazon SQS as an AWS Lambda event source, messages remain hidden only for the queue's visibility timeout while Lambda processes them. If that timeout is too short, the same message can become visible again and be delivered for another invocation, causing duplicate processing such as multiple emails. AWS guidance is to set the SQS visibility timeout longer than the Lambda processing time and to account for any batch window; AWS specifically recommends a visibility timeout of six times the function timeout, plus the batching window when used. That makes increasing the queue visibility timeout the lowest-overhead fix.

**Learn more:** [Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html) · [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect has created two IAM policies, Policy1 and Policy2. Both policies are attached to an IAM group.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640541883-x8iht478.png)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640545510-odhzq1ac.png)  
  
A cloud engineer is added as an IAM user to the IAM group. Which action will the cloud engineer be able to perform?

options.text: Deleting IAM users
Deleting directories
Deleting Amazon EC2 instances
Deleting logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM evaluates permissions by combining applicable policies, and any explicit `Deny` overrides an `Allow`. Policy1 grants `ec2:*`, which includes terminating or deleting Amazon EC2 instances. Although Policy1 also grants `ds:*`, Policy2 explicitly denies `ds:Delete*`, so deleting directories is not allowed. The IAM permissions are limited to `iam:Get*` and `iam:List*`, which do not allow deleting IAM users, and the CloudWatch Logs permissions are limited to `logs:Get*` and `logs:Describe*`, which do not allow deleting log data.

**Learn more:** [Policy evaluation logic - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html) · [Amazon EC2 actions, resources, and condition keys for IAM policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonec2.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time, and then ingest the data into the data lake.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed streaming delivery service that automatically scales to ingest and deliver data with minimal operational overhead. Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics enables real-time processing and analysis of streaming data using SQL. Together, they provide a managed pipeline for ingesting payment data every minute and analyzing it in real time before delivery to S3, without requiring custom consumer logic or EC2 management.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Data Firehose destination settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html) · [What is Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/latest/java/what-is.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Amazon EC2 instances. As part of the application deployment, the application includes a UI that uses Amazon DynamoDB and data services that use Amazon S3.  
  
The company must ensure that EKS Pods for the UI can access only Amazon DynamoDB, and that EKS Pods for the data services can access only Amazon S3. The company uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create separate IAM policies for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB access with the required permissions. Attach both IAM policies to the EC2 instance profile. Use role-based access control (RBAC) to control access to Amazon S3 or DynamoDB for the respective EKS Pods.

Create separate IAM policies for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB access with the required permissions. Attach the Amazon S3 IAM policy directly to the EKS Pods for the data services and the DynamoDB policy to the EKS Pods for the UI.

Create separate Kubernetes service accounts for the UI and data services to assume an IAM role. Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess policy to the data services account and the AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess policy to the UI service account.

Create separate Kubernetes service accounts for the UI and data services to assume an IAM role. Use IAM Role for Service Accounts (IRSA) to provide access to the EKS Pods for the UI to Amazon S3 and the EKS Pods for the data services to DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) enables least-privilege AWS access per Kubernetes service account: Pods using the UI service account assume an IAM role with DynamoDB permissions, while Pods using the data-services service account assume a different IAM role with S3 permissions. IAM policies are attached to those IAM roles, and the service accounts are configured to assume them. This isolates the workload permissions; an EC2 node instance profile would not provide that per-Pod AWS permission boundary.

**Learn more:** [Assign IAM roles to Kubernetes service accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/associate-service-account-role.html) · [IAM roles for service accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html)

A company runs multiple production applications. One application includes resources from Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) in multiple AWS Regions. All company resources use a tag named `application` with a value that matches each application.  
  
A solutions architect must provide the fastest way to identify all components that have been tagged.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CloudTrail to generate a list of resources with the application tag.
Use the AWS CLI to query each service across all Regions to report the tagged components.
Run a query in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to report on the components with the application tag.
Run a query with the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to report on the resources globally with the application tag.

questions.explanation:
AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor is the fastest fit because it is built to find AWS resources by tag key and value across multiple Regions and across supported resource types. That directly matches the need to identify all resources tagged with the `application` tag for a specific application. The other options do not provide a direct cross-service, cross-Region tag inventory: AWS CloudTrail records API activity, CloudWatch Logs Insights queries logs, and using the AWS CLI against each service in each Region would require custom scripting and more effort than Tag Editor.

**Learn more:** [Finding resources to tag - Tagging AWS Resources and Tag Editor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/tag-editor/latest/userguide/find-resources-to-tag.html) · [Add and remove tags for Amazon EC2 resources - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags_Console.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon RDS with default backup settings for its database tier. The company needs to make a daily backup of the database to meet regulatory requirements. The company must retain the backups for **30 days**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function to create an RDS snapshot every day.
Modify the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups.
Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to modify the RDS backup retention period.
Create a manual snapshot every day by using the AWS CLI. Modify the RDS backup retention period.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS automated backups are built in, run daily, and support a configurable backup retention period of up to 35 days. Setting the DB instance backup retention period to 30 days satisfies the daily-backup and 30-day-retention requirements without adding custom automation or manual snapshot operations, so it is the lowest-overhead approach.

**Learn more:** [Backup retention period - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupRetention.html) · [Managing automated backups - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ManagingAutomatedBackups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team is building an event-driven application that uses AWS Lambda functions. Events are generated when files are added to an Amazon S3 bucket. The team currently has Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) configured as the event target from Amazon S3.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to process the Amazon S3 events in a scalable way?

options.text: Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) before the event runs in Lambda.
Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) before the event runs in Lambda
Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SOS queue to trigger a Lambda function.
Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure the Lambda function to poll from the SMS event.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon SQS between Amazon SNS and AWS Lambda provides a durable, scalable buffer for Amazon S3 event notifications. Amazon S3 can publish notifications to SNS, SNS can deliver them to SQS, and Lambda can be configured with an Amazon SQS event source mapping to poll the queue and scale processing as message volume changes. This decouples event production from function execution and handles traffic spikes more reliably than invoking compute platforms such as Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS for this purpose. AWS SMS is not an event-processing service for this workflow.

**Learn more:** [Event notification types and destinations - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html) · [Amazon SNS event sources and destinations - Amazon Simple Notification Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-event-sources-and-destinations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application in a VPC that contains public and private subnets. The VPC spans multiple Availability Zones. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets, and it uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.  
  
A solutions architect must design a secure way to establish connectivity between the EC2 instances and the SQS queue.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the private subnets. Add to the endpoint a security group that has an inbound access rule that allows traffic from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.

Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach to the interface endpoint a VPC endpoint policy that allows access from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.

Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach an Amazon SQS access policy to the interface VPC endpoint that allows requests from only a specified VPC endpoint.
Implement a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS. Add a NAT gateway to the private subnets. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances that allows access to the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is accessed privately from a VPC by using an **interface VPC endpoint** powered by AWS PrivateLink. Interface endpoints create endpoint network interfaces with private IP addresses in the selected subnets, and AWS recommends attaching a security group that allows the expected inbound HTTPS traffic from the VPC resources that will use the endpoint. This lets EC2 instances in private subnets connect to SQS without using the public internet, an internet gateway, or a NAT device. SQS does not use a gateway endpoint, so the gateway-endpoint option is invalid.

**Learn more:** [Internetwork traffic privacy in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-internetwork-traffic-privacy.html) · [Tutorial: Sending a message to an Amazon SQS queue from Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-sending-messages-from-vpc.html)

A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company's VPC. The application is publicly reachable on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center. This public endpoint can handle up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same performance level for the new public endpoint in AWS.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.
Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer is the correct fit because it is the AWS load balancer for Layer 4 traffic, supports TCP listeners on nonstandard ports, and is designed for ultra-low latency and millions of requests per second. The other options are built around HTTP/HTTPS-style application traffic rather than exposing a generic high-performance public TCP endpoint on a custom port.

**Learn more:** [PERF04-BP04 Use load balancing to distribute traffic across multiple resources - AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2024-06-27/framework/perf_networking_load_balancing_distribute_traffic.html) · [How does AWS PrivateLink work? - Securely Access Services Over AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-privatelink/how-does-aws-privatelink-work.html)

options.text: Turn on AWS Config with the appropriate rules.
Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor with the appropriate checks.
Turn on Amazon Inspector with the appropriate assessment template.
Turn on Amazon S3 server access logging. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon Cloud Watch Events).

questions.explanation:
AWS Config is the correct service because it records Amazon S3 bucket configurations, tracks configuration changes, and evaluates resources against AWS Config rules. AWS Config rules can be triggered by configuration changes, allowing the company to detect when an S3 bucket’s settings drift from the authorized state or become noncompliant. Trusted Advisor offers advisory checks rather than detailed configuration-change governance, Amazon Inspector is for vulnerability assessment, and S3 server access logging records access requests instead of enforcing or evaluating bucket configuration compliance.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Config Works - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/how-does-config-work.html) · [s3-bucket-blacklisted-actions-prohibited - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-blacklisted-actions-prohibited.html)

A company routinely uploads GB-sized files to Amazon S3. After the uploads complete, the company uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to transcode the files into another format. The company must scale throughput:  
  
- when uploading data from the on-premises data center to Amazon S3, and  
- when downloading data from Amazon S3 to the EC2 instances.  
  
Which solutions will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use the S3 bucket access point instead of accessing the S3 bucket directly.
Upload the files into multiple S3 buckets.
Use S3 multipart uploads.
Fetch multiple byte-ranges of an object in parallel.
Add a random prefix to each object when uploading the files.

questions.explanation:
For large Amazon S3 objects, multipart upload improves upload throughput by splitting a file into parts that can be uploaded in parallel. For high-throughput downloads, S3 performance guidance recommends issuing concurrent GET requests for multiple byte ranges of the same object, which increases aggregate download throughput. These two techniques directly address the required upload and download scaling behavior for GB-sized files.

**Learn more:** [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) · [Performance guidelines for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-guidelines.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is getting ready to deploy a new serverless workload. A solutions architect must apply the principle of least privilege to configure the permissions that will be used to run an AWS Lambda function. An Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule will invoke the function.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and * as the principal.
Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: lambda.amazonaws.com as the principal.
Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:* as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.
Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.

questions.explanation:
To allow Amazon EventBridge to invoke a Lambda function with least privilege, the permission should be granted in the Lambda function's resource-based policy to the EventBridge service principal, `events.amazonaws.com`, with only the `lambda:InvokeFunction` action. The Lambda execution role is for permissions the function itself uses when accessing other AWS services, not for authorizing EventBridge to call the function. Using `lambda:*` is broader than necessary and violates least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Using resource-based policies for Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-use-resource-based.html) · [Granting Lambda function access to AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/permissions-function-services.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends details about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API for processing. The company needs to make sure that orders are processed in the same order in which they are received.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.

Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.

Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS FIFO queues are built for workloads where message order must be preserved. AWS documents that FIFO queues strictly preserve the order in which messages are sent and received, and that Lambda processing with an SQS FIFO queue maintains ordered processing within a message group. Using API Gateway to send each order to an SQS FIFO queue and having Lambda process the queue satisfies the need for asynchronous processing while preserving order.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html) · [Amazon SQS FIFO queue and Lambda concurrency behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/fifo-queue-lambda-behavior.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is tuning a website for an upcoming musical event. Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then made available on demand. The event is expected to draw a global online audience.  
  
Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand streaming?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon Route 53
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the correct service because it is AWS’s content delivery network for distributing content to a global audience with edge locations, and AWS documentation specifically states that CloudFront can deliver both video on demand (VOD) and live streaming video. That makes it the appropriate service to improve playback performance for both the live event and the later on-demand streams.

**Learn more:** [Video on demand and live streaming video with CloudFront - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/on-demand-streaming-video.html) · [Deliver video streaming with CloudFront and AWS Media Services - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/live-streaming.html)

Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon Cloud Watch Events)."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"AWS Config is the correct service because it records Amazon S3 bucket configurations, tracks configuration changes, and evaluates resources against AWS Config rules. AWS Config rules can be triggered by configuration changes, allowing the company to detect when an S3 bucket’s settings drift from the authorized state or become noncompliant.
