53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company routinely uploads GB-sized files to Amazon S3. After the uploads complete, the company uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to transcode the files into another format. The company must scale throughput:"}],"
",["$","ul",null,{"children":["
",["$","li",null,{"children":"when uploading data from the on-premises data center to Amazon S3, and"}],"
",["$","li",null,{"children":"when downloading data from Amazon S3 to the EC2 instances."}],"
"]}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solutions will meet these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use the S3 bucket access point instead of accessing the S3 bucket directly.","B":"Upload the files into multiple S3 buckets.","C":"Use S3 multipart uploads.","D":"Fetch multiple byte-ranges of an object in parallel.","E":"Add a random prefix to each object when uploading the files."},"correctAnswer":"CD","explanation":"For large Amazon S3 objects, multipart upload improves upload throughput by splitting a file into parts that can be uploaded in parallel. For high-throughput downloads, S3 performance guidance recommends issuing concurrent GET requests for multiple byte ranges of the same object, which increases aggregate download throughput. These two techniques directly address the required upload and download scaling behavior for GB-sized files.

**Learn more:** [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) · [Performance guidelines for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-guidelines.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"35a6b006-5786-4423-8703-cc0fe2c164c5","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is getting ready to deploy a new serverless workload. A solutions architect must apply the principle of least privilege to configure the permissions that will be used to run an AWS Lambda function. An Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule will invoke the function."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and * as the principal.","B":"Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: lambda.amazonaws.com as the principal.","C":"Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:* as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.","D":"Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"To allow Amazon EventBridge to invoke a Lambda function with least privilege, the permission should be granted in the Lambda function's resource-based policy to the EventBridge service principal, `events.amazonaws.com`, with only the `lambda:InvokeFunction` action. The Lambda execution role is for permissions the function itself uses when accessing other AWS services, not for authorizing EventBridge to call the function. Using `lambda:*` is broader than necessary and violates least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Using resource-based policies for Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-use-resource-based.html) · [Granting Lambda function access to AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/permissions-function-services.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"5d6eb209-63f8-49d3-bc59-e057543545d9","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
55:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is developing an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends details about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API for processing. The company needs to make sure that orders are processed in the same order in which they are received."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.","B":"Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.","C":"Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.","D":"Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"Amazon SQS FIFO queues are built for workloads where message order must be preserved. AWS documents that FIFO queues strictly preserve the order in which messages are sent and received, and that Lambda processing with an SQS FIFO queue maintains ordered processing within a message group. Using API Gateway to send each order to an SQS FIFO queue and having Lambda process the queue satisfies the need for asynchronous processing while preserving order.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html) · [Amazon SQS FIFO queue and Lambda concurrency behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/fifo-queue-lambda-behavior.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"2cec62d6-9b9f-4959-89fa-0f4063502e2a","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]

A solutions architect has created a new AWS account and needs to secure access for the AWS account root user.  
  
Which combination of actions will achieve this? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Ensure the root user uses a strong password.
Enable multi-factor authentication to the root user.
Store root user access keys in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket.
Add the root user to a group containing administrative permissions.
Apply the required permissions to the root user with an inline policy document.

questions.explanation:
To secure an AWS account root user, AWS recommends protecting the root credentials with a strong, unique password and enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA). These are core root-user security best practices in AWS IAM documentation. By contrast, AWS advises against creating root access keys, and IAM groups or inline IAM policies are for IAM identities rather than for managing or limiting the built-in root user's inherent full-account permissions.

**Learn more:** [Root user best practices for your AWS account - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html) · [Multi-factor authentication for AWS account root user - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/enable-mfa-for-root.html)

A company needs to migrate **20 TB of data** from a data center to the **AWS Cloud** within **30 days**. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to **15 Mbps** and must not go above **70% utilization**.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Snowball.
Use AWS DataSync.
Use a secure VPN connection.
Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

questions.explanation:
AWS Snowball is the right choice because the effective available WAN bandwidth is only about 10.5 Mbps, which is not enough to move 20 TB within 30 days. Snowball is designed for offline data transfer into AWS for cases involving large data volumes or constrained network connectivity, whereas AWS DataSync, a VPN connection, and Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration still depend on the network path and therefore would not satisfy the transfer window under the stated bandwidth constraint.

**Learn more:** [Large data migration with Snowball Edge - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/LargeDataMigration.html) · [AWS Snowball FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/snowball/faqs/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must design a solution that uses Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 origin to host a static website. The company’s security policy requires that all website traffic be inspected by AWS WAF.  
  
How should the solutions architect meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an S3 bucket policy to accept requests coming from the AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) only.
Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward all incoming requests to AWS WAF before requesting content from the S3 origin.
Configure a security group that allows Amazon CloudFront IP addresses to access Amazon S3 only. Associate AWS WAF to CloudFront.
Configure Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the S3 bucket. Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF protects a CloudFront distribution by attaching a web ACL to the distribution, so all viewer requests are inspected at CloudFront before the content is served. To ensure traffic cannot bypass that inspection and reach the content directly from Amazon S3, the S3 bucket should be restricted so that only CloudFront can access it. In the given choices, using an origin access identity (OAI) with CloudFront and enabling AWS WAF on the distribution is the correct design.

**Learn more:** [Use AWS WAF protections - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html) · [Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs workloads on AWS. The company needs to connect to a service from an external provider. The service is hosted in the provider's VPC. According to the company’s security team, the connectivity must be private and must be limited to the target service. The connection must be initiated only from the company’s VPC.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the company's VPC and the provider's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
Ask the provider to create a virtual private gateway in its VPC. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.
Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet of the company’s VPUpdate the route table to connect to the target service.
Ask the provider to create a VPC endpoint for the target service. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink enables private, one-way connectivity from a consumer VPC to a specific service hosted by a provider, without exposing full VPC-to-VPC connectivity or using the public internet. The provider creates a VPC endpoint service, and the consumer creates an interface VPC endpoint to connect to it. This satisfies all requirements: private connectivity, restriction to the target service only, and initiation only from the company's VPC.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS PrivateLink?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/endpoint-services-overview.html) · [AWS PrivateLink concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a legacy application to generate data in CSV format. The legacy application saves the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can run complex SQL queries to analyze data stored only in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3. However, the COTS application cannot process the `.csv` files that the legacy application generates.  
  
The company cannot modify the legacy application to generate data in a different format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data produced by the legacy application.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.

Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue is a fully managed, serverless ETL service that can transform CSV data from Amazon S3 and load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift. That makes the legacy output usable by an application that can query Redshift, while avoiding the extra infrastructure management of Amazon EC2 or Amazon EMR. DynamoDB does not satisfy the storage constraint because the application can use only Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3. Amazon Redshift also supports querying data in Amazon S3 through external tables, but among the listed options, the managed Glue ETL approach is the lowest-overhead way to convert the CSV output into data the COTS application can analyze.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Redshift Spectrum](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c-using-spectrum.html) · [Querying your data lake - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/gsg/data-lake.html)

A company offers an API to its users that automates requests for tax calculations based on item prices. The company has a higher volume of requests only during the holiday season, and this increase causes slower response times. A solutions architect must design a solution that is both scalable and elastic.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to achieve this?

options.text: Provide an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance performs the required computations when the API request is made.
Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that accepts the item names. API Gateway passes item names to AWS Lambda for tax computations.
Create an Application Load Balancer that has two Amazon EC2 instances behind it. The EC2 instances will compute the tax on the received item names.
Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that connects with an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. API Gateway accepts and passes the item names to the EC2 instance for tax computations.

questions.explanation:
A REST API built with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda is the most scalable and elastic option because it uses a serverless architecture. API Gateway provides the API endpoint, and Lambda executes the tax-computation logic only when requests arrive, automatically scaling with demand instead of requiring preprovisioned Amazon EC2 capacity. That makes it well suited for seasonal traffic spikes such as holiday-only increases in request volume.

**Learn more:** [Lambda integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-integrations.html) · [Lambda scaling behavior - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating applications from a self-managed, on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to AWS. The company deploys the applications across multiple AWS accounts and uses AWS Organizations to manage those accounts centrally.  
  
The security team requires a single sign-on solution across all of the company's AWS accounts. The company must continue to manage users and groups in the on-premises Active Directory.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Enterprise Edition Active Directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Configure the Active Directory to be the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center.

Enable AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure a two-way forest trust relationship to connect the company's self-managed Active Directory with IAM Identity Center by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
Use AWS Directory Service and create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Active Directory.
Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on Amazon EC2. Link the IdP as an identity source within AWS IAM Identity Center.

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM Identity Center is the AWS service for centralized single sign-on across multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. When identities must continue to be managed in an on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory, the supported approach is to connect that directory to IAM Identity Center by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory with a **two-way forest trust**. The two-way trust is required so IAM Identity Center can both authenticate users and read user and group information from the on-premises directory for assignments and access management.

**Learn more:** [Connect a self-managed directory in Active Directory to IAM Identity Center](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/connectonpremad.html) · [Manage your identity source - AWS IAM Identity Center](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/manage-your-identity-source.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to improve its on-premises disaster recovery (DR) configuration. The company's core production business application uses Microsoft SQL Server Standard and runs on a virtual machine (VM). The application has:  
  
- a recovery point objective (RPO) of 30 seconds or fewer  
- a recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes  
  
The DR solution must minimize costs wherever possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure a multi-site active/active setup between the on-premises server and AWS by using Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise with Always On availability groups.
Configure a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database on AWS. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to use change data capture (CDC).
Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery configured to replicate disk changes to AWS as a pilot light.
Use third-party backup software to capture backups every night. Store a secondary set of backups in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery is the best match because it provides continuous block-level replication for on-premises server workloads into AWS, uses a pilot light approach to keep costs low, and is documented to support recovery point objectives measured in seconds or sub-seconds with recovery times typically measured in minutes. That satisfies the required RPO of 30 seconds or less and the RTO of 60 minutes while protecting the VM-based SQL Server Standard application as a whole. Nightly backups cannot meet the RPO, and a multi-site active/active design with SQL Server Enterprise is unnecessarily expensive and depends on a different edition than the stated SQL Server Standard workload.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Disaster Recovery Concepts - AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/CloudEndure-Concepts.html) · [Disaster recovery options in the cloud - Disaster Recovery of Workloads on AWS: Recovery in the Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)

A solutions architect is creating a new Amazon CloudFront distribution for an application. Some of the information submitted by users is sensitive. The application uses HTTPS but requires another layer of security. The sensitive information must be protected throughout the entire application stack, and access to the information must be limited to certain applications.  
  
Which action should the solutions architect take?

options.text: Configure a CloudFront signed URL.
Configure a CloudFront signed cookie.
Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.
Configure CloudFront and set the Origin Protocol Policy setting to HTTPS Only for the Viewer Protocol Policy.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront field-level encryption provides an additional security layer beyond HTTPS by encrypting selected sensitive form fields at the edge. Those fields remain encrypted throughout the application stack, and only applications that have the credentials to decrypt them can access the data. That directly matches the need to protect sensitive user-submitted information end to end within the application flow while restricting access to specific applications.

**Learn more:** [Use field-level encryption to help protect sensitive data - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html) · [Data protection in Amazon CloudFront - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/data-protection-summary.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its data management application to AWS. The company wants to move to an event-driven architecture. The architecture must be more distributed and must use serverless concepts while handling the different parts of the workflow. The company also wants to reduce operational overhead as much as possible.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Build out the workflow in AWS Glue. Use AWS Glue to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.
Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Step Functions to invoke the workflow steps on the EC2 instances.
Build out the workflow in Amazon EventBridge. Use EventBridge to invoke AWS Lambda functions on a schedule to process the workflow steps.
Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Use Step Functions to create a state machine. Use the state machine to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.

questions.explanation:
AWS Step Functions is a serverless workflow orchestration service that coordinates distributed application components by using state machines, and it integrates natively with AWS Lambda for serverless step execution. That combination satisfies the need for an event-driven, distributed, serverless workflow while minimizing operational overhead because there are no servers to manage. AWS Glue is aimed at data integration and ETL rather than general application workflow orchestration, EventBridge provides event routing and scheduling rather than multi-step stateful workflow control, and Amazon EC2 introduces instance management overhead that conflicts with the serverless and low-operations requirements.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Step Functions?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/welcome.html) · [AWS Step Functions Developer Guide - State machines](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-statemachines.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its data and applications to AWS as part of a multiyear migration project. The company needs to securely access data on Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location. The data must not travel across the internet. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 interface endpoints use AWS PrivateLink to provide private connectivity to S3 by using private IP addresses in a VPC, and they support access from on-premises applications through AWS Direct Connect while keeping traffic on the AWS network. By contrast, S3 gateway endpoints are for VPC access only and do not support access from on-premises networks over Direct Connect. AWS Transit Gateway does not create S3 service access in this way, and AWS KMS only handles encryption, not private network connectivity.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink for Amazon S3 - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon VPC User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's marketing data is uploaded from multiple sources into an Amazon S3 bucket. A series of data preparation jobs aggregates the data for reporting. The data preparation jobs must run at regular intervals in parallel, and a few jobs must run later in a specific sequence.  
  
The company wants to eliminate the operational overhead of job error handling, retry logic, and state management.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data as soon as the data is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Invoke other Lambda functions at regularly scheduled intervals.
Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke Athena on a regular internal.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to run the DataBrew data preparation jobs.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to process the data. Schedule Data Pipeline to process the data once at midnight.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue DataBrew is built for data preparation, and AWS Step Functions can orchestrate DataBrew jobs in workflows that include parallel execution, ordered steps, built-in retry behavior, error handling, and managed state. That combination directly matches the need for regularly scheduled data-preparation jobs with some branches running concurrently and others running later in sequence, without requiring the company to implement its own orchestration logic.

**Learn more:** [Start AWS Glue DataBrew jobs with Step Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-databrew.html) · [Handling errors in Step Functions workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to create a web application on AWS. Client requests to access the website are unpredictable and might remain idle for extended periods. Only customers who have paid a subscription fee should be able to sign in and use the web application.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.
Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.
Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.
Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.
Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.

questions.explanation:
API Gateway with AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB is a strong cost-effective architecture for bursty, idle-heavy web workloads because it is serverless and scales on demand without requiring continuously running application servers or database instances. Amazon Cognito user pools are the AWS service for authenticating application users and controlling sign-in for subscribed users. AWS Amplify Hosting is designed to host frontend web content such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and it uses Amazon CloudFront for content delivery. By contrast, Cognito identity pools provide temporary AWS credentials rather than primary app-user authentication, ECS with RDS would usually cost more for long idle periods, and Amazon S3 static website hosting does not execute PHP.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Cognito user pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools.html) · [How authentication works with Amazon Cognito](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-how-to-authenticate.html)

An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that has an Elastic IP address in VPC A. The application requires access to a database in VPC B. Both VPCs are in the same AWS account.  
  
Which solution will provide the required access **MOST securely**?

options.text: Create a DB instance security group that allows all traffic from the public IP address of the application server in VPC A.
Configure a VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B.
Make the DB instance publicly accessible. Assign a public IP address to the DB instance.
Launch an EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address into VPC B. Proxy all requests through the new EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
A VPC peering connection is the most secure solution because it allows resources in VPC A and VPC B to communicate using private IP addresses without traversing the public internet. AWS RDS guidance specifically identifies VPC peering as the way to access a DB instance from an EC2 instance in a different VPC. Using the application server’s public IP, making the database publicly accessible, or inserting a public proxy EC2 instance all increase exposure compared with private VPC-to-VPC connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Scenarios for accessing a DB instance in a VPC - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.Scenarios.html) · [Connect VPCs using VPC peering - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-peering.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to improve its ecommerce order-processing application that runs on AWS. The application must process every order exactly one time without affecting the customer experience during unpredictable traffic spikes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Put all the orders in the SQS queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topic. Publish all the orders to the SNS standard topic. Configure the application as a notification target.
Create a flow by using Amazon AppFlow. Send the orders to the flow. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
Configure AWS X-Ray in the application to track the order requests. Configure the application to process the orders by pulling the orders from Amazon CloudWatch.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS FIFO queues are built for workloads that cannot tolerate duplicates and need exactly-once processing semantics with durable buffering. Using a FIFO queue decouples order submission from backend processing so the application can absorb traffic surges without slowing the customer-facing experience, and an AWS Lambda consumer can process queued orders asynchronously. By contrast, an Amazon SNS standard topic does not provide exactly-once processing, Amazon AppFlow is intended for data-transfer integrations rather than transactional order buffering, and AWS X-Ray with CloudWatch provides tracing and monitoring rather than message-based order processing.

**Learn more:** [Exactly-once processing in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html) · [Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a three-tier application for image sharing. The application uses an Amazon EC2 instance for the front-end layer, a second EC2 instance for the application layer, and a third EC2 instance for a MySQL database.  
  
A solutions architect must design a scalable and highly available solution that requires the least amount of change to the application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.

Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance with multiple read replicas to serve users’ images.

Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the application layer. Move the database to a memory optimized instance type to store and serve users’ images.

Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.

questions.explanation:
A load-balanced, Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment provides horizontal scaling and high availability for the front-end and application tiers while preserving an EC2-based web application model with minimal refactoring. Amazon RDS Multi-AZ is the correct high-availability target for a MySQL database because it keeps a relational MySQL-compatible database and provides failover support without requiring the application to be redesigned. Amazon S3 is the appropriate service to store and serve users’ images because it provides durable, scalable object storage shared across instances. Read replicas are primarily for read scaling, and a standard RDS Multi-AZ DB instance standby does not serve read traffic.

**Learn more:** [Environment types - AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features-managing-env-types.html) · [Load balancer for your Elastic Beanstalk environment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.managing.elb.html)

A company's developers need a secure method to obtain SSH access to the company's Amazon EC2 instances that run the latest version of Amazon Linux. The developers work both remotely and from the corporate office.  
  
The company wants to use AWS services as part of the solution. The EC2 instances are hosted in a VPC private subnet and access the internet through a NAT gateway deployed in a public subnet.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create a bastion host in the same subnet as the EC2 instances. Grant the ec2:CreateVpnConnection IAM permission to the developers. Install EC2 Instance Connect so that the developers can connect to the EC2 instances.

Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the corporate network and the VPC. Instruct the developers to use the Site-to-Site VPN connection to access the EC2 instances when the developers are on the corporate network. Instruct the developers to set up another VPN connection for access when they work remotely.

Create a bastion host in the public subnet of the VPConfigure the security groups and SSH keys of the bastion host to only allow connections and SSH authentication from the developers’ corporate and remote networks. Instruct the developers to connect through the bastion host by using SSH to reach the EC2 instances.

Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore IAM policy to an IAM role that is associated with the EC2 instances. Instruct the developers to use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to access the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure shell access to EC2 instances without requiring inbound SSH access, a bastion host, or a VPN. Amazon Linux instances can be managed through Systems Manager by attaching an IAM role that includes the `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` policy and ensuring the instance has outbound connectivity to Systems Manager endpoints, which a private-subnet instance can obtain through the existing NAT gateway. This approach reduces cost and operational overhead while improving security because no public access path to port 22 is needed.

**Learn more:** [Set up Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-getting-started.html) · [AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore AWS managed policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.html)

A company hosts a data lake on AWS. The data lake contains data in Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.  
  
The company needs a reporting solution that provides data visualization and includes all the data sources in the data lake. Only the company's management team should have full access to all the visualizations. The rest of the company should have only limited access.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate IAM roles.
Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate users and groups.

Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to produce reports. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.

Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena Federated Query to access data within Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Generate reports by using Amazon Athena. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon QuickSight is the appropriate AWS service for building visualizations and dashboards from multiple data sources, including Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. QuickSight dashboards are published from analyses and can be shared with specific QuickSight users and groups, with different permission levels such as viewer or co-owner, which supports giving management broader access while limiting access for other employees.

**Learn more:** [Supported data sources - Amazon QuickSight](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/supported-data-sources.html) · [Sharing Amazon QuickSight dashboards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/sharing-a-dashboard.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has recently migrated its full IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company finds that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and changing security group rules without following the proper change control process.  
  
A solutions architect must design a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes.  
  
Which actions should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail is the correct service for auditing because it records AWS API and console activity, including Amazon EC2 actions, with details such as who made the request, when it occurred, and the source IP. AWS Config is the correct service for tracking inventory and configuration changes because it continuously records supported resource configurations, keeps configuration history, and can evaluate resources against AWS Config rules for compliance. Together, CloudTrail and AWS Config provide the required audit trail plus configuration and compliance tracking for EC2 instance sizing and security group changes.

**Learn more:** [What Is AWS CloudTrail? - AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html) · [Log Amazon EC2 API calls using AWS CloudTrail - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/monitor-with-cloudtrail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores data in Amazon S3. Based on regulatory requirements, the data must not include personally identifiable information (PII). The company recently discovered that some objects in its S3 buckets contain PII.  
  
The company needs to automatically detect PII in the S3 buckets and notify the company’s security team.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.

Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.

Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.

Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Macie is AWS's managed service for discovering and classifying sensitive data, including PII in S3 objects. It generates findings with type SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal for personally identifiable information. EventBridge can filter these findings and route them to Amazon SNS for immediate notification to the security team. GuardDuty detects security threats, not data classification, making it unsuitable for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Processing Macie findings with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/findings-monitor-events-eventbridge.html)

options.text: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.

Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.

Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon SNS with Amazon SQS queues and SNS subscription filter policies lets the application publish each quote request once and have SNS route it to the correct SQS queue based on quote type. SQS is the durable work queue in this pattern: messages are retained until processed or expired, with retention configurable up to 14 days, so requests can wait up to 24 hours without being lost. This is more operationally efficient and lower maintenance than building separate Kinesis stream consumers, and it is more appropriate than Firehose, which is designed for data delivery to destinations such as OpenSearch rather than backend work-item processing.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SNS message filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-message-filtering.html) · [Amazon SNS features and capabilities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome-features.html)

A company wants to back up its on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to AWS. The company's backup solution exports the on-premises backups to an Amazon S3 bucket as objects. The S3 backups must be kept for 30 days and must be deleted automatically after 30 days.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Create an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock enabled.
Create an S3 bucket that has object versioning enabled.
Configure a default retention period of 30 days for the objects.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to protect the objects for 30 days.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to expire the objects after 30 days.
Configure the backup solution to tag the objects with a 30-day retention period

questions.explanation:
Creating an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled automatically turns on S3 Versioning as part of that same action, so a separate step to enable versioning is redundant once Object Lock is chosen at bucket creation. Configuring a default retention period of 30 days enforces that objects cannot be deleted or overwritten before the period elapses, and an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires objects after 30 days removes them automatically once that window ends. Object Lock alone provides no automatic cleanup and a lifecycle rule alone provides no protection against early deletion, so both must be paired with the retention configuration.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with Object Lock - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [Configuring S3 Object Lock - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-configure.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has 15 employees. The company stores employee start dates in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to send an email message to each employee on the day of the employee's work anniversary.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

questions.explanation:
A scheduled AWS Lambda function is the most operationally efficient choice because it is serverless and avoids the overhead of managing an Amazon EC2 instance and cron job. Amazon SNS can deliver notification messages to email subscribers, whereas Amazon SQS is a message queue and does not directly send email to employees. For a small daily task that scans DynamoDB and sends notifications only when needed, Lambda plus a daily schedule and SNS best fits the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Invoke a Lambda function on a schedule - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html) · [What is Amazon SNS? - Amazon Simple Notification Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to transfer data from an Amazon EC2 instance to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that neither API calls nor data traffic traverse public internet routes. Only the EC2 instance can be allowed to upload data to the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the Availability Zone where the EC2 instance is located. Attach appropriate security groups to the endpoint. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Run the nslookup tool from inside the EC2 instance to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Use the AWS provided, publicly available ip-ranges.json file to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

questions.explanation:
An interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink) places an elastic network interface with a private IP in the EC2 instance's subnet, so both API calls and data traffic to Amazon S3 stay on the AWS private network and never traverse the public internet; an attached S3 bucket resource policy then restricts uploads to only the EC2 instance's IAM role. Option A is the only technically valid choice. Option B is invalid because gateway VPC endpoints are not deployed 'in an Availability Zone' and cannot have security groups attached — they are route-table constructs. Options C and D rely on discovering a 'private IP' of S3 and adding a static route, which is not how S3 connectivity works and would not keep traffic off the internet.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Choosing your VPC endpoint strategy for S3](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/choosing-your-vpc-endpoint-strategy-for-amazon-s3/)

A company is releasing a new application and will show application metrics on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard.  
  
The company's product manager needs periodic access to this dashboard. The product manager does not have an AWS account.  
  
A solutions architect must provide access for the product manager while following the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Share the dashboard from the CloudWatch console. Enter the product manager's email address, and complete the sharing steps. Provide a shareable link for the dashboard to the product manager.

Create an IAM user specifically for the product manager. Attach the CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Share the browser URL of the correct dashboard with the product manager.

Create an IAM user for the company's employees. Attach the ViewOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Ask the product manager to navigate to the CloudWatch console and locate the dashboard by name in the Dashboards section.

Deploy a bastion server in a public subnet. When the product manager requires access to the dashboard, start the server and share the RDP credentials. On the bastion server, ensure that the browser is configured to open the dashboard URL with cached AWS credentials that have appropriate permissions to view the dashboard.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch can share a single dashboard with specific email addresses, allowing external users to access that dashboard without creating an AWS account. AWS sends the invited user credentials for the shared dashboard, and this limits access more tightly than creating an IAM user with broad read-only console permissions. That makes dashboard sharing with the product manager's email address the least-privilege solution.

**Learn more:** [Sharing a CloudWatch dashboard with specific users - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/share-cloudwatch-dashboard-email-addresses.html) · [Sharing CloudWatch dashboards - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch-dashboard-sharing.html)

Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Using Amazon SNS with Amazon SQS queues and SNS subscription filter policies lets the application publish each quote request once and have SNS route it to the correct SQS queue based on quote type. SQS is the durable work queue in this pattern: messages are retained until processed or expired, with retention configurable up to 14 days, so requests can wait up to 24 hours without being lost. This is more operationally efficient and lower maintenance than building separate Kinesis stream consumers, and it is more appropriate than Firehose, which is designed for data delivery to destinations such as OpenSearch rather than backend work-item processing.

A company runs a food delivery service. Due to recent growth, its order-processing system is encountering scaling issues during peak-traffic periods. The existing architecture has Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that collect orders from an application. A second Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances fulfills the orders.  
  
The order-collection process completes quickly, whereas order fulfillment can take longer. Data must not be lost as a result of a scaling event.  
  
A solutions architect must ensure that both the order-collection process and the order-fulfillment process can scale sufficiently during peak-traffic periods.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to meet its peak workload value.

Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to create additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.

Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.

Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on the number of messages in each queue.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS durably buffers messages between independently scaling components, preventing orders from being lost when consumer capacity changes. Having each EC2 Auto Scaling group poll its respective queue decouples the fast collection stage from the slower fulfillment stage. Queue message backlog provides the demand signal for scaling each group independently; in production, this is commonly implemented as a backlog-per-instance CloudWatch metric.

**Learn more:** [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html) · [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)

A company has 5 TB of datasets. The datasets consist of 1 million user profiles and 10 million connections. The user profiles have connections as many-to-many relationships. The company needs a performance-efficient way to find mutual connections up to five levels.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the datasets. Use Amazon Athena to perform SQL JOIN queries to find connections.
Use Amazon Neptune to store the datasets with edges and vertices. Query the data to find connections.
Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the datasets. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize connections.
Use Amazon RDS to store the datasets with multiple tables. Perform SQL JOIN queries to find connections.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Neptune is the correct service because this is a highly connected many-to-many dataset that requires efficient multi-level relationship traversal. Neptune is a purpose-built graph database that models data as vertices and edges and is optimized for storing billions of relationships and querying connected data with low latency. That makes it a better fit than relational SQL JOINs or S3-based analytics for finding mutual connections across up to five hops.

**Learn more:** [What Is Amazon Neptune?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Getting started with Amazon Neptune](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/graph-get-started.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team must host a website that will be accessed by other teams. The website content consists of:  
  
- HTML  
- CSS  
- client-side JavaScript  
- images  
  
Which method is the **MOST cost-effective** for hosting the website?

options.text: Containerize the website and host it in AWS Fargate.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket and host the website there.
Deploy a web server on an Amazon EC2 instance to host the website.
Configure an Application Load Balancer with an AWS Lambda target that uses the Express.js framework.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective choice for a website made entirely of static content such as HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images. AWS documentation states that Amazon S3 can host a static website directly, eliminating the need to run or manage web servers or containers. Using AWS Fargate, Amazon EC2, or an Application Load Balancer with AWS Lambda would add unnecessary compute and infrastructure cost for a purely static site.

**Learn more:** [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3 - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html) · [Use Amazon S3 website hosting to host without a single web server - Hosting Static Websites on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/build-static-websites-aws/use-amazon-s3-website-hosting-to-host-without-a-single-web-server.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a large data workload that runs for 6 hours each day. The company cannot lose any data while the process is running. A solutions architect is designing an Amazon EMR cluster configuration to support this critical data workload.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance and the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance, the core nodes on Spot Instances, and the task nodes on Spot Instances.

questions.explanation:
For a daily workload that runs only part of the day, an Amazon EMR transient cluster is more cost-effective than a long-running cluster because it can terminate after the processing completes instead of accruing charges continuously. For a data-critical workload, the primary and core nodes should run on On-Demand Instances, because core nodes store HDFS data and using Spot for core nodes risks data loss if they are interrupted. Task nodes do not store data in HDFS, so running task nodes on Spot Instances provides the cost savings without violating the no-data-loss requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configuring an Amazon EMR cluster to continue or terminate after step execution - Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-longrunning-transient.html) · [Understand node types in Amazon EMR: primary, core, and task nodes - Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-master-core-task-nodes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has more than 5 TB of file data on on-premises Windows file servers. Users and applications interact with the data every day.  
  
The company is migrating its Windows workloads to AWS. While this migration continues, the company must have access to both AWS file storage and on-premises file storage with minimum latency. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead and does not require significant changes to existing file access patterns. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for connectivity to AWS.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Move the on-premises file data to FSx for Windows File Server. Reconfigure the workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.

Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the S3 File Gateway. Reconfigure the on-premises workloads and the cloud workloads to use the S3 File Gateway.

Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to Amazon S3. Reconfigure the workloads to use either Amazon S3 directly or the S3 File Gateway. depending on each workload's location.

Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Configure the on-premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the managed AWS service that preserves native Windows SMB file access patterns for migrated Windows workloads, and Amazon FSx File Gateway is built to extend that FSx storage to on-premises users and applications with a local cache for low-latency access. This combination provides shared hybrid access to the same file data from AWS and on premises, minimizes management effort, and avoids redesigning applications around Amazon S3 object storage.

**Learn more:** [Accessing your data - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html) · [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html)

A company has an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that stores a reference dataset. The company has applications running on Amazon EC2 instances that need to read the dataset.  
  
However, the applications must not be able to change the dataset. The company wants to use IAM access control to prevent the applications from modifying or deleting the dataset.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Mount the EFS file system in read-only mode from within the EC2 instances.
Create a resource policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action to the IAM roles that are attached to the EC2 instances.
Create an identity policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action on the EFS file system.
Create an EFS access point for each application. Use Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX) file permissions to allow read-only access to files in the root directory.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS IAM authorization distinguishes between mounting a file system and writing to it. `elasticfilesystem:ClientMount` allows read access, while `elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite` grants write permissions. Because EFS evaluates a file system resource policy together with any identity-based IAM policies for the EC2 instance roles, a resource policy that denies `elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite` for those roles allows the applications to read the dataset but prevents modifications and deletions. This directly satisfies the requirement to enforce the restriction by using IAM access control.

**Learn more:** [Using IAM to control access to file systems - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/iam-access-control-nfs-efs.html) · [Creating file system policies - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/create-file-system-policy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company did not configure encryption on the S3 bucket before the objects were loaded. A solutions architect must enable encryption for all existing objects and for all objects that will be added to the S3 bucket in the future.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** amount of effort?

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket. Turn on the default encryption settings for the new S3 bucket. Download all existing objects to temporary local storage. Upload the objects to the new S3 bucket.

Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file that lists the unencrypted objects. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.

Create a new encryption key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Change the settings on the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Turn on versioning for the S3 bucket.

Navigate to Amazon S3 in the AWS Management Console. Browse the S3 bucket’s objects. Sort by the encryption field. Select each unencrypted object. Use the Modify button to apply default encryption settings to every unencrypted object in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 default encryption applies to new objects going forward, but it does not encrypt objects that were already in the bucket. Existing unencrypted objects must be rewritten, and Amazon S3 Batch Operations can use a copy operation to write those objects back as encrypted objects at scale. S3 Inventory can produce the list of unencrypted objects to use as the batch manifest. This combination satisfies both requirements with minimal operational effort for a bucket containing millions of objects.

**Learn more:** [Default encryption FAQ - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/default-encryption-faq.html) · [Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)

A company operates a media store on multiple Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones within a single VPC. The company needs a high-performance way to share data among all EC2 instances and prefers that the data remain only within the VPC.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and call the service APIs from each instance's application
Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure all instances to access it as a mounted volume
Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and mount it across all instances
Configure an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and mount it across all instances

questions.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a managed, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones in a VPC. It is designed for shared, high-performance file access while keeping network access controlled through VPC mount targets and security groups.

A company is designing an application on AWS that handles sensitive data. The application stores and processes financial data for multiple customers.  
  
To satisfy compliance requirements, each customer's data must be encrypted separately at rest by using a secure, centralized key-management solution. The company wants to use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to implement encryption.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Generate a unique encryption key for each customer. Store the keys in an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable server-side encryption.

Deploy a hardware security appliance in the AWS environment that securely stores customer-provided encryption keys. Integrate the security appliance with AWS KMS to encrypt the sensitive data in the application.
Create a single AWS KMS key to encrypt all sensitive data across the application.
Create separate AWS KMS keys for each customer's data that have granular access control and logging enabled.

questions.explanation:
Separate customer-managed AWS KMS keys provide cryptographic separation for each customer's data while allowing key policies and grants to enforce granular access control. AWS KMS integrates with AWS CloudTrail to audit KMS key-management and cryptographic operations, without the operational burden of managing encryption keys in storage or operating dedicated hardware.

**Learn more:** [AWS KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/concepts.html) · [Logging AWS KMS API calls with AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html)
