A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS supports native envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enabling EKS secrets encryption encrypts the Kubernetes `secrets` resources stored by the cluster, which is exactly the data identified in the requirement. This is the lowest-overhead approach because the encryption is handled by the managed EKS control plane rather than by custom application logic, Lambda automation, or moving the data to another service. For EKS API encryption, the supported encrypted resource is `secrets`, and AWS documents that Kubernetes secrets are encrypted by using the AWS KMS key you select.

**Learn more:** [Encrypt Kubernetes secrets with KMS on existing clusters - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-kms.html) · [EncryptionConfig - Amazon EKS API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/APIReference/API_EncryptionConfig.html)

An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to build and train models. The company will use the models to visualize complex scenarios and detect trends in customer data. The architecture team wants to integrate the ML models with a reporting platform so it can analyze the enriched data and use that data directly in its business intelligence dashboards.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS Glue to create an ML transform to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
Use Amazon SageMaker to build and train models. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
Use a pre-built ML Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the AWS Marketplace to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
Use Amazon QuickSight to build and train models by using calculated fields. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker is the AWS fully managed service for building and training ML models, which directly satisfies the model development requirement. Amazon QuickSight is AWS’s business intelligence service for analyses, visualizations, and dashboards, so it fits the reporting-platform and dashboard requirement while minimizing infrastructure management. The other options either use a tool not intended for general ML model building and training, or require managing more infrastructure than necessary.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon SageMaker AI?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/sagemaker/latest/dg/whatis.html) · [Train a Model with Amazon SageMaker](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/how-it-works-training.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is designing the network for an online multi-player game. The game uses the UDP networking protocol and will be deployed in eight AWS Regions. The network architecture must minimize latency and packet loss to provide end users with a high-quality gaming experience.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Setup a transit gateway in each Region. Create inter-Region peering attachments between each transit gateway.
Set up AWS Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region.
Set up Amazon CloudFront with UDP turned on. Configure an origin in each Region.
Set up a VPC peering mesh between each Region. Turn on UDP for each VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct solution because it provides global entry points that route client traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy regional endpoint, which is intended to improve latency and reliability for globally distributed applications. Standard accelerators support UDP listeners, and listeners are associated with endpoint groups that are defined per AWS Region, fitting a deployment across eight Regions. Transit Gateway peering and VPC peering only connect AWS networks to each other, and CloudFront is not the service for general UDP application traffic.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-listeners.html) · [Endpoint groups for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoint-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is getting ready to launch a public-facing web application in the AWS Cloud. The architecture includes Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC behind an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB). A third-party DNS service is being used.  
  
The company's solutions architect must recommend a way to detect and protect against large-scale DDoS attacks.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty on the account.
Enable Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.
Enable AWS Shield and assign Amazon Route 53 to it.
Enable AWS Shield Advanced and assign the ELB to it.

questions.explanation:
AWS Shield Advanced is the AWS service designed for enhanced detection and mitigation of large-scale DDoS attacks, and it can be applied directly to Elastic Load Balancing load balancers. Because the company is not using Amazon Route 53 for DNS, protecting a Route 53 hosted zone would not address the stated architecture. GuardDuty and Inspector serve different purposes—threat detection and vulnerability assessment, respectively—and do not provide the required DDoS protection for the internet-facing load balancer.

**Learn more:** [AWS Shield Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/shield/) · [List of resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-protections-by-resource-type.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a centralized AWS account to store log data in multiple Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect must ensure that the data is encrypted at rest **before** it is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for S3 uploads.
Enable the security option to encrypt the S3 buckets through the use of a default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.

questions.explanation:
Client-side encryption is the correct solution because it encrypts the data locally before it is sent to Amazon S3, which satisfies the requirement that the data be encrypted at rest before upload. AWS documentation for the Amazon S3 Encryption Client states that client-side encryption encrypts objects before sending them to S3 and provides end-to-end protection in transit and at rest. By contrast, server-side encryption, bucket policies requiring SSE-S3, and default bucket encryption apply encryption only after Amazon S3 receives the object.

**Learn more:** [Protecting data by using client-side encryption - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html) · [Client-side and server-side encryption - Amazon S3 Encryption Client](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/client-server-side.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's order system sends requests from clients to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances process the orders and then store the orders in a database on Amazon RDS. Users report that they have to reprocess orders when the system fails. The company wants a resilient solution that can automatically process orders if a system outage occurs.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to target an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task.
Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the order system to send messages to the ALB endpoint.

Move the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group. Configure the order system to send messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the EC2 instances to consume messages from the queue.

Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function, and subscribe the function to the SNS topic. Configure the order system to send messages to the SNS topic. Send a command to the EC2 instances to process the messages by using AWS Systems Manager Run Command.

questions.explanation:
A durable queue between the order system and the EC2 workers makes the workflow resilient because messages remain available even if processing instances fail temporarily. Amazon SQS is specifically intended to decouple distributed components and buffer requests durably, and EC2 instances can poll the queue and process outstanding messages after recovery or scaling events. Putting the workers in an Auto Scaling group supports replacement and scaling of failed instances, while SQS prevents order loss during outages. Official AWS guidance describes SQS as a durable, available queue for decoupling components and documents scaling EC2 Auto Scaling workloads that consume messages from SQS.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html) · [Configure scaling based on Amazon SQS - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scale-sqs-queue-cli.html)

A company runs workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to centrally collect security data to assess security across the entire company and to improve workload protection.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Configure a data lake in AWS Lake Formation. Use AWS Glue crawlers to ingest the security data into the data lake.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to collect the security data in .csv format. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Configure a data lake in Amazon Security Lake to collect the security data. Upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to load the security data into an Amazon RDS cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Security Lake is a fully managed, purpose-built security data lake service that automatically centralizes security data from AWS environments and other sources into an S3-backed data lake. It is designed to help organizations analyze security data, understand security posture across the entire organization, and improve protection of workloads, applications, and data. Because it provides native collection and normalization for security data, it requires less development effort than building a generic lake with Lake Formation and Glue or creating custom Lambda ingestion logic.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Security Lake?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/security-lake/latest/userguide/what-is-security-lake.html) · [Amazon Security Lake Features](https://aws.amazon.com/security-lake/features/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's website uses an Amazon EC2 instance store for its catalog of items. The company wants to ensure that the catalog is highly available and that it is stored in a durable location.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Move the catalog to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
Deploy a larger EC2 instance with a larger instance store.
Move the catalog from the instance store to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 instance store provides temporary storage, so it is not suitable when the catalog must remain durable. A Regional Amazon EFS file system is designed for data that requires the highest durability and availability, stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones in a Region, and can be mounted from Amazon EC2 instances. That makes EFS the appropriate replacement for an active website catalog that must be both highly available and durable.

**Learn more:** [Data persistence for Amazon EC2 instance store volumes - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-store-lifetime.html) · [Features of Amazon EFS - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/features.html)

A company has a nightly batch-processing routine that analyzes report files that an on-premises file system receives each day through SFTP. The company wants to migrate the solution to the AWS Cloud.  
  
The solution must be:  
  
- highly available and resilient  
- minimal in operational effort  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.

Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.

Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.

Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. Modify the application to pull the batch files from Amazon S3 to an Amazon EC2 instance for processing. Use an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family is the managed AWS service for SFTP, so it minimizes operational overhead compared with running an SFTP server on Amazon EC2. Amazon S3 provides highly durable, highly available object storage without requiring management of a file server, and AWS Transfer Family supports using Amazon S3 as the backend storage. A nightly workload is predictable, so using an EC2 Auto Scaling group with scheduled scaling is an appropriate way to run the batch processing only when needed. An EC2-hosted SFTP server with desired capacity 1 is still a single-instance dependency, and using Amazon EFS is unnecessary when the workload only needs durable file intake and batch retrieval rather than shared POSIX file-system behavior. The combination that best satisfies availability, resilience, and lowest operational effort is AWS Transfer for SFTP with Amazon S3 storage and scheduled EC2 processing. Official AWS documentation states that Transfer Family supports either Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS as storage, and that scheduled scaling is intended for predictable time-based capacity changes.

**Learn more:** [Configure storage to use with AWS Transfer Family servers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/configure-storage.html) · [What is AWS Transfer Family?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html)

A company is designing an event-driven order processing system. After an order is created, the order must go through multiple validation steps. An idempotent AWS Lambda function performs each validation step. Each validation step is independent of the other validation steps, and each step needs only a subset of the order event data.  
  
The company wants to make sure that each validation-step Lambda function can access only the information from the order event that it requires. The order processing components should be loosely coupled so the design can accommodate future business changes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for each validation step. Create a new Lambda function to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires and to publish the messages to the appropriate SQS queues. Subscribe each validation step Lambda function to its corresponding SQS queue.

Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the validation step Lambda functions to the SNS topic. Use message body filtering to send only the required data to each subscribed Lambda function.
Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create an event rule for each validation step. Configure the input transformer to send only the required data to each target validation step Lambda function.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a new Lambda function to subscribe to the SQS queue and to transform the order data to the format that each validation step requires. Use the new Lambda function to perform synchronous invocations of the validation step Lambda functions in parallel on separate threads.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge supports loosely coupled event-driven architectures by routing one event to multiple independent targets through separate rules. For each validation Lambda target, an EventBridge input transformer can extract specific fields from the original event and send a customized payload containing only the data that target requires. Amazon SNS subscription filtering can filter which subscribers receive a message, but it does not reshape the message body per subscriber into different reduced payloads. The SQS options add unnecessary intermediary orchestration and tighter coupling instead of native event routing and per-target transformation.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EventBridge input transformation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-transform-target-input.html) · [Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html)

A company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The company already uses several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The company needs a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside business hours. The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.

questions.explanation:
Using AWS Lambda with a scheduled Amazon EventBridge rule provides a native serverless automation pattern for starting and stopping Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS instances. This approach minimizes both cost and operational overhead because there is no additional server to run or maintain, unlike a cron job on an EC2 instance. AWS documentation also shows that RDS DB instances can be stopped and started through the API, and AWS provides an official scheduling solution for EC2 and RDS based on Lambda-driven automation.

**Learn more:** [Automate starting and stopping AWS instances - Instance Scheduler on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/instance-scheduler-on-aws/solution-overview.html) · [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is performing an internal audit. The company wants to make sure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket associated with the company’s AWS Lake Formation data lake does not include sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Macie is the AWS service built to discover sensitive data in Amazon S3 objects. It can run sensitive data discovery jobs and use managed data identifiers to detect specific PII and financial data types, including passport numbers and credit card numbers. That directly matches the need to inspect the contents of the S3 bucket for sensitive customer or employee data rather than only auditing controls or querying object metadata.

**Learn more:** [Using managed data identifiers - Amazon Macie](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/managed-data-identifiers.html) · [Types of Macie findings - Amazon Macie](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/findings-types.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a three-tier web application deployed on AWS. The web servers are in a public subnet in a VPC. The application servers and database servers are in private subnets in the same VPC. The company has deployed a third-party virtual firewall appliance from AWS Marketplace in an inspection VPC. The appliance is configured with an IP interface that can accept IP packets.  
  
A solutions architect needs to integrate the web application with the appliance so that **all traffic to the application is inspected before the traffic reaches the web server**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer in the public subnet of the application's VPC to route the traffic to the appliance for packet inspection.
Create an Application Load Balancer in the public subnet of the application's VPC to route the traffic to the appliance for packet inspection.
Deploy a transit gateway in the inspection VPConfigure route tables to route the incoming packets through the transit gateway.
Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer in the inspection VPC. Create a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint to receive the incoming packets and forward the packets to the appliance.

questions.explanation:
AWS Gateway Load Balancer is designed to deploy, scale, and manage third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls inline with traffic flows. It operates at Layer 3, listens for IP packets, and uses Gateway Load Balancer endpoints to steer traffic across VPC boundaries to the appliance VPC for inspection before forwarding it to the destination. That makes it the lowest-overhead AWS-native way to insert a third-party firewall appliance transparently in front of the application. Network Load Balancer and Application Load Balancer are not intended for this kind of transparent packet-inspection insertion, and a transit gateway-based design is more operationally complex than necessary for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [What is a Gateway Load Balancer? - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html) · [Access virtual appliances through AWS PrivateLink - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpce-gateway-load-balancer.html)

A company has a Windows-based application that must be migrated to AWS. The application requires a shared Windows file system that is attached to multiple Amazon EC2 Windows instances deployed across multiple Availability Zones.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Configure AWS Storage Gateway in volume gateway mode. Mount the volume to each Windows instance.
Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.
Configure a file system by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS file system to each Windows instance.
Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with the required size. Attach each EC2 instance to the volume. Mount the file system within the volume to each Windows instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the correct service because it provides a managed shared Windows file system over SMB for Windows workloads, and EC2 instances in the VPC can access it regardless of Availability Zone. This matches the need for multiple EC2 Windows instances to share the same Windows file system across multiple AZs. Amazon EFS does not support Microsoft Windows–based EC2 instances, and Amazon EBS does not provide a cross-AZ shared file system because Multi-Attach is limited to instances in a single Availability Zone.

**Learn more:** [Accessing your data - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html) · [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application backed by Amazon RDS. A new database administrator caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table. To help recover from this type of incident, the company wants the ability to restore the database to its state from 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days.  
  
Which feature should the solutions architect include in the design to meet this requirement?

options.text: Read replicas
Manual snapshots
Automated backups
Multi-AZ deployments

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS automated backups support point-in-time recovery, which lets you restore a DB instance to any specific time within the configured backup retention period. Because the company needs recovery to a point 5 minutes before an accidental table edit and wants that capability for the last 30 days, automated backups are the feature that satisfies the requirement. Manual snapshots are only single restore points, while read replicas and Multi-AZ deployments do not provide recovery from logical data changes.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to RDS backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html) · [Restoring a DB instance to a specified time (PITR)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIT.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must provide a globally distributed development team with secure access to the company's AWS resources while complying with security policies.  
  
The company currently uses an on-premises Active Directory for internal authentication. It uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts that support multiple projects.  
  
The company requires a solution that integrates with the existing infrastructure to deliver centralized identity management and access control.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up AWS Directory Service to create an AWS managed Microsoft Active Directory on AWS. Establish a trust relationship with the on-premises Active Directory. Use IAM rotes that are assigned to Active Directory groups to access AWS resources within the company's AWS accounts.

Create an IAM user for each developer. Manually manage permissions for each IAM user based on each user's involvement with each project. Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) as an additional layer of security.

Use AD Connector in AWS Directory Service to connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Integrate AD Connector with AWS IAM Identity Center. Configure permissions sets to give each AD group access to specific AWS accounts and resources.

Use Amazon Cognito to deploy an identity federation solution. Integrate the identity federation solution with the on-premises Active Directory. Use Amazon Cognito to provide access tokens for developers to access AWS accounts and resources.

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce access across AWS Organizations accounts through permission sets assigned to Active Directory groups. AD Connector forwards authentication to the existing self-managed Active Directory, so the company can reuse its established identities without operating a new managed directory or manually maintaining individual IAM users. AWS documents that AD Connector can integrate with IAM Identity Center and that permission sets assign users or groups access across one or more AWS accounts.

**Learn more:** [Using Active Directory as an identity source - AWS IAM Identity Center](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/gs-ad.html) · [What gets created with your AD Connector - AWS Directory Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/create_details_ad_connector.html)

A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers need to access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is a managed shared file system for Linux workloads that multiple EC2 web servers can mount at the same time by using NFS, so the servers can access the same content through normal file-system semantics without modifying the application. Amazon S3 is object storage rather than a shared POSIX file system, and a gp3 Amazon EBS volume is block storage that cannot be mounted to all web servers as a shared file store in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Use Amazon EFS with Amazon EC2 Linux instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEFS.html) · [How Amazon EFS works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a custom application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. The application has frontend nodes that must run **24 hours a day, 7 days a week** and backend nodes that need to run only briefly based on workload. The number of backend nodes changes throughout the day.  
  
The company must scale out and scale in additional instances according to workload.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Spot Instances for the backend nodes.
Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Reserved Instances for the backend nodes.
Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.

questions.explanation:
Reserved Instances are the best fit for the frontend layer because that capacity is required continuously, making it a steady-state EC2 workload with lower cost than On-Demand. Spot Instances are the best fit for the backend layer because those nodes are short-lived and variable, and Spot is specifically intended for flexible, fault-tolerant capacity at the lowest cost. This combination delivers committed savings for always-on instances and discounted elastic capacity for fluctuating instances.

**Learn more:** [Reserved Instances for Amazon EC2 overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-reserved-instances.html) · [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's image-hosting website enables users worldwide to upload, view, and download images from mobile devices. The company currently hosts the static website in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
Because the website has become increasingly popular, its performance has declined. Users have reported latency when uploading and downloading images.  
  
The company must improve the website's performance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket to improve the download performance. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to improve the upload performance.

Configure Amazon EC2 instances of the right sizes in multiple AWS Regions. Migrate the application to the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the website traffic equally among the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Global Accelerator to address global demand with low latency.

Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the S3 bucket as an origin to improve the download performance. Configure the application to use CloudFront to upload images to improve the upload performance. Create S3 buckets in multiple AWS Regions. Configure replication rules for the buckets to replicate users' data based on the users' location. Redirect downloads to the S3 bucket that is closest to each user's location.
Configure AWS Global Accelerator for the S3 bucket to improve network performance. Create an endpoint for the application to use Global Accelerator instead of the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront can use the Amazon S3 bucket as its origin and serve downloaded images from edge caches closer to users. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration improves transfers between globally distributed clients and an S3 bucket by routing data through AWS edge locations over an optimized network path. Together, these services address download and upload latency without migrating the website or operating multi-Region infrastructure.

A company wants to monitor its AWS costs for a financial review. The cloud operations team is designing an architecture in the AWS Organizations management account to query AWS Cost and Usage Reports for all member accounts. The team must run this query once each month and provide a detailed analysis of the bill.  
  
Which solution is the **MOST** scalable and cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon EMR for analysis.
Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Redshift for analysis.
Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon QuickSight tor analysis.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cost and Usage Reports for an organization should be generated from the AWS Organizations management account when the goal is to analyze charges for all member accounts under consolidated billing. AWS delivers CUR data to Amazon S3, and Amazon Athena is the recommended serverless service for querying CUR files in S3 with SQL. That makes Athena more scalable and more cost-effective than maintaining EMR or Redshift for a workload that runs only monthly, and it avoids the operational overhead of creating separate reports in each member account.

**Learn more:** [Using Cost and Usage Reports for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/cur-consolidated-billing.html) · [Querying Cost and Usage Reports using Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/cur-query-athena.html)

options.text: Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a cluster placement group.
Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a partition placement group.
Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system.

questions.explanation:
For latency-sensitive HPC workloads, Amazon EC2 cluster placement groups place instances close together in a single Availability Zone to provide the low-latency, high-throughput networking typical of tightly coupled HPC applications. For storage, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the AWS file service in these options that supports true multi-protocol access, including concurrent NFS and SMB access to the same volume. FSx for Lustre is an HPC file system but does not provide the required NFS and SMB multi-protocol access, and FSx for OpenZFS supports NFS rather than SMB multi-protocol sharing.

**Learn more:** [Placement groups for your Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-groups.html) · [Placement strategies for your placement groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)

A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script that polls for and processes messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining the ability to process an increasing number of messages added to the queue.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the correct choice because Lambda can process Amazon SQS messages through an event source mapping, where Lambda polls the queue on behalf of the application and automatically scales concurrency based on queue depth. This removes the need to run and manage a continuously operating EC2 instance, which lowers operational overhead and can reduce cost while still supporting growth in message volume.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A social media company lets users upload images to its website. The website runs on Amazon EC2 instances. During upload requests, the website resizes the images to a standard size and stores the resized images in Amazon S3. Users are experiencing slow upload requests to the website.  
  
The company needs to reduce coupling in the application and improve website performance. A solutions architect must design the most operationally efficient process for image uploads.  
  
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure the application to upload images to S3 Glacier.
Configure the web server to upload the original images to Amazon S3.
Configure the application to upload images directly from each user's browser to Amazon S3 through the use of a presigned URL
Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an image is uploaded. Use the function to resize the image.
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function on a schedule to resize uploaded images.

questions.explanation:
The most operationally efficient design is to upload images directly from the user's browser to Amazon S3 by using a presigned URL, which removes the EC2 application servers from the upload data path and reduces request latency. After the object is created in S3, S3 Event Notifications can asynchronously invoke an AWS Lambda function to resize the image, decoupling image processing from the web request and improving application performance. AWS documentation confirms that presigned URLs allow clients to upload directly to S3 and that Amazon S3 can invoke Lambda when an object is uploaded. 

**Learn more:** [Uploading objects with presigned URLs - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/PresignedUrlUploadObject.html) · [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda - AWS Lambda Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently launched a variety of new workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in its AWS account.  
  
The company needs to create a strategy to access and administer the instances remotely and securely. The company must implement a repeatable process that uses native AWS services and follows the AWS Well-Architected Framework.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use the EC2 serial console to directly access the terminal interface of each instance for administration.
Attach the appropriate IAM role to each existing instance and new instance. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish a remote SSH session.
Create an administrative SSH key pair. Load the public key into each EC2 instance. Deploy a bastion host in a public subnet to provide a tunnel for administration of each instance.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Instruct administrators to use their local on-premises machines to connect directly to the instances by using SSH keys across the VPN tunnel.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager is the correct choice because it provides secure remote administration of EC2 instances by using native AWS managed capabilities instead of requiring inbound SSH access, bastion hosts, or customer-managed SSH key distribution. Attaching the appropriate IAM role to the instances makes them managed nodes for Systems Manager, creating a repeatable and scalable pattern for both existing and new instances. This minimizes ongoing operations while improving security posture, which is more consistent with the AWS Well-Architected Framework than using a serial console, a bastion host, or a Site-to-Site VPN for direct SSH access.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html) · [Step 2: Verify or add instance permissions for Session Manager - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-getting-started-instance-profile.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming traffic. A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and whether the rule's target is being invoked.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.
Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.
Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge publishes operational metrics to Amazon CloudWatch under the `AWS/Events` namespace. Those metrics include `TriggeredRules`, which shows when a rule matched an event, and `Invocations` or `InvocationAttempts`, which show whether EventBridge invoked the configured target. These metrics directly verify both whether the rule conditions are being met and whether the third-party API target is being called.

**Learn more:** [Monitoring Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring.html) · [Best practices for monitoring event delivery in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring-events-best-practices.html)

A company has thousands of edge devices that together generate **1 TB of status alerts each day**. Each alert is about **2 KB** in size. A solutions architect must implement a solution to ingest and store the alerts for future analysis.  
  
The company wants a **highly available** solution. However, it must **minimize costs** and **avoid managing additional infrastructure**. The company also wants to keep **14 days of data** available for immediate analysis and **archive all data older than 14 days**.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.

Launch Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones and place them behind an Elastic Load Balancer to ingest the alerts. Create a script on the EC2 instances that will store the alerts in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.

Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster. Set up the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster to take manual snapshots every day and delete data from the cluster that is older than 14 days.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to ingest the alerts, and set the message retention period to 14 days. Configure consumers to poll the SQS queue, check the age of the message, and analyze the message data as needed. If the message is 14 days old, the consumer should copy the message to an Amazon S3 bucket and delete the message from the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed ingestion service that can reliably stream data directly into Amazon S3 without requiring server administration. Amazon S3 provides durable, highly available storage, and S3 Lifecycle rules can automatically transition objects to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days, which cleanly satisfies the immediate-analysis retention window and archival requirement with minimal operational effort. Using EC2 or OpenSearch would add unnecessary infrastructure and administration, and Amazon SQS is limited to message retention rather than long-term analytical storage.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Data Firehose?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)

A company uses AWS Lambda functions with high concurrency to process a continuously growing number of messages in a message queue during marketing events. The Lambda functions run CPU-intensive code to process the messages. The company wants to reduce compute costs and maintain service latency for its customers.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions. Decrease the memory allocated to the Lambda functions.
Configure reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions. Increase the memory according to AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations.
Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions. Decrease the memory allocated to the Lambda functions.
Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions. Increase the memory according to AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations.

questions.explanation:
Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of execution environments pre-initialized, eliminating cold-start latency during the sudden invocation spikes of a marketing event and directly protecting the required service latency, whereas reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees an allocation of concurrent instances without pre-warming any of them. Because Lambda allocates CPU power in proportion to configured memory, right-sizing memory for CPU-bound code using AWS Compute Optimizer's function-specific recommendations can shorten execution duration enough to lower overall cost, rather than simply cutting memory and risking longer, more expensive runs.

**Learn more:** [Configuring provisioned concurrency - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost **programmatically**.  
  
The company must be able to access:  
  
- cost data for the current year, and  
- forecast costs for the next 12 months.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.
Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.
Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.
Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cost Explorer API is the correct service because it provides programmatic access to AWS cost and usage data and supports cost forecasting. AWS documentation states that the Cost Explorer API can access historical cost data and provide up to 12 months of forecast data at monthly granularity, which matches the requirement for current-year costs plus a 12-month forecast. The other options rely on emailed or downloaded reports, or misuse AWS Budgets features that are not intended as a low-overhead programmatic data source for an operations dashboard.

**Learn more:** [Using the AWS Cost Explorer API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-api.html) · [Best practices for the AWS Cost Explorer API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-api-best-practices.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises business application that creates hundreds of files each day. These files are kept on an SMB file share and need a low-latency connection to the application servers. A new company policy requires that all application-generated files be copied to AWS. An existing VPN connection to AWS is already in place.  
  
The application development team does not have time to implement the code changes needed to move the application to AWS.  
  
Which service should a solutions architect recommend so the application can copy files to AWS?

options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
AWS Snowball
AWS Storage Gateway

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway is the correct choice because File Gateway provides an SMB file share interface for on-premises applications while storing the files in AWS and using local caching for low-latency access. That lets the application continue writing to an SMB share without code changes, while the files are copied to AWS over the existing network connection. Amazon EFS does not provide SMB shares, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server would place the file system in AWS rather than preserving low-latency on-premises access, and AWS Snowball is for batch data transfer rather than continuous file share integration.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html) · [Create an SMB file share - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/create-smb-file-share.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has data collection sensors in multiple locations. The sensors stream a large volume of data to the company. The company wants to design an AWS platform to ingest and process high-volume streaming data. The solution must scale and support near-real-time data collection. The company must store the data in Amazon S3 for future reporting.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
Use AWS Glue to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
Use AWS Lambda to deliver streaming data and store the data to Amazon S3.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is the best fit because it is a fully managed service designed to ingest and deliver real-time streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3 without requiring custom ingestion code or management of streaming infrastructure. That gives the company scalable, near-real-time delivery to S3 with less operational overhead than building a Lambda-based pipeline, running AWS Glue streaming ETL jobs, or using AWS DMS, which is intended for database migration and change data capture rather than general sensor-stream ingestion.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Data Firehose?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html) · [Welcome - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has launched a new version of its production application. The company's workload uses Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Amazon SageMaker.  
  
The company wants to optimize costs for the workload now that usage has reached a steady state. The company wants to cover the greatest number of services with the fewest savings plans.  
  
Which combination of savings plans will satisfy these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Amazon EC2, Lambda, and SageMaker.
Purchase a SageMaker Savings Plan.
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda, Fargate, and Amazon EC2.
Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and Fargate.

Compute Savings Plans apply across Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, and AWS Fargate, making them the single plan that covers the most non-SageMaker compute services. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must store the results of a medical trial in an Amazon S3 repository. The repository must:  
  
- allow a small number of scientists to add new files  
- limit all other users to read-only access  
- prevent all users from modifying or deleting any files in the repository  
- retain every file in the repository for at least 1 year from its creation date  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a legal hold of 1 year.
Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days.
Use an IAM role to restrict all users from deleting or changing objects in the S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to only allow the IAM role.

Configure the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function every time an object is added. Configure the function to track the hash of the saved object so that modified objects can be marked accordingly.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Object Lock in **compliance mode** provides immutable WORM protection for each object version for the configured retention period, so protected objects cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user during that time. A retention period of **365 days** satisfies the requirement to keep every file for a minimum of 1 year after creation. Governance mode is insufficient because authorized users can bypass it, and a legal hold does not define a 1-year retention period.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with Object Lock - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [Configuring S3 Object Lock - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-configure.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises web application. During peak hours, the application has latency problems. These latency problems happen twice each month. At the beginning of a latency event, the application's CPU utilization immediately rises to 10 times its normal level.  
  
The company wants to migrate the application to AWS to reduce latency. The company also wants the application to scale automatically when application demand increases. The company will use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the application.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale on a schedule.
Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale on predictive metrics.

questions.explanation:
Compute optimized EC2 instances are designed for compute-bound workloads such as high-performance web servers, making them a better fit for an application that experiences immediate 10x CPU spikes. In Elastic Beanstalk, Auto Scaling can use request count as a trigger, which directly supports automatic scale-out when demand increases. Scheduled scaling is inappropriate because the requirement is to react to increases in demand, not to scale only at predefined times. Burstable unlimited instances can handle bursts, but they are optimized for workloads that generally run below baseline and consume CPU credits for spikes, so they are less suitable than compute optimized instances for sharp, compute-intensive demand.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
Turn on server-side encryption on the SNS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.

Turn on encryption on the SNS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the topic policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.

When access to the encryption key must be limited to specific principals, a customer managed KMS key is the correct choice because its key policy can explicitly restrict who may use the key. For Amazon SQS, encryption in transit is enforced by adding an `aws:SecureTransport` condition in the queue policy so only TLS connections are allowed. That makes the correct combination the SNS step that uses a customer managed KMS key with a restrictive key policy, and the SQS step that uses a customer managed KMS key with a restrictive key policy plus TLS-only access.

A social media company is building a rewards program website for its users. The company awards users points when they create and upload videos to the website. Users redeem their points for gifts or discounts from the company's affiliated partners. A unique ID identifies users. The partners use this ID to verify whether users are eligible for rewards.  
  
The partners want to receive notifications of user IDs through an HTTP endpoint when the company awards users points. Hundreds of vendors are interested in becoming affiliated partners every day. The company wants to design an architecture that allows the website to add partners quickly in a scalable manner.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST implementation effort**?

options.text: Create an Amazon Timestream database to keep a list of affiliated partners. Implement an AWS Lambda function to read the list. Configure the Lambda function to send user IDs to each partner when the company gives users points.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) is the best fit because it provides a managed publish/subscribe model and supports HTTP/HTTPS endpoints as subscribers. The company can publish each user ID once to an SNS topic, and SNS will fan out the notification to all subscribed partner endpoints. This minimizes custom development and makes onboarding new partners straightforward because each new partner only needs a subscription to the topic. A company operates an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is developing a new feature that will allow the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts. The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics.  
  
What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the **MOST secure** way?

options.text: Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company’s account.
Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.
Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company that uses AWS Organizations runs 150 applications across 30 different AWS accounts. The company used AWS Cost and Usage Report to create a new report in the management account. The company’s senior leadership wants to view a custom dashboard that provides NAT gateway costs each day starting at the beginning of the current month.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

Share an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure QuickSight to use Amazon Athena to query the new report.

Share an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that includes the requested table visual. Configure CloudWatch to use Amazon Athena to query the new report.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that has a target group. The company designed the application to use session affinity (sticky sessions) to provide a better user experience.  
  
The application must be publicly available over the internet through an endpoint. A WAF must be applied to the endpoint for additional security. Session affinity (sticky sessions) must be configured on the endpoint.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Create a public Network Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
Create a public Application Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
Create a second target group. Add Elastic IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
Create a web ACL in AWS WAF. Associate the web ACL with the endpoint

questions.explanation:
A public **Application Load Balancer** is the correct internet-facing endpoint because ALBs support **sticky sessions** for EC2 targets through target group stickiness. **AWS WAF** web ACLs can be associated with an **Application Load Balancer**, so creating a web ACL and attaching it to that endpoint satisfies the security requirement. Network Load Balancers and Gateway Load Balancers do not meet the combined requirement of ALB-style sticky web sessions plus direct AWS WAF association.

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html) · [Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has **150 TB** of archived image data stored on-premises that must be moved to the AWS Cloud **within the next month**. The company’s existing network connection supports uploads of up to **100 Mbps** for this purpose **during the night only**.  
  
What is the **MOST cost-effective** way to move this data and still meet the migration deadline?

options.text: Use AWS Snowmobile to ship the data to AWS.
Order multiple AWS Snowball devices to ship the data to AWS.
Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration and securely upload the data.
Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint and establish a VPN to upload the data.

questions.explanation:
For 150 TB, the available network bandwidth is far too limited to complete the transfer within one month, so online upload methods are not practical. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration can improve internet transfer performance, but it still depends on the available WAN bandwidth. AWS Snowball devices are designed for offline data migration at this scale and can be ordered in multiple units to transfer large datasets cost-effectively. AWS Snowmobile is meant for much larger, exabyte-scale migrations, so it is not the economical choice for 150 TB.

**Learn more:** [AWS Snowball Edge Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/) · [Migration and transfer - Overview of Amazon Web Services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-overview/migration-services.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a web application with thousands of users. Which storage solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

Move uploaded images to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive Move all generated AI images to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A transaction processing company runs weekly scripted batch jobs on Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The number of transactions can vary, but the baseline CPU utilization observed on each run is at least 60%.  
  
The company must provision capacity **30 minutes before** the jobs run.  
  
Currently, engineers perform this task manually by modifying the Auto Scaling group parameters. The company does not have the resources to analyze the capacity trends that are required for the Auto Scaling group counts. The company needs an automated way to modify the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on the CPU utilization metric. Set the target value for the metric to 60%.

Create a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Set the appropriate desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity. Set the recurrence to weekly. Set the start time to 30 minutes before the batch jobs run.

Create a predictive scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on forecast. Set the scaling metric to CPU utilization. Set the target value for the metric to 60%. In the policy, set the instances to pre-launch 30 minutes before the jobs run.

Create an Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the CPU utilization metric value for the Auto Scaling group reaches 60%. Configure the Lambda function to increase the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity and maximum capacity by 20%.

questions.explanation:
Scheduled scaling is the best fit for a known recurring weekly workload because Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled actions can run on a recurring schedule and set the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity at a specified time. That directly satisfies the requirement to increase capacity 30 minutes before the batch jobs start, without needing trend analysis or custom code. Dynamic scaling is reactive to metrics after load rises, predictive scaling is more complex than necessary for a fixed weekly schedule, and EventBridge plus Lambda adds unnecessary operational overhead. Official AWS documentation states that scheduled scaling is intended for scaling activities at specific times and recurring schedules, with desired, minimum, and maximum capacity settings.

**Learn more:** [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Create a scheduled action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scheduled-scaling-create-scheduled-action.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A media company operates a multi-account AWS environment in the `us-east-1` Region. Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group with the new AMI.
Enable AMI creation and define lifecycle rules in Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Create an AWS Lambda function that modifies the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke AWS Backup lifecycle policies that provision AMIs. Configure Auto Scaling group capacity limits as an event source in EventBridge.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS Fast Snapshot Restore is the feature designed to minimize startup latency for EBS-backed AMIs. Volumes created from ordinary snapshots can incur increased latency on first access because the snapshot data is loaded lazily, but Fast Snapshot Restore creates volumes that are fully initialized at creation and can immediately deliver their provisioned performance. Using an AMI backed by a snapshot with Fast Snapshot Restore enabled therefore gives the Auto Scaling group the lowest initialization latency among the choices.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS fast snapshot restore - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html) · [Amazon EBS volume performance - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-performance.html)

A company wants to use artificial intelligence (AI) to assess the quality of its customer service calls. The company currently handles calls in four different languages, including English, and will add more languages in the future. The company does not have the resources to routinely maintain machine learning (ML) models.  
  
The company must create written sentiment analysis reports from the customer service call recordings. The text from the customer service call recordings must be translated into English.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to translate the audio recordings into English.
Use Amazon Lex to create the written sentiment analysis reports.
Use Amazon Polly to convert the audio recordings into text.
Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio recordings in any language into text.
Use Amazon Translate to translate text in any language to English.
Use Amazon Comprehend to create the sentiment analysis reports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Transcribe is the managed AWS service that converts speech in call recordings to text, Amazon Translate translates that text from supported source languages into English, and Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis on text to generate the sentiment results used in written reports. This combination satisfies the need for multilingual audio processing, English translation, and sentiment analysis without the company having to build and maintain its own ML models.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Transcribe?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/what-is.html) · [Language identification with batch transcription jobs - Amazon Transcribe](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/lang-id-batch.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must connect several VPCs in the `us-east-1` Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company’s networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution to connect the VPCs?

options.text: Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet’s route table
Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet
Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team’s AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.
Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team’s AWS account to connect to each VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is the native hub-and-spoke service for connecting large numbers of VPCs and AWS accounts at scale. Deploying Transit Gateway in a central networking account dramatically simplifies connectivity compared to managing hundreds of VPC peering connections. Transit Gateway supports static and dynamic routing and integrates with AWS Resource Access Manager for cross-account sharing, making it the most operationally efficient solution for this scenario.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html) · [Connect VPCs using a transit gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/extend-tgw.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to give users access to AWS resources. The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises resources by using Active Directory user groups on the corporate network. However, the company does not want users to need to maintain another identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on-premises resources.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2 0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.

questions.explanation:
SAML 2.0 federation is the appropriate solution for enterprise users who already exist in Active Directory and should use their existing identities to access AWS. AWS IAM supports federated single sign-on with a SAML 2.0-compatible identity provider such as Active Directory Federation Services, so users do not need separate IAM user accounts. Permissions are assigned through IAM roles, and access can be aligned to existing Active Directory groups by mapping those groups to the roles. This matches the requirement to preserve the on-premises identity model while granting AWS access with temporary credentials.

**Learn more:** [SAML 2.0 federation - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_saml.html) · [Access to externally authenticated users (identity federation) - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_federated-users.html)
