lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A serverless application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. The Lambda function requires permission to read from and write to the DynamoDB table.  
  
Which solution will provide the Lambda function access to the DynamoDB table **MOST securely**?

options.text: Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters as part of the Lambda environment variables. Ensure that other AWS users do not have read and write access to the Lambda function configuration.

Create an IAM role that includes Lambda as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Update the configuration of the Lambda function to use the new role as the execution role.

Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as secure string parameters. Update the Lambda function code to retrieve the secure string parameters before connecting to the DynamoDB table.

Create an IAM role that includes DynamoDB as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access from the Lambda function. Update the code of the Lambda function to attach to the new role as an execution role.

questions.explanation:
The most secure approach is to assign the Lambda function an IAM execution role that trusts the Lambda service and grants only the necessary DynamoDB permissions. AWS documentation states that functions access other AWS resources through an execution role that Lambda assumes at invocation time, which avoids embedding or retrieving long-term IAM user access keys in code, environment variables, or Parameter Store. This follows least-privilege and temporary-credential best practices.

**Learn more:** [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html) · [How Lambda works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/concepts-basics.html)

A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on-premises resources."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.","B":"Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.","C":"Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.","D":"Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2 0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached Map the roles to the Active Directory groups."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"SAML 2.0 federation is the appropriate solution for enterprise users who already exist in Active Directory and should use their existing identities to access AWS. AWS IAM supports federated single sign-on with a SAML 2.0-compatible identity provider such as Active Directory Federation Services, so users do not need separate IAM user accounts. Permissions are assigned through IAM roles, and access can be aligned to existing Active Directory groups by mapping those groups to the roles. This matches the requirement to preserve the on-premises identity model while granting AWS access with temporary credentials.

**Learn more:** [SAML 2.0 federation - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_saml.html) · [Access to externally authenticated users (identity federation) - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_federated-users.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"cdc96b13-5b79-4709-ad2c-23c7221266cf","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters as part of the Lambda environment variables. Ensure that other AWS users do not have read and write access to the Lambda function configuration.","B":"Create an IAM role that includes Lambda as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Update the configuration of the Lambda function to use the new role as the execution role.","C":"Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as secure string parameters. Update the Lambda function code to retrieve the secure string parameters before connecting to the DynamoDB table.","D":"Create an IAM role that includes DynamoDB as a trusted service. Update the code of the Lambda function to attach to the new role as an execution role."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"The most secure approach is to assign the Lambda function an IAM execution role that trusts the Lambda service and grants only the necessary DynamoDB permissions. AWS documentation states that functions access other AWS resources through an execution role that Lambda assumes at invocation time, which avoids embedding or retrieving long-term IAM user access keys in code, environment variables, or Parameter Store. This follows least-privilege and temporary-credential best practices.

**Learn more:** [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html) · [How Lambda works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/concepts-basics.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"ff9788da-19e4-4dec-8c61-66f5d9b27772","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
A company has deployed a serverless application that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses the Lambda function to process the documents. After a recent marketing campaign, the company noticed that the application did not process many of the documents.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to improve the architecture of this application?

options.text: Set the Lambda function's runtime timeout value to 15 minutes.
Configure an S3 bucket replication policy. Stage the documents in the S3 bucket for later processing.
Deploy an additional Lambda function. Load balance the processing of the documents across the two Lambda functions.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Send the requests to the queue. Configure the queue as an event source for Lambda.

questions.explanation:
To handle bursty document uploads reliably, the architecture should introduce a durable queue between Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda. Amazon S3 can publish event notifications to Amazon SQS, and Lambda can poll the SQS queue through an event source mapping, processing messages in batches and scaling against the backlog. This decouples upload traffic from processing throughput and prevents spikes in S3 events from overwhelming direct Lambda invocation.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [Event notification types and destinations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)

A solutions architect is implementing a complex Java application with a MySQL database. The Java application must be deployed on Apache Tomcat and must be highly available.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the application in AWS Lambda. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to connect with the Lambda functions.
Deploy the application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Configure a load-balanced environment and a rolling deployment policy.
Migrate the database to Amazon ElastiCache. Configure the ElastiCache security group to allow access from the application.
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Install a MySQL server on the EC2 instance. Configure the application on the server. Create an AMI. Use the AMI to create a launch template with an Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Beanstalk is the best fit because it has a Tomcat platform for Java web applications and can be configured as a load-balanced environment for high availability. Elastic Beanstalk also supports rolling deployment policies, which update instances in batches behind the load balancer. By contrast, AWS Lambda does not provide an Apache Tomcat hosting model, Amazon ElastiCache is not a MySQL relational database, and running MySQL on a single EC2 instance creates a single point of failure for the database tier.

**Learn more:** [Using the Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat platform](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-tomcat-platform.html) · [Deployment policies and settings - AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud across three Availability Zones. The architecture includes an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that stores user session state, and a MySQL database running on an EC2 instance. The company anticipates sudden increases in application traffic. It wants to scale to meet future capacity needs and ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster provides high availability across three Availability Zones for a MySQL workload, and an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones allows the web tier to scale horizontally for traffic spikes. Because the web servers currently hold session state locally, the session data must be externalized to a shared store so instances can scale in and out without losing user state. ElastiCache for Redis is the best fit because it supports high availability and replication and is commonly used for shared session storage as well as read caching. Memcached is suitable for caching but is not the preferred highly available session store, DynamoDB would require redesigning the relational MySQL database model, and a single-AZ RDS deployment would not satisfy the availability requirement.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html) · [What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

A company plans to migrate a legacy application to AWS. The application currently uses NFS to communicate with an on-premises storage solution for storing application data. The application cannot be changed to use any communication protocol other than NFS for this purpose.  
  
Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend after the migration?

options.text: AWS DataSync
Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon EMR File System (Amazon EMRFS)

questions.explanation:
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) provides managed shared file storage and supports the NFSv4 protocol, allowing an application that requires NFS-based access to continue operating without a protocol change.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Elastic File System?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/whatisefs.html) · [How Amazon EFS works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
A company plans to migrate a legacy application to AWS. The application currently uses NFS to communicate with an on-premises storage solution for storing application data. The application cannot be changed to use any communication protocol other than NFS for this purpose.  
  
Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend after the migration?

options.text: Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in private subnets. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.
Configure a VPC with two private subnets and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the private subnets.
Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in public subnets across two Availability Zones. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.

Configure a VPC with one public subnet, one private subnet, and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the public subnet.D. Configure a VPC with two public subnets, two private subnets, and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the public subnets.

questions.explanation:
Option A ensures EC2 and RDS are launched in private subnets (protecting from public exposure) with RDS Multi-AZ for high availability. Option D provides a VPC with public subnets for the ALB (enabling user traffic), private subnets for application tier, and NAT gateways in each Availability Zone to allow EC2 outbound internet access for payment processing while maintaining security and redundancy.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateways - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html) · [Example: VPC with servers in private subnets and NAT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-example-private-subnets-nat.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its ecommerce platform on AWS. The platform is essential to the company's operations and handles a high volume of traffic and transactions. The company configures a multi-factor authentication (MFA) device to protect its AWS account root user credentials. The company wants to make sure it will not lose access to the root user account if the MFA device is lost.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up a backup administrator account that the company can use to log in if the company loses the MFA device.
Add multiple MFA devices for the root user account to handle the disaster scenario.
Create a new administrator account when the company cannot access the root account.
Attach the administrator policy to another IAM user when the company cannot access the root account.

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM supports associating multiple MFA devices with an AWS account root user. This provides redundancy so the root user can still sign in with another registered MFA device if one device is lost or unavailable. IAM administrator accounts can perform many administrative tasks, but they do not replace root-user access, and creating or elevating another IAM user after lockout does not solve loss of access to the root account itself.

**Learn more:** [Root user best practices for your AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html) · [Multi-factor authentication for AWS account root user](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/enable-mfa-for-root.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to move its on-premises Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise edition database to AWS. The company's online application uses the database to handle transactions. The data analysis team uses the same production database to run reports for analytical processing. The company wants to lower operational overhead by moving to managed services wherever possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SOL Server. Use read replicas for reporting purposes
Migrate to Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2. Use Always On read replicas for reporting purposes
Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB on-demand replicas for reporting purposes
Migrate to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Use Aurora read replicas for reporting purposes

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server is the managed AWS service that preserves the SQL Server engine while offloading much of the database administration work. AWS documentation states that Amazon RDS for SQL Server supports read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition, which can offload reporting and analytical read activity from the primary transactional database. Using SQL Server on Amazon EC2 with Always On would increase operational responsibility because the company would manage the instances and SQL Server configuration itself, while DynamoDB and Aurora MySQL change the database platform entirely and do not match a least-effort migration of an existing SQL Server workload.

**Learn more:** [Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server in Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.ReadReplicas.html) · [Amazon RDS for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-sql-server/rds-sql.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a stateless web application in production on a set of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer.  
  
The application has heavy use during an 8-hour period each business day. Application usage is moderate and steady overnight. Application usage is low on weekends.  
  
The company wants to minimize its EC2 costs without affecting the application's availability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Spot Instances for the entire workload.
Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
Use On-Demand Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
Use Dedicated Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use On-Demand Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.

questions.explanation:
For a workload with a consistent baseline and predictable higher-demand periods, the lowest-cost approach that preserves availability is to purchase discounted baseline capacity with Reserved Instances and use Spot Instances only for the flexible extra capacity. AWS documentation states that Reserved Instances reduce EC2 cost for consistent usage, while Spot Instances are well suited to stateless, fault-tolerant workloads but can be interrupted, so they should not carry the entire required capacity for an availability-sensitive production application.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html) · [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html)

A company has an application that uploads hundreds of `.csv` files to an Amazon S3 bucket every hour. The files are 1 GB in size. Whenever a file is uploaded, the company must convert that file to Apache Parquet format and place the resulting output file into an S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to download the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function for each S3 PUT event.

Create an Apache Spark job to read the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the Spark job.

Create an AWS Glue table and an AWS Glue crawler for the S3 bucket where the application places the .csv files. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically use Amazon Athena to query the AWS Glue table, convert the query results into Parquet format, and place the output files into an S3 bucket.

Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Parquet format and place the output files into an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the ETL job.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue ETL is the best fit because it is a fully managed ETL service built for transforming data in Amazon S3, with native support for reading CSV and writing Parquet. A Glue ETL job can be invoked when an S3 object is created, which satisfies the per-upload processing requirement while avoiding the size and runtime limitations that make AWS Lambda unsuitable for heavy 1 GB file conversion. Compared with building a separate Spark environment or orchestrating crawlers, Athena, and scheduled functions, Glue ETL provides the needed large-scale transformation with less infrastructure and administration. Official AWS documentation states that AWS Glue for Spark supports common S3 formats including CSV and Parquet, and Glue jobs can be started programmatically with StartJobRun.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 connections - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-s3-home.html) · [Use StartJobRun with an AWS SDK or CLI - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/example_glue_StartJobRun_section.html)

A company plans to migrate two DNS servers to AWS. The servers host a total of approximately 200 zones and receive an average of 1 million requests per day.  
  
The company wants to **maximize availability** while **minimizing the operational overhead** associated with managing the two servers.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console Import zone files.
Launch a single large Amazon EC2 instance Import zone tiles. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
Migrate the servers to AWS by using AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones. Import zone files. Set the desired capacity to 1 and the maximum capacity to 3 for the Auto Scaling group. Configure scaling alarms to scale based on CPU utilization.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 is a highly available, scalable managed authoritative DNS service, so it best fits a workload of many DNS zones and daily query volume without requiring the company to run and maintain DNS servers on Amazon EC2. For migration from another DNS provider, AWS supports creating hosted zones in Route 53 and importing existing zone files, which directly addresses the need to move the current DNS configuration while reducing operational overhead compared with self-managed instances.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Route 53? - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/Welcome.html) · [Creating records by importing a zone file - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-creating-import.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a shared storage solution for a media application that it hosts on AWS. The company requires the ability for SMB clients to access the stored data.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway. Configure tapes to use Amazon S3. Connect the application server to the Tape Gateway.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Connect the application server to the file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed AWS file storage service that natively supports the SMB protocol for shared file access, making it the best fit for Windows-style shared storage with minimal operational effort. By contrast, Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block storage rather than SMB shares, Tape Gateway is intended for virtual tape backup workloads, and a self-managed Windows file server on Amazon EC2 would require ongoing server administration, patching, and file-service management. The managed SMB capability of Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the specific requirement that makes it the lowest-overhead solution.

**Learn more:** [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [Accessing your data - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/supported-fsx-clients.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A meteorological startup company has a custom web application that sells weather data to users online. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store its data and wants to build a new service that sends an alert to the managers of four internal teams every time a new weather event is recorded. The company does not want this new service to affect the performance of the current application.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the **LEAST** amount of operational overhead?

options.text: Use DynamoDB transactions to write new event data to the table. Configure the transactions to notify internal teams.
Have the current application publish a message to four Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Have each team subscribe to one topic.
Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table. Use triggers to write to a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to which the teams can subscribe.

Add a custom attribute to each record to flag new items. Write a cron job that scans the table every minute for items that are new and notifies an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to which the teams can subscribe.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB Streams is the appropriate way to capture newly written items asynchronously from a DynamoDB table, so the existing application does not need to perform extra notification work in its request path. A Lambda trigger can process stream records and publish a message to a single Amazon SNS topic, and SNS provides simple fan-out so all four teams can subscribe to the same topic. This minimizes operational overhead, avoids table scans or custom polling, and decouples notification handling from the application’s write performance.

**Learn more:** [Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/streamsmain.html) · [DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda triggers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates primary and secondary data centers that are 500 miles (804.7 km) apart and connected by high-speed fiber-optic cable. The company requires a highly available, secure network connection between its data centers and a VPC on AWS for a mission-critical workload. A solutions architect must select a connection solution that delivers maximum resiliency.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from the primary data center terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on the same device
Two AWS Direct Connect connections from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on two separate devices

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect maximum resiliency for critical workloads uses separate connections terminating on distinct devices in more than one Direct Connect location. Deploying two connections from each data center across two locations and separate devices provides redundancy against device failures, fiber/connectivity failures, and complete Direct Connect location outages.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect Resiliency Toolkit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/resiliency_toolkit.html) · [Provision redundant connectivity between private networks in the cloud and on-premises environments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/rel_planning_network_topology_ha_conn_private_networks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an on-premises application that uses SFTP to collect financial data from multiple vendors. The company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company has created an application that uses Amazon S3 APIs to upload files from vendors.  
  
Some vendors run their systems on legacy applications that do not support S3 APIs. The vendors want to continue using SFTP-based applications to upload data. The company wants to use managed services for the needs of the vendors that use legacy applications.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) instance to replicate data from the storage of the vendors that use legacy applications to Amazon S3. Provide the vendors with the credentials to access the AWS DMS instance.
Create an AWS Transfer Family endpoint for vendors that use legacy applications.
Configure an Amazon EC2 instance to run an SFTP server. Instruct the vendors that use legacy applications to use the SFTP server to upload data.
Configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway for vendors that use legacy applications to upload files to an SMB file share.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed file transfer service that supports SFTP and can store transferred data directly in Amazon S3. That makes it the best fit for vendors that must keep using legacy SFTP clients while minimizing administration. The other options either do not provide SFTP-based uploads to S3 as the primary use case or require additional infrastructure management: AWS DMS is for data replication and migration, EC2-hosted SFTP adds server operations work, and Amazon S3 File Gateway provides NFS/SMB access rather than SFTP.

**Learn more:** [AWS Transfer Family Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/) · [Getting started with AWS Transfer Family server endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/getting-started.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate its web applications from on premises to AWS. The company is located close to the `eu-central-1` Region. Because of regulations, the company cannot launch some of its applications in `eu-central-1`. The company wants to achieve single-digit millisecond latency.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to an edge location in Amazon CloudFront.
Deploy the applications in AWS Local Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Local Zone.
Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the regional edge caches in Amazon CloudFront.
Deploy the applications in AWS Wavelength Zones by extending the company’s VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Wavelength Zone.

questions.explanation:
AWS Local Zones are a logical extension of a parent AWS Region, and you can extend a VPC from that Region into the chosen Local Zone by creating a subnet there. Local Zones are intended for workloads that need to run closer to users and are designed to provide single-digit millisecond latency. CloudFront edge locations and regional edge caches do not let you run application workloads by extending a VPC, and Wavelength Zones are specialized for telecom 5G ultra-low-latency scenarios rather than this general nearby web-application placement requirement.

**Learn more:** [Connectivity options for Local Zones - AWS Local Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/local-zones/latest/ug/local-zones-connectivity.html) · [Subnets in AWS Local Zones - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/local-zone.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has several Windows file servers on premises. The company wants to migrate and consolidate the files into an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. File permissions must be preserved so that access rights do not change.  
  
Which solutions meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

questions.explanation:
AWS recommends AWS DataSync for migrating existing files into Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. DataSync can transfer file data together with metadata such as ownership and access permissions, and it supports copying NTFS ACLs and SACLs when transferring between SMB file servers and FSx for Windows File Server. That makes a direct DataSync-based migration from the on-premises Windows file servers to FSx valid, including when the DataSync agent is deployed on premises or run on an AWS Snowcone device. By contrast, workflows that first copy the data into Amazon S3 do not preserve Windows file-system permissions in a way that satisfies the requirement to keep NTFS access rights unchanged for FSx.

**Learn more:** [Migrating existing files to FSx for Windows File Server using AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/migrate-files-to-fsx-datasync.html) · [Configuring transfers with FSx for Windows File Server - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-fsx-location.html)

A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company performs periodic financial assessments of its AWS costs. The company recently identified unusual spending.  
  
The company needs a solution to prevent unusual spending. The solution must monitor costs and notify responsible stakeholders if unusual spending occurs.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Budgets template to create a zero spend budget.
Create an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
Create AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for the current running workload pricing details.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor costs and to identify unusual spending.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection is designed to identify unusual AWS spend patterns by using machine learning on billing data and to notify subscribers when an anomaly exceeds a configured threshold. That directly matches the need to monitor costs and alert responsible stakeholders about unusual spending. AWS Budgets can alert on threshold-based budget overruns, but a zero spend budget does not detect anomalous spending patterns. AWS Pricing Calculator is only for cost estimation, and CloudWatch is not the primary AWS service for billing anomaly detection.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/getting-started-ad.html) · [Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to reduce the cost of its **1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect** connection. The company's average connection utilization is **less than 10%**. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will lower the cost **without compromising security**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.
Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect dedicated connections created directly through AWS are ordered at 1 Gbps or higher, while sub-1 Gbps options such as 200 Mbps are available as hosted connections that must be provisioned through an AWS Direct Connect Partner. Since the current 1 Gbps circuit is significantly underutilized, moving to a 200 Mbps hosted connection reduces port cost while preserving private Direct Connect connectivity to AWS for the existing account.

**Learn more:** [Hosted Direct Connect connections - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/hosted_connection.html) · [Direct Connect connection options - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders. The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received.  
  
A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST development effort**?

options.text: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SNS handles failed deliveries at the subscription level by sending undeliverable messages to a dead-letter queue, and for SNS that dead-letter queue must be an Amazon SQS queue. Amazon SQS supports message retention for up to 14 days, which satisfies the requirement to keep failed order messages available for later analysis without redesigning the application flow or adding custom processing.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SNS dead-letter queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-dead-letter-queues.html) · [Configuring an Amazon SNS dead-letter queue for a subscription](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-configure-dead-letter-queue.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on several Amazon EC2 instances that store persistent data on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The company needs to replicate the data to another AWS Region by using an AWS managed service solution.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use the EFS-to-EFS backup solution to replicate the data to an EFS file system in another Region.
Run a nightly script to copy data from the EFS file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the S3 bucket.
Create a VPC in another Region. Establish a cross-Region VPC peer. Run a nightly rsync to copy data from the original Region to the new Region.
Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with a rule that takes a daily backup and replicates it to another Region. Assign the EFS file system resource to the backup plan.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup natively supports Amazon EFS and can run a scheduled backup plan with a rule that copies the daily backup to another AWS Region, giving a fully AWS-managed, low-effort way to replicate the file system's data without building or operating custom scripts, VPC peering, or rsync jobs. The AWS-provided EFS-to-EFS backup solution referenced in the other network-file-copy style option is designed to run within the same Region as the source file system, so it cannot satisfy a cross-Region requirement.

**Learn more:** [Creating backup copies across AWS Regions - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/cross-region-backup.html)

questions.question:
A company keeps user data in AWS. The data is used continuously, with peak use during business hours. Access patterns differ, and some data goes unused for months at a time. A solutions architect must select a cost-effective solution that preserves the highest level of durability while providing high availability.  
  
Which storage solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Amazon S3 Standard
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is designed for data with changing or unpredictable access patterns. It automatically moves objects to lower-cost access tiers when they have not been accessed, while retaining Amazon S3’s high durability and avoiding retrieval performance delays for actively accessed data.

questions.question:
A company keeps user data in AWS. The data is used continuously, with peak use during business hours. Access patterns differ, and some data goes unused for months at a time. A solutions architect must select a cost-effective solution that preserves the highest level of durability while providing high availability.  
  
Which storage solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Edit the job to use job bookmarks.
Edit the job to delete data after the data is processed.
Edit the job by setting the NumberOfWorkers field to 1.
Use a FindMatches machine learning (ML) transform.

questions.explanation:
AWS Glue job bookmarks persist state from prior successful runs so the job can process only new data on subsequent scheduled runs instead of rereading previously processed files. AWS supports job bookmarks for Amazon S3 sources, including XML, so enabling job bookmarks is the appropriate way to avoid reprocessing old S3 XML data.

**Learn more:** [Tracking processed data using job bookmarks - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/monitor-continuations.html) · [Using the XML format in AWS Glue - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-format-xml-home.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authorization model for a company's AWS account. The company has identified five specific employees who must have full access to AWS services and resources in the AWS account.  
  
The solutions architect has created an IAM user for each of the five designated employees and has also created an IAM user group.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the SystemAdministrator identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the AdministratorAccess identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the SystemAdministrator resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.

questions.explanation:
In AWS IAM, permissions for multiple users are typically assigned by attaching an identity-based policy to an IAM group and adding the users to that group. The AWS managed policy `AdministratorAccess` provides full access to AWS services and resources, which matches the requirement exactly. `SystemAdministrator` is a job-function policy and does not represent unrestricted full administrative access, and resource-based policies are attached to resources rather than IAM groups.

**Learn more:** [AdministratorAccess - AWS Managed Policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AdministratorAccess.html) · [Identity-based policies and resource-based policies - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_identity-vs-resource.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).  
  
The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.

Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.

Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

questions.explanation:
AWS Certificate Manager publishes an `ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration` event to Amazon EventBridge for imported certificates before they expire, and these events can be matched with an EventBridge rule. The rule can invoke an AWS Lambda function, which can then send a custom notification through Amazon SNS. This is the native AWS mechanism specifically documented for monitoring expiration of imported ACM certificates and alerting before expiration.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EventBridge support for ACM - AWS Certificate Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/supported-events.html) · [Import certificates into AWS Certificate Manager - AWS Certificate Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/import-certificate.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company's IT security guidelines require database credentials to be encrypted and rotated every 14 days.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.

Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager encrypts secrets with AWS KMS and supports automatic rotation for Amazon Aurora database credentials on a configurable rotation schedule. Associating the secret with the Aurora DB cluster and setting a 14-day schedule provides encrypted credential storage and managed rotation without maintaining custom Lambda code or credential files. [Password management with Amazon Aurora and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html)

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon Aurora and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [Rotation schedules - AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_schedule.html)

A financial company needs to handle highly sensitive data. The company will store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that the data is encrypted both in transit and at rest. The company must manage the encryption keys outside the AWS Cloud.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with server-side encryption (SSE) that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.
Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with server-side encryption (SSE) that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key.
Encrypt the data in the S3 bucket with the default server-side encryption (SSE).
Encrypt the data at the company's data center before storing the data in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
When encryption keys must be managed outside AWS, the data must be encrypted before it is sent to Amazon S3 by using client-side encryption. AWS states that client-side encryption encrypts data locally, protects it in transit and at rest, and lets the customer choose and protect the wrapping keys. Server-side encryption options for S3 use keys managed by AWS services, including AWS KMS, so they do not satisfy the requirement to manage keys outside the AWS Cloud.

**Learn more:** [Protecting data by using client-side encryption - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html) · [Client-side and server-side encryption - Amazon S3 Encryption Client](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/client-server-side.html)

A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its on-premises location to an AWS account. The AWS account contains **30 different VPCs** in the same AWS Region. The VPCs use private virtual interfaces (VIFs). Each VPC has a CIDR block that does not overlap with any other network under the company's control.  
  
The company wants to **centrally manage the networking architecture** while still allowing each VPC to communicate with **all other VPCs** and with **on-premises networks**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a transit gateway, and associate the Direct Connect connection with a new transit VIF. Turn on the transit gateway's route propagation feature.
Create a Direct Connect gateway. Recreate the private VIFs to use the new gateway. Associate each VPC by creating new virtual private gateways.
Create a transit VPConnect the Direct Connect connection to the transit VPCreate a peering connection between all other VPCs in the Region. Update the route tables.
Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from on premises to each VPC. Ensure that both VPN tunnels are UP for each connection. Turn on the route propagation feature.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is the hub-and-spoke service built to centrally connect many VPCs and on-premises networks, and it supports dynamic route propagation for VPC, VPN, and Direct Connect gateway attachments. For Direct Connect, the scalable pattern is to use a transit virtual interface to reach a transit gateway through a Direct Connect gateway. By contrast, a Direct Connect gateway with private virtual interfaces and virtual private gateways does not support direct communication between the VPCs associated with that same Direct Connect gateway, so it fails the requirement for all VPCs to communicate with one another. A full mesh of VPC peering connections or separate Site-to-Site VPN connections to each VPC would create substantially more operational overhead. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html?utm_source=openai))

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transit Gateway for Amazon VPC?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html)

A company wants to move a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers:  
  
- an application tier  
- a business tier  
- a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server  
  
The company wants to use specific SQL Server features such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.  
  
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

options.text: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.

Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

questions.explanation:
Because the solution must use SQL Server features including Data Quality Services, the SQL Server database tier cannot be placed on Amazon RDS for SQL Server, since Amazon RDS does not support running Data Quality Services on the same server as the RDS instance. Hosting SQL Server on Amazon EC2 preserves full SQL Server feature compatibility, including native backups. For shared files between Windows-based tiers, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the correct service because it provides managed SMB shared storage for Windows workloads running on EC2.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html) · [Features not supported and features with limited support - Amazon RDS for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.Concepts.General.FeatureNonSupport.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that the company often accesses for up to 7 days after the files are created. After 7 days, the company must still be able to access the files with a maximum retrieval time of 24 hours.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
Create an Amazon FSx File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data after 7 days.
Configure access to Amazon S3 for each user. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway maintains SMB protocol compatibility, allowing seamless migration from on-premises SMB file servers without requiring users to change access patterns. S3 Glacier Deep Archive standard retrieval completes within 12 hours, satisfying the 24-hour requirement for archived files. The gateway-based approach provides lower operational overhead than manual data migration or EC2-based batch processes.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to run applications in containers in the AWS Cloud. These applications are stateless and can tolerate disruptions in the underlying infrastructure. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and operational overhead.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
Use Spot Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.
Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.

questions.explanation:
Spot Instances are appropriate for stateless, fault-tolerant container workloads because they reduce compute cost while allowing for possible interruptions. Among the choices, an Amazon EKS managed node group adds less operational overhead than managing container hosts directly in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group, because Amazon EKS automates node provisioning and lifecycle management for the cluster. AWS documentation also states that managed node groups can use either On-Demand or Spot capacity, and that fault-tolerant applications can be scheduled on Spot managed node groups.

**Learn more:** [Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/managed-node-groups.html) · [Cost optimization - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/scaling-amazon-eks-infrastructure/cost-optimization.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon S3 to store its confidential audit documents. The S3 bucket uses bucket policies to restrict access to audit team IAM user credentials according to the principle of least privilege. Company managers are concerned about accidental deletion of documents in the S3 bucket and want a more secure solution.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to secure the audit documents?

options.text: Enable the versioning and MFA Delete features on the S3 bucket.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the IAM user credentials for each audit team IAM user account.
Add an S3 Lifecycle policy to the audit team's IAM user accounts to deny the s3:DeleteObject action during audit dates.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the S3 bucket and restrict audit team IAM user accounts from accessing the KMS key.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of an object, which allows recovery from accidental deletions or overwrites. Enabling MFA Delete adds an additional control so that permanently deleting an object version or changing the bucket's versioning state requires multi-factor authentication. That combination directly addresses the stated concern about accidental deletion while keeping the documents protected in S3.

**Learn more:** [Configuring MFA delete - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiFactorAuthenticationDelete.html) · [Retaining multiple versions of objects with S3 Versioning - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Versioning.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS DataSync to migrate millions of files from an on-premises system to AWS. The files average 10 KB in size.  
  
The company wants to use Amazon S3 for file storage. During the first year after migration, the files will be accessed once or twice and must be immediately available. After 1 year, the files must be archived for at least 7 years.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to migrate the objects. Store the objects in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for the first year. Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to copy the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Configure the destination storage class for the files as S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Configure a DataSync task to transfer the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

questions.explanation:
Aggregating millions of 10 KB files into large objects avoids the 128 KB minimum billable object size in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and reduces the per-object archival metadata overhead in S3 Glacier Deep Archive. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond, real-time access for infrequently accessed data during the first year. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class for long-term archival data, making it appropriate after that year when immediate access is no longer required.

**Learn more:** [Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes for long-term data storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html) · [Understanding archival storage in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/archival-storage.html)

A company is moving its applications and databases to the AWS Cloud. The company will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Direct Connect, and Amazon RDS.  
  
Which activities will be managed by the company’s operations team? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Management of the Amazon RDS infrastructure layer, operating system, and platforms
Creation of an Amazon RDS DB instance and configuring the scheduled maintenance window
Configuration of additional software components on Amazon ECS for monitoring, patch management, log management, and host intrusion detection
Installation of patches for all minor and major database versions for Amazon RDS
Ensure the physical security of the Amazon RDS infrastructure in the data center
Encryption of the data that moves in transit through Direct Connect

questions.explanation:
Under the AWS shared responsibility model, the customer manages configuration and protections they choose to apply within AWS services, while AWS manages the underlying cloud infrastructure. For Amazon RDS, the customer creates the DB instance and sets items such as the preferred maintenance window, but AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, operating system, platform, and physical facilities. For Amazon ECS, the customer is responsible for application-level and host/workload security tooling such as monitoring, patch-management agents, log-management components, and host intrusion detection. For AWS Direct Connect, traffic is not encrypted by default, so if encryption in transit is required, the customer must enable and manage an appropriate encryption method. That makes B, C, and F the customer-managed activities.

**Learn more:** [AWS shared responsibility model for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/security-shared-model.html) · [Maintaining a DB instance - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Maintenance.html)

A company wants to implement a backup strategy for Amazon EC2 data and multiple Amazon S3 buckets. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must retain backup files for a specific time period. The company must not alter the files for the duration of the retention period.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in governance mode. Create the required backup plan.
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create the required automated snapshot policy.
Use Amazon S3 File Gateway to create the backup. Configure the appropriate S3 Lifecycle management.
Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in compliance mode. Create the required backup plan.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the service here that can protect both Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3 resources in a backup plan, and AWS Backup Vault Lock in **compliance mode** provides WORM-style immutability for the retention period. In compliance mode, once the grace period ends, the vault lock cannot be changed or removed, and recovery points in the vault cannot be deleted or have lifecycle settings altered before their retention period expires. Governance mode does not satisfy the requirement because authorized IAM users can still remove the lock.

**Learn more:** [AWS Backup Vault Lock - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/vault-lock.html) · [How AWS Backup works with supported AWS services - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/working-with-supported-services.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table for storage. A solutions architect determines that many requests to the table are not returning the most recent data. The company's users have not reported any other database performance problems, and latency is within an acceptable range.  
  
Which design change should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Add read replicas to the table.
Use a global secondary index (GSI).
Request strongly consistent reads for the table.
Request eventually consistent reads for the table.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB eventually consistent reads can return stale data for a short time after a write, while strongly consistent reads return the latest committed value for prior successful writes to the same item in the same AWS Region. Because the issue is data freshness rather than latency or throughput, the appropriate change is to request strongly consistent reads instead of changing indexing or replication strategy.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB read consistency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadConsistency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A software company must upgrade a critical web application. The application currently operates on one Amazon EC2 instance that the company hosts in a public subnet. The EC2 instance runs a MySQL database. The application's DNS records are published in an Amazon Route 53 zone.  
  
A solutions architect must reconfigure the application for scalability and high availability. The solutions architect must also lower MySQL read latency.  
  
Which combination of solutions will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Launch a second EC2 instance in a second AWS Region. Use a Route 53 failover routing policy to redirect the traffic to the second EC2 instance.
Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. Create the primary DB instance and reader DB instance in separate Availability Zones.
Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with cross-Region read replicas.

questions.explanation:
An Auto Scaling group that spans multiple Availability Zones and uses an Application Load Balancer provides a scalable, highly available web tier. An Aurora MySQL cluster with a primary instance and an Aurora reader instance in separate Availability Zones provides database resilience; reader instances offload read-only workloads from the primary instance, reducing read load and latency.

**Learn more:** [Set up a scaled and load-balanced application](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/tutorial-ec2-auto-scaling-load-balancer.html) · [Amazon Aurora DB clusters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud. A Multi-AZ Amazon RDS for MySQL server forms the database layer. Amazon ElastiCache forms the cache layer.  
  
The company wants a caching strategy that adds or updates data in the cache when a customer adds an item to the database. The data in the cache must always match the data in the database.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Implement the lazy loading caching strategy
Implement the write-through caching strategy
Implement the adding TTL caching strategy
Implement the AWS AppConfig caching strategy

questions.explanation:
Write-through caching updates the cache whenever the application writes data to the primary database, so newly added or changed records are placed into the cache immediately instead of waiting for a later read. That behavior fits a requirement for the cache contents to stay aligned with the database after inserts or updates. Lazy loading only refreshes cache entries on demand after a cache miss, TTL only controls expiration, and AWS AppConfig is not a data-cache consistency strategy.

**Learn more:** [ElastiCache caching strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Strategies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to direct requests to its **UDP-based** application for users worldwide. The application runs on redundant servers in the company's on-premises data centers in the United States, Asia, and Europe. The company's compliance requirements specify that the application must be hosted on premises. The company wants to improve the application's performance and availability.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the NLBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.

Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the ALBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.

Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three NLBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three ALBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct fit for improving global performance and availability for a UDP application while keeping the application hosted on premises. Network Load Balancers support UDP and can front targets that represent the on-premises application path, and Global Accelerator can use NLBs as regional endpoints to route users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy endpoint. Application Load Balancers are not suitable because they support HTTP/HTTPS rather than UDP, and CloudFront is also not appropriate because it is a CDN for web traffic, not generic UDP application delivery.

**Learn more:** [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html) · [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html)
