A company stores call transcript files on a monthly basis. Users access the files randomly during the first year after the call, but after 1 year, users access the files infrequently.  
  
The company wants to optimize the solution by allowing users to query for and retrieve files that are less than 1 year old as quickly as possible. A delay in retrieving older files is acceptable.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Query the tags to retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

Store individual files in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files that are in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena. Query and retrieve the files that are in S3 Glacier by using S3 Glacier Select.

Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Store search metadata for each archive in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files by searching for metadata from Amazon S3.

Store individual files in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Store search metadata in Amazon RDS. Query the files from Amazon RDS. Retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Standard provides immediate access for transcripts that are less than 1 year old, which satisfies the requirement for the fastest possible query and retrieval of recent files. After 1 year, moving the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the most economical archival option when retrieval delays are acceptable, because Deep Archive is intended for data that is rarely accessed and must be restored before use. Storing searchable metadata separately in Amazon RDS lets users quickly identify the needed transcript without depending on direct real-time querying of archived objects. AWS documentation states that S3 Glacier Deep Archive objects are not immediately accessible and must be restored, while Athena can query Glacier-class data only after restoration, which makes metadata indexing plus archival storage the best fit here.

**Learn more:** [Understanding archive retrieval options - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/restoring-objects-retrieval-options.html) · [Restoring an archived object - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/restoring-objects.html)

A company runs a popular gaming platform on AWS. The application is latency-sensitive because latency can affect the user experience and can create unfair advantages for some players. The application is deployed in every AWS Region. It runs on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs).  
  
A solutions architect must implement a mechanism to monitor the application's health and route traffic to healthy endpoints.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Add a listener for the port that the application listens on, and attach it to a Regional endpoint in each Region. Add the ALB as the endpoint.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify the ALB as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify Amazon S3 as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.

Configure an Amazon DynamoDB database to serve as the data store for the application. Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster to act as the in-memory cache for DynamoDB hosting the application data.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators are built for multi-Region, latency-sensitive applications such as real-time gaming. Global Accelerator continuously checks endpoint health and routes clients to the optimal healthy Regional endpoint over the AWS global network. It also supports Application Load Balancers as endpoints, which matches an architecture of EC2 Auto Scaling groups behind ALBs in every Region. CloudFront is mainly for content delivery and caching, not health-based multi-Region traffic steering for live game sessions, and DynamoDB DAX does not provide client traffic routing or endpoint failover.

A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before deleting the DB instance at the end of the test cycle, a solutions architect created two backups. The first backup was created by using the `mysqldump` utility to produce a database dump. The second backup was created by enabling the final DB snapshot option when terminating RDS.  
  
The company is now preparing for a new test cycle and wants to create a new DB instance from the most recent backup. The company has selected a MySQL-compatible edition of Amazon Aurora to host the DB instance.  
  
Which solutions will create the new DB instance? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Import the RDS snapshot directly into Aurora.
Upload the RDS snapshot to Amazon S3. Then import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then import the database dump into Aurora.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the database dump into Aurora.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora MySQL supports creating a new Aurora DB cluster directly from an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB snapshot by using the restore-from-snapshot workflow. Aurora MySQL also supports migration from MySQL dump files created with `mysqldump`; those dump files can be staged in Amazon S3 and then imported into Aurora. AWS DMS is intended for database migration/replication between running source and target databases, not for importing an RDS snapshot artifact or a mysqldump file in the way described here.

**Learn more:** [Migrating an RDS for MySQL snapshot to Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Migrating.RDSMySQL.Snapshot.html) · [Migrating data from an external MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Migrating.ExtMySQL.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years. The log files will be analyzed by a reporting tool that must be able to access all the files concurrently.  
  
Which storage solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon EC2 instance store
Amazon S3

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective choice for retaining log files for 7 years because it is highly durable object storage built for long-term data retention, and it can store a centralized set of log objects that analytics and reporting tools can access at scale. Amazon EFS provides shared concurrent file access, but it is a file system service rather than the lowest-cost long-term archive option. Amazon EBS is block storage primarily for instance-attached volumes, and EC2 instance store is ephemeral, so neither is appropriate for durable 7-year shared log retention.

**Learn more:** [Data protection in Amazon S3 - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html) · [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently migrated to AWS and wants to implement a solution to protect the traffic flowing into and out of the production VPC. In its on-premises data center, the company used an inspection server that performed specific functions such as traffic flow inspection and traffic filtering. The company wants the same capabilities in the AWS Cloud.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon GuardDuty for traffic inspection and traffic filtering in the production VPC.
Use Traffic Mirroring to mirror traffic from the production VPC for traffic inspection and filtering.
Use AWS Network Firewall to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall is the AWS managed service built for inline inspection and filtering of network traffic entering, leaving, or moving within a VPC. It supports stateless and stateful rule processing, so it can enforce traffic filtering policies in the VPC in the same way an on-premises inspection firewall or inspection server would. GuardDuty only detects potentially malicious activity, Traffic Mirroring only sends copies of packets to monitoring tools, and Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall policies but does not itself perform packet inspection.

**Learn more:** [AWS Network Firewall - Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html) · [Filter network traffic using AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/network-firewall.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a three-tier web application to provide training to new employees. The application is accessed for only 12 hours every day. The company uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store information and wants to minimize costs.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an IAM policy for AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Create an IAM role for the policy. Update the trust relationship of the role. Set up automatic start and stop for the DB instance.

Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache cluster that gives users the ability to access the data from the cache when the DB instance is stopped. Invalidate the cache after the DB instance is started.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Create an IAM role that grants access to Amazon RDS. Attach the role to the EC2 instance. Configure a cron job to start and stop the EC2 instance on the desired schedule.

Create AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the DB instance. Create Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled rules to invoke the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions as event targets for the rules.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS DB instances can be stopped temporarily for cost optimization, including daily development or training use cases, and AWS notes that you are not charged for DB instance hours while the instance is stopped. To automate that daily schedule, the appropriate solution is to use scheduled Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke AWS Lambda functions that call the RDS start and stop APIs for the DB instance.

**Learn more:** [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily - Amazon RDS User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html) · [StopDBInstance - Amazon RDS API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_StopDBInstance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a payment processing system that requires messages for a particular payment ID to be received in the same order in which they were sent. Otherwise, the payments could be processed incorrectly.  
  
Which actions should a solutions architect take to meet this requirement? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Write the messages to an Amazon DynamoDB table with the payment ID as the partition key.
Write the messages to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with the payment ID as the partition key.
Write the messages to an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with the payment ID as the key.
Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Set the message attribute to use the payment ID.
Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the message group to use the payment ID.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS FIFO queues provide strict first-in, first-out delivery within each message group, so setting the message group to the payment ID preserves ordering for all messages for that payment ID. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams routes records with the same partition key to the same shard, where records are ordered, so using the payment ID as the partition key preserves per-payment-ID ordering. Standard SQS does not guarantee message order, and DynamoDB or Memcached do not provide ordered message delivery semantics.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html) · [FIFO queue delivery logic in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-understanding-logic.html)

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager is the native AWS service for secure administrative access to EC2 instances without requiring shared SSH keys or inbound SSH access. It centralizes authorization through IAM and reduces operational effort compared with maintaining bastion hosts or building a custom temporary-key system. AWS documentation explicitly positions Session Manager as a way to connect to managed nodes without providing SSH keys, without opening inbound ports, and with reduced operational overhead. AWS STS issues temporary AWS credentials rather than SSH keys, so it does not satisfy the stated mechanism in that option.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html) · [Amazon EC2 key pairs and Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-key-pairs.html)

A company's infrastructure includes Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS DB instance in a single AWS Region. The company wants to back up its data to a different Region.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS Backup to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to the separate Region. Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance in the separate Region.

Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Copy the EBS snapshots to the separate Region. Create RDS snapshots. Export the RDS snapshots to Amazon S3. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to the separate Region.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the simplest managed option because it can protect both Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS resources and can automatically copy recovery points to another AWS Region through a backup plan. Amazon DLM does not cover RDS backups, and the other approaches require separate manual mechanisms for EC2 and RDS or use replication features that are not the same as centralized backup management. Using one service to schedule and copy both workloads cross-Region minimizes administration.

**Learn more:** [Creating backup copies across AWS Regions - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/cross-region-backup.html) · [What is AWS Backup?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/whatisbackup.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect configured a VPC with a small IP address range. The number of Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC is growing, and there are not enough IP addresses available for future workloads.  
  
Which solution resolves this issue with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Add an additional IPv4 CIDR block to increase the number of IP addresses and create additional subnets in the VPC. Create new resources in the new subnets by using the new CIDR.
Create a second VPC with additional subnets. Use a peering connection to connect the second VPC with the first VPC Update the routes and create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
Use AWS Transit Gateway to add a transit gateway and connect a second VPC with the first VPUpdate the routes of the transit gateway and VPCs. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.

Create a second VPC. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the first VPC and the second VPC by using a VPN-hosted solution on Amazon EC2 and a virtual private gateway. Update the route between VPCs to the traffic through the VPN. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC supports associating additional IPv4 CIDR blocks with an existing VPC and then creating new subnets from those ranges. That expands the available private IP space without introducing another VPC or extra connectivity components. Using a second VPC with peering, Transit Gateway, or VPN adds unnecessary routing, connectivity, and management complexity, so adding a secondary IPv4 CIDR block to the existing VPC is the simplest operational solution.

**Learn more:** [Add or remove a CIDR block from your VPC - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/add-ipv4-cidr.html) · [Amazon VPC quotas - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/amazon-vpc-limits.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A research company uses on-premises devices to generate data for analysis. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to analyze the data. The devices generate `.csv` files and support writing the data to an SMB file share. Company analysts must be able to use SQL commands to query the data. The analysts will run queries periodically throughout the day.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon FSx File Gateway made.
Set up an AWS Glue crawler to create a table based on the data that is in Amazon S3.
Set up an Amazon EMR cluster with EMR File System (EMRFS) to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
Set up an Amazon Redshift cluster to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
Setup Amazon Athena to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway provides an on-premises SMB file share whose files are stored in Amazon S3, which fits devices that can write CSV files only to SMB. An AWS Glue crawler can scan CSV data in S3 and create the corresponding table metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Amazon Athena can then query the S3 data by using standard SQL without requiring always-on cluster infrastructure, making it the most cost-effective choice for periodic queries during the day compared with Amazon EMR or Amazon Redshift.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html) · [Using crawlers to populate the Data Catalog](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores critical data in Amazon DynamoDB tables in the company's AWS account. An IT administrator accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table. The deletion caused a significant loss of data and disrupted the company's operations. The company wants to prevent this type of disruption in the future.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Configure a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for delete actions. Create an AWS Lambda function to automatically restore deleted DynamoDB tables.
Create a backup and restore plan for the DynamoDB tables. Recover the DynamoDB tables manually.
Configure deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables.
Enable point-in-time recovery on the DynamoDB tables.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB deletion protection is the built-in feature that directly prevents accidental table deletion. AWS documentation says deletion protection helps ensure tables are not accidentally deleted during regular administration and helps prevent disruption to business operations. Point-in-time recovery is for restoring data after an accidental delete or write event, but it does not stop the deletion from happening and still requires a restore to a new table. A manual backup plan or an event-driven restore workflow introduces more operational effort than enabling deletion protection.

**Learn more:** [Basic operations on DynamoDB tables - Using deletion protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/WorkingWithTables.Basics.html) · [Backup and restore for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Backup-and-Restore.html)

A company plans to run a high-performance computing (HPC) workload on Amazon EC2 instances. The workload requires low-latency network performance and high network throughput with tightly coupled node-to-node communication.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the EC2 instances to be part of a cluster placement group.
Launch the EC2 instances with Dedicated Instance tenancy.
Launch the EC2 instances as Spot Instances.
Configure an On-Demand Capacity Reservation when the EC2 instances are launched.

questions.explanation:
A cluster placement group is designed for workloads whose instances need to be physically located close together within a single Availability Zone, which provides the low network latency and high network throughput needed for tightly coupled HPC communication. AWS documentation specifically identifies cluster placement groups as suitable for tightly coupled node-to-node communication typical of HPC applications. Dedicated tenancy, Spot pricing, and Capacity Reservations do not provide this network-placement benefit.

**Learn more:** [Placement groups for your Amazon EC2 instances - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-groups.html) · [Placement strategies for your placement groups - Amazon EC2 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)

A company is moving its databases to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and its applications to Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to optimize costs for long-running workloads.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Use On-Demand Instances for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year Compute Savings Plan with the No Upfront option for the EC2 instances.

Purchase Reserved Instances for a 1 year term with the No Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the No Upfront option for the EC2 instances.

Purchase Reserved Instances for a 1 year term with the Partial Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 1 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the Partial Upfront option for the EC2 instances.

Purchase Reserved Instances for a 3 year term with the All Upfront option for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL workloads. Purchase a 3 year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with the All Upfront option for the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
For steady, long-running usage, Amazon RDS Reserved Instances reduce DB instance costs versus On-Demand pricing, and the 3-year All Upfront option provides the highest discount. Savings Plans provide discounted EC2 usage in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment, and All Upfront provides the maximum savings. A 3-year All Upfront RDS Reserved Instance together with a 3-year All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan therefore gives the lowest effective cost among these choices.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Reserved Instances](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/reserved-instances/) · [What are Savings Plans?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/what-is-savings-plans.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that provides on-demand training videos to students worldwide. The application also lets authorized content developers upload videos. The data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the `us-east-2` Region.  
  
The company has created an S3 bucket in the `eu-west-2` Region and an S3 bucket in the `ap-southeast-1` Region. The company wants to replicate the data to the new S3 buckets. The company must minimize latency for developers who upload videos and for students who stream videos near `eu-west-2` and `ap-southeast-1`.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the **fewest** changes to the application? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the eu-west-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
Configure two-way (bidirectional) replication among the S3 buckets that are in all three Regions.

Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming. Do not modify the application for video uploads.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming and uploads.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points provide a single global endpoint that routes requests to the closest active bucket, which reduces latency for both video streaming and object uploads. Because requests can be routed to any regional bucket and Multi-Region Access Points do not check which bucket already contains the object, the buckets need to stay synchronized. AWS recommends two-way (bidirectional) replication when data might be written in multiple Regions so objects written to one bucket are replicated to the others. That makes bidirectional replication across all three buckets, together with using the Multi-Region Access Point ARN for both streaming and uploads, the solution that satisfies the latency requirement with minimal application change.

**Learn more:** [Managing multi-Region traffic with Multi-Region Access Points - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPoints.html) · [Multi-Region Access Point request routing - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPointRequestRouting.html)

A company needs to create an AWS Lambda function that will run in a VPC in the company's primary AWS account. The Lambda function must access files that the company stores in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The EFS file system is in a secondary AWS account. As the company adds files to the file system, the solution must scale to meet demand.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create a new EFS file system in the primary account. Use AWS DataSync to copy the contents of the original EFS file system to the new EFS file system.
Create a VPC peering connection between the VPCs that are in the primary account and the secondary account.

Create a second Lambda function in the secondary account that has a mount that is configured for the file system. Use the primary account's Lambda function to invoke the secondary account's Lambda function.
Move the contents of the file system to a Lambda layer. Configure the Lambda layer's permissions to allow the company's secondary account to use the Lambda layer.

questions.explanation:
The lowest-cost design is to let the Lambda function access the existing cross-account EFS file system over private network connectivity. AWS Lambda supports access to resources in a VPC in another account through VPC peering, and Amazon EFS supports mounts from another VPC, including across accounts, when the VPCs are connected. This preserves the existing elastic, automatically scaling EFS storage and avoids paying for duplicate storage, synchronization, or an additional intermediary function.

**Learn more:** [Giving Lambda functions access to a resource in an Amazon VPC in another account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc-cross-account.html) · [Mounting EFS file systems from another VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mount-fs-different-vpc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company wants to collect user clickstream data from the company's website for real-time analysis. The website has fluctuating traffic patterns during the day. The company needs a scalable solution that can adjust to changing traffic levels.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in on-demand mode to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Glue to process the data in real time.
Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) to capture the clickstream data. Use AWS Lambda to process the data in real time.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is designed to ingest real-time streaming data such as clickstream events, and its on-demand mode automatically scales without shard capacity planning for unpredictable or highly variable traffic. AWS Lambda can be invoked from Kinesis Data Streams to process incoming records in near real time. This combination directly satisfies the requirements for scalable clickstream ingestion and real-time analysis. AWS Glue streaming is more appropriate for streaming ETL pipelines, Kinesis Video Streams is for video data, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink is a processing service rather than the primary clickstream capture service in this option set.

**Learn more:** [Choose the right mode to stream in - Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-size-a-stream.html) · [AWS Lambda event source mapping for Amazon Kinesis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters and Amazon RDS DB instances to build and run a payment processing application. For compliance reasons, the company will run the application in its on-premises data center.  
  
A solutions architect wants to include AWS Outposts in the solution and is working with the company's operations team to build the application.  
  
Which activities are the responsibility of the company's operational team? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks
Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services that run on Outposts
Physical security and access controls of the data center environment
Availability of the Outposts infrastructure including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the Outposts racks
Physical maintenance of Outposts components
Providing extra capacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events

questions.explanation:
Under the AWS Outposts shared responsibility model, the customer is responsible for the on-premises environment that hosts the Outposts, including supplying resilient power and network connectivity and enforcing physical security and access controls for the data center. The customer is also responsible for capacity planning on the Outpost, including allocating enough additional capacity for workloads such as Amazon ECS to handle host failures and maintenance events. AWS, by contrast, manages the Outposts infrastructure, virtualization layer, managed AWS services on Outposts, and the physical maintenance of Outposts equipment.

**Learn more:** [Resilience in AWS Outposts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/network-userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) · [Capacity management for AWS Outposts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/outposts-capacity.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a website analytics application on a single Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instance. The analytics application is highly resilient and designed to operate in stateless mode.  
  
The company notices performance degradation and 5xx errors during busy periods. The company needs the application to scale seamlessly.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.
Create an AWS Lambda function to stop the EC2 instance and change the instance type. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function when CPU utilization is more than 75%.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the web application. Apply the AMI to a launch template. Create an Auto Scaling group that includes the launch template. Configure the launch template to use a Spot Fleet. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can add and remove application instances as demand changes, and an Application Load Balancer distributes traffic across the healthy instances that the Auto Scaling group registers. Stateless, fault-tolerant web and analytics workloads are suitable for Spot capacity, which reduces compute cost; Auto Scaling can replace interrupted Spot capacity. This combination supplies dynamic scaling, load distribution, and lower cost.

**Learn more:** [Auto Scaling groups with multiple instance types and purchase options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-mixed-instances-groups.html) · [Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute incoming application traffic in your Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an internal application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances are compute optimized and use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.  
  
The company needs to identify cost-optimization opportunities across the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Create a new AWS Cost and Usage Report. Search the report for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes.
Create new Amazon CloudWatch billing alerts. Check the alert statuses for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group, and the EBS volumes.
Configure AWS Compute Optimizer for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances, the Auto Scaling group and the EBS volumes.

Configure AWS Compute Optimizer for cost recommendations for the EC2 instances. Create a new AWS Cost and Usage Report. Search the report for cost recommendations for the Auto Scaling group and the EBS volumes.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer generates optimization recommendations from resource configuration and utilization metrics for Amazon EC2 instances, EC2 Auto Scaling groups, and Amazon EBS volumes. A single Compute Optimizer configuration therefore provides the required rightsizing and cost recommendations across all requested resource types.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Compute Optimizer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html) · [AWS Compute Optimizer API Reference — Welcome](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html)

A company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The company runs Amazon EC2 instances across four AWS accounts in the root organizational unit (OU). There are three nonproduction accounts and one production account. The company wants to prevent users from launching EC2 instances of a certain size in the nonproduction accounts. The company has created a service control policy (SCP) that denies launching instances that use the prohibited types.  
  
Which solutions for deploying the SCP will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Attach the SCP to the root OU for the organization.
Attach the SCP to the three nonproduction Organizations member accounts.
Attach the SCP to the Organizations management account.
Create an OU for the production account. Attach the SCP to the OU. Move the production member account into the new OU.
Create an OU for the required accounts. Attach the SCP to the OU. Move the nonproduction member accounts into the new OU.

questions.explanation:
In AWS Organizations, an SCP can be attached to the root, an OU, or individual member accounts. To affect only the three nonproduction accounts, the SCP must be attached either directly to those three member accounts or to an OU that contains only those nonproduction accounts. Attaching the SCP at the root would also affect the production member account, and attaching it to the management account would not enforce the restriction because SCPs do not apply to users or roles in the management account.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [Attaching organization policies with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_policies_attach.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company keeps about 300 TB in Amazon S3 Standard storage from month to month. The S3 objects are typically about 50 GB each and are often replaced by multipart uploads from the company's global application. The number and size of the S3 objects stay the same, but the company's Amazon S3 storage costs increase every month.  
  
How should a solutions architect reduce costs in this situation?

options.text: Switch from multipart uploads to Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy that deletes incomplete multipart uploads.
Configure S3 inventory to prevent objects from being archived too quickly.
Configure Amazon CloudFront to reduce the number of objects stored in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 charges for uploaded multipart parts until the multipart upload is completed or aborted. If large multipart uploads are started frequently and some are not finished, the unused parts continue to consume billed storage and can cause monthly S3 costs to rise even though the final object set stays constant. An S3 Lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads removes those orphaned parts and reduces the unnecessary storage charges.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/) · [Aborting incomplete multipart uploads using a bucket lifecycle configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpu-abort-incomplete-mpu-lifecycle-config.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company's global customer base must be able to access these images quickly. The company must block access for users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.

Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon S3 for image storage and Amazon CloudFront for distribution is the lowest-cost AWS pattern for serving static content globally with low latency. CloudFront supports geographic restrictions to deny access by country, and CloudFront signed URLs provide private, time-limited access to protected files instead of exposing the S3 bucket publicly. AWS documentation specifically recommends using an S3 bucket as the origin for private CloudFront content and using signed URLs when you want to distribute content securely to approved users.

**Learn more:** [Restrict the geographic distribution of your content - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/georestrictions.html) · [Restrict access to files - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 Linux instances in multiple Availability Zones. The application requires a storage layer that is highly available and POSIX-compliant. The storage layer must provide maximum data durability and be shareable across the EC2 instances. Data in the storage layer will be accessed frequently for the first 30 days and infrequently after that.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier.
Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA).
Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA).

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is the AWS shared file storage service for Linux workloads that need POSIX-compliant access from multiple EC2 instances. The EFS Standard storage class stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones, which satisfies the high-availability and maximum-durability requirements. EFS lifecycle management can automatically move files that have not been accessed for 30 days into EFS Standard-IA, reducing cost for the infrequently accessed period while preserving the shared file system model. EFS One Zone is cheaper but does not provide multi-AZ resilience, and S3 storage classes are not the best fit for this shared POSIX file-system requirement.

**Learn more:** [Creating and managing EFS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/creating-using.html) · [Managing storage lifecycle - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/lifecycle-management-efs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its infrastructure on AWS and has a registered base of 700,000 users for its document management application. The company plans to build a product that converts large `.pdf` files into `.jpg` image files. The `.pdf` files average 5 MB in size. The company must store both the original files and the converted files. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable solution to handle demand that will increase rapidly over time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Save the .pdf files to Amazon S3. Configure an S3 PUT event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in Amazon S3.
Save the .pdf files to Amazon DynamoDUse the DynamoDB Streams feature to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in DynamoDB.

Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the files to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.

Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the file to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the correct storage service for 5 MB PDF and JPG objects because it provides highly scalable object storage for any amount of data, and Amazon S3 event notifications can invoke AWS Lambda when an object is created so the conversion can run in a serverless, on-demand model. That combination scales automatically and avoids the ongoing EC2, EBS, or EFS cost and administration of Elastic Beanstalk-based designs. DynamoDB is not suitable for storing these files because a DynamoDB item is limited to 400 KB, which is far smaller than the 5 MB PDFs.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3? - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html) · [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html)

An ecommerce company has an order-processing application that uses Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. During a recent sales event, there was a sudden increase in customer orders. Some customers experienced timeouts, and the application did not process those customers' orders.  
  
A solutions architect determined that CPU utilization and memory utilization were high on the database because of a large number of open connections. The solutions architect must prevent the timeout errors while making the fewest possible changes to the application.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Modify the database to be a global database in multiple AWS Regions.
Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy for the database. Modify the Lambda function to use the RDS Proxy endpoint instead of the database endpoint.
Create a read replica for the database in a different AWS Region. Use query string parameters in API Gateway to route traffic to the read replica.
Migrate the data from Aurora PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Modify the Lambda function to use the DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy is the correct solution because it is designed to sit between Lambda and Aurora PostgreSQL and pool and reuse database connections, reducing the number of open connections that reach the database. AWS documentation specifically recommends RDS Proxy when applications frequently open and close connections or keep many long-lived connections open, and applications connect by using the proxy endpoint instead of the DB endpoint. This directly addresses the connection-exhaustion problem that is driving high CPU and memory on the database, while requiring only a minimal change in the Lambda function’s connection target.

**Learn more:** [Performance and scaling for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Managing.html) · [Connecting to a database through RDS Proxy - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy-connecting.html)

A solutions architect is designing a user authentication solution for a company.  
  
The solution must invoke two-factor authentication for users who sign in from inconsistent geographical locations, IP addresses, or devices. The solution must also scale to support millions of users.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Cognito user pools for user authentication. Enable the risk-based adaptive authentication feature with multifactor authentication (MFA).
Configure Amazon Cognito identity pools for user authentication. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users for user authentication. Attach an IAM policy that allows the AllowManageOwnUserMFA action.
Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) authentication for user authentication. Configure the permission sets to require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito user pools are designed for application user authentication at very large scale, and Cognito adaptive authentication can evaluate sign-in risk based on factors such as IP address, device-related context, and geographic distance from prior sign-ins. When risk is elevated, Cognito can require MFA, which directly matches the requirement for two-factor authentication on inconsistent locations, IP addresses, or devices. Cognito identity pools do not perform primary user authentication, and IAM users or IAM Identity Center are not the right fit for a consumer-facing system that must support millions of end users with risk-based adaptive MFA.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Cognito user pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools.html) · [Working with adaptive authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pool-settings-adaptive-authentication.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an SAP application with a backend SQL Server database in an on-premises environment. The company wants to migrate the on-premises application and database server to AWS. The company needs an instance type that can satisfy the high demands of its SAP database. On-premises performance data indicates that both the SAP application and the database have high memory utilization.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the compute optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
Use the storage optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
Use the memory optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
Use the high performance computing (HPC) optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.

questions.explanation:
Memory-optimized EC2 instances are the best fit when both the SAP application tier and the SQL Server database tier are memory-intensive. AWS documents that memory-optimized instances are built for workloads that process large datasets in memory, AWS guidance for SQL Server on EC2 says memory-optimized instances are a common recommendation because SQL Server benefits from a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, and AWS SAP guidance identifies memory-optimized R-series instances for memory-intensive SAP applications. Because both tiers show high memory utilization, using memory-optimized instances for both is the only option that aligns with the workload profile.

**Learn more:** [Specifications for Amazon EC2 memory optimized instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/instancetypes/mo.html) · [Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 concepts and terminology](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sql-server-ec2/latest/userguide/sql-server-on-ec2-concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving its multi-tier on-premises application to AWS. The application includes a single-node MySQL database and a multi-node web tier. The company must minimize application changes during the migration. The company also wants to improve application resiliency after the migration.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.
Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment.
Migrate the web tier to an AWS Lambda function.
Migrate the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
For the web tier, Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer provide horizontal scaling, health checks, and distribution of HTTP/HTTPS traffic with minimal architectural change for a traditional multi-node web application. For the database tier, Amazon RDS Multi-AZ is the best fit because it keeps the workload on MySQL while adding high availability and automatic failover using the same endpoint, which improves resiliency without requiring a redesign of the application to a different database model. AWS documents describe Multi-AZ deployments for RDS as providing failover support and improved availability, and EC2 Auto Scaling with an Application Load Balancer as the standard scaled and load-balanced application pattern.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Set up a scaled and load-balanced application - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/tutorial-ec2-auto-scaling-load-balancer.html) · [Configuring and managing a Multi-AZ deployment for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application depends on hundreds of cron jobs that run for between 1 and 20 minutes on different recurring schedules during the day.  
  
The company needs a solution on AWS to schedule and run the cron jobs with minimal refactoring. The solution must also support running the cron jobs in response to an event at a future time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks as AWS Lambda functions.
Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use AWS Batch on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with a scheduling policy to run the cron jobs.
Create a container image for the cron jobs. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to create a recurring schedule. Run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.

Create a container image for the cron jobs. Create a workflow in AWS Step Functions that uses a Wait state to run the cron jobs at a specified time. Use the RunTask action to run the cron job tasks on AWS Fargate.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler is designed for time-based invocation and supports recurring `cron` schedules as well as one-time future schedules with `at(...)`. It can directly target Amazon ECS tasks, including tasks that run on AWS Fargate, which is a strong fit for containerized cron jobs that need little code change. This also avoids AWS Lambda’s 15-minute maximum execution time, which would not reliably support jobs that can run for 20 minutes. AWS Step Functions with a Wait state can delay execution, but it is a more complex orchestration pattern than needed for hundreds of cron-style scheduled jobs.

**Learn more:** [CreateSchedule - EventBridge Scheduler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/scheduler/latest/APIReference/API_CreateSchedule.html) · [Using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to schedule Amazon ECS tasks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/tasks-scheduled-eventbridge-scheduler.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a legacy system on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application code cannot be changed, and the system cannot run on more than one instance. A solutions architect must design a resilient solution that improves the system's recovery time.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable termination protection for the EC2 instance.
Configure the EC2 instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to recover the EC2 instance in case of failure.
Launch the EC2 instance with two Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that use RAID configurations for storage redundancy.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon CloudWatch alarm can monitor EC2 status checks and invoke the EC2 recovery action when the instance becomes impaired because of an underlying host issue. This approach preserves the single-instance architecture, requires no application changes, and restores the workload faster by automatically recovering the instance onto new hardware. Termination protection only blocks accidental termination, Multi-AZ is not a deployment mode for one standalone EC2 instance, and RAID on EBS volumes improves disk redundancy rather than instance recovery.

**Learn more:** [Create CloudWatch alarms for Amazon EC2 instances that fail status checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/creating_status_check_alarms.html) · [Create alarms that stop, terminate, reboot, or recover an instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/UsingAlarmActions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When a badge is scanned, the readers send an HTTPS message to indicate who tried to access that specific entrance.  
  
A solutions architect must design a system to process these messages from the sensors. The solution must be highly available, and the results must be available for the company's security team to analyze.  
  
Which system architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as the HTTPS endpoint and to process the messages. Configure the EC2 instance to save the results to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Use Amazon Route 53 to direct incoming sensor messages to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection from the facility network to the VPC so that sensor data can be written directly to an S3 bucket by way of the VPC endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway can provide the required HTTPS endpoint, AWS Lambda can process each badge-reader event without managing servers, and Amazon DynamoDB can store the processed results in a durable, highly available database for later analysis. This serverless design is highly available because Lambda runs across multiple Availability Zones and scales automatically, while API Gateway is built for HTTPS API ingestion. Route 53 does not directly invoke Lambda, a single EC2 instance is not highly available by itself, and S3 gateway VPC endpoints cannot be used by resources across a Site-to-Site VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [API Gateway HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api.html) · [Invoking a Lambda function using an Amazon API Gateway endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-apigateway.html)

options.text: Create an IAM role that specifies EBS encryption. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
Create the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. Attach the EBS volumes to the EC2 instances.
Create an EC2 instance tag that has a key of Encrypt and a value of True. Tag all instances that require encryption at the EBS level.
Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy that enforces EBS encryption in the account. Ensure that the key policy is active.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS provides encryption at rest by creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. AWS states that when you create a new EBS volume, you can enable encryption for that volume, and EBS encryption secures data at rest on the volume and related snapshots by using AWS KMS keys. IAM roles and tags do not turn on EBS encryption, and a KMS key policy by itself does not enforce encryption for all EBS volume creation.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS encryption - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html) · [Create an Amazon EBS volume - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-creating-volume.html)

A company gathers data from thousands of remote devices through a RESTful web services application running on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance accepts the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Soon, the number of remote devices will grow into the millions. The company requires a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.
Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.
Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data.
Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
A highly scalable, low-operations design should move ingestion and transformation from self-managed EC2 to managed serverless services. Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams can absorb very large numbers of incoming device requests, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose can use the stream as a source to deliver data to Amazon S3. AWS Glue can then process and transform data stored in Amazon S3 as a serverless ETL service. This combination removes most EC2 management while scaling better than routing traffic across more EC2 instances or using SQS with EC2-based workers.

**Learn more:** [Welcome - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html) · [CreateDeliveryStream - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_CreateDeliveryStream.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to create a map of its IT infrastructure to identify and enforce policies on resources that create security risks. The company's security team must be able to query data in the IT infrastructure map and rapidly identify security risks.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon RDS to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon Neptune to store the data. Use SPARQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon Redshift to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the data. Use PartiQL to query the data to identify security risks.

questions.explanation:
An IT infrastructure map used to find risky resources is a graph use case because the important information is the relationships among assets, identities, configurations, and dependencies. Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database built for highly connected datasets and supports SPARQL for querying RDF graph data. AWS documentation specifically positions Neptune for network security and explains that graph databases are optimized for storing and querying relationships, whereas relational or NoSQL alternatives are not the best fit for graph traversal and relationship-centric analysis.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Neptune Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/) · [Getting started with Amazon Neptune](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/graph-get-started.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company’s IT security guidelines require that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational effort**?

options.text: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.

Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the lowest-effort solution because it is designed to store database credentials as encrypted secrets and automate rotation for Amazon Aurora credentials on a defined schedule. Aurora supports managing master user passwords in Secrets Manager, and the secret can be encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key. A 14-day rotation interval can be configured directly, avoiding custom code and operational overhead such as building Lambda-based rotation workflows or distributing credentials through Parameter Store, EFS, or S3.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon Aurora and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)

A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling requirements. The read replicas must lag by no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database regularly runs scheduled stored procedures.  
  
As website traffic increases, the replicas incur additional lag during peak-load periods. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must also minimize ongoing operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.

Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.

Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora MySQL has substantially lower replication lag compared to standard RDS for MySQL read replicas because of its architecture and log forwarding. Aurora Replicas can be scaled to 15 instances with much faster replication. This solution requires minimal application code changes while significantly reducing the replica lag issue during peak loads.

**Learn more:** [Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html) · [Replication with Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html)
