3f:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is launching a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must ensure that all data written to the EBS volumes is encrypted at rest."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet this requirement?"}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an IAM role that specifies EBS encryption. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.","B":"Create the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. Attach the EBS volumes to the EC2 instances.","C":"Create an EC2 instance tag that has a key of Encrypt and a value of True. Tag all instances that require encryption at the EBS level.","D":"Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy that enforces EBS encryption in the account. Ensure that the key policy is active."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"Amazon EBS provides encryption at rest by creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. AWS states that when you create a new EBS volume, you can enable encryption for that volume, and EBS encryption secures data at rest on the volume and related snapshots by using AWS KMS keys. IAM roles and tags do not turn on EBS encryption, and a KMS key policy by itself does not enforce encryption for all EBS volume creation.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS encryption - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html) · [Create an Amazon EBS volume - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-creating-volume.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c09eae60-3d94-4ffb-a2eb-3efebe57a01c","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company gathers data from thousands of remote devices through a RESTful web services application running on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance accepts the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Soon, the number of remote devices will grow into the millions. The company requires a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.","B":"Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.","C":"Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.","D":"Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data.","E":"Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3."},"correctAnswer":"AE","explanation":"A highly scalable, low-operations design should move ingestion and transformation from self-managed EC2 to managed serverless services. Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams can absorb very large numbers of incoming device requests, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose can use the stream as a source to deliver data to Amazon S3. AWS Glue can then process and transform data stored in Amazon S3 as a serverless ETL service. This combination removes most EC2 management while scaling better than routing traffic across more EC2 instances or using SQS with EC2-based workers.

**Learn more:** [Welcome - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html) · [CreateDeliveryStream - Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_CreateDeliveryStream.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c0d5a653-b8f8-4a22-b6ad-a9828cad7a4e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company wants to create a map of its IT infrastructure to identify and enforce policies on resources that create security risks. The company's security team must be able to query data in the IT infrastructure map and rapidly identify security risks."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution will meet these requirements with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST operational overhead"}],"?"]}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use Amazon RDS to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.","B":"Use Amazon Neptune to store the data. Use SPARQL to query the data to identify security risks.","C":"Use Amazon Redshift to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.","D":"Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the data. Use PartiQL to query the data to identify security risks."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"An IT infrastructure map used to find risky resources is a graph use case because the important information is the relationships among assets, identities, configurations, and dependencies. Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database built for highly connected datasets and supports SPARQL for querying RDF graph data. AWS documentation specifically positions Neptune for network security and explains that graph databases are optimized for storing and querying relationships, whereas relational or NoSQL alternatives are not the best fit for graph traversal and relationship-centric analysis.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Neptune Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/) · [Getting started with Amazon Neptune](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/graph-get-started.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"a8c3fb32-11cf-4ca1-9354-6ca7653fc3cd","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company runs a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company’s IT security guidelines require that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST operational effort"}],"?"]}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.","B":"Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.","C":"Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.","D":"Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"AWS Secrets Manager is the lowest-effort solution because it is designed to store database credentials as encrypted secrets and automate rotation for Amazon Aurora credentials on a defined schedule. Aurora supports managing master user passwords in Secrets Manager, and the secret can be encrypted with a customer managed AWS KMS key. A 14-day rotation interval can be configured directly, avoiding custom code and operational overhead such as building Lambda-based rotation workflows or distributing credentials through Parameter Store, EFS, or S3.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon Aurora and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"5c25d6c7-0715-4527-a24d-ed56c11f12d1","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
55:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling requirements. The read replicas must lag by no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database regularly runs scheduled stored procedures."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"As website traffic increases, the replicas incur additional lag during peak-load periods. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must also minimize ongoing operational overhead."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.","B":"Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.","C":"Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.","D":"Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon Aurora MySQL has substantially lower replication lag compared to standard RDS for MySQL read replicas because of its architecture and log forwarding. Aurora Replicas can be scaled to 15 instances with much faster replication. This solution requires minimal application code changes while significantly reducing the replica lag issue during peak loads.

**Learn more:** [Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html) · [Replication with Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"0b2d589c-a686-48b2-b20a-3adc4b8d52c5","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
A marketing company receives a large volume of new clickstream data in Amazon S3 from a marketing campaign. The company must analyze the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly. Then, the company needs to decide whether to process the data further in the data pipeline.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create external tables in a Spark catalog. Configure jobs in AWS Glue to query the data.
Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Athena to query the data.
Create external tables in a Hive metastore. Configure Spark jobs in Amazon EMR to query the data.
Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to use SQL to query the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service for analyzing data directly in Amazon S3 with SQL, which makes it well suited for quickly inspecting newly arrived clickstream data before deciding on additional pipeline processing. An AWS Glue crawler can automatically discover the schema and register tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, which Athena can query immediately. This combination minimizes administration because it removes the need to manage Spark infrastructure, EMR clusters, or a Hive metastore.

**Learn more:** [Use a crawler to add a table - Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/schema-crawlers.html) · [Using crawlers to populate the Data Catalog - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html)

A company runs a service that reads and writes large volumes of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC private subnet. The service currently communicates with Amazon S3 through a NAT gateway in a public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that reduces data output costs.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.

Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 traffic.
Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 traffic.

questions.explanation:
For Amazon S3 access from EC2 instances in private subnets, the most cost-effective design is to use an Amazon VPC gateway endpoint for S3 and associate the private subnet route table with that endpoint. Gateway endpoints let traffic to S3 stay on the AWS network without requiring a NAT gateway, eliminating the NAT gateway data processing charges for that S3 traffic. AWS documentation also notes that gateway endpoints for S3 are available in the same Region as the bucket and add endpoint routes to the selected route tables automatically.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a multi-tier application that runs six front-end web servers in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect needs to modify the infrastructure to be highly available without modifying the application.  
  
Which architecture should the solutions architect choose that provides high availability?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses three instances across each of two Regions.
Modify the Auto Scaling group to use three instances across each of two Availability Zones.
Create an Auto Scaling template that can be used to quickly create more instances in another Region.
Change the ALB in front of the Amazon EC2 instances in a round-robin configuration to balance traffic to the web tier.

questions.explanation:
High availability for the web tier is achieved by spanning the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones and placing instances in each zone so the Application Load Balancer can continue routing traffic if one Availability Zone fails. AWS recommends distributing an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones for resiliency, and Application Load Balancers are designed to distribute traffic to targets in multiple Availability Zones.

**Learn more:** [Add an Availability Zone - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html) · [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling? - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A manufacturing company has machine sensors that upload `.csv` files to an Amazon S3 bucket. These `.csv` files must be converted into images and made available as quickly as possible for the automatic generation of graphical reports.  
  
The images are no longer relevant after 1 month, but the `.csv` files must be retained to train machine learning (ML) models twice a year. The ML training sessions and audits are scheduled weeks in advance.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance that downloads the .csv files every hour, generates the image files, and uploads the images to the S3 bucket.
Design an AWS Lambda function that converts the .csv files into images and stores the images in the S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function when a .csv file is uploaded.

Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.

Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.

Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Keep the image files in Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS).

questions.explanation:
An S3-triggered AWS Lambda function is the most cost-effective way to convert each uploaded `.csv` file into an image immediately, because Amazon S3 can invoke Lambda on object creation without running continuously. For retention, the image files should expire after 30 days because they lose value after 1 month. The `.csv` files fit S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval because that class is intended for archive data accessed only once or twice a year and not needing immediate retrieval, which aligns with ML training and audits planned weeks ahead.

**Learn more:** [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html) · [Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes for long-term data storage - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)

A company plans to deploy its application on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 cluster. The application will receive large volumes of traffic. The company wants to optimize the cluster's storage performance as the application load increases.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure the cluster to use the Aurora Standard storage configuration.
Configure the cluster storage type as Provisioned IOPS.
Configure the cluster storage type as General Purpose.
Configure the cluster to use the Aurora I/O-Optimized storage configuration.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora provides two cluster storage configurations: Aurora Standard and Aurora I/O-Optimized. For I/O-intensive workloads, Aurora I/O-Optimized is the correct choice because it is designed for improved price performance and more predictable cost under heavy read/write activity by eliminating per-I/O charges. Provisioned IOPS and General Purpose are not Aurora cluster storage configuration choices. Therefore, for a high-traffic Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 workload whose storage demands increase with load, Aurora I/O-Optimized is the most cost-effective option.

**Learn more:** [Supported Regions and Aurora DB engines for cluster storage configurations - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.Aurora_Fea_Regions_DB-eng.Feature.storage-type.html) · [Creating an Amazon Aurora DB cluster - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.CreateInstance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must provide a team of developers with access to the company’s AWS resources while maintaining a high level of security for those resources.  
  
The company needs an access-control solution that prevents unauthorized access to sensitive data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Share the IAM user credentials for each development team member with the rest of the team to simplify access management and to streamline development workflows.
Define IAM roles that have fine-grained permissions based on the principle of least privilege. Assign an IAM role to each developer.
Create IAM access keys to grant programmatic access to AWS resources. Allow only developers to interact with AWS resources through API calls by using the access keys.
Create an AWS Cognito user pool. Grant developers access to AWS resources by using the user pool.

questions.explanation:
IAM roles with fine-grained, least-privilege permissions limit every developer to only the specific actions and resources necessary for their duties. This enforces authorization boundaries around sensitive data and avoids the security and accountability risks of shared credentials or broadly usable long-term access keys.

**Learn more:** [Security best practices in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html) · [Prepare for least-privilege permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/getting-started-reduce-permissions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS accounts that are billed separately. The company recently purchased a Savings Plan. Because of changes in the company’s business requirements, the company has decommissioned a large number of EC2 instances. The company wants to use its Savings Plan discounts on its other AWS accounts.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: From the AWS Account Management Console of the management account, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section.
From the AWS Account Management Console of the account that purchased the existing Savings Plan, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section. Include all accounts.
From the AWS Organizations management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Savings Plan with other accounts.
Create an organization in AWS Organizations in a new payer account. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the existing AWS account with the existing EC2 instances and Savings Plan. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.

questions.explanation:
Savings Plans discounts are shared across accounts only when the accounts are in the same AWS Organizations consolidated billing family and discount sharing is enabled. AWS documentation states that, in a consolidated billing family, Savings Plans apply to other accounts’ usage only if sharing is enabled, and that the management account controls Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount sharing from Billing preferences. Therefore the required actions are to place the accounts into an AWS Organization with consolidated billing and then enable discount sharing from the management account. AWS RAM does not share Savings Plans, and an individual member account that purchased the plan does not control the organization-wide discount-sharing setting.

**Learn more:** [Understanding how Savings Plans apply to your usage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-applying.html) · [Customizing your Billing preferences](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/billing-pref.html)

A company is creating an application made up of several microservices. The company has chosen to use container technologies to deploy its software on AWS. The company requires a solution that minimizes ongoing maintenance and scaling effort. The company cannot manage additional infrastructure.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster.
Deploy the Kubernetes control plane on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones.
Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with an Amazon EC2 launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with a Fargate launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
Deploy Kubernetes worker nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones. Create a deployment that specifies two or more replicas for each microservice.

questions.explanation:
AWS Fargate is the serverless compute engine for Amazon ECS and removes the need to manage servers or cluster capacity. An ECS service with Fargate launch type and a desired count of 2 or more ensures replicas run across Availability Zones, providing automatic replacement of failed tasks. This meets the requirement to minimize infrastructure management while achieving high availability and scalability.

A company is building a new dynamic ordering website. The company wants to reduce server maintenance and patching to a minimum. The website must be highly available and must scale read and write capacity as fast as possible to match changes in user demand.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.

Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.

Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned write capacity for the database.

Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database.

questions.explanation:
A serverless architecture using Amazon S3 for static content, Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda for dynamic content, and Amazon CloudFront for delivery minimizes operational overhead because there are no application servers to patch or manage. Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity is the best database fit because it is serverless and automatically scales read and write throughput with very fast response to changing demand. Aurora Auto Scaling primarily adds or removes Aurora Replicas to increase read capacity, so it does not provide the same direct rapid scaling for write capacity. EC2-based designs require instance management and patching, so they do not meet the requirement to minimize server maintenance.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html) · [What is Amazon DynamoDB? - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)

A company runs a three-tier web application in a VPC across multiple Availability Zones. Amazon EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group for the application tier.  
  
The company needs to create an automated scaling plan that analyzes each resource's daily and weekly historical workload trends. The configuration must scale resources appropriately based on both the forecast and live changes in utilization.  
  
Which scaling strategy should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Implement dynamic scaling with step scaling based on average CPU utilization from the EC2 instances.
Enable predictive scaling to forecast and scale. Configure dynamic scaling with target tracking
Create an automated scheduled scaling action based on the traffic patterns of the web application.
Set up a simple scaling policy. Increase the cooldown period based on the EC2 instance startup time.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling predictive scaling is intended to analyze historical traffic patterns, including recurring daily and weekly trends, to forecast future capacity needs ahead of time. To also respond to real-time utilization changes after the forecast is applied, AWS recommends combining predictive scaling with dynamic scaling through target tracking. That combination satisfies both proactive scaling from forecasted demand and reactive adjustment from live metrics.

**Learn more:** [How predictive scaling works - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/predictive-scaling-policy-overview.html) · [Predictive scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is creating a prototype of the infrastructure for its new website by manually provisioning the required resources. This infrastructure includes:  
  
- an Auto Scaling group  
- an Application Load Balancer  
- an Amazon RDS database  
  
After the configuration has been fully validated, the company wants the ability to immediately deploy the infrastructure for development and production in two Availability Zones by using an automated approach.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager to replicate and provision the prototype infrastructure in two Availability Zones
Define the infrastructure as a template by using the prototype infrastructure as a guide. Deploy the infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation.
Use AWS Config to record the inventory of resources that are used in the prototype infrastructure. Use AWS Config to deploy the prototype infrastructure into two Availability Zones.
Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk and configure it to use an automated reference to the prototype infrastructure to automatically deploy new environments in two Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation is the AWS infrastructure-as-code service for defining a set of resources in a template and deploying them repeatedly as consistent stacks. That fits the need to take a validated prototype containing an Auto Scaling group, an Application Load Balancer, and an Amazon RDS database and reproduce it automatically for multiple environments. AWS Config records resource configuration and compliance state rather than provisioning stacks, and AWS Systems Manager focuses on operating and automating management tasks on existing resources. Elastic Beanstalk is an application deployment platform, but the core requirement here is repeatable infrastructure templating and deployment, which CloudFormation is designed to provide.

**Learn more:** [Working with CloudFormation templates - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/template-guide.html) · [CloudFormation best practices - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html)

A company has hired a solutions architect to design a reliable architecture for its application. The application consists of one Amazon RDS DB instance and two manually provisioned Amazon EC2 instances that run web servers. The EC2 instances are in a single Availability Zone.  
  
An employee recently deleted the DB instance, and as a result the application was unavailable for 24 hours. The company is concerned about the overall reliability of its environment.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to maximize the reliability of the application's infrastructure?

options.text: Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other EC2 instance. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.

Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection. Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, and run them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.

Create an additional DB instance along with an Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. Configure the application to invoke the Lambda function through API Gateway. Have the Lambda function write the data to the two DB instances.

Place the EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group that has multiple subnets located in multiple Availability Zones. Use Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the instances Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.

questions.explanation:
The most reliable design removes single points of failure in both tiers. Amazon RDS Multi-AZ increases database availability through a standby in another Availability Zone, and deletion protection helps prevent accidental removal of the DB instance. For the web tier, placing instances behind an Application Load Balancer and running them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones provides load distribution, instance replacement, and resilience to an Availability Zone failure. Using Spot Instances would weaken reliability, and reducing the web tier to one instance would also decrease availability.

A company must store user transaction data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and retain that data for 7 years.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to back up the table continuously.
Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
Create an on-demand backup of the table by using the DynamoDB console. Store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.

Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to back up the table and to store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup is the most operationally efficient choice because it natively supports Amazon DynamoDB, lets you define backup schedules, and manages backup lifecycle and retention policies automatically. That directly addresses a 7-year retention requirement with a managed service. DynamoDB point-in-time recovery does not meet the requirement because it supports only up to 35 days of recovery points, not multi-year retention.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application allows users at a company's headquarters to access product data. The product data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The operations team has identified an application performance slowdown and wants to separate read traffic from write traffic. A solutions architect needs to optimize the application's performance quickly.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the primary Availability Zone.
Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the secondary Availability Zone.
Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with half of the compute and storage resources as the source database.
Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with the same compute and storage resources as the source database.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS read replicas are the feature intended to offload read-only queries from a primary MySQL DB instance, which separates read traffic from write traffic and improves performance for read-heavy workloads. A standard Multi-AZ deployment provides a standby for high availability and failover, not a readable secondary for serving application reads. AWS documentation also recommends using the same or larger DB instance class and storage type for the read replica so it can handle redirected read traffic effectively.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Tutorial: Managing a MySQL DB instance environment from development to production - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/tutorial-managing-MySQL-DB.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to isolate its workloads by creating a separate AWS account for each workload. The company requires a solution that centrally manages networking components for those workloads. The solution must also create accounts with automatic security controls (guardrails).  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.

Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.
Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.
Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Deploy a VPC in each workload account. Configure each VPC to route through an inspection VPC by using a transit gateway attachment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower provides Account Factory for standardized account provisioning and applies governance controls, also called guardrails. Amazon VPC subnet sharing through AWS Resource Access Manager lets a centrally managed networking account own the VPC and share its subnets with workload accounts. This satisfies centralized networking and automated account guardrails without operating a VPC and transit-gateway inspection path in every workload account.

**Learn more:** [What Is AWS Control Tower?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/what-is-control-tower.html) · [Provision and manage accounts with Account Factory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/account-factory.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application that stores data on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Increased traffic is causing performance issues. The company determines that database queries are the main cause of the slow performance.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to improve the application's performance?

options.text: Serve read traffic from the Multi-AZ standby replica.
Configure the DB instance to use Transfer Acceleration.
Create a read replica from the source DB instance. Serve read traffic from the read replica.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose between the application and Amazon RDS to increase the concurrency of database requests.

questions.explanation:
For an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB **instance**, the standby replica exists only for failover and high availability and does **not** serve read traffic. To improve performance when query load is the bottleneck, the correct approach is to create an Amazon RDS read replica and direct read traffic to it, which offloads read-heavy queries from the primary DB instance and increases read throughput.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing an application that will allow business users to upload objects to Amazon S3.  
  
The solution must maximize object durability. Objects also must be readily available at any time and for any length of time.  
  
Users will access objects frequently within the first 30 days after the objects are uploaded, but users are much less likely to access objects that are older than 30 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.
Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
Store all the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.

questions.explanation:
S3 Standard is appropriate for the first 30 days because the objects are accessed frequently. After 30 days, S3 Standard-IA is the best fit because it is designed for long-lived, infrequently accessed data while still providing millisecond access and multi-AZ durability. S3 Glacier does not meet the requirement for ready access at any time because archived objects require restore operations, and S3 One Zone-IA is less resilient because it stores data in only one Availability Zone. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is intended for unknown or changing access patterns and adds monitoring charges, so it is less cost-effective than a simple lifecycle transition to S3 Standard-IA when the 30-day pattern is already known.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Data protection in Amazon S3 - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application that stores and displays engineering drawings. All application components will run on AWS infrastructure.  
  
The design must support caching to minimize the time users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must also be able to store petabytes of data.  
  
Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?

options.text: Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront
Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache
Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront
AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the appropriate storage service because it provides massively scalable object storage for very large datasets, making it suitable for petabyte-scale drawing files. Amazon CloudFront is the appropriate caching layer because it caches content at edge locations and commonly serves objects from an S3 origin with low-latency delivery to users. EBS is block storage for EC2 rather than petabyte-scale web object storage, S3 Glacier storage classes are intended for archive use rather than a primary interactive file store, and Storage Gateway is a hybrid service for connecting on-premises environments to AWS rather than a native web application storage choice.

**Learn more:** [Request and response behavior for Amazon S3 origins - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/RequestAndResponseBehaviorS3Origin.html) · [Amazon EBS volume constraints - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/volume_constraints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in its data center. The application uses Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) to communicate with a message queue. The data center cannot scale quickly enough to support the company’s growing business needs, and the company wants to move the workloads to AWS.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.
Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
Use highly available Amazon EC2 instances to run the application. Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
Use AWS Lambda functions to run the application. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.

questions.explanation:
Amazon MQ is the correct messaging service because it supports migration of applications that depend on standard messaging protocols such as AMQP, whereas Amazon SQS does not provide AMQP protocol compatibility. For the compute platform, Amazon EKS is the best fit because the workload already runs on Kubernetes, and Amazon EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that lets the company keep its Kubernetes-based deployment model while offloading much of the cluster control plane management to AWS. Self-managing highly available Amazon EC2 instances would create more infrastructure overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html) · [What is Amazon EKS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/what-is-eks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application stores its data in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster.  
  
The company must create a disaster recovery (DR) solution. The acceptable recovery time for the DR solution is up to 30 minutes. The DR solution does not need to support customer use while the primary infrastructure is healthy.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB and an Auto Scaling group. Set the desired capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to a minimum value. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database. Configure Amazon Route 53 for an active-passive failover with ALB endpoints.

Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALUpdate the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.

Back up the Aurora MySQL DB cluster data by using AWS Backup. Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB. Update the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora MySQL DB cluster in the second Region Restore the data from the backup.

Back up the infrastructure configuration by using AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Set the Auto Scaling group desired capacity to zero. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.

questions.explanation:
A warm standby application stack in a second Region, with minimal Auto Scaling capacity, can be activated after a disaster without serving customers during normal primary operation. Amazon Route 53 active-passive failover directs traffic to the secondary ALB only when the primary is unavailable. Aurora Global Database provides a cross-Region secondary cluster and supports disaster-recovery failover with an RTO on the order of minutes, meeting a 30-minute recovery-time requirement. An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group is Regional and cannot include instances from a second Region.

**Learn more:** [Using switchover or failover in Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html) · [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/autoscaling/faqs/)

options.text: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the Kinesis Data Analytics application.
Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the EMR cluster.
Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data.
Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is the lowest-operations choice for delivering streaming data to Amazon S3 because it is a fully managed service, supports server-side encryption, and can convert incoming records to Apache Parquet before storing them in S3. Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics is designed to continuously read and process streaming data in near real time, so it satisfies the analytics requirement without the cluster administration overhead of Amazon EMR. That combination meets the near-real-time analysis, encryption, and Parquet-in-S3 requirements with the least operational effort.

**Learn more:** [Convert input data format in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/record-format-conversion.html) · [Data protection in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/encryption.html)

A global marketing company has applications running in the **ap-southeast-2** Region and the **eu-west-1** Region. Applications running in a VPC in **eu-west-1** must communicate securely with databases running in a VPC in **ap-southeast-2**.  
  
Which network design will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.

Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPUpdate the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.

Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

questions.explanation:
Inter-Region VPC peering is the appropriate AWS design for private communication between VPCs in different Regions, and it requires routing updates on the participating subnets or route tables. For cross-Region peering, AWS does **not** support referencing a peer VPC’s security group in security group rules, so access must be allowed by using IP addresses or CIDR-based rules on the database security group instead. That makes the design with inter-Region VPC peering, updated route tables, and an inbound database rule allowing the eu-west-1 application servers’ IP addresses the correct solution.

**Learn more:** [VPC peering connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/working-with-vpc-peering.html) · [How VPC peering connections work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)

A financial services company that operates on AWS has designed its security controls to comply with industry standards. The standards include the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).  
  
The company's third-party auditors require evidence that the designed controls have been implemented and are operating correctly. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts in one organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to monitor the current status of the controls across accounts.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Designate one account as the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. Integrate Inspector with Organizations to discover and scan resources across all AWS accounts. Enable Inspector industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.

Designate one account as the Amazon GuardDuty delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated GuardDuty administrator account, enable GuardDuty to protect all member accounts. Enable GuardDuty industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.

Configure an AWS CloudTrail organization trail in the Organizations management account. Designate one account as the compliance account. Enable CloudTrail security standards for NIST and PCI DSS in the compliance account.

Designate one account as the AWS Security Hub delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated Security Hub administrator account, enable Security Hub for all member accounts. Enable Security Hub standards for NIST and PCI DSS.

questions.explanation:
AWS Security Hub is the AWS service for centralized cloud security posture management across AWS accounts. With AWS Organizations, you can designate a delegated administrator account and enable Security Hub across member accounts. Security Hub continuously runs automated security checks and maps controls to supported standards, including NIST and PCI DSS, giving a current cross-account view that auditors can use as evidence of control implementation and operation. GuardDuty is for threat detection, Inspector is for vulnerability management, and CloudTrail is for logging rather than enabling compliance standards.

**Learn more:** [Integrating Security Hub CSPM with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/designate-orgs-admin-account.html) · [AWS Security Hub FAQ](https://aws.amazon.com/security-hub/faqs/)

A survey company has collected data for several years from regions in the United States. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is 3 TB in size and increasing.  
  
The company has begun sharing the data with a European marketing firm that has S3 buckets. The company wants to make sure that its data transfer costs stay as low as possible.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company's S3 bucket.
Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication from the company's S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.
Configure cross-account access for the marketing firm so that the marketing firm has access to the company's S3 bucket.
Configure the company's S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm's S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Requester Pays is intended for sharing large datasets without making the bucket owner absorb the access costs. In a Requester Pays bucket, the requester pays the request charges and data download charges, while the bucket owner continues to pay only for storage. That directly minimizes the survey company’s transfer costs when the marketing firm accesses the data. Cross-Region Replication or syncing data to another bucket would add ongoing copy and transfer charges, and simple cross-account access does not shift the download costs to the other company.

**Learn more:** [Using Requester Pays general purpose buckets for storage transfers and usage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html) · [Configuring Requester Pays on a bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysExamples.html)

The company also wants the application to align with the AWS Well-Architected Framework and to follow AWS recommended best practices for security, scalability, and resiliency.  
  
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Create a VPC across two Availability Zones with the application's existing architecture. Host the application with existing architecture on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in each Availability Zone with EC2 Auto Scaling groups. Secure the EC2 instance with security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs).
Set up security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs) to control access to the database layer. Set up a single Amazon RDS database in a private subnet.

Create a VPC across two Availability Zones. Refactor the application to host the web tier, application tier, and database tier. Host each tier on its own private subnet with Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and application tier.
Use a single Amazon RDS database. Allow database access only from the application tier security group.
Use Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier. Control access by using security groups containing references to each layer's security groups.
Use an Amazon RDS database Multi-AZ cluster deployment in private subnets. Allow database access only from application tier security groups.

questions.explanation:
Option C separates the web, application, and database tiers into distinct subnets across multiple Availability Zones with Auto Scaling for stateless tiers. Option E places Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier to distribute traffic and control access with security groups. Option F deploys an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ cluster with automatic failover and places it in private subnets with restricted access only from the application tier. These three options together implement the AWS Well-Architected Framework for security, scalability, and resiliency.

A company is building a real-time multiplayer game that uses UDP for communication between the client and servers in an Auto Scaling group. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB on-demand for data storage.

questions.explanation:

A social media company has workloads that collect and process data. The workloads keep the data in on-premises NFS storage. The data store cannot scale quickly enough to support the company’s growing business needs. The company wants to migrate the existing data store to AWS.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Use an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to the appropriate storage class.
Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway. Use an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to the appropriate storage class.
Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard-Infrequent Access (Standard-IA) storage class. Activate the infrequent access lifecycle policy.
Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone-Infrequent Access (One Zone-IA) storage class. Activate the infrequent access lifecycle policy.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway is the best fit because it presents NFS or SMB file shares to clients while storing the data as objects in Amazon S3, which provides far greater scalability than the existing on-premises NFS store. Using Amazon S3 lifecycle policies can then transition the stored objects to lower-cost S3 storage classes, making this the most cost-effective option. Volume Gateway is for iSCSI block storage rather than NFS file access, and Amazon EFS options provide managed NFS file systems but are typically not as cost-efficient as S3-backed file storage with lifecycle tiering for this migration pattern.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html) · [File Gateway setup requirements - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/Requirements.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare company is building an AWS Lambda function that sends notifications to an encrypted Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The notifications include protected health information (PHI).  
  
The SNS topic uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys for encryption. The company must make sure that the application has the required permissions to securely publish messages to the SNS topic.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a resource policy for the SNS topic that allows the Lambda function to publish messages to the topic.
Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the SNS topic instead of customer managed keys.
Create a resource policy for the encryption key that the SNS topic uses that has the necessary AWS KMS permissions.
Specify the Lambda function's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the SNS topic's resource policy.
Associate an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with the SNS topic to control access to the topic by using API Gateway resource policies.
Configure a Lambda execution role that has the necessary IAM permissions to use a customer managed key in AWS KMS.

questions.explanation:
Publishing to an SSE-KMS encrypted SNS topic requires permission to publish to the topic and permission to use its customer managed KMS key. A topic resource policy can allow publishing, the KMS key policy must authorize the necessary KMS operations, and the Lambda execution role must receive the applicable KMS permissions. SNS documentation specifies that publishers of encrypted messages need `kms:GenerateDataKey*` and `kms:Decrypt`, in addition to `sns:Publish`.

**Learn more:** [Managing Amazon SNS encryption keys and costs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-key-management.html) · [Permissions for custom KMS keys for Amazon SNS topic encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-enable-encryption-for-topic.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a prototype ecommerce website on AWS. The website includes an Application Load Balancer, an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances serving as web servers, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance using the Single-AZ configuration.  
  
The website responds slowly when users search the product catalog. The product catalog consists of a set of tables in the MySQL database that the company does not update often. A solutions architect has found that CPU utilization on the DB instance is high during product catalog searches.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend to improve website performance during product catalog searches?

options.text: Migrate the product catalog to an Amazon Redshift database. Use the COPY command to load the product catalog tables.
Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to cache the product catalog. Use lazy loading to populate the cache.
Add an additional scaling policy to the Auto Scaling group to launch additional EC2 instances when database response is slow.
Turn on the Multi-AZ configuration for the DB instance. Configure the EC2 instances to throttle the product catalog queries that are sent to the database.

questions.explanation: An Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster can store frequently searched, rarely changing product-catalog data in memory. Lazy loading populates cache entries when requested and allows subsequent searches to be served from the cache, reducing read workload and CPU utilization on the Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has **700 TB** of backup data stored on **network attached storage (NAS)** in its data center. The backup data must remain available for **infrequent regulatory requests** and must be retained for **7 years**. The company has decided to migrate this backup data from the data center to **AWS**. The migration must be completed within **1 month**. The company has **500 Mbps** of dedicated bandwidth on its public internet connection available for data transfer.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to migrate and store the data at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Deploy a VPN connection between the data center and Amazon VPC. Use the AWS CLI to copy the data from on premises to Amazon S3 Glacier.
Provision a 500 Mbps AWS Direct Connect connection and transfer the data to Amazon S3. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data and deploy a DataSync agent on premises. Use the DataSync task to copy files from the on-premises NAS storage to Amazon S3 Glacier.

questions.explanation:
AWS Snowball is the appropriate transfer method for hundreds of terabytes to petabyte-scale migrations when network bandwidth is insufficient to meet the migration window. With only 500 Mbps available, transferring 700 TB online within 1 month is not feasible. After ingestion into Amazon S3, an S3 Lifecycle rule can transition the objects to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which is the lowest-cost S3 archival storage class for long-term retention with infrequent access. AWS documentation supports Snowball for large migrations from 500 TB to multiple petabytes and S3 Lifecycle transitions to Glacier Deep Archive for archival storage.

**Learn more:** [Creating a large data migration plan with Snowball Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/create-data-migration-plan.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)

A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Storage Lens is the AWS feature designed for organization-wide visibility into Amazon S3 usage and cost-optimization metrics across accounts and Regions. It supports AWS Organizations and includes the specific metric **IncompleteMultipartUploadObjectCount**, which reports the number of incomplete multipart upload objects. That makes it the lowest-overhead way to produce centralized reporting for this requirement. AWS Config and SCPs do not provide this S3 multipart-upload count reporting capability, and S3 Multi-Region Access Points are for global request routing, not storage analytics or compliance reporting.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon S3 Storage Lens with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_with_organizations.html) · [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application needs to access an Amazon DynamoDB table.  
  
What is the **MOST secure** way to access the table while ensuring that the traffic does not leave the AWS network?

options.text: Use a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
Use a NAT gateway in a public subnet.
Use a NAT instance in a private subnet.
Use the internet gateway attached to the VPC.

questions.explanation:
A VPC endpoint for DynamoDB is the correct solution because it provides private connectivity from EC2 instances in private subnets to DynamoDB without requiring a NAT device or internet gateway. AWS documents that DynamoDB VPC endpoints let instances use private IP addresses to access DynamoDB with no exposure to the public internet, and the traffic stays on the Amazon network. For DynamoDB, this is the secure private-access pattern supported by AWS.

**Learn more:** [Infrastructure security in Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/network-isolation.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate its existing on-premises monolithic application to AWS.  
  
The company wants to keep as much of the front-end code and the backend code as possible. However, it also wants to split the application into smaller applications, and each application will be managed by a different team.  
  
The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Host the application on AWS Lambda. Integrate the application with Amazon API Gateway.
Host the application with AWS Amplify. Connect the application to an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with AWS Lambda.
Host the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Set up an Application Load Balancer with EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group as targets.
Host the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up an Application Load Balancer with Amazon ECS as the target.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS is the best fit for decomposing a monolithic application into smaller independently managed services while preserving most of the existing application code, because containerizing services usually requires less code rewrite than moving to a Lambda-based serverless model. ECS also provides managed container orchestration and integrates with an Application Load Balancer for scalable service routing, which reduces operational overhead compared with managing Amazon EC2 instances directly. AWS guidance for decomposing monoliths into microservices and migrating with the strangler pattern specifically points to container services such as Amazon ECS as a modernization target, whereas Amplify is primarily a frontend hosting/development service and Lambda commonly involves more refactoring into fine-grained functions.

**Learn more:** [Decomposing monoliths into microservices - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/modernization-decomposing-monoliths/welcome.html) · [Seamlessly migrate on-premises legacy workloads using a strangler pattern | AWS Architecture Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/seamlessly-migrate-on-premises-legacy-workloads-using-a-strangler-pattern/)

A solutions architect must ensure that API calls to Amazon DynamoDB from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC do not traverse the internet.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create a route table entry for the endpoint.
Create a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2.
Create an elastic network interface for the endpoint in each of the subnets of the VPC.
Create a security group entry in the endpoint's security group to provide access.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB can be accessed privately from a VPC by using a **gateway VPC endpoint**. For this endpoint type, the VPC's **route tables** must direct DynamoDB-bound traffic to the endpoint so instances use the AWS private network path instead of internet-based routing. The interface-endpoint actions in the other options, such as creating elastic network interfaces in subnets and managing an endpoint security group, are not the required pattern for the DynamoDB gateway-endpoint solution.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) to run its self-managed database. The company has 350 TB of data distributed across all EBS volumes. The company takes daily EBS snapshots and retains the snapshots for 1 month. The daily change rate is 5% of the EBS volumes.  
  
Because of new regulations, the company must retain the monthly snapshots for 7 years. The company needs to modify its backup strategy to comply with the new regulations and to ensure that data is available with minimal administrative effort.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Copy the monthly snapshot to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year retention period.
Continue with the current EBS snapshot policy. Add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period.
Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Keep the monthly snapshot in the standard tier for 7 years. Use incremental snapshots.

Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier. Use EBS direct APIs to take snapshots of all the EBS volumes every month. Store the snapshots in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Infrequent Access tier for 7 years.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive is the low-cost EBS snapshot tier designed for long-term retention of rarely accessed snapshots, including compliance use cases over 90 days. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager can automate EBS snapshot lifecycle management, including moving snapshots from the standard tier to the archive tier, which satisfies the 7-year retention requirement with minimal administration and lower cost than leaving snapshots in the standard tier. EBS snapshots are not managed by copying them as native restorable snapshot objects into S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Standard-IA buckets for this use case.

**Learn more:** [Archive Amazon EBS snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-archive.html) · [Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle-dlm.html)
