A solutions architect is designing a REST API in Amazon API Gateway for a cash payback service. The application requires **1 GB of memory** and **2 GB of storage** for its compute resources. The application will also require the data to be in a **relational** format.  
  
Which additional combination of AWS services will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative effort**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Amazon EC2
AWS Lambda
Amazon RDS
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Services (Amazon EKS)

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the best fit for the compute tier because it is serverless and requires less operational management than Amazon EC2 or Amazon EKS. Lambda supports configurable memory from 128 MB up to 10,240 MB and ephemeral storage in `/tmp` from 512 MB up to 10,240 MB, so a function can be configured to provide 1 GB of memory and 2 GB of storage. For the data layer, Amazon RDS is the managed relational database service, so it meets the relational-data requirement with less administrative effort than self-managed alternatives. Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and does not satisfy the relational requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure ephemeral storage for Lambda functions - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-ephemeral-storage.html) · [Troubleshoot configuration issues in Lambda - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/troubleshooting-configuration.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an application on AWS. The application uses multiple AWS Lambda functions to retrieve sensitive data from one Amazon S3 bucket for processing. The company must ensure that only authorized Lambda functions can access the data. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Grant full S3 bucket access to all Lambda functions through a shared IAM role.
Configure the Lambda functions to run within a VPC. Configure a bucket policy to grant access based on the Lambda functions' VPC endpoint IP addresses.
Create individual IAM roles for each Lambda function. Grant the IAM roles access to the S3 bucket. Assign each IAM role as the Lambda execution role for its corresponding Lambda function.
Configure a bucket policy granting access to the Lambda functions based on their function ARNs.

questions.explanation:
A Lambda execution role is the IAM identity through which a function accesses AWS resources. Assigning a distinct execution role to each function and granting that role only the required permissions on the S3 bucket limits bucket access to the authorized functions and avoids sharing unnecessarily broad permissions.

**Learn more:** [Defining Lambda function permissions with an execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html) · [Managing permissions in AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-permissions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and to return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that grants access to protected resources stored in another S3 bucket.  
  
After the application is deployed, users report errors and cannot access the protected content. A solutions architect must fix this issue by providing the correct permissions so that users can access the protected content.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito identity pools assign authenticated users temporary AWS credentials by having them assume IAM roles, and those IAM roles define permissions to access AWS resources such as Amazon S3 objects. To let authenticated users read protected content in a second S3 bucket, the identity pool must be configured to use an IAM role that includes the required S3 permissions. S3 ACLs are not the primary mechanism for granting federated Cognito users this access, and redeploying the application does not address an authorization failure.

**Learn more:** [Using role-based access control - Amazon Cognito](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/role-based-access-control.html) · [IAM roles - Amazon Cognito](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team runs monthly resource-intensive tests on its general purpose Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Performance Insights enabled.  
  
The testing lasts for 48 hours once a month and is the only process that uses the database.  
  
The team wants to reduce the cost of running the tests without reducing the compute and memory attributes of the DB instance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Stop the DB instance when tests are completed. Restart the DB instance when required.
Use an Auto Scaling policy with the DB instance to automatically scale when tests are completed.
Create a snapshot when tests are completed. Terminate the DB instance and restore the snapshot when required.
Modify the DB instance to a low-capacity instance when tests are completed. Modify the DB instance again when required.

questions.explanation:
Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance is the built-in cost-optimization approach for periods of temporary inactivity because it preserves the DB instance configuration and avoids changing the instance class. AWS documentation states that stopping and starting a DB instance is faster and more efficient than creating a snapshot, deleting the instance, and restoring it later. Auto Scaling is not the mechanism for a single RDS DB instance in this scenario, and modifying to a smaller instance would reduce compute and memory attributes, which violates the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html) · [StopDBInstance - Amazon RDS API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_StopDBInstance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The application must write sensitive data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must not traverse the public internet.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Create a route in the VPC route table to the endpoint.
Create an internal Network Load Balancer that has the S3 bucket as the target.
Deploy the S3 bucket inside the VPCreate a route in the VPC route table to the bucket.
Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC and an S3 regional endpoint.

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 allows instances in a VPC to access S3 over the AWS network without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device, so the traffic does not go over the public internet. The endpoint is associated with the VPC route tables so traffic destined for S3 is routed to the endpoint. An S3 bucket is not placed inside a VPC, an NLB cannot use an S3 bucket as a target, and Direct Connect is not the mechanism for private S3 access from EC2 instances already running inside the VPC.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores backup files by using Amazon S3 Standard storage. The files are accessed frequently for 1 month. However, after 1 month, the files are not accessed. The company must retain the files indefinitely.  
  
Which storage solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically migrate objects.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 1 month.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 month.

questions.explanation:
For backup files that are accessed often only during the first 30 days and then retained for the long term without further access, an S3 Lifecycle rule that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month is the lowest-cost fit. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is intended for long-lived archive data with very infrequent access, while S3 Standard should be kept during the initial month of frequent access. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is less cost-efficient here because the access pattern is already known and it includes monitoring and automation charges, and S3 One Zone-IA is not the right choice for a primary backup copy because it stores data in only one Availability Zone.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Data protection in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data includes personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use this data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications can process the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Object Lambda intercepts GET requests and applies custom transformation logic to objects before returning them to the requesting application. The company can use Object Lambda to redact PII for applications that do not need it, while the application that requires PII receives the original data. This approach maintains a single S3 dataset while providing application-specific views, minimizing operational overhead compared to maintaining multiple per-application datasets.

**Learn more:** [Transforming objects with S3 Object Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transforming-objects.html) · [Writing Lambda functions for S3 Object Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/olap-writing-lambda.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application that uploads files to an Amazon S3 bucket. After upload, the files must be processed to extract metadata, and this processing takes less than 5 seconds. The number and rate of uploads vary from a few files per hour to hundreds of simultaneous uploads.  
  
The company asks a solutions architect to design a **cost-effective** architecture that meets these requirements.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail trails to log S3 API calls. Use AWS AppSync to process the files.
Configure an object-created event notification within the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process and send data to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to process the files uploaded to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can publish object-created event notifications directly to AWS Lambda, and Lambda can process each uploaded object without provisioning servers. This is the simplest and most cost-effective design for short, bursty, event-driven workloads because Lambda scales automatically with upload volume and supports execution times far longer than the required less than 5 seconds. CloudTrail is for auditing API activity, Kinesis Data Streams is unnecessary for files already landing in S3, and SNS is a fanout messaging service rather than the direct processing mechanism needed here.

**Learn more:** [Event notification types and destinations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html) · [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers. The applications run in different AWS accounts within the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts.  
  
The company wants more detailed cost information for each product line by using the consolidated billing feature in Organizations.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.
Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.
Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.
Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.
Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.

questions.explanation:
Product-line chargeback in AWS consolidated billing is done with **user-defined cost allocation tags**. Since the resource tags were created by the teams, they are user-defined rather than AWS-generated. AWS requires those tag keys to be activated in the **AWS Billing and Cost Management console** before they appear in billing and cost reports. For accounts in AWS Organizations, the **management account** activates the cost allocation tags so the tagged costs are visible in the organization’s consolidated billing data.

**Learn more:** [Activating user-defined cost allocation tags - AWS Billing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/activating-tags.html) · [Using user-defined cost allocation tags - AWS Billing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/custom-tags.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its production workload on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. A solutions architect must analyze the current EBS volume cost and recommend optimizations. The recommendations must include estimated monthly savings opportunities.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Inspector reporting to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use AWS Systems Manager reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use AWS Compute Optimizer to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer is the AWS service that generates optimization recommendations for Amazon EBS volumes by analyzing their specifications and utilization metrics. Its EBS recommendations include proposed volume changes such as type, size, IOPS, and throughput, and it also shows estimated monthly savings and savings opportunity, which directly satisfies the cost-analysis and savings-estimation requirement.

**Learn more:** [Viewing Amazon EBS volume recommendations - AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/view-ebs-recommendations.html) · [GetEBSVolumeRecommendations - AWS Compute Optimizer API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/APIReference/API_GetEBSVolumeRecommendations.html)

options.text: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Restore the snapshots onto EC2 instance store volumes in the test environment.

Configure the production EBS volumes to use the EBS Multi-Attach feature. Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Attach the production EBS volumes to the EC2 instances in the test environment.

Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Create and initialize new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment before restoring the volumes from the production EBS snapshots.

Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots. Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS snapshots can be used to create separate new EBS volumes for a test environment, which preserves isolation so test changes do not affect production. For high and predictable I/O performance with minimal restore time, the snapshots should use Fast Snapshot Restore, because volumes created from Fast Snapshot Restore-enabled snapshots are fully initialized at creation and immediately deliver full performance. By contrast, standard volumes restored from snapshots are lazily initialized and can experience increased latency and reduced performance until initialization completes.

**Learn more:** [Initialize Amazon EBS volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/initalize-volume.html) · [Amazon EBS fast snapshot restore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html)

A company is moving its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases. It wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to improve database security and reduce operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS is a fully managed relational database service, so it reduces the operational burden compared with self-managing databases on Amazon EC2. For sensitive database workloads, RDS supports encryption at rest by using AWS KMS keys, which directly improves data security for stored database data. Amazon Macie is designed for discovering sensitive data in Amazon S3, and Amazon CloudWatch Logs is for logging and monitoring rather than protecting primary database data.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/) · [Encrypting Amazon RDS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company currently operates an on-premises, resource-intensive application that uses ASP.NET on Linux machines and serves customers directly.  
  
The company wants to modernize the application to .NET. It wants to run the application in containers, scale it based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and reduce the time spent on operational maintenance activities.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS App2Container to containerize the application. Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
Use AWS App2Container to containerize the application. Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 instances.
Use AWS App Runner to containerize the application. Use App Runner to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
Use AWS App Runner to containerize the application. Use App Runner to deploy the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on Amazon EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS App2Container can containerize existing supported applications and generate deployment artifacts. Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate provides serverless container compute, eliminating the need to operate and maintain EC2 container instances. ECS services provide CloudWatch utilization metrics that can be used for service auto scaling. App Runner does not containerize an application for deployment onto ECS or EKS.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS App2Container?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/app2container/latest/UserGuide/what-is-a2c.html) · [Amazon ECS CloudWatch metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/cloudwatch-metrics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to enhance the availability and performance of its hybrid application. The application includes a stateful, TCP-based workload running on Amazon EC2 instances across different AWS Regions and a stateless, UDP-based workload hosted on premises.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to enhance availability and performance? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator. Add the load balancers as endpoints.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the load balancers.
Configure two Application Load Balancers in each Region. The first will route to the EC2 endpoints, and the second will route to the on-premises endpoints.
Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region to address the EC2 endpoints. Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region that routes to the on-premises endpoints.
Configure a Network Load Balancer in each Region to address the EC2 endpoints. Configure an Application Load Balancer in each Region that routes to the on-premises endpoints.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides static entry-point IP addresses, directs traffic over the AWS global network, and routes traffic to healthy regional endpoints, improving multi-Region availability and performance. Network Load Balancers operate at Layer 4 and support both TCP and UDP listeners; they can distribute the TCP workload to EC2 targets and route to appropriately connected on-premises targets. Application Load Balancers and CloudFront do not provide UDP load balancing.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its workloads on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The container images used by the ECS task definition must be scanned for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). Newly created container images must also be scanned.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **fewest** changes to the workloads?

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository to store the container images. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR basic scan.
Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to scan the images. Use an S3 Event Notification to initiate a Macie scan for every event with an s3:ObjectCreated:Put event type.

Deploy the workloads to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR enhanced scan.

Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket that has versioning enabled. Configure an S3 Event Notification for s3:ObjectCreated:* events to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to initiate an Amazon Inspector scan.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) is the AWS-native private container registry used with Amazon ECS, and Amazon ECR scanning can scan images for CVEs. ECR basic scanning supports **scan on push**, which automatically scans newly pushed images, satisfying the requirement to scan new container images with minimal architectural change. Migrating the workloads to Amazon EKS would be a larger change than necessary, and Amazon S3 with Macie or Lambda/Inspector is not the standard mechanism for container image CVE scanning because Amazon Inspector container image scanning integrates with Amazon ECR repositories.

**Learn more:** [Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html) · [Configuring basic scanning for images in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning-basic-enabling.html)

A company recently deployed a new auditing system to centralize information about operating system versions, patching, and installed software for Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
A solutions architect must ensure that all instances provisioned through EC2 Auto Scaling groups successfully send reports to the auditing system as soon as they are launched and terminated.  
  
Which solution achieves these goals **MOST efficiently**?

options.text: Use a scheduled AWS Lambda function and run a script remotely on all EC2 instances to send data to the audit system.
Use EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to run a custom script to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
Use an EC2 Auto Scaling launch configuration to run a custom script through user data to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
Run a custom script on the instance operating system to send data to the audit system. Configure the script to be invoked by the EC2 Auto Scaling group when the instance starts and is terminated.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks let an Auto Scaling group pause instances during both the launch and termination transitions so custom processing can occur at exactly those moments. That directly matches the requirement to send audit data immediately when instances are launched and when they are being terminated. User data in a launch configuration can help only at startup, not at termination, and scheduled or remote-script approaches are less efficient and less event-driven than lifecycle hooks.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html) · [Run commands when you launch an EC2 instance with user data input](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/user-data.html)

A company is building a web application that delivers a content management system. The content management system runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Users are continually adding and updating files, blogs, and other website assets in the content management system.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution so that all the EC2 instances share current website content with the least possible lag time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Update the EC2 user data in the Auto Scaling group lifecycle policy to copy the website assets from the EC2 instance that was launched most recently. Configure the ALB to make changes to the website assets only in the newest EC2 instance.

Copy the website assets to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure each EC2 instance to mount the EFS file system locally. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the EFS file system.

Copy the website assets to an Amazon S3 bucket. Ensure that each EC2 instance downloads the website assets from the S3 bucket to the attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Run the S3 sync command once each hour to keep files up to date.

Restore an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshot with the website assets. Attach the EBS snapshot as a secondary EBS volume when a new EC2 instance is launched. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the secondary EBS volume.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is a shared file storage service that supports concurrent read and write access from multiple Amazon EC2 instances and can be accessed from multiple Availability Zones in the same Region. Mounting one EFS file system on each EC2 instance gives all instances a common, immediately shared content store, which best satisfies the requirement for up-to-date website assets with minimal lag. By contrast, S3-to-EBS synchronization is delayed, EBS snapshots are point-in-time copies rather than shared live storage, and copying content from one instance to another does not provide a reliable shared filesystem architecture.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Creating and managing EFS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/creating-using.html)

An ecommerce company runs its application on AWS. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in Multi-AZ mode for the underlying database. During a recent promotional campaign, the application experienced heavy read load and write load. Users experienced timeout issues when they attempted to access the application.  
  
A solutions architect needs to make the application architecture more scalable and highly available.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST downtime**?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has the Aurora cluster as a source. Create an AWS Lambda function to log the state change events of the Aurora cluster. Add the Lambda function as a target for the EventBridge rule. Add additional reader nodes to fail over to.
Modify the Aurora cluster and activate the zero-downtime restart (ZDR) feature. Use Database Activity Streams on the cluster to track the cluster status.
Add additional reader instances to the Aurora cluster. Create an Amazon RDS Proxy target group for the Aurora cluster.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache. Replicate data from the Aurora cluster to Redis by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with a write-around approach.

questions.explanation:
Adding Aurora reader instances increases read scalability and gives Aurora additional replicas that can be promoted during failover, improving availability. Adding Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the Aurora cluster provides connection pooling and faster, more transparent failover handling, which helps reduce timeouts during load spikes and lowers application disruption. AWS documentation states that Aurora reader instances improve cluster availability and failover options, and that RDS Proxy is highly available across multiple AZs, preserves application connections, and can reduce failover times for Aurora Multi-AZ deployments.

**Learn more:** [High availability for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html) · [Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building an application that exposes order-shipping statistics for retrieval through a REST API. The company needs to extract the shipping statistics, arrange the data in an easy-to-read HTML format, and send the report to several email addresses at the same time every morning.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge can run work on a schedule, and invoking an AWS Lambda function is the appropriate serverless way to call the application's REST API each morning and prepare the report data. Amazon SES is the AWS email service for sending messages and supports HTML bodies, so it can deliver the formatted report to the required recipients. AWS Glue is not the best fit for this simple scheduled API retrieval task, and Kinesis Data Firehose, S3 event notifications, and SNS do not provide the required scheduled HTML report generation workflow.

**Learn more:** [Invoke a Lambda function on a schedule - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html) · [Body - Amazon Simple Email Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/APIReference/API_Body.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must expose the Lambda function so that the third party can call it.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **MOST operational efficiency**?

options.text: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda function URLs provide a simple, dedicated HTTP(S) endpoint directly for a Lambda function, which is exactly what a third-party webhook sender needs. AWS documentation specifically identifies Lambda function URLs as a good choice for simple webhooks and notes that they provide a direct HTTP endpoint without introducing additional infrastructure. Using an Application Load Balancer would work but adds extra components to deploy and manage. Amazon SNS and Amazon SQS do not expose a generic webhook endpoint for arbitrary third-party HTTP callers; they are AWS messaging services that require publishing through AWS APIs rather than a simple public webhook URL.

**Learn more:** [Invoking Lambda function URLs - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-invocation.html) · [Tutorial: Creating a webhook endpoint using a Lambda function URL - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-webhook-tutorial.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to run an application. The company creates one snapshot of each EBS volume every day to satisfy compliance requirements.  
  
The company wants to implement an architecture that prevents accidental deletion of EBS volume snapshots. The solution must not change the administrative rights of the storage administrator user.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative effort**?

options.text: Create an IAM role that has permission to delete snapshots. Attach the role to a new EC2 instance. Use the AWS CLI from the new EC2 instance to delete snapshots.
Create an IAM policy that denies snapshot deletion. Attach the policy to the storage administrator user.
Add tags to the snapshots. Create retention rules in Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots that have the tags.
Lock the EBS snapshots to prevent deletion.

questions.explanation:
Locking an EBS snapshot in Compliance or Governance mode causes the DeleteSnapshot API call itself to be rejected, so deletion is genuinely blocked without touching any IAM permission the storage administrator already holds. Recycle Bin, by contrast, still lets the delete request succeed and only retains the deleted snapshot in a recoverable state for a configured window, which protects against permanent loss but does not itself prevent the deletion from occurring. Locking can also be applied directly (or enforced automatically through a default lock policy) without the added steps of tagging every snapshot and authoring a separate retention rule, making it the lower-effort option too.

**Learn more:** [Lock a snapshot - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-snapshot-lock.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an application on AWS that connects to an Amazon RDS database. The company needs to manage the application configuration and securely store and retrieve credentials for the database and other services.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use AWS Lambda to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use an encrypted application configuration file. Store the file in Amazon S3 for the application configuration. Create another S3 file to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use Amazon RDS to store and retrieve the credentials.

questions.explanation:
AWS AppConfig is a managed service for centralized application configuration, and AWS Secrets Manager is the AWS service specifically intended to securely store, retrieve, and rotate secrets such as database credentials and other service credentials. Using these two managed services avoids building custom storage or management logic and results in the lowest operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS AppConfig?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/what-is-appconfig.html) · [AWS Secrets Manager Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A data analytics company wants to move its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically throughout the day by using FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job requires hours to complete.  
  
The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as quickly as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each file needs to take **3–8 minutes**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST operationally efficient** way?

options.text: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.

Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family is the managed AWS service for FTP-based file ingestion and can store uploaded files directly in Amazon S3, avoiding the operational overhead of running an FTP server on Amazon EC2. Amazon S3 can emit an event notification when each file arrives, enabling near-immediate per-file processing instead of waiting for a nightly batch window. AWS Lambda can run for up to 15 minutes, so it can handle a 3–8 minute processing time for each file and then delete the object after successful completion. Options that use EC2-managed FTP servers are less operationally efficient, and the option that uses Amazon EBS with AWS Transfer Family is not valid because Transfer Family uses Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS as storage backends.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transfer Family?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html) · [Transferring files over a server endpoint using a client - AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/transfer-file.html)

A company runs an online shopping application that stores all orders in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance.  
  
Management wants to remove single points of failure and has asked a solutions architect to recommend a way to minimize database downtime without requiring any application code changes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Convert the existing database instance to a Multi-AZ deployment by modifying the database instance and specifying the Multi-AZ option.
Create a new RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Take a snapshot of the current RDS instance and restore the new Multi-AZ deployment with the snapshot.
Create a read-only replica of the PostgreSQL database in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across the databases.
Place the RDS for PostgreSQL database in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of two. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across instances.

questions.explanation:
An existing Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance can be modified to a Multi-AZ deployment, which creates a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone and provides automatic failover using the same managed RDS setup. Because the existing DB instance is converted rather than replaced at the application layer, this approach minimizes downtime and does not require code changes to handle a new database access pattern. Read replicas are intended for read scaling and do not provide transparent write failover for this use case, and Amazon RDS DB instances are not placed in EC2 Auto Scaling groups.

**Learn more:** [Converting a DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Migrating.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to send its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website becomes unavailable. The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53. The domain currently points to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the traffic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.

Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.

Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.

Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check. Direct traffic to the website if the health check passes. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 failover routing supports active-passive DNS failover, where traffic goes to the primary endpoint while it is healthy and switches to a secondary endpoint when the primary becomes unhealthy. AWS documentation explicitly describes using a primary web resource with a secondary Amazon S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint for this pattern. That matches the need for a backup static error page with minimal additional infrastructure, because the ALB can remain the primary target and the fallback page can be served from S3 instead of adding compute resources.

**Learn more:** [Failover routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html) · [Active-active and active-passive failover - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)

A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift-and-shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.

questions.explanation:
For a lift-and-shift migration that preserves the existing architecture, the storage should remain block storage attached to the compute instance. Amazon EBS is the AWS block storage service for Amazon EC2, so it matches locally attached storage more closely than FSx file systems. Among the general-purpose SSD EBS choices, gp3 is the most cost-effective because AWS states gp3 delivers consistent baseline performance and costs up to 20% less than gp2 while allowing performance to scale independently of capacity.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html) · [Migrate Amazon EBS volumes from gp2 to gp3 - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/optimize-costs-microsoft-workloads/ebs-migrate-gp2-gp3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a workload to store hourly energy consumption for business tenants in a building. Sensors will send HTTP requests to a database that add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services whenever possible. The workload will gain additional features in the future as independent components are added.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.

Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB provide a serverless managed architecture with minimal infrastructure administration. API Gateway can receive HTTP requests, Lambda can process each request, and DynamoDB is a fully managed serverless NoSQL database that scales without instance or database server management. This best matches the requirement to use managed services where possible and supports future growth through independently added components more cleanly than EC2-, EFS-, or self-managed SQL Server-based designs.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create a CRUD HTTP API with Lambda and DynamoDB - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-dynamo-db.html) · [What is Amazon DynamoDB? - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. The workload is not consistent throughout the day. A solutions architect notices that the number of nodes does not automatically scale out when the existing nodes have reached maximum capacity in the cluster, which causes performance issues.  
  
Which solution will resolve this issue with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Scale out the nodes by tracking the memory usage.
Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster automatically.
Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to distribute the workload.

questions.explanation:
The Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler increases or decreases the number of pods, but it does not add cluster nodes when pods cannot be scheduled because the existing nodes are full. In Amazon EKS, the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler is designed to manage node count automatically by detecting unschedulable pods and adjusting the backing node groups, which directly addresses node-capacity shortages with less operational effort than building custom automation. AWS documentation also notes that Amazon EKS does not automatically scale node groups unless you configure Cluster Autoscaler to do so.

**Learn more:** [Scale pod deployments with Horizontal Pod Autoscaler - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/horizontal-pod-autoscaler.html) · [Scale cluster compute with Karpenter and Cluster Autoscaler - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/autoscaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must design a resilient web application that processes customer orders. The web application must automatically accommodate increases in web traffic and application usage without degrading the customer experience or losing customer orders.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a NAT gateway to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive, process, and store processed customer orders. Use an AWS Lambda function to capture and store unprocessed orders.

Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to manage web traffic. Use an Application Load Balancer to receive customer orders from the NLUse Amazon Redshift with a Multi-AZ deployment to store unprocessed and processed customer orders.

Use a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to manage web traffic. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to receive and process customer orders. Use the GWLB to capture and store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store processed customer orders.

Use an Application Load Balancer to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive and process customer orders. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store processed customer orders.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer distributes web traffic across healthy application targets and scales with changing traffic. EC2 Auto Scaling supplies additional order-processing capacity as demand rises. Amazon SQS provides durable, highly available buffering for unprocessed orders, decoupling order intake from processing during spikes, while Amazon RDS Multi-AZ provides high availability and automatic failover for the processed-order database.

**Learn more:** [What is an Application Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html) · [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a web application that uses an embedded NoSQL database. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group within a single Availability Zone.  
  
A recent increase in traffic means the application must be highly available, and the database must be eventually consistent.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

questions.explanation:
High availability for the application tier requires the Auto Scaling group to run across multiple Availability Zones rather than a single Availability Zone. The lowest-operations way to satisfy the database requirement is to move from an embedded, self-managed NoSQL database on EC2 to Amazon DynamoDB, which is a fully managed distributed NoSQL service that automatically replicates data across three Availability Zones in a Region and supports eventually consistent reads. AWS Database Migration Service can be used to migrate data to DynamoDB. Replacing an ALB with a Network Load Balancer does not solve the availability or database-management problem for this web application architecture.

**Learn more:** [Resilience and disaster recovery in Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) · [What is Amazon DynamoDB?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer's application uses an SFTP client to download the files.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead** and **no changes** to the customer's application?

options.text: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that provides SFTP access directly to Amazon S3 and supports authentication through Microsoft Active Directory. That lets the customer keep using the existing SFTP client with no application changes, while avoiding the operational burden of building and maintaining a self-managed SFTP server on Amazon EC2. AWS DMS and AWS DataSync are migration and synchronization services rather than managed SFTP endpoints for client downloads from S3, so they do not meet the requirement as directly or with lower overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transfer Family?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html) · [Create an SFTP-enabled server - AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/create-server-sftp.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to move an on-premises legacy application to AWS. The application receives customer order files from an on-premises enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The application then uploads the files to an SFTP server. The application uses a scheduled job that checks for order files every hour.  
  
The company already has an AWS account with connectivity to the on-premises network. The new application on AWS must support integration with the existing ERP system. The new application must be secure and resilient, and it must use the SFTP protocol to process orders from the ERP system immediately.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internet-facing server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon S3 storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use S3 Event Notifications to send s3:ObjectCreated:* events to the Lambda function.

Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internet-facing server in one Availability Zone. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use a Transfer Family managed workflow to invoke the Lambda function.

Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internal server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to process order files. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke the state machine to periodically check Amazon EFS for order files.

Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP internal server in two Availability Zones. Use Amazon S3 storage. Create an AWS Lambda function to process order files. Use a Transfer Family managed workflow to invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
An internal AWS Transfer Family SFTP server uses private VPC-connected access, which is appropriate when the ERP system reaches AWS over existing private connectivity and the endpoint must be secure. Deploying the endpoint across two Availability Zones improves resiliency. To process files immediately after upload, AWS Transfer Family managed workflows can start automatically on completed uploads and invoke an AWS Lambda function for custom order processing. A scheduled checker does not meet the immediate-processing requirement, an internet-facing endpoint is less aligned with the stated secure private integration need, and a single-AZ design is less resilient.

**Learn more:** [Create a server in a virtual private cloud - AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/create-server-in-vpc.html) · [AWS Transfer Family managed workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/transfer-workflows.html)

A hospital must store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital’s compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted both in transit and at rest, and the compliance team must administer the encryption key used for data at rest.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3. Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.

questions.explanation:
To require encryption in transit for Amazon S3, the bucket policy should use the `aws:SecureTransport` condition so requests are allowed only over HTTPS (TLS). For encryption at rest with customer administration of the key, the bucket should use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) and a customer managed KMS key, because AWS KMS supports customer-managed keys and key-policy administration. SSE-S3 does encrypt data at rest, but its keys are managed by Amazon S3 rather than by the compliance team.

**Learn more:** [Bucket policy examples using condition keys - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/amazon-s3-policy-keys.html) · [Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)

A solutions architect is designing the architecture for a new application that will be deployed to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and will automatically scale across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances will scale in and out frequently during the day. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) will distribute the load. The architecture must support distributed session data management. The company is willing to modify code if necessary.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to make sure the architecture supports distributed session data management?

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache to manage and store session data.
Use session affinity (sticky sessions) of the ALB to manage session data.
Use Session Manager from AWS Systems Manager to manage the session.
Use the GetSessionToken API operation in AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to manage the session.

questions.explanation:
For an application that scales horizontally across multiple Availability Zones and frequently replaces EC2 instances, session state should be externalized from the instances and stored in a shared distributed store. Amazon ElastiCache provides a managed in-memory datastore commonly used for session state, allowing any instance behind the ALB to access the same session data. ALB sticky sessions only pin a user to one target instead of creating shared session storage, and they become fragile when targets are added or removed. Systems Manager Session Manager and AWS STS GetSessionToken are unrelated to application session-state storage.

**Learn more:** [REL05-BP06 Make services stateless where possible - AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-04-10/framework/rel_mitigate_interaction_failure_stateless.html) · [Common ElastiCache Use Cases and How ElastiCache Can Help](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/elasticache-use-cases.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that operates in a single AWS Region. The architecture includes web servers and application servers running on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture also includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that spans multiple Availability Zones.  
  
The company wants to expand globally and ensure that the application has minimal downtime.  
  
Which solution provides the **MOST** fault tolerance?

options.text: Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

questions.explanation:
The most fault-tolerant design is to deploy the web and application tiers in a second AWS Region and use Amazon Aurora global database with a secondary cluster in that Region, then use Amazon Route 53 failover routing with health checks to direct traffic to the secondary Region during a failure. AWS documentation states that an Aurora global database has a primary cluster in one Region and at least one secondary cluster in another Region for cross-Region resilience, and Route 53 failover routing is specifically for active-passive failover. Promoting the secondary Aurora global database cluster to primary during a regional outage provides the best disaster recovery fit among the options.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html) · [Configuration requirements of an Amazon Aurora global database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.configuration.requirements.html)

options.text: Deploy software VPN tunnels between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC.

Deploy VPC peering connections between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC through the peering connection.

Deploy an AWS Direct Connect connection between the application VPCs and the shared services VPAdd routes from the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC and the applications VPCs. Add routes from the shared services VPC subnets to the applications VPCs.

Deploy a transit gateway with associations between the transit gateway and the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets and the application VPCs to the shared services VPC through the transit gateway.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway centrally connects attached VPCs and supports transitive routing among them through transit gateway route tables. This provides scalable any-to-any connectivity between application VPCs and the shared-services VPC without maintaining individual VPN tunnels or a full mesh of VPC peering connections. VPC peering does not support transitive routing.

**Learn more:** [Communicating across VPCs and AWS Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/secure-outbound-network-traffic/vpc-region-communication.html) · [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)

A company has implemented a multi-account strategy on AWS by using AWS Control Tower. The company has assigned individual AWS accounts to each developer. The company wants to put controls in place to limit the AWS resource costs that the developers incur.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Instruct each developer to tag all their resources with a tag that has a key of CostCenter and a value of the developer's name. Use the required-tags AWS Config managed rule to check for the tag. Create an AWS Lambda function to terminate resources that do not have the tag. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending.

Use AWS Budgets to establish budgets for each developer account. Set up budget alerts for actual and forecast values to notify developers when they exceed or expect to exceed their assigned budget. Use AWS Budgets actions to apply a DenyAll policy to the developer's IAM role to prevent additional resources from being launched when the assigned budget is reached.

Use AWS Cost Explorer to monitor and report on costs for each developer account. Configure Cost Explorer to send a daily report to each developer to monitor their spending. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to detect anomalous spending and provide alerts.

Use AWS Service Catalog to allow developers to launch resources within a limited cost range. Create AWS Lambda functions in each AWS account to stop running resources at the end of each work day. Configure the Lambda functions to resume the resources at the start of each work day.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets is designed for account-level cost governance with low operational effort. In this design, each developer already has a separate AWS account, so creating a budget per developer account cleanly maps spend to that developer. AWS Budgets can send notifications on actual and forecasted spend, and budget actions can automatically apply an IAM deny policy or an SCP when a threshold is reached to prevent launching additional resources. That provides both monitoring and automated enforcement without requiring custom tagging enforcement or account-by-account Lambda automation.

**Learn more:** [Configuring budget actions - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-controls.html) · [required-tags - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/required-tags.html)

A company has an on-premises data center that is running out of storage capacity. The company wants to migrate its storage infrastructure to AWS while minimizing bandwidth costs. The solution must allow for immediate retrieval of data at no additional cost.  
  
How can these requirements be met?

options.text: Deploy Amazon S3 Glacier Vault and enable expedited retrieval. Enable provisioned retrieval capacity for the workload.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using cached volumes. Use Storage Gateway to store data in Amazon S3 while retaining copies of frequently accessed data subsets locally.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using stored volumes to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.

Deploy AWS Direct Connect to connect with the on-premises data center. Configure AWS Storage Gateway to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway cached volumes use Amazon S3 as the primary storage location while retaining only frequently accessed data locally in cache. This reduces the amount of on-premises storage required and provides low-latency access to active data. By contrast, stored volumes keep the full dataset on premises and send only snapshots to Amazon S3, so they do not address a local capacity shortfall. Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and related expedited retrieval options are not appropriate because archived objects are not immediately accessible and expedited retrieval is a premium charged feature. Direct Connect would add connection cost and is not required to satisfy the stated bandwidth-cost goal.

**Learn more:** [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html) · [How Volume Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object. The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures.  
  
The company wants to reduce costs and has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense.  
  
Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.
Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.
Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.
Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Lifecycle is the native, lowest-overhead way to manage version retention in a versioning-enabled bucket. A lifecycle rule can expire noncurrent object versions and optionally keep a specified number of newer noncurrent versions, which lets the bucket retain only the most recent versions while automatically deleting older ones. This reduces storage cost without custom code or recurring manual operations.

**Learn more:** [Lifecycle configuration elements - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intro-lifecycle-rules.html) · [Setting an S3 Lifecycle configuration on a bucket - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/how-to-set-lifecycle-configuration-intro.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently set up a disaster recovery site in another AWS Region. The company must transfer large volumes of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a recurring basis.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync.
Use AWS Snowball devices.
Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is a fully managed data transfer service optimized for moving large amounts of data between NFS file systems in different AWS Regions. DataSync handles data validation, retry logic, and scheduling automatically with minimal setup, making it far more operationally efficient than building a custom EC2-based transfer solution or using offline Snowball devices for recurring transfers.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS DataSync?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html)
