A company wants to transition from many standalone AWS accounts to a consolidated, multi-account architecture. The company plans to create many new AWS accounts for different business units. The company must authenticate access to these AWS accounts by using a centralized corporate directory service.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on. Create the new AWS accounts in the organization.
Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to accept Amazon Cognito authentication.
Configure a service control policy (SCP) to manage the AWS accounts. Add AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to AWS Directory Service.
Create a new organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the organization's authentication mechanism to use AWS Directory Service directly.
Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the organization. Configure IAM Identity Center, and integrate it with the company's corporate directory service.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations is the correct service to create and centrally manage multiple AWS accounts in a multi-account architecture, and using all features supports the advanced organization capabilities typically required for governance at scale. AWS IAM Identity Center is the AWS service designed to provide centralized workforce access across accounts in an organization, and it can integrate with a corporate directory such as Active Directory or an external identity provider so users authenticate with existing corporate credentials.

**Learn more:** [Creating an organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_org_create.html) · [Creating a member account in an organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has AWS Lambda functions that use environment variables. The company does not want its developers to view the environment variables in plaintext.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Deploy code to Amazon EC2 instances instead of using Lambda functions.
Configure SSL encryption on the Lambda functions to use AWS CloudHSM to store and encrypt the environment variables.
Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Configure the Lambda functions to use the certificate to encrypt the environment variables.
Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable encryption helpers on the Lambda functions to use the KMS key to store and encrypt the environment variables.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda secures environment variables by using AWS KMS for encryption, and AWS documents that a customer managed KMS key can be used so only principals with the appropriate KMS permissions can view or manage the variables. AWS also provides encryption helpers for Lambda environment variables, which use the KMS key for additional client-side/in-transit protection. This is the AWS-native way to prevent developers from seeing the values in plaintext in the Lambda console.

**Learn more:** [Securing Lambda environment variables - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-envvars-encryption.html) · [Working with Lambda environment variables - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-envvars.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's website offers users downloadable historical performance reports.  
  
The website requires a solution that:  
  
- scales globally to meet the company's website demand,  
- is cost-effective,  
- limits the provisioning of infrastructure resources, and  
- provides the fastest possible response time.  
  
Which combination should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB
Application Load Balancer with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
Amazon Route 53 with internal Application Load Balancers

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is a low-cost, fully managed service for storing and serving downloadable static content such as historical reports, and Amazon CloudFront distributes that content through global edge locations to provide low-latency, high-performance delivery. This combination scales worldwide without managing servers and reduces infrastructure provisioning, making it the best fit for cost-effective global delivery of downloadable files.

**Learn more:** [Amazon CloudFront Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/) · [Use Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/getting-started/s3/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a multiplayer game for mobile devices. The game requires live location tracking of players based on latitude and longitude. The data store for the game must support rapid updates and retrieval of locations.  
  
The game uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas to store the location data. During peak usage periods, the database is unable to maintain the performance that is needed for reading and writing updates. The game's user base is increasing rapidly.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to improve the performance of the data tier?

options.text: Take a snapshot of the existing DB instance. Restore the snapshot with Multi-AZ enabled.
Migrate from Amazon RDS to Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards.
Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use DAX.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use Redis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is the best fit because Redis is an in-memory data store that supports native geospatial operations, allowing very low-latency writes and reads for player coordinates at scale. That makes it well suited for rapidly changing latitude/longitude data in a multiplayer game. Multi-AZ on Amazon RDS improves availability rather than database performance, and DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cannot be used with Amazon RDS because it is a cache specifically for DynamoDB. AWS documentation shows that ElastiCache for Redis supports geospatial commands such as GEOADD, GEOPOS, GEORADIUS, and GEOSEARCH, which directly match this workload.

**Learn more:** [Supported and restricted Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS commands - Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/SupportedCommands.html) · [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has multiple AWS accounts with applications deployed in the `us-west-2` Region. Application logs are stored in Amazon S3 buckets in each account. The company wants to create a centralized log analysis solution that uses a single S3 bucket. Logs must not leave `us-west-2`, and the company wants to keep operational overhead to a minimum.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements and is **MOST cost-effective**?

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy that copies the objects from one of the application S3 buckets to the centralized S3 bucket.
Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate logs from the S3 buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
Write a script that uses the PutObject API operation every day to copy the entire contents of the buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.

Write AWS Lambda functions in these accounts that are triggered every time logs are delivered to the S3 buckets (s3:ObjectCreated:* event). Copy the logs to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) automatically replicates objects between S3 buckets in the same AWS Region, including across different AWS accounts. That makes it the native managed way to aggregate logs into one bucket while ensuring the data stays in `us-west-2` and avoiding custom scripts or Lambda functions. S3 Lifecycle rules are for transitioning or expiring objects, not continuously copying objects into another bucket for centralized analysis.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Lifecycle configuration elements - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intro-lifecycle-rules.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate its MySQL database from on premises to AWS. The company recently experienced a database outage that had a significant business impact. To help ensure this does not happen again, the company needs a dependable database solution on AWS that minimizes data loss and stores every transaction on at least two nodes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with synchronous replication to three nodes in three Availability Zones.
Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance with Multi-AZ functionality enabled to synchronously replicate the data.
Create an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance and then create a read replica in a separate AWS Region that synchronously replicates the data.
Create an Amazon EC2 instance with a MySQL engine installed that triggers an AWS Lambda function to synchronously replicate the data to an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled is the managed high-availability option that uses synchronous replication to maintain a standby replica in a different Availability Zone. Because writes are synchronously replicated to the standby, committed transactions are stored on both the primary and standby nodes, which minimizes data loss and supports automatic failover during an outage. Read replicas do not meet this requirement because they use asynchronous replication, and an EC2-plus-Lambda design does not provide the same managed transactional high-availability behavior.

**Learn more:** [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html) · [Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company uses a Regional Amazon API Gateway API for its public REST APIs. The API Gateway endpoint uses a custom domain name that points to an Amazon Route 53 alias record. A solutions architect must create a solution that will have minimal impact on customers and minimal data loss when releasing a new version of the APIs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a canary release deployment stage for API Gateway. Deploy the latest API version. Point an appropriate percentage of traffic to the canary stage. After API verification, promote the canary stage to the production stage.

Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI YAML file format. Use the import-to-update operation in merge mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.

Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI JSON file format. Use the import-to-update operation in overwrite mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.

questions.explanation:
An API Gateway canary release deployment lets the production stage keep serving the current API version while a configurable percentage of requests is routed to the new deployment. That enables controlled validation, fast rollback, and promotion to full production without changing the custom domain name or Route 53 alias target. AWS documentation also distinguishes canary release from OpenAPI import update modes such as merge and overwrite, which update the API definition rather than perform a gradual production traffic shift.

A company uses an Amazon S3 bucket as the storage platform for its data lake. The S3 bucket holds a massive volume of data that is accessed randomly by multiple teams and hundreds of applications. The company wants to lower S3 storage costs while providing immediate availability for frequently accessed objects.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.
Store objects in Amazon S3 Glacier. Use S3 Select to provide applications with access to the data.
Use data from S3 storage class analysis to create S3 Lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class.

Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an AWS Lambda function to transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class when they are accessed by an application.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the best fit for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns. It automatically monitors object access and moves objects to lower-cost access tiers when they become less frequently used, while keeping low-latency, immediate access for frequently accessed data. If an object is accessed after being moved down, Amazon S3 automatically returns it to the Frequent Access tier, which satisfies the requirement without custom code or ongoing manual tuning. AWS documentation also identifies S3 Intelligent-Tiering as appropriate for unpredictable access patterns, whereas S3 Standard-IA is for less frequently accessed data and Glacier classes are for archive-style access rather than general immediate availability.

**Learn more:** [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html) · [Managing storage costs with Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a two-tier web application on AWS. The developers have deployed the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that connects directly to a backend Amazon RDS database.  
  
The company must not hardcode database credentials in the application. The company also must implement a solution that automatically rotates the database credentials on a regular basis.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.

Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.
Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.

Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the AWS service designed to store database credentials securely, let applications retrieve them dynamically at runtime instead of hardcoding them, and automatically rotate those credentials for Amazon RDS on a schedule. Granting the EC2 instance role permission to read the secret satisfies secure access without embedding credentials in code. This has less operational overhead than building a custom EventBridge and Lambda rotation process, and Parameter Store is not the recommended service for credentials that require automatic rotation.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)

A company must design a hybrid network architecture. Its workloads currently reside in the AWS Cloud and in on-premises data centers. The workloads need single-digit latency for communication. The company uses an AWS Transit Gateway transit gateway to connect multiple VPCs.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way? (Choose two.)

options.text: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to each VPC.
Associate an AWS Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to an AWS Direct Connect gateway.
Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection. Create a transit virtual interface (VIF) to a Direct Connect gateway.
Associate AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated hybrid connectivity suitable for low-latency communication. A Direct Connect gateway can be associated with a Transit Gateway that has multiple VPC attachments, and a transit virtual interface connects the Direct Connect connection to that Direct Connect gateway. This lets one Direct Connect connection provide on-premises connectivity to the VPCs attached to the Transit Gateway.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro.html) · [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a custom application that contains embedded credentials and retrieves information from an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance.  
  
Management states that the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager is the correct service for replacing hardcoded database credentials because it is designed to store, retrieve, and rotate secrets such as Amazon RDS credentials. For RDS MySQL, Secrets Manager supports setting a rotation schedule so the application can read the credentials from Secrets Manager instead of embedding them in code, improving security with minimal custom development. Using AWS KMS alone does not provide application credential storage and retrieval, and Systems Manager Parameter Store is not the preferred service when automatic credential rotation is required.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)

Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is the best fit for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns. It automatically monitors object access and moves objects to lower-cost access tiers when they become less frequently used, while keeping low-latency, immediate access for frequently accessed data. If an object is accessed after being moved down, Amazon S3 automatically returns it to the Frequent Access tier, which satisfies the requirement without custom code or ongoing manual tuning. AWS documentation also identifies S3 Intelligent-Tiering as appropriate for unpredictable access patterns, whereas S3 Standard-IA is for less frequently accessed data and Glacier classes are for archive-style access rather than general immediate availability.

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company must not hardcode database credentials in the application. The company also must implement a solution that automatically rotates the database credentials on a regular basis."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution will meet these requirements with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST operational overhead"}],"?"]}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.","B":"Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.","C":"Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.","D":"Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"AWS Secrets Manager is the AWS service designed to store database credentials securely, let applications retrieve them dynamically at runtime instead of hardcoding them, and automatically rotate those credentials for Amazon RDS on a schedule. Granting the EC2 instance role permission to read the secret satisfies secure access without embedding credentials in code. This has less operational overhead than building a custom EventBridge and Lambda rotation process, and Parameter Store is not the recommended service for credentials that require automatic rotation.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"3e954b89-1c95-42fd-975a-7207b8e3f327","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]

Create a transit virtual interface (VIF) to a Direct Connect gateway.","E":"Associate AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs."},"correctAnswer":"BD","explanation":"AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated hybrid connectivity suitable for low-latency communication. 53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has a custom application that contains embedded credentials and retrieves information from an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Management states that the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation.","B":"Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.","C":"Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.","D":"Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"AWS Secrets Manager is the correct service for replacing hardcoded database credentials because it is designed to store, retrieve, and rotate secrets such as Amazon RDS credentials. For RDS MySQL, Secrets Manager supports setting a rotation schedule so the application can read the credentials from Secrets Manager instead of embedding them in code, improving security with minimal custom development. Using AWS KMS alone does not provide application credential storage and retrieval, and Systems Manager Parameter Store is not the preferred service when automatic credential rotation is required.

A company is moving applications to AWS. The applications are deployed in different accounts. The company centrally manages the accounts by using AWS Organizations. The company's security team needs a single sign-on (SSO) solution across all the company's accounts. The company must continue to manage users and groups in its on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a one-way forest trust or a one-way domain trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.

Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a two-way forest trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
Use AWS Directory Service. Create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on premises. Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console.

questions.explanation:
AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS Single Sign-On) is the AWS service designed to provide centralized SSO across AWS accounts in an organization. When the identity source remains an on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory, IAM Identity Center integrates through AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory and requires a **two-way forest trust** so it can authenticate users and synchronize user and group metadata from the on-premises directory. One-way trust is explicitly insufficient for IAM Identity Center, and AWS Directory Service by itself does not deliver the required cross-account SSO experience.

**Learn more:** [Connect a self-managed directory in Active Directory to IAM Identity Center](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/connectonpremad.html) · [AWS IAM Identity Center and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-and-orgs.html)

An ecommerce company is moving its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently includes a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage.  
  
The company anticipates a high volume of customers during a promotional event. The new AWS Cloud infrastructure must be highly available and scalable.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.

Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.

Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.

Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
Running the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer provides elasticity and high availability for traffic spikes. For the Microsoft SQL Server database, Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment is the managed high-availability option: AWS maintains a synchronous standby and performs automatic failover without the operational overhead of managing SQL Server replication and failover on EC2 yourself. This combination satisfies scalability, availability, and minimum administration better than the alternatives.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Set up a scaled and load-balanced application - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/tutorial-ec2-auto-scaling-load-balancer.html) · [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling? - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html)

A company has a business-critical application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must be able to restore the table to any point in time during the last 24 hours.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure point-in-time recovery for the table.
Use AWS Backup for the table.
Use an AWS Lambda function to make an on-demand backup of the table every hour.
Turn on streams on the table to capture a log of all changes to the table in the last 24 hours. Store a copy of the stream in an Amazon S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) continuously protects the table and lets you restore it to a specific second within the recovery window, which can cover the last 24 hours and up to 35 days. It is fully managed by DynamoDB, so there is no need to build backup schedules, Lambda automation, or change-log processing. Hourly on-demand backups do not satisfy an any-point-in-time requirement, and DynamoDB Streams capture changes but are not a direct point-in-time table recovery solution.

**Learn more:** [Backup and restore for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Backup-and-Restore.html) · [Restore a table in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/pointintimerecovery_restores.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company maintains an Amazon RDS database that maps users to cost centers. The company has accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
The company needs a solution to tag all resources that are created in a specific AWS account in the organization. The solution must tag each resource with the cost center ID of the user who created the resource.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Move the specific AWS account to a new organizational unit (OU) in Organizations from the management account. Create a service control policy (SCP) that requires all existing resources to have the correct cost center tag before the resources are created. Apply the SCP to the new OU.

Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources after the Lambda function looks up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function.

Create an AWS CloudFormation stack to deploy an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to look up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database and to tag resources. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the CloudFormation stack.

Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources with a default value. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function when a resource is missing the cost center tag.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge can create rules that react to AWS API calls recorded by AWS CloudTrail, and those rules can invoke an AWS Lambda function. A Lambda function can read the creator identity from the CloudTrail event, look up that user's cost center in the Amazon RDS mapping database, and then call the appropriate tagging APIs for the newly created resource. SCPs in AWS Organizations only define permission guardrails and do not perform dynamic lookups or apply tags, and a scheduled CloudFormation-based approach would not tag resources at creation time. A default-value tagging approach also fails because the requirement is to use the specific creator's cost center ID.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create an EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS API calls via CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-log-api-call.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

A company wants to securely exchange data between its software as a service (SaaS) application Salesforce account and Amazon S3.  
  
The company must:  
  
- encrypt the data at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs)  
- also encrypt the data in transit  
  
The company has enabled API access for the Salesforce account.

options.text: Create AWS Lambda functions to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Define the task to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
Create Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
Create a custom connector for Salesforce to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon AppFlow is the managed AWS service built for transferring data between SaaS applications such as Salesforce and AWS services such as Amazon S3. It supports Salesforce as a source, Amazon S3 as a destination, encryption in transit with TLS, and encryption at rest with AWS KMS, including customer managed keys for data written to S3. Because Salesforce is already a supported native connector, no custom connector, Lambda function, or Step Functions workflow is required.

**Learn more:** [Data protection in Amazon AppFlow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/data-protection.html) · [Salesforce connector for Amazon AppFlow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/salesforce.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to store data in Amazon S3 and must ensure that the data cannot be modified.  
  
The company wants newly uploaded Amazon S3 objects to stay immutable for an unspecified length of time until the company chooses to modify the objects.  
  
Only designated users in the company's AWS account can have permission to delete the objects.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an S3 Glacier vault. Apply a write-once, read-many (WORM) vault lock policy to the objects.
Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Set a retention period of 100 years. Use governance mode as the S3 bucket’s default retention mode for new objects.
Create an S3 bucket. Use AWS CloudTrail to track any S3 API events that modify the objects. Upon notification, restore the modified objects from any backup versions that the company has.

Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Add a legal hold to the objects. Add the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission to the IAM policies of users who need to delete the objects.

questions.explanation:
S3 Object Lock with legal hold is the correct choice for undefined duration immutability. A legal hold prevents an object from being overwritten or deleted and has no associated retention period—it persists until explicitly removed. Governance mode retention requires a fixed retention period, which does not match the requirement for an unspecified length of time. Only users with s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission can remove the legal hold.

**Learn more:** [Locking objects with S3 Object Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html) · [PutObjectLegalHold API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_PutObjectLegalHold.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a multi-tier web application on Amazon Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The company notices that the Auto Scaling group launches additional On-Demand Instances when the application's end users request large volumes of static web content. The company wants to optimize cost.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to redesign the application **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Update the Auto Scaling group to use Reserved Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
Update the Auto Scaling group to scale by launching Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to host the static web contents from an Amazon S3 bucket.
Create an AWS Lambda function behind an Amazon API Gateway API to host the static website contents.

questions.explanation:
Static web assets should be separated from the EC2 application tier and served from Amazon S3 through Amazon CloudFront. AWS guidance recommends using an S3 bucket as the origin with CloudFront to distribute static content, and CloudFront caching reduces requests that reach the origin. That offloads static-content traffic from the Auto Scaling group so the company does not need to launch extra On-Demand Instances just to serve files such as images, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Reserved Instances and Spot Instances still keep static delivery on EC2, while API Gateway plus Lambda is not the standard low-cost architecture for static website hosting.

**Learn more:** [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html) · [Ways to use CloudFront - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/IntroductionUseCases.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for its Amazon EC2 instances that have an SMB file share mounted as a volume in the `us-east-1` Region.  
  
The company has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes for planned system maintenance or unplanned service disruptions. The company must replicate the file system to the `us-west-2` Region. The replicated data must not be deletable by any user for 5 years.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ is the correct deployment type because it provides automatic failover for planned maintenance and unplanned service disruptions, typically in less than 30 seconds, whereas Single-AZ deployments are for workloads that can tolerate up to 20 minutes of unavailability and possible data loss since the last backup. Replication to another Region can be achieved by copying FSx backups to `us-west-2` with AWS Backup. To ensure no user can delete the replicated backup data for 5 years, the destination backup vault must use AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode, because compliance mode makes the vault and its recovery points immutable for the retention period, while governance mode can still be changed or deleted by users with sufficient permissions.

**Learn more:** [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html) · [Protecting your data with backups - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/using-backups.html)

A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Based on the application's history, the company expects a traffic spike during a holiday each year. A solutions architect must design a strategy to make sure that the Auto Scaling group increases capacity proactively to minimize any performance effect on application users.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale up the EC2 instances when CPU utilization exceeds 90%.
Create a recurring scheduled action to scale up the Auto Scaling group before the expected period of peak demand.
Increase the minimum and maximum number of EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group during the peak demand period.
Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to send alerts when there are autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH events.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled actions are designed for predictable load changes. When demand is known in advance—such as an annual holiday spike—a recurring scheduled action can increase the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity before the surge begins, so instances are already available when traffic arrives. CloudWatch alarm scaling is reactive, SNS notifications do not add capacity, and merely stating higher minimum and maximum values without a scheduled scaling mechanism does not ensure the change occurs at the correct time.

**Learn more:** [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Create a scheduled action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scheduled-scaling-create-scheduled-action.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). The EC2 instances use the latest Amazon Linux release. The applications are having availability problems when the company's employees store and retrieve files that are **25 GB or larger**.  
  
The company needs a solution that does **not** require transferring files between EC2 instances. The files must be available:  
  
- across many EC2 instances, and  
- across multiple Availability Zones.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate all the files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the employees to access the files from the S3 bucket.
Take a snapshot of the existing EBS volume. Mount the snapshot as an EBS volume across the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system across all the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instances. Configure new EC2 instances from the AMI that use an instance store volume. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is the correct choice because it provides a shared, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple EC2 instances, and it is designed for regional availability across multiple Availability Zones. Amazon EBS volumes are attached within a single Availability Zone, and even Multi-Attach does not satisfy a multi-AZ shared-file requirement. Instance store volumes are ephemeral and are not shared storage. Although Amazon S3 can hold large objects, the requirement is for files to be available directly across many EC2 instances without moving them between instances, which is the standard EFS use case for shared file storage on EC2.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon EFS works - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html) · [Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach - Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html)

A company must store data from its healthcare application. The application's data changes frequently. A new regulation now requires audit access at every level of the stored data.  
  
The company runs the application on on-premises infrastructure that is running out of storage capacity. A solutions architect must securely migrate the existing data to AWS while meeting the new regulation.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
Use AWS Snowcone to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
Use AWS Storage Gateway to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is designed to transfer data from on-premises storage systems to Amazon S3 and supports repeated synchronization for data that changes frequently. For auditing S3 at the stored-data level, AWS CloudTrail data events are required because they record S3 object-level API activity such as `GetObject`, `PutObject`, and `DeleteObject`. CloudTrail management events log bucket- or account-level control plane actions, not object-level access, so they would not satisfy the audit requirement at all levels of the stored data.

**Learn more:** [Transferring to or from on-premises storage with AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/transferring-on-premises-storage.html) · [Understanding CloudTrail events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-events.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A security audit reveals that Amazon EC2 instances are not being patched regularly. A solutions architect must provide a solution that will run regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances. The solution must also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a report of each instance's patch status.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.

Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Inspector is the AWS service for automated vulnerability management on Amazon EC2, including detecting software vulnerabilities on instances. AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager can scan and install patches on a schedule for large fleets of managed instances, and Patch Manager/Systems Manager Compliance provides per-instance patch compliance and reporting. That combination satisfies all three requirements: regular security scans, scheduled patching, and instance patch-status reports.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Amazon Inspector findings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/findings-understanding.html) · [Working with patch compliance reports - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-compliance-reports.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a REST API. The company has strict TLS requirements for the API.  
  
The company requires:  
  
- TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints  
- the TLS certificate to be signed by a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA)  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CImport the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.

Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.

Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

questions.explanation:
AWS Certificate Manager cannot request certificates from customer-specified third-party CAs; it can only issue certificates from Amazon's CA or import existing certificates. To use a third-party CA certificate, import it into ACM first. Amazon API Gateway REST APIs support TLS 1.3 security policies on custom domain names. Lambda function URLs do not support custom certificate configuration or TLS 1.3 enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Choose a security policy for your custom domain in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-custom-domain-tls-version.html) · [Get certificates ready in AWS Certificate Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-specify-certificate-for-custom-domain-name.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances, and the company must encrypt the data at rest.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS encryption at rest uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). When you create or configure an encrypted RDS DB instance, you enable storage encryption and use either the AWS managed RDS KMS key or a customer managed KMS key. SSL/TLS certificates from ACM or IAM protect data in transit, not data at rest, and AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets rather than serving as the key mechanism for RDS storage encryption. Official AWS documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.Keys.html

**Learn more:** [Encrypting Amazon RDS resources - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.html) · [AWS KMS key management - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Encryption.Keys.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an asynchronous API that ingests user requests and, depending on the request type, routes the requests to the correct microservice for processing. The company uses Amazon API Gateway to host the API frontend, and an AWS Lambda function that calls Amazon DynamoDB to save user requests before sending them to the processing microservices.  
  
The company has provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget permits, but it is still encountering availability problems and is losing user requests.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to solve this issue **without affecting existing users**?

options.text: Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.
Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.
Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS should be used as a durable buffer between the API/Lambda ingestion layer and DynamoDB. An SQS queue decouples components and absorbs traffic spikes so incoming requests are retained even when DynamoDB writes cannot keep up immediately. Lambda can poll SQS and process messages asynchronously with retries and backoff, which improves availability and prevents dropped requests. API Gateway throttling would cause client-visible throttling, DAX is a write-through cache for DynamoDB rather than a write buffer and is not suited to write-heavy buffering, and adding a secondary index does not address the lost-request problem.

**Learn more:** [Creating event-driven architectures with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/concepts-event-driven-architectures.html) · [How Lambda processes records from stream and queue-based event sources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-eventsourcemapping.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is extending a secure on-premises network into the AWS Cloud by using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The on-premises network does not have direct internet access. An application running on the on-premises network must use an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create a public virtual interface (VIF). Route the AWS traffic over the public VIF.
Create a VPC and a NAT gateway. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the NAT gateway.
Create a VPC and an Amazon S3 interface endpoint. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the S3 interface endpoint.
Create a VPC peering connection between the on-premises network and Direct Connect. Route the AWS traffic over the peering connection.

questions.explanation:
A public virtual interface on AWS Direct Connect is designed to access AWS public services, including Amazon S3, over the Direct Connect connection without using direct internet access through an ISP. That makes it the simplest and lowest-cost option here. An S3 interface endpoint can also enable on-premises access through Direct Connect, but it requires a VPC and AWS PrivateLink charges, so it is typically less cost-effective for this requirement. A NAT gateway is unrelated to providing Direct Connect access from on premises to S3, and VPC peering cannot connect an on-premises network to Direct Connect.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html) · [What is Direct Connect? - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to use its on-premises LDAP directory service to authenticate its users to the AWS Management Console. The directory service is not compatible with Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML).  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) between AWS and the on-premises LDAP.
Create an IAM policy that uses AWS credentials, and integrate the policy into LDAP.
Set up a process that rotates the IAM credentials whenever LDAP credentials are updated.
Develop an on-premises custom identity broker application or process that uses AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to get short-lived credentials.

questions.explanation:
When the on-premises directory is not SAML-compatible, AWS recommends identity federation through a custom identity broker. The broker authenticates the user against the existing LDAP-based directory, then uses AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to obtain short-lived AWS credentials for console access. This matches AWS guidance for non-SAML identity stores and avoids using long-term IAM user credentials.

**Learn more:** [Access to externally authenticated users (identity federation)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_federated-users.html) · [Enable custom identity broker access to the AWS console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_enable-console-custom-url.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has migrated millions of archival files to Amazon S3. A solutions architect must implement a solution to encrypt all the archival data by using a customer-provided key. The solution needs to encrypt both existing unencrypted objects and future objects.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering an Amazon S3 Inventory report. Configure an S3 Batch Operations job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).
Use S3 Storage Lens metrics to identify unencrypted S3 buckets. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Batch job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Inventory reports include encryption status for each object; filtering this report identifies unencrypted objects. S3 Batch Operations can encrypt those objects in bulk with SSE-C. Configuring S3 default encryption completes the solution for future uploads, though default encryption technically does not support SSE-C. This approach addresses both existing and future encryption requirements within the constraints of available options.

**Learn more:** [Using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ServerSideEncryptionCustomerKeys.html) · [Amazon S3 Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-inventory.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a new service behind Amazon API Gateway.  
  
The service's request patterns will be unpredictable and can suddenly shift from 0 requests to more than 500 per second.  
  
The total amount of data that must be persisted in a backend database is currently less than 1 GB, with unpredictable future growth.  
  
Data can be queried by using simple key-value requests.  
  
Which combination of AWS services would satisfy these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: AWS Fargate
AWS Lambda
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the best compute choice because it integrates directly with Amazon API Gateway and automatically scales in response to sudden changes in request volume. Amazon DynamoDB is the best database choice because it is a serverless key-value NoSQL database that supports simple key-based access patterns and automatically scales for unpredictable traffic and data growth. This combination matches a bursty API workload while minimizing operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Lambda scaling behavior - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html) · [Get started with API Gateway - Amazon API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/getting-started.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs several Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares synchronize data with each other and keep duplicate copies.  
  
The company wants a storage solution that is highly available and durable while preserving the way users currently access the files.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the managed AWS service designed for Windows shared file storage. It provides native SMB access, Microsoft Active Directory integration, and Windows ACL support, so users can continue accessing files as Windows file shares. A Multi-AZ deployment is specifically recommended for production workloads that require high availability for shared Windows file data, making it the correct replacement for duplicated EC2-based Windows file servers.

**Learn more:** [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html)

options.text: Send Amazon CloudWatch logs to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon QuickS ght to perform further analysis.
Enable detailed monitoring on all EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
Create an AWS Lambda function to fetch EC2 logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
Send EC2 logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift to fetch logs from the S3 bucket to process raw data for further analysis with Amazon QuickSight.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring publishes CloudWatch metrics at 1-minute intervals, whereas basic monitoring provides most EC2 metrics every 5 minutes. One-minute CloudWatch metrics meet a maximum 2-minute analysis granularity.

**Learn more:** [Manage detailed monitoring for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/manage-detailed-monitoring.html) · [Basic and detailed monitoring in Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch-metrics-basic-detailed.html)

A company runs a photo hosting service in the `us-east-1` Region. The service allows users in multiple countries to upload and view photos. Some photos receive heavy views for months, while others are viewed for less than a week. The application supports uploads of up to `20 MB` per photo. The service uses photo metadata to decide which photos to show to each user.  
  
Which solution provides the appropriate user access in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Store the photos in Amazon DynamoDB. Turn on DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache frequently viewed items.
Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Store the photo metadata and its S3 location in DynamoDB.

Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to move photos older than 30 days to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Use the object tags to keep track of metadata.

Store the photos in the Amazon S3 Glacier storage class. Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to move photos older than 30 days to the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. Store the photo metadata and its S3 location in Amazon OpenSearch Service.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the correct place to store 20 MB photo objects because DynamoDB has a 400 KB item limit. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is intended for data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns and automatically shifts objects to the most cost-efficient access tier based on actual access, which fits photos that may be hot for months or only briefly viewed. Storing the photo metadata and S3 object location in DynamoDB is appropriate because the application uses metadata to determine which photos to display, and DynamoDB is well suited for low-latency key-value metadata lookups. An age-based lifecycle rule to Standard-IA is less accurate for this pattern, and Glacier classes do not provide the immediate access expected for an active photo hosting service.

**Learn more:** [Constraints in Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Constraints.html) · [Best practices for storing large items and attributes in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-use-s3-too.html)

A company gathers and distributes research data to the company's employees around the world. The company wants to collect and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket and process the data in the AWS Cloud. The company will share the data with the company's employees. The company needs a secure solution in the AWS Cloud that minimizes operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to create an S3 presigned URL. Instruct employees to use the URL.
Create an IAM user for each employee. Create an IAM policy for each employee to allow S3 access. Instruct employees to use the AWS Management Console.
Create an S3 File Gateway. Create a share for uploading and a share for downloading. Allow employees to mount shares on their local computers to use S3 File Gateway.
Configure AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints. Select the custom identity provider options. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the user credentials Instruct employees to use Transfer Family.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service for secure file transfer directly into and out of Amazon S3, making it a strong fit when employees need global access to shared data without requiring AWS Management Console access or individually managed IAM users. Using SFTP endpoints with a custom identity provider allows centralized authentication and authorization, and AWS documentation supports custom identity provider patterns for enterprise user management. This approach delivers secure access to S3-backed data while keeping the operational burden lower than managing IAM users per employee or deploying file gateway infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Configuring an SFTP, FTPS, or FTP server endpoint - AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/sftp-for-transfer-family.html) · [Working with custom identity providers - AWS Transfer Family](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/custom-idp-intro.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's dynamic website is hosted on on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe and wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product will launch in a few days, so an immediate solution is required.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.
Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is the correct choice because it can front a dynamic website with a custom origin that points to on-premises servers, while using its global edge network to reduce latency for users in Europe. This satisfies the requirement to keep the backend in the United States and provides a fast-to-deploy performance improvement. Route 53 geoproximity routing only affects which endpoint DNS resolves to and does not itself accelerate delivery, and Amazon S3 with Cross-Region Replication is for replicated static object content rather than an on-premises dynamic backend.

**Learn more:** [Use various origins with CloudFront distributions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistS3AndCustomOrigins.html) · [Origin - Amazon CloudFront API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_Origin.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company needs a secure way to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS integrates with AWS Secrets Manager to manage the master user password securely and automate credential rotation, which minimizes operational effort compared with building a custom Lambda-based rotation process or performing manual CLI updates. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store can store encrypted values, but it does not provide the same built-in secret rotation and database credential lifecycle management that RDS and Secrets Manager provide together.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [Rotation schedules - AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_schedule.html)

A company needs a backup strategy for its three-tier stateless web application. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a dynamic scaling policy that responds to scaling events. The database tier runs on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The web application does not need temporary local storage on the EC2 instances. The company’s recovery point objective (RPO) is 2 hours.  
  
The backup strategy must maximize scalability and optimize resource utilization for this environment.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances and database every 2 hours to meet the RPO.
Configure a snapshot lifecycle policy to take Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS to meet the RPO.
Retain the latest Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the web and application tiers. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.
Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances every 2 hours. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.

questions.explanation:
For stateless EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group, the scalable and resource-efficient approach is to recreate instances from a standardized image instead of taking frequent EBS snapshots of ephemeral fleet members. Because the application does not rely on local instance storage, retaining current AMIs for the web and application tiers is sufficient for rebuilding capacity. For Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, automated backups provide point-in-time recovery, which is the appropriate mechanism to meet a 2-hour RPO because the database can be restored to a specific time within the backup retention period. AWS documents that RDS automated backups support point-in-time recovery, and that EC2 Auto Scaling is intended for automatically scaling fleets of instances rather than preserving each instance as unique state.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to backups - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html) · [Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIT.html)

A company operates a publicly accessible serverless application that uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The application's traffic has recently increased because of fraudulent requests from botnets.  
  
Which steps should a solutions architect take to block requests from unauthorized users? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create a usage plan with an API key that is shared with genuine users only.
Integrate logic within the Lambda function to ignore the requests from fraudulent IP addresses.
Implement an AWS WAF rule to target malicious requests and trigger actions to filter them out.
Convert the existing public API to a private API. Update the DNS records to redirect users to the new API endpoint.
Create an IAM role for each user attempting to access the API. A user will assume the role when making the API call.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF can be attached to Amazon API Gateway to identify and filter malicious web requests, making it the correct control for blocking botnet-style traffic. API Gateway can also require an API key on methods associated with a usage plan, so callers without a valid key receive a 403 response, which blocks unauthorized access in this scenario. Adding logic inside Lambda only ignores requests after they already reached the function, converting the API to private would prevent normal public access, and creating a separate IAM role for each user is not an appropriate design for a public API endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html) · [Choose an API key source in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-key-source.html)
