A company wants to migrate **100 GB of historical data** from an on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has a **100 megabits per second (Mbps)** internet connection on premises. The company needs to **encrypt the data in transit** to the S3 bucket. The company will store new data directly in Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use the s3 sync command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the on-premises location to an S3 bucket
Use AWS Snowball to move the data to an S3 bucket
Set up an IPsec VPN from the on-premises location to AWS. Use the s3 cp command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is the managed service purpose-built for moving data from on-premises storage to Amazon S3, and it encrypts transfer traffic in transit. For only 100 GB over an existing 100 Mbps connection, an online transfer is practical, so AWS Snowball would be unnecessary extra effort. Creating an IPsec VPN is also unnecessary because uploads to Amazon S3 already use HTTPS/TLS for encryption in transit. Compared with manually running AWS CLI copy or sync commands, DataSync provides the migration capability with less ongoing setup and management overhead.

**Learn more:** [AWS DataSync encryption in transit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/encryption-in-transit.html) · [Protecting data in transit with encryption - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingEncryptionInTransit.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Salesforce. The company must load existing data and ongoing data changes from Salesforce into Amazon Redshift for analysis. The company does not want the data to traverse the public internet.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST** development effort?

options.text: Establish a VPN connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection from the VPC to Salesforce. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to transfer data.
Create an AWS PrivateLink connection in the VPC to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.
Create a VPC peering connection to Salesforce. Use Amazon AppFlow to transfer data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon AppFlow is the managed AWS service designed to transfer data between SaaS applications such as Salesforce and AWS destinations such as Amazon Redshift with minimal or no custom code. For the private-network requirement, Amazon AppFlow supports private flows that use AWS PrivateLink, and Salesforce is one of the supported SaaS applications for that private connectivity model. That combination satisfies both the ongoing synchronization requirement and the requirement to avoid public internet transit with the least development effort.

**Learn more:** [Private Amazon AppFlow flows - Amazon AppFlow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/private-flows.html) · [Salesforce connector for Amazon AppFlow - Amazon AppFlow](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appflow/latest/userguide/salesforce.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a website that stores images of historical events. Users of the website must be able to search for and view images based on the year in which the event shown in the image occurred. On average, each image is requested by users only once or twice per year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and serve the images to users.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is the appropriate service for highly available storage and direct delivery of static image content without running web servers. That makes it more cost-effective than Amazon EBS or Amazon EFS, which would require Amazon EC2 instances. For data that is accessed only once or twice a year, S3 Standard-IA is designed for infrequently accessed objects and offers lower storage cost than S3 Standard, although it includes retrieval charges. Because the images are rarely accessed, S3 Standard-IA with S3 static website hosting is the most cost-effective option among the choices. AWS documentation states that S3 Standard-IA is for long-lived, less frequently accessed data and that S3 can be used to host a static website without a single web server.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Cost optimization - Amazon Simple Storage Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cost-optimization.html)

options.text: Set up AWS WAF in both Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
Set up AWS Firewall Manager in both Regions. Centrally configure AWS WAF rules.
Set up AWS Shield in bath Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
Set up AWS Shield in one of the Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF is the AWS service that protects API Gateway REST APIs from common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting by associating a Regional web ACL with an API stage. When the protection must be applied across multiple AWS accounts with minimal ongoing administration, AWS Firewall Manager is the correct choice because it centrally deploys and manages AWS WAF rules and policies across accounts and resources in an organization, including automatic application to in-scope resources. AWS Shield is focused on DDoS protection rather than SQL injection and XSS filtering.

**Learn more:** [Use AWS WAF to protect your REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html) · [AWS Firewall Manager - AWS WAF, AWS Firewall Manager, AWS Shield Advanced, and AWS Shield network security director](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-chapter.html)

A company intends to rehost an application on Amazon EC2 instances that use attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage.  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that ensures all newly created Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted by default. The solution must also stop unencrypted EBS volumes from being created.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the EC2 account attributes to always encrypt new EBS volumes.
Use AWS Config. Configure the encrypted-volumes identifier. Apply the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
Configure AWS Systems Manager to create encrypted copies of the EBS volumes. Reconfigure the EC2 instances to use the encrypted volumes.
Create a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure AWS Migration Hub to use the key when the company migrates workloads.

questions.explanation:
The EC2 account attribute for EBS encryption by default enforces encryption for all newly created EBS volumes in the configured Region. When it is enabled, encryption is automatic and cannot be disabled for an individual volume creation. [Enable Amazon EBS encryption by default](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html)

**Learn more:** [Enable Amazon EBS encryption by default](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html) · [EnableEbsEncryptionByDefault API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_EnableEbsEncryptionByDefault.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On-Demand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day.  
  
Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.

questions.explanation:
Spot Instances are the best fit for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch workloads, and AWS specifically describes Spot as a cost-effective option when applications can be flexible and can tolerate interruption. This scenario is resilient to instance failure because failed work is reprocessed by another instance, so interruption risk is acceptable. By contrast, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are commitment-based discounts with hourly billing or hourly spend commitments across the full term, which is a poorer match for a workload that runs only 6 hours each day rather than continuously.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html) · [Request Spot Instances for fault-tolerant and flexible applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/launch-template-spot-instances.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its application on an Oracle database. The company plans to migrate to AWS quickly because it has limited resources for database administration, backup administration, and data center maintenance. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access.  
  
Which solution will help the company migrate the database to AWS in the **MOST cost-effective** way?

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Replace third-party features with cloud services.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by rewriting the application code to remove dependency on Oracle APEX.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle is the best fit because it supports Oracle workloads that need privileged database and operating system access for third-party or legacy features, while still providing more managed-service benefits than running Oracle directly on Amazon EC2. Standard Amazon RDS for Oracle is more managed, but it restricts SYS/SYSDBA and host access, so it does not meet the privileged-access requirement. Migrating to Oracle on EC2 would meet the access requirement but would increase administrative overhead for backups, operations, and maintenance. Replatforming to PostgreSQL would require significant application changes and would not be the quickest or most cost-effective option for this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Custom - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-custom.html) · [Privileged access - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/replatform-oracle-database-options/administration.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must copy files from an Amazon S3 bucket to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and to another S3 bucket. The files need to be copied continuously. New files are added to the original S3 bucket on a consistent basis. The copied files should be overwritten only when the source file changes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed.

Create an AWS Lambda function. Mount the file system to the function. Set up an S3 event notification to invoke the function when files are created and changed in Amazon S3. Configure the function to copy files to the file system and the destination S3 bucket.

Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer all data.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system. Create a script to routinely synchronize all objects that changed in the origin S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket and the mounted file system.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync is the managed AWS service designed to transfer data between storage services such as Amazon S3 and Amazon EFS with minimal administration. A DataSync task can be scheduled to run periodically, and when the transfer mode is set to transfer only changed data, DataSync performs incremental copies after the initial transfer so unchanged files are not recopied or overwritten. That directly matches the requirement for ongoing copies with overwrite behavior only when the source changes, while avoiding the custom code and maintenance required by Lambda or EC2-based scripting.

**Learn more:** [Configuring how to handle files, objects, and metadata - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-metadata.html) · [Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs - AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/task-scheduling.html)

An application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs access to an Amazon S3 bucket. The traffic must not traverse the internet.  
  
How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 lets EC2 instances in a VPC access S3 over the AWS network without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device. That is the AWS-native configuration specifically designed for private S3 access from a VPC.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions to run its application. The company has VPCs with public subnets and private subnets in its AWS account. The EC2 instances run in a private subnet in one of the VPCs. The Lambda functions need direct network access to the EC2 instances for the application to work.  
  
The application will run for at least 1 year. The company expects the number of Lambda functions that the application uses to increase during that time. The company wants to maximize its savings on all application resources and to keep network latency between the services low.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage and the number of invocations. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to a public subnet in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.

Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.

questions.explanation:
Compute Savings Plans are the correct cost option because they apply to both Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda usage, whereas EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover Lambda. Because the workload will run for at least 1 year and Lambda usage is expected to grow, a Compute Savings Plan maximizes savings across all application resources. To give Lambda direct, low-latency network access to EC2 instances in a private subnet, the Lambda functions should be configured for VPC access using private subnets in that VPC, not left in the Lambda service VPC or placed in a public subnet for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [Savings Plans types - AWS Savings Plans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html) · [Compute Savings Plans and Reserved Instances - AWS Savings Plans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-ris.html)

An ecommerce company wants to launch a one-deal-a-day website on AWS. Each day, exactly one product will be on sale for a 24-hour period. The company must be able to handle millions of requests per hour with millisecond latency during peak hours.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to host the full website in different S3 buckets. Add Amazon CloudFront distributions. Set the S3 buckets as origins for the distributions. Store the order data in Amazon S3.

Deploy the full website on Amazon EC2 instances that run in Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute the website traffic. Add another ALB for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Migrate the full application to run in containers. Host the containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to increase and decrease the number of pods to process bursts in traffic. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the S3 bucket as the origin. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
A serverless architecture is the best fit for extremely high request volume, very low latency, and minimal operational management. Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront can serve static website content at global scale with low latency. Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda provide backend APIs without managing servers or clusters. Amazon DynamoDB is designed for single-digit millisecond performance at scale and is more suitable than a relational database for this very high-throughput access pattern. This combination delivers the required scalability and latency with less operational overhead than managing EC2 fleets, load balancers, or Kubernetes clusters.

**Learn more:** [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html) · [What is Amazon CloudFront?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)

A reporting team receives files each day in an Amazon S3 bucket. The team manually reviews the files and copies them from this initial S3 bucket to an analysis S3 bucket each day at the same time for use with Amazon QuickSight. Additional teams are beginning to send more files, and the file sizes are increasing, to the initial S3 bucket.  
  
The reporting team wants to move the files automatically to the analysis S3 bucket as the files arrive in the initial S3 bucket. The team also wants to use AWS Lambda functions to run pattern-matching code on the copied data. In addition, the team wants to send the data files to a pipeline in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.

Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.

Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.

Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 replication is the managed, lowest-overhead way to automatically copy newly created objects from one S3 bucket to another. After the objects arrive in the analysis bucket, configuring that bucket to send Object Created events to Amazon EventBridge allows one rule to fan out the same event to multiple targets, including AWS Lambda and Amazon SageMaker Pipelines. Direct S3 event notifications are not the right fit here because SageMaker Pipelines is supported as an EventBridge target, while a custom Lambda copy workflow adds unnecessary operational work compared with native S3 replication.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Using EventBridge - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventBridge.html)

A company runs its end-of-day sales process by using an AWS Batch job. The company requires a serverless solution that invokes a third-party reporting application when the AWS Batch job succeeds. The reporting application exposes an HTTP API that uses username-and-password authentication.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure the third-party API as an EventBridge API destination with a username and password. Set the API destination as the EventBridge rule target.

Configure Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure an AWS Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password. Set the Lambda function as the EventBridge rule target.

Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure an HTTP proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.

Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure a proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.

questions.explanation:
AWS Batch natively sends job state change events to Amazon EventBridge, so an EventBridge rule can match a job reaching the `SUCCEEDED` state. EventBridge API destinations are built to invoke external HTTP APIs, and their connections support username/password-style authentication through Basic auth. This provides a fully serverless event-driven integration without needing Lambda or API Gateway. EventBridge Scheduler does not match incoming service events; it is for time-based invocations.

**Learn more:** [AWS Batch events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-batch.html) · [Job state change events - AWS Batch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/batch_job_events.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company must retain the data on those tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company plans to migrate to AWS within the next 6 months. The data center that houses the tapes has 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball. Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud. Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.

questions.explanation:
A 1 Gbps link can transfer approximately 1.2 PB per month theoretically; migrating 5 PB in 6 months via network alone is impractical. AWS Snowball provides bulk data transport that bypasses network constraints entirely. AWS Tape Gateway bridges on-premises tape backups to cloud storage, supporting the tape-to-virtual-tape workflow. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost long-term archive class for 10-year retention requirements.

**Learn more:** [Using a Tape Gateway on an AWS Snowball Edge device](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/using-tape-gateway-snowball.html) · [Moving tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/moving-tapes-vtl.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses **50 TB of data** for reporting and wants to move this data from on premises to AWS. A custom application in the company’s data center runs a **weekly data transformation job**. The company plans to **pause the application until the data transfer is complete** and needs to **start the transfer process as soon as possible**.  
  
The data center does **not** have any available network bandwidth for additional workloads. A solutions architect must transfer the data and must configure the transformation job to continue running in the **AWS Cloud**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to move the data. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
Order an AWS Snowcone device to move the data. Deploy the transformation application to the device.
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Copy the data to the device. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device that includes Amazon EC2 compute. Copy the data to the device. Create a new EC2 instance on AWS to run the transformation application.

questions.explanation:
Because the data center has no spare network bandwidth, the transfer should use an offline device rather than a network-based service such as AWS DataSync. AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized is designed for large-scale data transport to AWS, which fits a 50 TB migration. After the data is imported, AWS Glue provides a managed way to build and run transformation jobs in AWS with less operational effort than managing custom compute infrastructure such as EC2. This makes the Snowball Edge Storage Optimized plus AWS Glue approach the lowest-overhead option.

**Learn more:** [AWS DataSync network requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/datasync-network.html) · [Connecting your network for AWS DataSync transfers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/networking-datasync.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a photo-processing application that must frequently upload and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets located in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect has identified rising data transfer charges and must implement a solution to reduce these costs.  
  
How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?

options.text: Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint is the correct solution because it provides private connectivity from resources in a VPC to S3 in the same Region without requiring a NAT gateway or internet gateway, and AWS states that gateway endpoints have no additional charge. An endpoint policy can be attached to limit access to the required S3 buckets.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

A company has an Amazon S3 data lake. It needs a solution that transforms data from the data lake and loads the data into a data warehouse every day. The data warehouse must provide massively parallel processing (MPP) capabilities.  
  
Data analysts must then be able to create and train machine learning (ML) models by using SQL commands on the data. The solution must use serverless AWS services wherever possible.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Run a daily Amazon EMR job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift ML to create and train the ML models.
Run a daily Amazon EMR job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Aurora Serverless. Use Amazon Aurora ML to create and train the ML models.
Run a daily AWS Glue job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Redshift Serverless. Use Amazon Redshift ML to create and train the ML models.
Run a daily AWS Glue job to transform the data and load the data into Amazon Athena tables. Use Amazon Athena ML to create and train the ML models.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Redshift is the AWS data warehouse that provides MPP capabilities, and Amazon Redshift Serverless is the serverless deployment option. AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service that can run daily transformations and load data into Redshift. Amazon Redshift ML lets SQL users create and train ML models with SQL commands, which matches the requirement for analysts to build models directly from SQL on warehouse data. The other options fail because Amazon EMR is not the most serverless choice, Aurora is not an MPP data warehouse, and Athena ML focuses on SQL-based inference against SageMaker endpoints rather than training ML models in an MPP data warehouse.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Redshift Serverless?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-whatis.html) · [Amazon Redshift Performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c_challenges_achieving_high_performance_queries.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a stateless web application that runs on AWS Lambda functions invoked by Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions to provide Regional failover capabilities.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to route traffic to multiple Regions?

options.text: Create Amazon Route 53 health checks for each Region. Use an active-active failover configuration.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin for each Region. Use CloudFront health checks to route traffic.
Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the API Gateway endpoint in each Region. Configure the transit gateway to route requests.
Create an Application Load Balancer in the primary Region. Set the target group to point to the API Gateway endpoint hostnames in each Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 is AWS's DNS and traffic routing service for multi-region failover. Route 53 health checks monitor the health of API Gateway endpoints in each Region and automatically route traffic to healthy endpoints using active-active or active-passive failover configurations. This is the standard AWS pattern for Regional API endpoint failover without requiring ALBs or CloudFront distribution.

**Learn more:** [Active-active and active-passive failover - Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html) · [Configuring DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An IoT company is launching a mattress with sensors that collect data about a user's sleep. The sensors will send the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The sensors gather approximately 2 MB of data each night for every mattress.  
  
The company must process and summarize the data for each mattress. The results must be available as quickly as possible. Data processing will require 1 GB of memory and will complete within 30 seconds.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Use AWS Glue with a Scala job
Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script
Use AWS Lambda with a Python script
Use AWS Glue with a PySpark job

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda is the most cost-effective fit for a small, short, event-driven workload like this. Lambda can be invoked directly from Amazon S3 event notifications, supports configuring well over 1 GB of memory, and allows executions up to 15 minutes, so a 30-second job needing 1 GB of memory fits easily. Its pricing is based on requests and execution duration, which is typically much cheaper than running AWS Glue or Amazon EMR for lightweight per-object processing. Glue and EMR are intended for larger ETL and big data jobs and add more infrastructure and startup overhead than this requirement needs.

**Learn more:** [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html) · [AWS Lambda Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-functions-chapter.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an ecommerce application on AWS. Amazon EC2 instances handle purchases and save the purchase details in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.  
  
Customers are seeing application timeouts during periods of peak usage. A solutions architect must rearchitect the application so it can scale to handle peak demand.  
  
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances to retry the purchases until the processing is complete. Update the applications to connect to the DB cluster by using Amazon RDS Proxy.
Configure the application to use an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
Update the application to send the purchase requests to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure an Auto Scaling group of new EC2 instances that read from the SQS queue.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to retry the ticket purchases until the processing is complete.
Configure an Amazon AP! Gateway REST API with a usage plan.

questions.explanation:
Using Amazon SQS between the application and the purchase-processing workers decouples the front end from the backend processing tier, so purchase requests can be buffered during traffic spikes instead of timing out while waiting for immediate processing. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers can then scale out to consume messages from the queue as demand increases. Amazon RDS Proxy is also appropriate for Aurora PostgreSQL because it pools and multiplexes database connections, reducing connection churn and helping the database handle surges in application connections more gracefully. Together, these changes address both peak-request buffering and database connection scalability in a cost-effective way.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html) · [Managing Aurora PostgreSQL connection churn with pooling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.BestPractices.connection_pooling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an Amazon DynamoDB table to store data received from devices. The DynamoDB table supports a customer-facing website that displays recent activity on customer devices. The company has configured the table with provisioned throughput for reads and writes.  
  
The company needs to calculate performance metrics for customer device data each day. The solution must have minimal impact on the table's provisioned read and write capacity.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an Amazon Athena SQL query with the Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
Use an AWS Glue job with the AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
Use an Amazon Redshift COPY command to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
Use an Amazon EMR job with an Apache Hive external table to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector invokes DynamoDB point-in-time export and processes the exported data from Amazon S3. DynamoDB table exports do not consume read capacity units and do not affect table performance or availability, so daily metric processing avoids competing with the customer-facing workload for provisioned read and write capacity. Point-in-time recovery must be enabled to use the export connector.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB connections - AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-dynamodb-home.html) · [Using DynamoDB with Amazon S3 to export and import table data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/dynamodb-full-table-copy-options/amazon-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and frequently includes intermittent traffic. The application must continue processing messages continuously without downtime.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.

questions.explanation:
A queue-based, parallel-processing workload backed by Amazon SQS is well suited to mixed EC2 purchasing options. Reserved Instances are appropriate for steady baseline capacity, while Spot Instances are the lowest-cost option for elastic excess capacity. Because the workers consume messages from SQS independently, the workload is interruption-tolerant: if some Spot Instances are reclaimed, other instances can continue processing and unprocessed messages can be retried from the queue. That makes baseline Reserved Instances plus Spot Instances for additional capacity the most cost-effective design that still supports continuous processing.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Spot Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html) · [Best practices for Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-best-practices.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A rapidly growing ecommerce company runs its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must design a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region.  
  
The company wants its database in the DR Region to stay current with the lowest possible latency. The rest of the infrastructure in the DR Region must operate at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if needed.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)**?

options.text: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a pilot light deployment.
Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora global database is the AWS database option in these choices that is designed for cross-Region disaster recovery with very low replication lag, typically under a second, which keeps the DR Region as current as possible. Warm standby is the DR pattern that keeps a scaled-down but fully running copy of the environment in the secondary Region, so it can scale up quickly and delivers a lower RTO than pilot light. Amazon RDS Multi-AZ does not meet the cross-Region requirement because Multi-AZ is for high availability across Availability Zones within a single Region.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html) · [Disaster recovery options in the cloud - Disaster Recovery of Workloads on AWS: Recovery in the Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use an AWS CloudFormation stack for its application in a test environment. The company keeps the CloudFormation template in an Amazon S3 bucket that blocks public access. The company needs to grant CloudFormation access to the template in the S3 bucket for specific user requests to create the test environment. The solution must adhere to security best practices.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the S3 object URL.
Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API that has the S3 bucket as the target. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the API Gateway URL.
Create a presigned URL for the template object. Configure the CloudFormation stack to use the presigned URL.
Allow public access to the template object in the S3 bucket. Block the public access after the test environment is created.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 presigned URL provides time-limited permission to retrieve a specific private template object, so it can be used for an individual CloudFormation stack-creation request without enabling public access to the bucket. AWS CloudFormation supports presigned S3 URLs as template URLs, and Amazon S3 documents that presigned URLs grant time-limited access using the credentials of the principal that created them.

**Learn more:** [Use quick-create links to create CloudFormation stacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-console-create-stacks-quick-create-links.html) · [Sharing objects with presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving a data center from its on-premises environment to AWS. The company has several legacy applications that are hosted on separate virtual servers. No changes can be made to the application designs.  
  
Each virtual server currently runs on its own EC2 instance. A solutions architect must ensure that the applications are reliable and fault tolerant after the migration to AWS. The applications will run on Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a minimum of one and a maximum of one. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Use the AMI to create EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group.

Use AWS Backup to create an hourly backup of the EC2 instance that hosts each application. Store the backup in Amazon S3 in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a disaster recovery process to restore the EC2 instance for each application from its most recent backup.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Launch two new EC2 instances from the AMI. Place each EC2 instance in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a Network Load Balancer that has the EC2 instances as targets.

Use AWS Mitigation Hub Refactor Spaces to migrate each application off the EC2 instance. Break down functionality from each application into individual components. Host each application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type.

questions.explanation:
For legacy applications that must remain on Amazon EC2 without redesign, the appropriate solution is to create an AMI for each server and run it in an Auto Scaling group so Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can automatically replace an unhealthy instance and maintain the desired capacity. With Elastic Load Balancing health checks enabled, the load balancer stops sending traffic to failed instances and Auto Scaling launches replacements. Refactoring to containers violates the no-design-change constraint, and backup/restore is recovery rather than fault-tolerant operation. Running two copies behind a load balancer is not a safe assumption for unchanged legacy single-server applications because active-active behavior may require application changes or shared-state handling.

**Learn more:** [Resilience in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) · [Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-health-checks.html)

A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application's peak hours begin at the same time each day. Users report slow application performance at the beginning of peak hours. The application runs normally 2–3 hours after peak hours start.  
  
The company wants to make sure that the application performs properly at the start of peak hours.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic properly to the instances.
Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.

questions.explanation:
Scheduled scaling is the correct approach for a workload whose demand pattern is predictable and occurs at the same time each day. It lets the Auto Scaling group increase capacity before the peak begins, so instances are already running when traffic arrives. Dynamic scaling based on CPU or memory responds only after utilization increases, which can leave the application underprovisioned at the start of the surge. An Application Load Balancer can distribute traffic across available instances, but it does not create capacity in advance. AWS Auto Scaling documentation specifically describes scheduled actions for known traffic patterns and dynamic scaling for reactive adjustments.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Dynamic scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scale-based-on-demand.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a business application that creates hundreds of reports every day. The application writes the reports in CSV format to a network share. The company must store this data in the AWS Cloud in near real time for analysis.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create a scheduled task that runs at the end of each day.
Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Update the business system to use a new network share from the S3 File Gateway.
Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create an application that uses the DataSync API in the automation workflow.
Deploy an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Create a script that checks for new files on the network share and uploads the new files by using SFTP.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway provides an SMB or NFS file share that applications can write to directly, and files written to the share are mapped to objects in Amazon S3 with asynchronous uploads. That satisfies the near-real-time requirement without requiring custom scripts, API-driven orchestration, or scheduled batch transfers. A DataSync job scheduled once per day is not near real time, and solutions that depend on custom automation or SFTP introduce more administrative overhead than simply redirecting the application to a File Gateway share.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html) · [Test your S3 File Gateway - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/GettingStartedTestFileShare.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to migrate a multi-tier application from on premises to the AWS Cloud to improve the application's performance. The application includes application tiers that communicate with one another through RESTful services. Transactions are dropped when one tier becomes overloaded. A solutions architect must design a solution that resolves these issues and modernizes the application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements and is the **MOST operationally efficient**?

options.text: Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.

Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze the application performance history to determine the servers' peak utilization during the performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to meet the peak requirements.

Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.

Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is designed to decouple application components and buffer messages so temporary overload in one tier does not cause transactions to be lost. Running the application servers on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group and scaling the consumers based on SQS queue depth provides elasticity with less operational effort than managing instance sizing for peak load. This directly addresses overloaded tiers and dropped transactions while modernizing the architecture through asynchronous decoupling. Amazon SNS is not a queue, so it is not the right service for queue-length-based buffering between tiers, and simply increasing EC2 instance size is less operationally efficient than horizontal scaling with a queue-backed design.

**Learn more:** [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html) · [Amazon Simple Queue Service Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)

options.text: Add the development team's OU Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Add the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Update the key policy to allow the development team's OU to use the AWS KMS keys that are used to decrypt the snapshots.
Add the development team’s account Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Recreate the AWS KMS key. Add a key policy to allow the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to use the AWS KMS key.

questions.explanation:
Option A adds the development OU ARN to the AMI launch permission list, allowing the development team to launch the AMI. Option C updates the AWS KMS key policy to allow the development OU to decrypt the snapshots that underlie the AMI. Both permissions are necessary: the launch permission grants access to the AMI resource itself, while the KMS policy grant enables decryption of the encrypted snapshots.

**Learn more:** [Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/sharingamis-explicit.html) · [Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-modifying-external-accounts.html)

A company runs a containerized web application on a fleet of on-premises servers that handle incoming requests. The request volume is increasing rapidly, and the on-premises servers can no longer support the higher load.  
  
The company wants to migrate the application to AWS with minimal code changes and minimal development effort.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS Fargate on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run the containerized web application with Service Auto Scaling. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
Use two Amazon EC2 instances to host the containerized web application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
Use AWS Lambda with a new code that uses one of the supported languages. Create multiple Lambda functions to support the load. Use Amazon API Gateway as an entry point to the Lambda functions.
Use a high performance computing (HPC) solution such as AWS ParallelCluster to establish an HPC cluster that can process the incoming requests at the appropriate scale.

questions.explanation:
AWS Fargate on Amazon ECS is the best fit because it allows the company to run the existing containerized application without managing EC2 instances, which minimizes operational overhead while preserving the container-based architecture. Service Auto Scaling and an Application Load Balancer provide elastic scaling and traffic distribution for a growing web workload. Using EC2 would add server management burden, AWS Lambda would require a significant application rewrite, and AWS ParallelCluster is intended for HPC workloads rather than standard web application request handling.

**Learn more:** [AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html) · [Amazon ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a legacy data processing application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Data is processed sequentially, but the order of results does not matter. The application uses a monolithic architecture. The only way the company can scale the application to meet increased demand is by increasing the instance size.  
  
The company’s developers have decided to rewrite the application to use a microservices architecture on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend for communication between the microservices?

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add code to the data producers, and send data to the queue. Add code to the data consumers to process data from the queue.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Add code to the data producers, and publish notifications to the topic. Add code to the data consumers to subscribe to the topic.

Create an AWS Lambda function to pass messages. Add code to the data producers to call the Lambda function with a data object. Add code to the data consumers to receive a data object that is passed from the Lambda function.

Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Enable DynamoDB Streams. Add code to the data producers to insert data into the table. Add code to the data consumers to use the DynamoDB Streams API to detect new table entries and retrieve the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS is the correct choice because a queue provides asynchronous, durable communication that decouples microservice producers from consumers, which is a core microservices pattern on AWS. This fits a workload where units of work can be processed independently and result ordering does not matter, allowing the consumer services on Amazon ECS to scale horizontally and pull messages from the queue as capacity increases. Amazon SNS is primarily for pub/sub fan-out, AWS Lambda is not a message-passing service, and DynamoDB Streams is intended for change-data-capture from table updates rather than as the primary communication mechanism for distributed work processing.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html) · [Communication mechanisms - Implementing Microservices on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/microservices-on-aws/communication-mechanisms.html)

A company has built a non-production application consisting of multiple microservices for each of its business units. One development team maintains every microservice.  
  
The existing architecture uses a static web frontend and a Java-based backend that contains the application logic. It also uses a MySQL database that the company hosts on an Amazon EC2 instance.  
  
The company must ensure that the application is secure and globally available.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudFront and AWS Amplify to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Use Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 and CloudFront provide secure, globally distributed static-content delivery. Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda provides a serverless API and compute layer, eliminating server and load-balancer operations. Amazon RDS for MySQL is a managed database service, avoiding the operational burden of hosting MySQL on EC2. This combination meets the availability and security goals with the lowest operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [AWS Serverless Multi-Tier Architectures with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/serverless-multi-tier-architectures-api-gateway-lambda/single-page-application.html) · [Get started with a secure static website](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/getting-started-secure-static-website-cloudformation-template.html)

A company runs its own Amazon EC2 instances that host MySQL databases. The company is manually handling replication and scaling as demand rises or falls.  
  
The company needs a new solution that simplifies adding compute capacity to the database tier or removing it as needed. The solution also must provide better performance, scaling, and durability with minimal operational effort.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.
Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.
Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL is the best match because it keeps MySQL compatibility while moving the databases to a managed Aurora platform that automatically scales compute capacity up and down as workload changes. Aurora also provides built-in high availability and durable distributed storage, reducing the operational work required compared with managing MySQL replication and EC2 instances manually. Aurora PostgreSQL changes the database engine, and the EC2-based options do not deliver the same managed scaling, durability, and reduced-operations benefits.

**Learn more:** [Using Aurora serverless - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html) · [How Aurora serverless works - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)

A company needs a solution to enforce data encryption at rest on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must automatically identify noncompliant resources and enforce compliance policies on findings.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative overhead**?

options.text: Use an IAM policy that allows users to create only encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Config and AWS Systems Manager to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.

Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage access to encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
Use Amazon Macie to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
Use Amazon inspector to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config provides a managed compliance control for EBS encryption through the `encrypted-volumes` rule, which flags unencrypted EBS volumes as noncompliant. AWS Systems Manager Automation can be attached as remediation to enforce the policy automatically. This is the lowest-overhead option because it uses managed compliance detection and managed remediation instead of custom event-driven code. Amazon Macie does not evaluate EBS encryption, and Amazon Inspector is not the service used to detect unencrypted EBS volumes for compliance enforcement. AWS KMS is part of the encryption mechanism, but by itself it does not identify noncompliant resources or remediate them.

**Learn more:** [encrypted-volumes - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/encrypted-volumes.html) · [Automatically encrypt existing and new Amazon EBS volumes - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/automatically-encrypt-existing-and-new-amazon-ebs-volumes.html)

A company is developing a mobile app on AWS and wants to extend its reach to millions of users. The company must build a platform that allows authorized users to watch the company’s content on their mobile devices.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is built to distribute content at global scale, and CloudFront signed URLs are an AWS mechanism for serving private content only to users your application has authorized. The application can verify that a user is entitled to access the content, generate a signed URL, and let CloudFront stream the content while enforcing the signature and expiration rules. This matches both the scale requirement and the requirement that only authorized users can watch the content.

**Learn more:** [Use signed URLs - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html) · [Restrict access to files - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-overview.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a public three-tier web application in a VPC. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances running in private subnets must communicate with a license server on the internet. The company needs a managed solution that minimizes operational maintenance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Provision a NAT instance in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
Provision a NAT instance in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
Provision a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
Provision a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
A NAT gateway is the AWS-managed option for allowing instances in private subnets to initiate outbound connections to the internet, and AWS recommends it over a NAT instance because it provides better availability and requires less administrative effort. For internet egress, the NAT gateway must be deployed in a public subnet, and each private subnet route table must use a default route that targets the NAT gateway.

**Learn more:** [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html) · [Compare NAT gateways and NAT instances - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-comparison.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A finance company's customers request appointments with financial advisors by sending text messages. A web application running on Amazon EC2 instances receives the appointment requests. The web application publishes the text messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Another application running on EC2 instances then sends meeting invitations and meeting confirmation email messages to the customers. After scheduling succeeds, this application stores the meeting details in an Amazon DynamoDB database.  
  
As the company grows, customers report that their meeting invitations are taking longer to arrive.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to fix this issue?

options.text: Add a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the DynamoDB database.
Add an Amazon API Gateway API in front of the web application that accepts the appointment requests.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the origin as the web application that accepts the appointment requests.
Add an Auto Scaling group for the application that sends meeting invitations. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale based on the depth of the SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
The correct solution is to scale the EC2-based worker application that processes messages from Amazon SQS and sends the invitations. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can scale a worker fleet based on SQS queue backlog or queue depth, which directly addresses rising latency caused by messages waiting too long to be processed. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) improves DynamoDB read performance, not asynchronous message processing. API Gateway and CloudFront can front a web application, but they do not remove the bottleneck in the queue-consuming invitation service.

**Learn more:** [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html) · [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will include dynamic server-side components so that users can enter their name, email address, phone number, and message.  
  
The company expects fewer than 100 site visits per month.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

questions.explanation:
A serverless design using Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon SES is the most cost-effective fit for a low-traffic contact form on an S3-hosted static site. API Gateway can receive the form submission, Lambda provides the required server-side processing, and SES can send the resulting email. This avoids paying for continuously running containers or virtual machines, which would cost more than necessary for fewer than 100 monthly visits. AWS also documents this exact pattern for adding dynamic contact forms to S3 static websites, and Lambda/API Gateway pricing is especially favorable for low-volume workloads.

**Learn more:** [Create Dynamic Contact Forms for S3 Static Websites Using AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/create-dynamic-contact-forms-for-s3-static-websites-using-aws-lambda-amazon-api-gateway-and-amazon-ses/) · [Select a method to invoke your Lambda function using an HTTP request - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/apig-http-invoke-decision.html)

A solutions architect must implement a solution to lower a company's storage costs. All of the company's data is currently in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. The company must retain all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.

questions.explanation:
An S3 Lifecycle rule that transitions objects to **S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years** keeps the newest 2 years in S3 Standard, which provides immediate access and high availability, and then moves older objects to the lowest-cost S3 archival class for long-term retention. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is intended for long-lived archive data and is not real-time accessible, so it should only be used after the 2-year immediate-retrieval window. S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiers is access-pattern driven and can archive data sooner than 2 years of age, and S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one Availability Zone, so it does not satisfy the highly available requirement for the most recent 2 years.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes for long-term data storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a frontend application that uses an Amazon API Gateway API backend integrated with AWS Lambda. When the API receives requests, the Lambda function loads many libraries. The Lambda function then connects to an Amazon RDS database, processes the data, and returns the data to the frontend application.  
  
The company wants to ensure that response latency is as low as possible for all users while making the fewest changes to the company's operations.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Establish a connection between the frontend application and the database to make queries faster by bypassing the API.
Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function that handles the requests.
Cache the results of the queries in Amazon S3 for faster retrieval of similar datasets.
Increase the size of the database to increase the number of connections Lambda can establish at one time.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments pre-initialized, which reduces cold-start latency and is specifically recommended when workloads need the lowest and most predictable response times. Because the function spends startup time loading many libraries before handling requests, provisioned concurrency directly addresses that delay with minimal architectural change. It is a much better fit than bypassing API Gateway, building a new S3-based cache layer, or increasing database size, none of which directly solves Lambda initialization latency.

**Learn more:** [Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html) · [Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A data analytics company has 80 offices distributed around the world. Each office hosts 1 PB of data and has between 1 and 2 Gbps of internet bandwidth.  
  
The company needs to perform a one-time migration of a large volume of data from its offices to Amazon S3. The migration must be completed within 4 weeks.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Establish a new 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to each office. Transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Use multiple AWS Snowball Edge storage-optimized devices to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Use an AWS Snowmobile to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to transfer the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices are built for moving large datasets into Amazon S3 by shipping physical devices, which avoids the bandwidth limits of 1–2 Gbps internet links. Using multiple devices in parallel across the offices can meet a one-time 1 PB-per-site migration deadline. AWS Snowmobile is intended for much larger centralized transfers, while AWS Direct Connect and Storage Gateway depend on network transfer and are not practical for moving 1 PB from each office within 4 weeks over those links. Official AWS documentation describes Snowball Edge as supporting import or export of data between local environments and Amazon S3 without using the internet, and Snowmobile as the option for exabyte-scale transfers.

**Learn more:** [What is Snowball Edge? - AWS Snowball Edge Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html) · [What is Volume Gateway? - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html)
