A company has an online gaming application with multiplayer gaming support over TCP and UDP. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to direct the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company must improve application performance and reduce latency for the online game in preparation for user growth.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is the correct choice because it improves global application performance by routing client traffic onto the AWS global network and sending it to the optimal healthy regional endpoint. Standard accelerators support Network Load Balancers as endpoints in multiple AWS Regions, and accelerator listeners can be configured for TCP, UDP, or both, which fits a multiplayer gaming application that uses both protocols. CloudFront and API Gateway are not intended for this kind of end-to-end TCP/UDP game traffic, and Application Load Balancers do not support UDP.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [AWS Global Accelerator components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-components.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company in the `ap-northeast-1` Region operates a fleet of thousands of AWS Outposts servers. The company has deployed these servers to remote locations worldwide. All servers regularly download new software versions that contain 100 files. Considerable latency occurs before every server is running the new software versions.  
  
The company must decrease the deployment latency for new software versions.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution in ap-northeast-1 that includes a CachingDisabled cache policy. Configure the S3 bucket as the origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Create a second S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. Configure replication between the buckets. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses ap-northeast-1 as the primary origin and us-east-1 as the secondary origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Configure Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration. Download the software by using the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket in ap-northeast-1. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the S3 bucket as the origin. Download the software by using signed URLs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront caches the software files at globally distributed edge locations, allowing remote servers to retrieve cached content from a nearby location instead of repeatedly downloading each file from the Amazon S3 origin in `ap-northeast-1`. Edge caching reduces latency and origin requests with minimal operational management. A CachingDisabled policy would prevent this benefit, while cross-Region replication introduces unnecessary operational complexity. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes data transport to and from an S3 bucket but does not provide CloudFront’s persistent edge caching for repeated software downloads.

**Learn more:** [Caching and availability - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/ConfiguringCaching.html) · [How CloudFront delivers content - Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html)

A solutions architect is designing a company's disaster recovery (DR) architecture. The company has a MySQL database running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet with scheduled backup. The DR design must include multiple AWS Regions.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Migrate the MySQL database to multiple EC2 instances. Configure a standby EC2 instance in the DR Region. Turn on replication.
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS. Use a Multi-AZ deployment. Turn on read replication for the primary DB instance in the different Availability Zones.
Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora global database. Host the primary DB cluster in the primary Region. Host the secondary DB cluster in the DR Region.
Store the scheduled backup of the MySQL database in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use the data backup to restore the database in the DR Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora global database is purpose-built for cross-Region disaster recovery. It lets you place the primary DB cluster in one AWS Region and one or more secondary clusters in other Regions, with Aurora automatically replicating changes across Regions by using dedicated infrastructure and providing faster recovery from Region-wide outages with less operational effort than self-managed MySQL replication or backup-and-restore approaches. By contrast, RDS Multi-AZ is a same-Region high-availability feature, not a multi-Region DR solution.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html) · [Using switchover or failover in Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A consulting company delivers professional services to customers around the world. The company offers solutions and tools that help customers accelerate data collection and analysis on AWS. The company must centrally manage and deploy a shared set of solutions and tools for customers to use through self-service.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create AWS CloudFormation templates for the customers.
Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
Create AWS Config items for the customers.

questions.explanation:
AWS Service Catalog is built to centrally manage approved IT services and make them available for self-service provisioning. Administrators organize approved products into portfolios, apply governance and access controls, and let users launch those products on their own. That matches the need for a centrally managed, common set of customer solutions and tools that customers can deploy themselves.

**Learn more:** [What Is Service Catalog? - AWS Service Catalog](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/introduction.html) · [AWS Service Catalog Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online photo-sharing company stores its photos in an Amazon S3 bucket in the `us-west-1` Region. The company must store a copy of all new photos in the `us-east-1` Region.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the **LEAST operational effort**?

options.text: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
Create a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration of the existing S3 bucket. Specify us-east-1 in the CORS rule's AllowedOrigin element.
Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1 across multiple Availability Zones. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to save photos into the second S3 bucket.

Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 event notifications on object creation and update events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication is the managed S3 feature designed to automatically replicate new objects from a source bucket to a destination bucket in a different AWS Region. That makes it the lowest-effort way to keep copies of new photos in `us-east-1`. CORS only governs cross-origin web access, not data replication, S3 Lifecycle rules manage transitions and expiration rather than copying to another bucket, and an S3 event notification plus Lambda solution would work but requires custom implementation and ongoing operational management. Official AWS documentation states that Cross-Region Replication replicates objects across buckets in different AWS Regions. See: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Using cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cors.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an AWS Lambda function in private subnets in a VPC. The subnets have a default route to the internet by using an Amazon EC2 NAT instance. The Lambda function processes input data and stores its output as an object in Amazon S3.  
  
Intermittently, the Lambda function times out when it tries to upload the object because traffic on the NAT instance's network is saturated. The company wants to access Amazon S3 without traversing the internet.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Replace the EC2 NAT instance with an AWS managed NAT gateway.
Increase the size of the EC2 NAT instance in the VPC to a network optimized instance type.
Provision a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPUpdate the route tables of the subnets accordingly.
Provision a transit gateway. Place transit gateway attachments in the private subnets where the Lambda function is running.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint is the correct solution because it provides private connectivity from resources in the VPC to S3 over the AWS network and updates the selected subnet route tables with a route to the endpoint. That removes S3 traffic from the NAT instance path, avoids internet traversal, and addresses the timeout caused by NAT network saturation.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online video game company must keep **ultra-low latency** for its game servers. The game servers run on **Amazon EC2 instances**. The company needs a solution that can process **millions of UDP internet traffic requests each second**.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Configure an Application Load Balancer with the required protocol and ports for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
Configure a Gateway Load Balancer for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
Configure a Network Load Balancer with the required protocol and ports for the internet traffic. Specify the EC2 instances as the targets.
Launch an identical set of game servers on EC2 instances in separate AWS Regions. Route internet traffic to both sets of EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer is the correct choice because it operates at Layer 4 and supports UDP, which matches the game's traffic pattern. It is intended for high-performance, low-latency traffic distribution to targets such as EC2 instances, making it suitable for handling millions of requests per second. An Application Load Balancer does not support UDP because it is for HTTP/HTTPS traffic, and a Gateway Load Balancer is meant for inline virtual appliances such as firewalls rather than fronting game servers. Duplicating servers across Regions would add substantial cost without being the most direct or economical way to load balance massive UDP traffic.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Load Balancing API Reference - Welcome](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html) · [What is a Gateway Load Balancer? - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A video game company is rolling out a new gaming application to users globally. The company needs a solution that provides near-real-time player reviews and rankings.  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that provides fast data access. The solution must also ensure that the data is persisted to disks if the company restarts the application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin. Store the player data in the S3 bucket.
Create Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Store the player data on the EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Route 53 with geolocation records to direct users to the closest EC2 instance.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis delivers low-latency, in-memory access for rapidly changing reviews and rankings while supporting durable snapshots and backups that can be restored after a restart. It is a managed service, avoiding the operational burden of running and synchronizing EC2 instances across Regions. Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached does not provide the required persistence capability.

**Learn more:** [Snapshot and restore - Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/backups.html) · [High availability using replication groups - Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an application to monitor changes in the database, analyze the relationships among the data entities, and provide recommendations to users.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Neptune is purpose-built for highly connected data and graph workloads such as social networks and recommendation engines, where analyzing relationships between entities is central. Neptune Streams is the native, fully managed change-log stream for Neptune and captures graph changes in real time, so it satisfies the requirement to monitor database changes without adding the extra operational work of managing a separate streaming service. Amazon QLDB is a ledger database for immutable and cryptographically verifiable transaction history, not for graph-style relationship analysis and recommendations.

**Learn more:** [What Is Amazon Neptune?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/intro.html) · [Getting started with Amazon Neptune](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/graph-get-started.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a Microsoft .NET application that runs on an on-premises Windows Server. The application stores data by using an Oracle Database Standard Edition server. The company is planning a migration to AWS and wants to minimize development changes while moving the application. The AWS application environment should be highly available.  
  
Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Refactor the application as serverless with AWS Lambda functions running .NET Core.
Rehost the application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment.
Replatform the application to run on Amazon EC2 with the Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Amazon DynamoDB in a Multi-AZ deployment.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment.

questions.explanation:
A rehost to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform preserves the existing application stack and minimizes code changes, while a load-balanced Elastic Beanstalk environment provides high availability by running multiple instances and supporting deployment across at least two Availability Zones. For the database, migrating Oracle to Oracle on Amazon RDS minimizes application and schema changes compared with moving to DynamoDB, and AWS Database Migration Service supports migrations from Oracle to Amazon RDS for Oracle.

**Learn more:** [The create new environment wizard - AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environments-create-wizard.html) · [Capacity configuration for your Elastic Beanstalk environment - AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environments-cfg-autoscaling-configuration-approaches.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a critical data-analysis job each week before the first day of the work week. The job needs at least 1 hour to finish the analysis. The job is stateful and cannot withstand interruptions. The company needs a solution to run the job on AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a container for the job. Schedule the job to run as an AWS Fargate task on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster by using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
Configure the job to run in an AWS Lambda function. Create a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function.
Configure an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that run Amazon Linux. Configure a crontab entry on the instances to run the analysis.
Configure an AWS DataSync task to run the job. Configure a cron expression to run the task on a schedule.

questions.explanation: An Amazon ECS task running on AWS Fargate can execute a containerized workload for longer than 1 hour and can be scheduled with Amazon EventBridge Scheduler. It avoids AWS Lambda's 15-minute execution limit and the interruption risk of EC2 Spot Instances.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations, and its resources are tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config can identify and report on untagged resources using managed rules like REQUIRED_TAGS. Once identified, resources can be tagged programmatically via SDK, and AWS Backup plans can use those tags as filtering criteria to automatically include resources. This automation-first approach minimizes operational overhead compared to manual review or resource discovery. Manually requiring account owners to review resources would add significant operational burden.

**Learn more:** [Assign resources by tags - AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources-console.html) · [What Is AWS Config?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html)

options.text: Deploy a self-managed database on Amazon EC2 instances by using open source software. Use Spot Instances for cost optimization. Configure automated backups to Amazon S3.
Use Amazon RDS. Use on-demand capacity mode for the database with General Purpose SSD storage. Configure automatic backups with a retention period of 7 days.
Use Amazon Aurora Serverless for the database. Use serverless capacity scaling. Configure automated backups to Amazon S3.
Deploy a self-managed NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for cost optimization. Configure automated backups directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Serverless provides a managed relational database whose serverless capacity can scale with variable application demand, avoiding the need to continuously provision database capacity for peak traffic. Aurora also provides automated backups and stores them in Amazon S3, satisfying the backup requirement without operating a self-managed database.

**Learn more:** [Using Aurora Serverless v2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html) · [Overview of backing up and restoring an Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.html)

A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the `us-west-1` Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image when needed.  
  
If a natural disaster occurs in the `us-west-1` Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the `us-west-2` Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances. The company also wants to automate backups of the EC2 instances.  
  
Which solutions will meet these requirements with the **LEAST administrative effort**? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Copy the image on demand.
Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.

Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.

Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.

Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.

questions.explanation:
The correct solutions are the ones that both automate recurring EC2 backups and automatically place recoverable copies in `us-west-2`. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager can create EBS-backed AMIs based on tags and supports cross-Region copying of those AMIs, so a twice-daily AMI lifecycle policy satisfies the 24-hour RPO and disaster recovery requirement. AWS Backup can create a tag-based backup plan for EC2 instances and can automatically copy backups to another AWS Region as part of the scheduled plan, which also satisfies the 24-hour RPO with minimal administration. Options that rely on on-demand copying are not fully automated, and using AWS Lambda to copy backups adds unnecessary operational effort because AWS Backup already provides native cross-Region copy.

**Learn more:** [Create Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager custom policy for EBS-backed AMIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ami-policy.html) · [Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager default policies vs custom policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/policy-differences.html)

A company must provide customers with secure access to its data. The company processes customer data and stores the results in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
All of the data is subject to strict regulations and security requirements. The data must be encrypted at rest. Each customer must be able to access only that customer's data from the customer's AWS account. Company employees must not be able to access the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the private certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In the S3 bucket policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In each KMS key policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the public certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

questions.explanation:
For encrypted Amazon S3 data, the correct control plane for who can decrypt the data is AWS KMS when using SSE-KMS. A separate customer-managed KMS key per customer provides cryptographic isolation, and the KMS key policy can allow cryptographic use only to the specific cross-account IAM role supplied by that customer. That design supports encryption at rest, lets each customer access only its own data from its own AWS account, and prevents company employees from decrypting the objects. ACM certificates are for TLS certificate management, not S3 data-at-rest authorization, and an S3 bucket policy cannot grant or deny the KMS `Decrypt` operation itself.

**Learn more:** [Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html) · [Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key - AWS Key Management Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-modifying-external-accounts.html)

A company keeps its accounting records in a custom application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
The company must migrate the data to an AWS managed service for development and maintenance of the application data. The solution must:  
  
- require minimal operational support  
- provide immutable, cryptographically verifiable logs of data changes  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Neptune cluster.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Timestream database.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) ledger.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (QLDB) is a fully managed ledger database designed to maintain immutable, cryptographically verifiable transaction logs of all data changes. This is precisely what accounting systems require for compliance, auditability, and fraud prevention. QLDB is serverless and fully managed, minimizing operational overhead. Redshift is for analytics, Neptune for graph relationships, and Timestream for time-series metrics.

**Learn more:** [Introducing Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (QLDB)](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2018/11/introducing-amazon-qldb/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A rapidly expanding global ecommerce company hosts its web application on AWS. The web application includes static content and dynamic content. The website stores online transaction processing (OLTP) data in an Amazon RDS database. The website’s users are experiencing slow page loads.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to resolve this issue? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
Host the dynamic web content in Amazon S3.
Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance.
Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS DB instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront improves page-load performance by delivering static and dynamic web content through nearby edge locations, which reduces latency for global users. An Amazon RDS read replica helps when application reads are contributing to slowness, because read traffic can be routed away from the primary DB instance to scale read-heavy workloads. Multi-AZ is mainly for high availability and failover rather than performance improvement, Amazon Redshift is an analytics data warehouse rather than an OLTP web-tier performance solution, and Amazon S3 is for static object storage rather than hosting dynamic web content.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon CloudFront?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html) · [Caching and availability - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/ConfiguringCaching.html)

An online gaming company is moving user-data storage to Amazon DynamoDB to accommodate its expanding user base. The current architecture has DynamoDB tables that store user profiles, achievements, and in-game transactions.  
  
The company must build a robust, continuously available, and resilient DynamoDB architecture to preserve a seamless gaming experience for users.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Create DynamoDB tables in a single AWS Region. Use on-demand capacity mode. Use global tables to replicate data across multiple Regions.
Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache frequently accessed data. Deploy tables in a single AWS Region and enable auto scaling. Configure Cross-Region Replication manually to additional Regions.
Create DynamoDB tables in multiple AWS Regions. Use on-demand capacity mode. Use DynamoDB Streams for Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
Use DynamoDB global tables for automatic multi-Region replication. Deploy tables in multiple AWS Regions. Use provisioned capacity mode. Enable auto scaling.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB global tables provide fully managed, automatic multi-Region replication with multi-active replicas, enabling an application to use local DynamoDB endpoints and remain resilient to a Regional failure. Provisioned capacity with auto scaling adjusts read and write throughput to demand and is generally more cost-effective than on-demand capacity for sustained or predictable workloads. [Using DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.html)

**Learn more:** [Using DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.html)

A company has already migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users use a visualization tool to query the data warehouse. The average size of a query result returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB, and each webpage delivered by the visualization tool is about 500 KB. Result sets from the data warehouse are not cached.  
  
Which solution delivers the **LOWEST** data transfer egress cost for the company?

options.text: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.

questions.explanation:
The lowest-cost design keeps the large 50 MB database result sets inside the same AWS Region by placing the visualization tool there with the data warehouse. AWS charges data transfer out over Direct Connect per GB, and internet egress is also billed; sending every uncached 50 MB result set back to an on-premises visualization tier would therefore create much more chargeable egress than sending only the much smaller 500 KB web pages to users. Hosting the visualization tool in the same Region minimizes paid egress to only the lightweight presentation traffic, making internet access to that tool the cheapest option among the choices.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/pricing/) · [Amazon EC2 On-Demand Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/)

Which solution satisfies these requirements?

Create an IAM policy to allow access to the AWS Management Console only from a defined set of corporate IP addresses. Restrict user access based on job responsibility by using an IAM policy and roles.

Configure AWS Site-to-Site VPN to connect to the VPConfigure route table entries to direct traffic from on premises to the VPConfigure instance security groups and network ACLs to allow only required traffic from on premises.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses encrypted IPsec tunnels to connect an on-premises network and a VPC. VPC route tables direct the required traffic, and instance security groups plus network ACLs can limit communication to only the required sources, destinations, ports, and protocols.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an online marketplace web application on AWS. The application serves hundreds of thousands of users during peak hours.  
  
The company needs a scalable, near-real-time solution to share the details of millions of financial transactions with several other internal applications.  
  
The transactions also must be processed to remove sensitive data before being stored in a document database for low-latency retrieval.  
  
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Store the transactions data into Amazon DynamoDB. Set up a rule in DynamoDB to remove sensitive data from every transaction upon write. Use DynamoDB Streams to share the transactions data with other applications.

Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to store data in Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3. Use AWS Lambda integration with Kinesis Data Firehose to remove sensitive data. Other applications can consume the data stored in Amazon S3.

Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use AWS Lambda integration to remove sensitive data from every transaction and then store the transactions data in Amazon DynamoDB. Other applications can consume the transactions data off the Kinesis data stream.

Store the batched transactions data in Amazon S3 as files. Use AWS Lambda to process every file and remove sensitive data before updating the files in Amazon S3. The Lambda function then stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB. Other applications can consume transaction files stored in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is the best fit for ingesting and distributing high-volume transaction events to multiple downstream consumers in near real time. AWS Lambda can consume records from the stream, remove sensitive fields, and write the sanitized transactions to Amazon DynamoDB, which provides low-latency retrieval and is a document/key-value database. DynamoDB Streams is primarily a change-data-capture stream from a DynamoDB table and is not the best primary event backbone for several applications, and Amazon Data Firehose is optimized for managed delivery to destinations rather than multiple application consumers.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Kinesis Data Streams terminology and concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/key-concepts.html) · [Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html)

A company is developing a shopping application on AWS. The application provides a catalog that changes once per month and must scale with traffic volume. The company requires the lowest possible latency for the application. Data from each user's shopping cart must be highly available. User session data must remain available even if the user disconnects and then reconnects.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to make sure the shopping cart data is preserved at all times?

options.text: Configure an Application Load Balancer to enable the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) for access to the catalog in Amazon Aurora.
Configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache catalog data from Amazon DynamoDB and shopping cart data from the user's session.
Configure Amazon OpenSearch Service to cache catalog data from Amazon DynamoDB and shopping cart data from the user's session.
Configure an Amazon EC2 instance with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage for the catalog and shopping cart. Configure automated snapshots.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB serves as the persistent store for shopping cart data with high availability, automatic scaling, and cross-session preservation. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis caches the catalog data to minimize latency for frequently accessed information. When a user disconnects and reconnects, DynamoDB retrieves the cart data, ensuring continuity. Sticky sessions and single-instance storage approaches lack the required durability and scale.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon ElastiCache?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.html) · [Caching patterns - Database Caching Strategies Using Redis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/database-caching-strategies-using-redis/caching-patterns.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations. The company wants to run some of its AWS accounts with different budgets. The company wants to receive alerts and automatically stop the provisioning of additional resources in AWS accounts when the allocated budget threshold is reached during a specific period.  
  
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Cost and Usage Reports section of the required AWS accounts.
Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Billing dashboards of the required AWS accounts.
Create an IAM user for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
Create an IAM role for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.

Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate config rule to prevent provisioning of additional resources.

Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate service control policy (SCP) to prevent provisioning of additional resources.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets can create account-specific cost budgets and send threshold notifications from the Billing and Cost Management console. To execute budget actions, AWS Budgets uses an IAM role created for budget actions rather than an IAM user. In an AWS Organizations environment, automatically preventing further resource provisioning at the account level is done by having the budget action apply a service control policy (SCP), because SCPs can deny API actions across the targeted account, whereas AWS Config rules evaluate compliance but do not directly block provisioning.

**Learn more:** [Creating a budget - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-create.html) · [Creating a cost budget - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-cost-budget.html)

A company wants to build a mobile app that lets users stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app records video clips and uploads them in raw format to an Amazon S3 bucket. The app then retrieves those video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format.  
  
Users are experiencing buffering and playback problems on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions that maximize the app's performance and scalability while minimizing operational overhead.  
  
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AW'S Regions in other S3 buckets.
Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
Deploy an Auto Sealing group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront improves video delivery performance by caching content at edge locations close to viewers, which reduces latency and offloads repeated reads from Amazon S3. Amazon Elastic Transcoder converts large source media in S3 into formats better suited for playback on consumer devices such as mobile phones, reducing buffering and compatibility issues. This combination addresses both distribution performance and mobile-friendly media format requirements with managed AWS services and minimal operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Hosting on-demand streaming video with Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, and Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/tutorial-s3-cloudfront-route53-video-streaming.html) · [Performance design patterns for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-design-patterns.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to limit access to the content of its web application. The company must protect that content by using authorization techniques available on AWS. The company also wants a serverless architecture for authorization and authentication with low login latency.  
  
The solution must integrate with the web application and serve web content globally. The application currently has a small user base, but the company expects the user base to grow.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Configure Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito is the AWS-native service for authentication and authorization for web applications and scales well for growing customer identities. Lambda@Edge can enforce authorization logic at CloudFront edge locations by inspecting tokens or headers before requests reach the origin, which helps minimize login and access latency for globally distributed users. Amazon CloudFront is the global content delivery service for serving web application content worldwide. AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is intended for Microsoft AD-aware workloads rather than a lightweight serverless internet-scale web app sign-in pattern, and Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration is for accelerating uploads and transfers to S3, not for globally serving a web application.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Cognito user pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools.html) · [Ways to use Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-ways-to-use.html)

A solutions architect is designing a payment processing application that runs on AWS Lambda in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses multiple Lambda functions and handles millions of transactions each day.  
  
The architecture must ensure that the application does not process duplicate payments.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket with an event notification to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the SQS queue and to process the due payments.

Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the FIFO queue and to process the due payments.
Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Store the due payments in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure streams on the DynamoDB table to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once message processing semantics and include built-in deduplication to prevent duplicate messages from being processed. For payment processing, where duplicate transactions must be prevented, FIFO queues are the purpose-built AWS solution. SQS standard queues only guarantee at-least-once delivery, which allows duplicates. DynamoDB Streams and Lambda event source mappings also provide at-least-once semantics, risking duplicate payment processing.

**Learn more:** [Exactly-once processing in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html) · [Using AWS Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company keeps its data objects in Amazon S3 Standard storage. A solutions architect has determined that 75% of the data is seldom accessed after 30 days. The company requires all of the data to stay immediately accessible with the same high availability and resiliency, while also wanting to minimize storage costs.  
  
Which storage solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Move the data objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Standard-IA is intended for infrequently accessed data that still requires millisecond access, and it stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones, unlike S3 One Zone-IA. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is archival storage and does not support immediate access because objects must be restored before use. Therefore, transitioning the objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days is the lowest-cost option that still preserves immediate accessibility and comparable multi-AZ resiliency.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Understanding archival storage in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/archival-storage.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. The company must retain all data for **5 years** and must delete all data after 5 years. The company also must keep **audit logs indefinitely** for actions performed within the database. Currently, the company has automated backups configured for Aurora.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Take a manual snapshot of the DB cluster.
Create a lifecycle policy for the automated backups.
Configure automated backup retention for 5 years.
Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster.
Use AWS Backup to take the backups and to keep the backups for 5 years.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora automated backups support a retention window of only 1 to 35 days, so they cannot satisfy a 5-year data-retention requirement. AWS Backup can manage Amazon Aurora backups and apply a lifecycle retention period of 5 years for the database backups. For indefinite retention of database audit activity, Aurora PostgreSQL logs should be exported to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, where the log group's retention can remain set to Never expire or another long-term retention setting. That combination satisfies both the 5-year data-retention requirement and the indefinite audit-log retention requirement.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Amazon Aurora backup storage usage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-storage-backup.html) · [Overview of backing up and restoring an Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has containerized a Windows job that runs on .NET 6 Framework in a Windows container. The company wants to run this job in the AWS Cloud. The job runs every 10 minutes, and its runtime varies between 1 minute and 3 minutes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function based on the container image of the job. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the function every 10 minutes.
Use AWS Batch to create a job that uses AWS Fargate resources. Configure the job scheduling to run every 10 minutes.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a scheduled task based on the container image of the job to run every 10 minutes.

Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a standalone task based on the container image of the job. Use Windows task scheduler to run the job every10 minutes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate is the best fit because AWS Fargate supports Windows containers for ECS tasks, and Amazon ECS supports scheduled tasks through Amazon EventBridge/EventBridge Scheduler. That lets the company run the container only every 10 minutes and pay only for the short 1–3 minute execution time, without managing servers or keeping a task running between executions. AWS Lambda is not a valid choice for a Windows container image, and using a standalone task with Windows Task Scheduler would require persistent infrastructure. AWS Batch can run scheduled Fargate jobs, but for a single recurring container job, ECS scheduled tasks are the more direct and economical serverless scheduling pattern.

**Learn more:** [Windows containers on Fargate considerations for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/windows-considerations.html) · [Learn how to create an Amazon ECS Windows task for Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/Windows_fargate-getting_started.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is designing a three-tier web application. The architecture includes:  
  
- an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB)  
- a web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets  
- an application tier with the business logic running on EC2 instances in private subnets  
- a database tier consisting of Microsoft SQL Server running on EC2 instances in private subnets  
  
Security is a high priority for the company.  
  
Which combination of security group configurations should the solutions architect use? **(Choose three.)**

options.text: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the ALB.
Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic to 0.0.0.0/0.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound Microsoft SQL Server traffic from the security group for the application tier.
Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the application tier to allow inbound HTTPS traffic from the security group for the web tier.
Configure the security group for the application tier to allow outbound HTTPS traffic and Microsoft SQL Server traffic to the security group for the web tier.

questions.explanation:
In a secure three-tier AWS architecture, security groups should enforce least-privilege access between adjacent tiers by referencing the source tier’s security group. The web tier should allow inbound HTTPS only from the ALB security group. The application tier should allow inbound HTTPS only from the web tier security group. The database tier should allow inbound Microsoft SQL Server traffic only from the application tier security group. AWS documentation for security group rules specifically describes allowing web servers to receive HTTP/HTTPS only from the load balancer and allowing database servers to receive database traffic from the upstream application or web tier by using security group references.

**Learn more:** [Security group rules - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html) · [Security group rules for different use cases - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/security-group-rules-reference.html)

questions.question:
A company is migrating an application from an on-premises environment to AWS. The application will store sensitive data in Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data before it is stored in Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with customer managed keys.
Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys.

questions.explanation: Client-side encryption encrypts data in the client application before it is uploaded to Amazon S3. Customer managed keys provide control over the encryption keys. Server-side encryption encrypts objects only after Amazon S3 receives them.
